Āryaśūra: Jātakamālā 1-15, revised text
  1. Vyāghrījātakam
  2. Śibijātakam

  4. Śreṣṭhijātakam
  5. Aviṣahyaśreṣṭhijātakam

body.translated_text: <s>Āryaśūra</s>: <s>Jātakamālā</s> 1-15, revised text. 1. The <s>Vyāghrī-Jātaka</s> (Tigress Story). 2. The <s>Śibi-Jātaka</s>. 3. The <s>Kulmāṣapiṇḍī-Jātaka</s>. 4. The <s>Śreṣṭhi-Jātaka</s>. 5. The <s>Aviṣahyaśreṣṭhi-Jātaka</s>. 6. The <s>Śaśa-Jātaka</s> (Hare Story). 7. The <s>Agastya-Jātaka</s>. 8. The <s>Maitrībala-Jātaka</s>. 9. The <s>Viśvaṃtara-Jātaka</s>. 10. The <s>Yajña-Jātaka</s>. 11. The <s>Śakra-Jātaka</s>. 12. The <s>Brāhmaṇa-Jātaka</s>. 13. The <s>Unmādayantī-Jātaka</s>. 14. The <s>Supāraga-Jātaka</s>. 15. The <s>Matsya-Jātaka</s> (Fish Story).

body.text: namo buddhāya //
body.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>.

children.text: śrīmanti sadguṇaparigrahamaṅgalāni kīrtyāspadāny anavagītamanoharāṇi /
children.translated_text: Glorious, adorned with the auspiciousness of embracing noble virtues, the abodes of fame, possessing an unsung charm—

children.text: pūrveṣu janmasu muneś caritādbhutāni bhaktyā svakāvyakusumāñjalinārcayiṣye // AJm_1.1 //
children.translated_text: The wondrous deeds of the Sage in his former births I shall worship with a flower-offering of my own poetry, with devotion.

children.text: ślāghyair amībhir abhilakṣitacihnabhūtair ādeśito bhavati yat sugatatvamārgaḥ /
children.translated_text: By these praiseworthy [deeds], distinguished as characteristic marks, the path to <s>Sugatahood</s> (Buddhahood) is revealed;

children.text: syād eva rūkṣamanasām api ca prasādo dharmyāḥ kathāś ca ramaṇīyataratvam īyuḥ // AJm_1.2 //
children.translated_text: May even those of harsh minds find serenity, and may these righteous stories attain the highest beauty.

children.text: lokārtham ity abhisamīkṣya kariṣyate 'yaṃ śrutyārṣayuktyaviguṇena pathā prayatnaḥ /
children.translated_text: Considering 'this is for the welfare of the world,' this effort is undertaken through a path not devoid of scriptural authority and sage-reasoning,

children.text: lokottamasya caritātiśayapradeśaiḥ svaṃ prātibhaṃ gamayituṃ śrutivallabhatvam // AJm_1.3 //
children.translated_text: To lead my own poetic talent to the beloved-of-the-ear through the extraordinary passages of the deeds of the Best of the World.

children.text: svārthodyatair api parārthacarasya yasya naivānvagamyata guṇapratipattiśobhā /
children.translated_text: He whose splendor of devotion to virtue was never fully comprehended even by those striving for their own aims, though he labored for the good of others—

children.text: sarvajña ity avitathākṣaradīptakīrtiṃ mūrdhnā name tam asamaṃ sahadharmasaṅgham // AJm_1.4 //
children.translated_text: To him, renowned by the true syllables 'Omniscient,' of blazing fame, together with the community of <s>Dharma</s>, incomparable, I bow my head.

children.text: 1. Vyāghrījātakam
children.translated_text: 1. The <s>Vyāghrī-Jātaka</s> (Tigress Story).

body.text: sarvasattveṣv akāraṇaparamavatsalasvabhāvaḥ sarvabhūtātmabhūtaḥ pūrvajanmasv api sa bhagavān iti buddhe bhagavati paraḥ prasādaḥ kāryaḥ //
body.translated_text: One whose very nature is supreme and unconditional tenderness toward all beings, who is the very self of all creatures—even in his former births, such was that <s>Bhagavān</s>. Thus the highest faith should be placed in the <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: tadyathānuśrūyate ratnatrayagurubhiḥ pratipattiguṇābhirādhitagurubhir guṇapracayagurubhir asmadgurubhiḥ parikīrtyamānam idaṃ bhagavataḥ pūrvajanmāvadānam / bodhisattvaḥ kila pratijñātiśayasadṛśair dānapriyavacanārthacaryāprabhṛtibhiḥ prajñāparigrahaniravadyaiḥ kāruṇyanisyandair lokam anugṛhṇan svadharmābhiratyupanataśucivṛttiny uditodite mahati brāhmaṇakule janmaparigrahaṃ cakāra // sa kṛtasaṃskārakramo jātakarmādibhir abhivardhamānaḥ prakṛtimedhāvitvāt sānāthyaviśeṣāj jñānakautūhalād akausīdyāc ca nacireṇaivāṣṭādaśasu vidyāsthāneṣu svakulakramāviruddhāsu ca sakalāsu kalāsv ācāryakaṃ param avāpa /
body.translated_text: As is traditionally heard, recounted by our teachers—venerable in their devotion to the Three Jewels, venerable in their qualities of practice, venerable in the accumulation of virtues—this is the story of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s former birth. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, it is said, favoring the world with acts of compassion—flawless, guided by wisdom—such as generosity, kind speech, beneficial conduct, and the like, befitting his extraordinary vows, took birth in a great and illustrious <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> family, of pure lineage and devoted to its own <s>dharma</s>. Having undergone the successive sacraments beginning with the birth-ceremony, and growing up, by his natural intelligence, the distinction of his patronage, his thirst for knowledge, and his diligence, in no long time he attained the highest mastery in the eighteen branches of learning and in all the arts not inconsistent with his family tradition.

children.text: sa brahmavad brahmavidāṃ babhūva rājeva rājñāṃ bahumānapātram /
children.translated_text: He became, like <s>Brahmā</s> among the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, like a king among kings, the object of great respect;

children.text: sākṣāt sahasrākṣa iva prajānāṃ jñānārthinām arthacaraḥ piteva // AJm_1.5 //
children.translated_text: Like <s>Sahasrākṣa</s> [<s>Indra</s>] himself for his people, a benefactor for seekers of knowledge, like a father.

body.text: tasya bhāgyaguṇātiśayasamāvarjito mahālābhasatkārayaśoviśeṣaḥ prādurabhūt/ dharmābhyāsabhāvitamatiḥ kṛtapravrajyāparicayas tu bodhisattvo na tenābhireme /
body.translated_text: An extraordinary abundance of great gain, honor, and fame arose for him, drawn by the superiority of his merit and virtue. But the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, his mind cultivated by the practice of <s>Dharma</s> and familiar with renunciation, took no delight in this.

children.text: sa pūrvacaryāpariśuddhabuddhiḥ kāmeṣu dṛṣṭvā bahudoṣajātam /
children.translated_text: He, whose understanding was purified by his former practice, having seen in sensual pleasures a multitude of faults,

children.text: gārhasthyam asvāsthyam ivāvadhūya kaṃ cid vanaprastham alaṃcakāra // AJm_1.6 //
children.translated_text: Shook off the householder's life like an illness, and graced a certain forest hermitage.

children.text: sa tatra niḥsaṅgatayā tayā ca prajñāvadātena śamena caiva /
children.translated_text: There, by that very detachment, and by his tranquility, radiant with wisdom,

children.text: pratyādideśeva kukāryasaṅgād viśliṣṭaśiṣṭopaśamaṃ nṛlokam // AJm_1.7 //
children.translated_text: He seemed to rebuke the human world, whose peace and refinement had departed through association with wrong deeds.

children.text: maitrīmayena praśamena tasya visyandinevānuparītacittāḥ /
children.translated_text: Their minds suffused as if by his tranquility, streaming forth with loving-kindness,

children.text: parasparadrohanivṛttabhāvās tapasvivad vyāḍamṛgā viceruḥ // AJm_1.8 //
children.translated_text: The wild beasts, having abandoned their nature of mutual hostility, roamed about like ascetics.

children.text: ācāraśuddhyā nibhṛtendriyatvāt saṃtoṣayogāt karuṇāguṇāc ca /
children.translated_text: Through the purity of his conduct, restraint of senses, contentment, and the virtue of compassion,

children.text: asaṃstutasyāpi janasya loke so 'bhūt priyas tasya yathaiva lokaḥ // AJm_1.9 //
children.translated_text: He became dear to people even without introduction, just as the world was dear to him.

children.text: alpecchabhāvāt kuhanānabhijñas tyaktaspṛho lābhayaśaḥsukhebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Of few desires, unknowing of hypocrisy, having abandoned craving for gain, fame, and comfort,

children.text: sa devatānām api mānasāni prasādabhaktipravaṇāni cakre // AJm_1.10 //
children.translated_text: He turned even the minds of the gods toward serene devotion.

children.text: śrutvātha taṃ pravrajitaṃ manuṣyā guṇais tadīyair avabaddhacittāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, having heard of his renunciation, people, their minds captivated by his virtues,

children.text: vihāya bandhūṃś ca parigrahāṃś ca tacchiṣyatāṃ siddhim ivopajagmuḥ // AJm_1.11 //
children.translated_text: Leaving behind kinsmen and possessions, came to be his disciples, as if attaining perfection.

children.text: śīle śucāv indriyabhāvanāyāṃ smṛtyapramoṣe praviviktatāyām /
children.translated_text: In moral conduct, purity, cultivation of the senses, unfailing mindfulness, seclusion,

children.text: maitryādike caiva manaḥsamādhau yathābalaṃ so 'nuśaśāsa śiṣyān // AJm_1.12 //
children.translated_text: Loving-kindness and the rest, and mental concentration—he instructed his disciples according to their capacity.

body.text: atha kadā cit sa mahātmā pariniṣpannabhūyiṣṭhe pṛthūbhūte śiṣyagaṇe pratiṣṭhāpite 'smin kalyāṇe vartmany avatārite naiṣkramyasatpathaṃ loke saṃvṛteṣv ivāpāyadvāreṣu rājamārgīkṛteṣv iva sugatimārgeṣu dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārārthaṃ tatkālaśiṣyeṇājitenānugamyamāno yogānukūlān parvatadarīnikuñjān anuvicacāra //
body.translated_text: Then once, that great soul, when his group of disciples had become for the most part accomplished and had grown large, when they were established on this auspicious path and led into the excellent way of renunciation—as if the doors to evil destinies in the world had been closed, as if the paths to good destinies had been made royal highways—for the sake of experiencing the bliss of the <s>Dharma</s> in this very life, accompanied by his current disciple <s>Ajita</s>, he wandered through mountain caves and groves conducive to meditation.

children.text: athātra vyāghravanitāṃ dadarśa girigahvare /
children.translated_text: And there, in a mountain cavern, he saw a tigress,

children.text: prasūtikleśadoṣeṇa gatāṃ vispandamandatām // AJm_1.13 //
children.translated_text: Brought to feeble motionlessness by the affliction of having recently given birth.

children.text: parikṣāmekṣaṇayugāṃ kṣudhā cchātatarodarīm /
children.translated_text: With her pair of eyes sunken, her belly hollow from hunger, more emaciated than before,

children.text: āhāram iva paśyantīṃ bālān svatanayān api // AJm_1.14 //
children.translated_text: She gazed upon her own cubs as if they were food.

children.text: stanyatarṣād upasṛtān mātṛviśrambhanirvyathān /
children.translated_text: The cubs, approaching trustfully as to a mother, drawn by thirst for milk,

children.text: rorūyitaravaiḥ krūrair bhartsayantīṃ parān iva // AJm_1.15 //
children.translated_text: She rebuffed with cruel growls, as if they were strangers.

children.text: bodhisattvas tu tāṃ dṛṣṭvā dhīro 'pi karuṇāvaśāt /
children.translated_text: But the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, though steadfast, upon seeing her, was overcome by compassion—

children.text: cakampe paraduḥkhena mahīkampād ivādrirāṭ // AJm_1.16 //
children.translated_text: He trembled at another's suffering, like the king of mountains at an earthquake.

children.text: mahatsv api svaduḥkheṣu vyaktadhairyāḥ kṛpātmakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who are compassionate by nature, even in the midst of their own great sufferings, remain visibly composed;

children.text: mṛdunāpy anyaduḥkhena kampante yat tad adbhutam // AJm_1.17 //
children.translated_text: That they tremble at the suffering of others, even slight—that is truly wondrous.

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ sasaṃbhramāmreḍitapadaṃ svabhāvātiśayavyañjakaṃ karuṇābalasamāhitākṣaraṃ śiṣyam uvāca / vatsa vatsa /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with words repeated in agitation—revealing the extraordinary depths of his nature—with syllables gathered by the force of compassion, spoke to his disciple: 'My child, my child!'

children.text: paśya saṃsāranairguṇyaṃ mṛgy eṣā svasutān api /
children.translated_text: 'Behold the wretchedness of <s>saṃsāra</s>! This wild creature, her own children even,

children.text: laṅghitasnehamaryādā bhoktum anvicchati kṣudhā // AJm_1.18 //
children.translated_text: Transgressing the bounds of motherly love, desires to devour in her hunger.'

children.text: aho batātikaṣṭeyam ātmasnehasya raudratā /
children.translated_text: 'Alas, how terrible is this cruelty of self-love,

children.text: yena mātāpi tanayān āhārayitum icchati // AJm_1.19 //
children.translated_text: By which even a mother desires to make food of her children!'

children.text: ātmasnehamayaṃ śatruṃ ko vardhayitum arhati /
children.translated_text: 'Who would nourish this enemy made of self-love,

children.text: yena kuryāt padanyāsam īdṛśeṣv api karmasu // AJm_1.20 //
children.translated_text: By which one could set foot in such [terrible] deeds?'

body.text: tac chīghram anviṣyatāṃ tāvat kutaś cid asyāḥ kṣudduḥkhapratīkārahetur yāvan na tanayān ātmānaṃ copahanti / aham api caināṃ prayatiṣye sāhasād asmād vārayitum / sa tathety asmai pratiśrutya tadāhārānveṣaṇaparo babhūva // atha bodhisattvas taṃ śiṣyaṃ savyapadeśam ativāhya cintām āpede /
body.translated_text: 'Therefore let some remedy for her suffering of hunger be quickly sought from somewhere, before she destroys her cubs and herself! I too shall try to restrain her from this violence.' Having promised 'So be it,' the disciple devoted himself to searching for food for her. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having sent that disciple away with a pretext, fell into reflection:

children.text: saṃvidyamāne sakale śarīre kasmāt parasmān mṛgayāmi māṃsam /
children.translated_text: 'When this entire body of mine exists, why should I seek flesh from another?

children.text: yādṛcchikī tasya hi lābhasaṃpat kāryātyayaḥ syāc ca tathā mamāyam // AJm_1.21 //
children.translated_text: For the chance of obtaining that is uncertain, and there would be a loss of this critical moment for me.'

body.text: api ca /
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: nirātmake bhedini sārahīne duḥkhe kṛtaghne satatāśucau ca /
children.translated_text: 'In this body—selfless, perishable, devoid of essence,

children.text: dehe parasmāy upayujyamāne na prītimān yo na vicakṣaṇaḥ saḥ // AJm_1.22 //
children.translated_text: Full of suffering, ungrateful, and perpetually impure—he who feels no joy when it is used for another's sake is not truly wise.'

children.text: svasaukhyasaṅgena parasya duḥkham upekṣyate śaktiparikṣayād vā /
children.translated_text: 'One neglects the suffering of others either from attachment to one's own comfort, or from exhaustion of capacity;

children.text: na cānyaduḥkhe sati me 'sti saukhyaṃ satyāṃ ca śaktau kim upekṣakaḥ syām // AJm_1.23 //
children.translated_text: But I have no comfort when another suffers, and since capacity exists, why should I be indifferent?'

children.text: satyāṃ ca śaktau mama yady upekṣā syād ātatāyiny api duḥkhamagne /
children.translated_text: 'If, when capacity exists, I were to be indifferent even to one plunged in suffering by an assailant,

children.text: kṛtveva pāpaṃ mama tena cittaṃ dahyeta kakṣaṃ mahatāgnineva // AJm_1.24 //
children.translated_text: My mind would burn as if I had committed a sin—like dry grass consumed by a great fire.'

children.text: tasmāt kariṣyāmi śarīrakeṇa taṭaprapātodgatajīvitena /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore I shall use this little body, whose life hangs over a precipice-edge,

children.text: saṃrakṣaṇaṃ putravadhāc ca mṛgyā mṛgyāḥ sakāśāc ca tadātmajānām // AJm_1.25 //
children.translated_text: To save the tigress from killing her cubs, and the cubs from their mother.'

body.text: kiṃ ca bhūyaḥ /
body.translated_text: And further:

children.text: saṃdarśanaṃ lokahitotsukānām uttejanaṃ mandaparākramāṇām /
children.translated_text: 'An inspiration for those eager for the world's welfare, an encouragement for those of feeble effort,

children.text: saṃharṣaṇaṃ tyāgaviśāradānām ākarṣaṇaṃ sajjanamānasānām // AJm_1.26 //
children.translated_text: A delight for those skilled in generosity, an attraction for the minds of the virtuous;'

children.text: viṣādanaṃ māramahācamūnāṃ prasādanaṃ buddhaguṇapriyāṇām /
children.translated_text: 'A dismay for the great armies of <s>Māra</s>, a joy for those devoted to the <s>Buddha</s>'s qualities,

children.text: vrīḍodayaṃ svārthaparāyaṇānāṃ mātsaryalobhopahatātmanāṃ ca // AJm_1.27 //
children.translated_text: A source of shame for the selfish, and for those afflicted by stinginess and greed;'

children.text: śraddhāpanaṃ yānavarāśritānāṃ vismāpanaṃ tyāgakṛtasmayānām /
children.translated_text: 'An inspiration of faith for those who follow the supreme Vehicle, an astonishment for those who take pride in [their own] generosity,

children.text: viśodhanaṃ svargamahāpathasya tyāgapriyāṇām anumodinṝṇām // AJm_1.28 //
children.translated_text: A purification of the great highway to heaven—for those who rejoice in the generosity of the generous;'

children.text: kadā nu gātrair api nāma kuryāṃ hitaṃ pareṣām iti yaś ca me 'bhūt /
children.translated_text: 'When shall I be able to do good to others even with my limbs?'—this desire of mine,

children.text: manorathas taṃ saphalīkriyāsaṃ saṃbodhim agryām api cāvidūre // AJm_1.29 //
children.translated_text: Let it be fulfilled, and supreme <s>bodhi</s> (enlightenment) too is not far off.'

children.text: na spardhayā naiva yaśo'bhilāṣān na svargalobhān na ca rājyahetoḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Not from rivalry, nor from desire for fame, nor from greed for heaven, nor for the sake of kingship,

children.text: nātyantike 'py ātmasukhe yathāyaṃ mamādaro 'nyatra parārthasiddheḥ // AJm_1.30 //
children.translated_text: Nor even for the ultimate happiness of the self—my zeal is for nothing other than the accomplishment of others' welfare.'

children.text: tathā mamānena samānakālaṃ lokasya duḥkhaṃ ca sukhodayaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: 'And thus, may I always have the power simultaneously

children.text: hartuṃ ca kartuṃ ca sadāstu śaktis tamaḥ prakāśaṃ ca yathaiva bhānoḥ // AJm_1.31 //
children.translated_text: To remove the world's suffering and to create its happiness—like the sun [dispelling] darkness and [creating] light.'

children.text: dṛṣṭaḥ śruto 'nusmṛtim āgato vā spṛṣṭaḥ kathāyogam upāgato vā /
children.translated_text: 'Whether I am seen, heard, remembered,

children.text: sarvaprakāraṃ jagato hitāni kuryām ajasraṃ sukhasaṃhitāni // AJm_1.32 //
children.translated_text: Touched, or become a topic of conversation—may I continuously bring about all manner of benefits and happiness for the world.'

children.text: evaṃ sa niścitya parārthasiddhyai prāṇātyaye 'py āpatitapramodaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having thus resolved, for the accomplishment of others' welfare, overjoyed even at the loss of his own life,

children.text: manāṃsi dhīrāṇy api devatānāṃ vismāpayan svāṃ tanum utsasarja // AJm_1.33 //
children.translated_text: Astonishing even the steadfast minds of the gods, he cast down his own body.

body.text: atha sā vyāghrī tena bodhisattvasya śarīranipātaśabdena samutthāpitakautūhalāmarṣā viramya svatanayavaiśasodyamāt tato nayane vicikṣepa / dṛṣṭvaiva ca tad bodhisattvaśarīram udgataprāṇaṃ sahasābhisṛtya bhakṣayitum upacakrame / atha sa tasya śiṣyo māṃsam anāsādyaiva pratinivṛttaḥ kutropādhyāya iti vilokayaṃs tad bodhisattvaśarīram udgataprāṇaṃ tayā vyāghrayuvatyā bhakṣyamāṇaṃ dadarśa / sa tatkarmātiśayavismayāt prativyūḍhaśokaduḥkhāvegas tadguṇāśrayabahumānam ivodgirann idam ātmagataṃ bruvāṇaḥ śobheta /
body.translated_text: Then the tigress, her curiosity and ferocity aroused by the sound of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s body falling, desisted from her attempt to slaughter her cubs and cast her eyes in that direction. And seeing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s body, now lifeless, she quickly approached and began to devour it. Meanwhile, his disciple, having found no meat, returned and, looking about [saying] 'Where is the teacher?', saw the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s lifeless body being eaten by that young tigress. Overwhelmed with wonder at that extraordinary deed, his torrent of grief and sorrow checked, as if pouring forth his reverence for the [master's] repository of virtues, he would have looked splendid saying this to himself:

children.text: aho dayāsya vyasanāture jane svasaukhyanaiḥsaṅgyam aho mahātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Oh, his compassion for people afflicted by calamity! Oh, the great soul's disregard for his own happiness!

children.text: aho prakarṣaṃ gamitā sthitiḥ satām aho pareṣāṃ mṛditā yaśaḥśriyaḥ // AJm_1.34 //
children.translated_text: Oh, the standard of the virtuous, carried to its utmost height! Oh, the glories and fame of others, trampled!'

children.text: aho parākrāntam apetasādhvasaṃ guṇāśrayaṃ prema paraṃ vidarśitam /
children.translated_text: 'Oh, fearless valor has been demonstrated, and supreme love for virtue's abode!

children.text: aho namaskāraviśeṣapātratāṃ prasahya nītā svaguṇātanus tanuḥ // AJm_1.35 //
children.translated_text: Oh, this body—thin with [the expenditure of] its own virtues—has been forcefully brought to the state of supreme worthiness of veneration!'

children.text: nisargasaumyasya vasuṃdharādhṛter aho pareṣāṃ vyasaneṣv amarṣitā /
children.translated_text: 'Oh, the impatience of this one, gentle by nature and steadfast as the earth, at the misfortunes of others!

children.text: aho madīyā gamitā prakāśatāṃ khaṭuṅkatā vikramasaṃpadānayā // AJm_1.36 //
children.translated_text: Oh, my own feebleness has been brought to light by this display of valorous splendor!'

children.text: anena nāthena sanāthatāṃ gataṃ na śocitavyaṃ khalu sāṃprataṃ jagat /
children.translated_text: 'The world has gained a protector through him, so there is indeed no cause for grief now;

children.text: parājayāśaṅkitajātasaṃbhramo dhruvaṃ viniśvāsaparo 'dya manmathaḥ // AJm_1.37 //
children.translated_text: Surely <s>Manmatha</s> [<s>Kāma</s>, the god of desire], alarmed by the apprehension of defeat, is today intent upon sighing.'

body.text: sarvathā namo 'stv asmai mahābhāgāya sarvabhūtaśaraṇyāyātivipulakāruṇyāyāprameyasattvāya bhūtārthabodhisattvāyeti // atha sa tam arthaṃ sabrahmacāribhyo nivedayām āsa /
body.translated_text: 'In every way, homage to this greatly blessed one, refuge of all beings, of immeasurably vast compassion, of immeasurable strength—a true <s>Bodhisattva</s>!' Then he reported this matter to his fellow renouncers.

children.text: tatkarmavismitamukhair atha tasya śiṣyair gandharvayakṣabhujagais tridaśādhipaiś ca /
children.translated_text: Then, by his disciples whose faces were astonished at that deed, and by <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, and lords of the gods,

children.text: mālyāmbarābharaṇacandanacūrṇavarṣaiś channā tadasthivasudhā vasudhā babhūva // AJm_1.38 //
children.translated_text: The earth where those bones [lay] became covered with showers of garlands, garments, ornaments, and sandal-powder—[and thus] became a blessed earth.

body.text: tad evaṃ sarvasattveṣv akāraṇaparamavatsalasvabhāvaḥ sarvabhūtātmabhūtaḥ pūrvajanmasv api sa bhagavān iti buddhe bhagavati paraḥ prasādaḥ kāryaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus, one whose very nature is supreme and unconditional tenderness toward all beings, who is the very self of all creatures—even in his former births, such was that <s>Bhagavān</s>. Therefore the highest faith should be placed in the <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: jātaprasādaiś ca buddhe bhagavati prītir utpādayitavyā / evam āyatanagato naḥ prasāda ity evam apy upaneyam / tathā satkṛtya dharmaḥ śrotavyaḥ / evaṃ duṣkaraśatasamudānītatvāt karuṇāvarṇe 'pi vācyam evaṃ svabhāvātiśayaniṣpādikā parānugrahapravṛttihetuḥ karuṇeti //
body.translated_text: And through the faith thus generated, devotion toward the blessed <s>Buddha</s> should be produced. Thus it should also be brought [to the audience] thus: 'Our faith has found its abode.' Likewise, the <s>Dharma</s> should be heard with due reverence. Thus, even when describing [his] compassion—since it was accomplished through hundreds of arduous deeds—one should say: 'Compassion is that which brings about the excellence of one's nature and is the cause of the inclination to benefit others.'

body.text: bodhisattvāvadānamālāyāṃ vyāghrījātakaṃ prathamam //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Bodhisattvāvadānamālā</s> (Garland of the Bodhisattva's Noble Deeds), the <s>Vyāghrī-jātaka</s> (Story of the Tigress) is the first.

children.text: 2. Śibijātakam
children.translated_text: 2. The <s>Śibi-jātaka</s> (Story of <s>Śibi</s>)

body.text: duṣkaraśatasamudānīto 'yam asmadarthaṃ tena bhagavatā saddharma iti satkṛtya śrotavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'This True <s>Dharma</s> was accomplished by that Blessed One through hundreds of arduous deeds for our sake'—thus should it be heard with reverence.

body.text: tadyathānuśrūyate / bodhisattvabhūtaḥ kilāyaṃ bhagavān aparimitakālābhyāsāt sātmībhūtopacitapuṇyakarmā kadā cic chibīnāṃ rājā babhūva / sa bālyāt prabhṛty eva vṛddhopāsanaratir vinayānurakto 'nuraktaprakṛtiḥ prakṛtimedhāvitvād anekavidyādhigamavimalataramatir utsāhamantraprabhāvaśaktidaivasaṃpannaḥ svā iva prajāḥ prajāḥ pālayati sma /
body.translated_text: Thus it is heard in tradition: The Blessed One, when he was a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having through practice over immeasurable time made meritorious deeds his very nature and accumulated [them], once became king of the <s>Śibis</s>. From childhood onward, he was devoted to attending upon elders, attached to good conduct, with subjects devoted [to him]; through natural intelligence, his mind was made supremely pure by the mastery of many sciences; endowed with energy, counsel, power, and divine fortune, he protected his people as if they were his own [children].

children.text: tasmiṃs trivargānuguṇā guṇaughāḥ saṃharṣayogād iva saṃniviṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: In him, hosts of virtues conforming to the three goals [of life] were established, as if through the bond of mutual delight;

children.text: samastarūpā vibabhur na cāsur virodhasaṃkṣobhavipannaśobhāḥ // AJm_2.1 //
children.translated_text: They shone in their fullness and were not robbed of their beauty by the agitation of mutual conflict.

children.text: viḍambanevāvinayoddhatānāṃ durmedhasām āpad ivātikaṣṭā /
children.translated_text: That which is like a mockery for the ill-mannered and arrogant, like an extremely harsh calamity for the dull-witted,

children.text: alpātmanāṃ yā madireva lakṣmīr babhūva sā tatra yathārthanāmā // AJm_2.2 //
children.translated_text: Which is like intoxicating liquor for the small-minded—<s>Lakṣmī</s> (Royal Fortune) there [in him] became true to her name.

children.text: udārabhāvāt karuṇāguṇāc ca vittādhipatyāc ca sa rājavaryaḥ /
children.translated_text: That best of kings, through his noble disposition, the quality of compassion, and his lordship of wealth,

children.text: reme 'rthinām īpsitasiddhiharṣād akliṣṭaśobhāni mukhāni paśyan // AJm_2.3 //
children.translated_text: Delighted in seeing the faces of petitioners—radiant with untroubled beauty, joyful at the fulfillment of their desires.

body.text: atha sa rājā dānapriyatvāt samantato nagarasya sarvopakaraṇadhanadhānyasamṛddhā dānaśālāḥ kārayitvā svamāhātmyānurūpaṃ yathābhiprāyasaṃpāditaṃ sopacāramanoharam anatikrāntakālasubhagaṃ dānavarṣaṃ kṛtayugamegha iva vavarṣa / annam annārthibhyaḥ pānaṃ pānārthibhyaḥ śayanāsanavasanabhojanagandhamālyasuvarṇarajatādi tattadarthibhyaḥ // atha tasya rājñaḥ pradānaudāryaśravaṇād vismitapramuditahṛdayā nānādigabhilakṣitadeśanivāsinaḥ puruṣās taṃ deśam abhijagmuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then that king, out of his love for giving, having built alms-halls all around the city, abundantly supplied with all provisions, wealth, and grain, rained a shower of gifts—befitting his own greatness, arranged according to [petitioners'] wishes, gracious with hospitality, charming with timely elegance—like a cloud in the <s>Kṛtayuga</s> (Golden Age). Food to those who wanted food, drink to those who wanted drink, bedding, seats, garments, victuals, perfumes, garlands, gold, silver, and so forth to those who wanted each. Then, upon hearing of the king's magnificent generosity, people dwelling in regions associated with various directions, their hearts filled with wonder and delight, came to that land.

children.text: parītya kṛtsnaṃ manasā nṛlokam anyeṣv alabdhapraṇayāvakāśāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having surveyed in their minds the entire world of men, finding no opportunity for favor elsewhere,

children.text: tam arthinaḥ prītimukhāḥ samīyur mahāhradaṃ vanyagajā yathaiva // AJm_2.4 //
children.translated_text: Those petitioners, with faces full of joy, gathered to him, just as wild elephants [gather] to a great lake.

body.text: atha sa rājā samantataḥ samāpatato lābhāśāpramuditamanasaḥ pathikanepathyapracchāditaśobhasya vanīpakajanasya
body.translated_text: Then that king, [seeing] the merchant-folk arriving from all directions, their minds delighted with the hope of gain, their beauty concealed by travelers' garb—

children.text: viproṣitasyeva suhṛjjanasya saṃdarśanāt prītivijṛmbhitākṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: With eyes wide with joy as at the sight of long-absent friends,

children.text: yācñāṃ priyākhyānam ivābhyanandad dattvā ca tuṣṭyārthijanaṃ jigāya // AJm_2.5 //
children.translated_text: He welcomed their requests as if [hearing] beloved tidings, and having given, he conquered the petitioners' hearts with satisfaction.

children.text: dānodbhavaḥ kīrtimayaḥ sa gandhas tasyārthināṃ vāganilaprakīrṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: The fragrance born of his generosity, consisting of fame, scattered by the wind of petitioners' words,

children.text: madaṃ jahārānyanarādhipānāṃ gandhadvipasyeva paradvipānām // AJm_2.6 //
children.translated_text: Stripped away the pride of other kings, as [the scent of] a rutting elephant [does that of] rival elephants.

body.text: atha kadā cit sa rājā dānaśālāḥ samanuvicaraṃs tṛptatvād arthijanasya praviralaṃ yācanakajanasaṃpātam abhisamīkṣya dānadharmasyānutsarpaṇān na tuṣṭim upajagāma /
body.translated_text: Then once, that king, while touring the alms-halls, observing that the throng of supplicants had thinned due to the petitioners' satisfaction, did not attain contentment because his practice of generosity (<s>dānadharma</s>) could not advance further.

children.text: tarṣaṃ vininye 'rthijanas tam etya na tv arthinaḥ prāpya sa dānaśauṇḍaḥ /
children.translated_text: The petitioners, having come to him, assuaged their thirst; but he, addicted to giving, did not [attain satisfaction] even upon receiving petitioners—

children.text: na hy asya dānavyavasāyam arthī yācñāpramāṇena śaśāka jetum // AJm_2.7 //
children.translated_text: For no supplicant could match his resolve to give with the measure of his request.

body.text: tasya buddhir abhavat / atisabhāgyās te satpuruṣaviśeṣā ye viśrambhaniryantraṇapraṇayam arthibhiḥ svagātrāṇy api yācyante / mama punaḥ pratyākhyānarūkṣākṣaravacanasaṃtarjita ivārthijano dhanamātrake 'py apragalbhapraṇayaḥ saṃvṛtta iti //
body.translated_text: He thought: 'Supremely fortunate are those extraordinary noble beings whose own bodily limbs are requested by supplicants with unreserved, unrestrained affection. But in my case, petitioners have become timid in their affection even for mere wealth, as if intimidated by the harsh syllables of refusal.'

children.text: atha kṣitīśasya tam atyudāraṃ gātreṣv api sveṣu nivṛttasaṅgam /
children.translated_text: Then, perceiving the king's exceedingly noble intention to give, free from attachment even to his own limbs,

children.text: vijñāya dānāśrayiṇaṃ vitarkaṃ patipriyā strīva mahī cakampe // AJm_2.8 //
children.translated_text: The earth trembled, like a wife devoted to her husband.

body.text: atha śakro devānām indraḥ kṣititalacalanād ākampite

children.text: vividha
children.translated_text: was shaken

children.text: ratnaprabhodbhāsini sumerau parvatarāje kim idam iti samutpatitavitarkas tasya rājña imaṃ vitarkātiśayaṃ dharaṇicalananimittam avetya vismayāvarjitahṛdayaś cintām āpede /
children.translated_text: by the trembling of the earth's surface—having started wondering 'What is this?'—upon realizing that this extraordinary resolve of the king was the cause of the earth's trembling, his heart seized with wonder, fell into reflection.

body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, when Mount <s>Sumeru</s>, king of mountains, blazing with the splendor of various gems,

children.text: dānātiharṣoddhatamānasena vitarkitaṃ kiṃ svid idaṃ nṛpeṇa /
children.translated_text: 'What has been conceived by this king, his mind elated with excessive joy in giving,

children.text: ābadhya dānavyavasāyakakṣyāṃ svagātradānasthiraniścayena // AJm_2.9 //
children.translated_text: Having bound on the girdle of his resolve to give, firm in his determination to give his own body?'

body.text: tan mīmāṃsiṣye tāvad enam iti // atha tasya rājñaḥ pariṣadi niṣannasyāmātyagaṇaparivṛtasya samucitāyāṃ kṛtāyām arthijanasya kaḥ kim icchatīty āhvānaghoṣaṇāyāṃ samudghāṭyamāneṣu kośādhyakṣādhiṣṭhiteṣu maṇikanakarajatadhananicayeṣu viśliṣyamāṇapuṭāsu vividhavasanaparipūrṇagarbhāsu vastrapeḍāsu samupavartyamāneṣu vinītavividhavāhanaskandhapratiṣṭhitayugeṣu vicitreṣu yānaviśeṣeṣu pravṛtte 'rthijanasaṃpāte śakro devānām indro vṛddham andhaṃ brāhmaṇarūpam abhinirmāya rājñaś cakṣuḥpathe prādurabhavat / atha sa rājñā kāruṇyamaitrīparibhāvitayā dhīraprasannasaumyayā pratyudgata iva pariṣvakta iva ca dṛṣṭyā kenārtha ity upanimantryamāṇaḥ kṣitipānucarair nṛpatisamīpam upetya jayāśīrvacanapuraḥsaraṃ rājānam ity uvāca /
body.translated_text: 'I shall test him then.' Then, while the king was seated in his assembly, surrounded by his retinue of ministers, when the appropriate call 'Who wishes what?' was being announced for the petitioners, when the treasuries overseen by treasury superintendents were being opened with heaps of gems, gold, silver, and wealth, when chests filled with various garments were being unfolded, when various elegant vehicles with teams of well-trained draft-animals were being brought forward, and when the throng of petitioners was streaming in—<s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, fashioned the form of an old, blind <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and appeared before the king. Then the king, with a gaze infused with compassion and friendliness, steady, clear, and gentle—as if going out to greet him, as if embracing him—invited him with the words 'What do you need?' The [<s>brāhmaṇa</s>], approaching the king's presence escorted by the king's attendants, preceded by words of blessing and victory, addressed the king thus:

children.text: dūrād apaśyan sthaviro 'bhyupetas tvaccakṣuṣo 'rthī kṣitipapradhāna /
children.translated_text: 'An old man, unable to see from afar, has come as a petitioner for your eyes, O foremost of kings—

children.text: ekekṣaṇenāpi hi paṅkajākṣa gamyeta lokādhipa lokayātrā // AJm_2.10 //
children.translated_text: For even with a single eye, O lotus-eyed lord of the world, one could conduct the journey of life.'

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ samabhilaṣitamanorathaprasiddhyā paraṃ prītyutsavam anubhavan kiṃ svid idaṃ satyam evoktaṃ brāhmaṇena syād uta vikalpābhyāsān mayaivam upadhāritam iti jātapratyavamarśaś cakṣuryācñāpriyavacanaśravaṇatṛṣitamatis taṃ cakṣuryācanakam uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, experiencing the supreme festival of joy at the fulfillment of his long-cherished wish, yet reflecting with self-examination—'Is this truly what the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> has said, or have I merely imagined it from habit of such fancies?'—his mind thirsting to hear those dear words requesting his eyes, addressed the eye-petitioner thus:

children.text: kenānuśiṣṭas tvam ihābhyupeto māṃ yācituṃ brāhmaṇamukhya cakṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Instructed by whom have you come here to ask me for my eyes, O best of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>?

children.text: sudustyajaṃ cakṣur iti pravādasaṃbhāvanā kasya mayi vyatītā // AJm_2.11 //
children.translated_text: Who has gone beyond the common presumption that eyes are extremely difficult to give up, in regard to me?'

body.text: atha sa brāhmaṇaveṣadhārī śakras tasya rājña āśayaṃ viditvovāca /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, wearing the guise of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having perceived the king's intention, spoke:

children.text: śakrasya śakrapratimānuśiṣṭyā tvāṃ yācituṃ cakṣur ihāgato 'smi /
children.translated_text: 'By the instruction of <s>Śakra</s>, whose equal is <s>Śakra</s> alone, I have come here to ask you for eyes.

children.text: saṃbhāvanāṃ tasya mamāpi cāśāṃ cakṣuḥpradānāt saphalīkuruṣva // AJm_2.12 //
children.translated_text: By the gift of eyes, make fruitful both his expectation and my hope.'

body.text: atha sa rājā śakrasaṃkīrtanān nūnam asya brāhmaṇasya bhavitrī devatānubhāvād anena vidhinā cakṣuḥsaṃpad iti matvā pramodaviśadākṣaram enam uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then that king, upon hearing <s>Śakra</s>'s name mentioned, thinking, 'Surely this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> will recover his eyesight through divine power by this means,' spoke to him with words clear with delight:

children.text: yenābhyupeto 'si manorathena tam eṣa te brāhmaṇa pūrayāmi /
children.translated_text: 'The wish with which you have come, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, I shall fulfill.

children.text: ākāṅkṣamāṇāya mad ekam akṣi dadāmi cakṣurdvayam apy ahaṃ te // AJm_2.13 //
children.translated_text: To you who desired from me only one eye, I give both my eyes.'

children.text: sa tvaṃ vibuddhanayanotpalaśobhitāsyaḥ saṃpaśyato vraja yathābhimataṃ janasya /
children.translated_text: 'Then you, with your face adorned with eyes [like] blossoming lotuses, go as you wish before the watching people—

children.text: syāt kiṃ nu so 'yam uta neti vicāradolālolasya so 'yam iti cotthitavismayasya // AJm_2.14 //
children.translated_text: Who will waver on the swing of deliberation—"Is this he or not?"—and who will be filled with arisen wonder, [saying] "This is indeed he!"'

body.text: atha tasya rājño 'mātyāś cakṣuḥpradānavyavasāyam avetya sasaṃbhramāvegaviṣādavyathitamanaso rājānam ūcuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the king's ministers, perceiving his resolve to give his eyes, their minds distressed with agitation, urgency, and grief, addressed the king:

children.text: dānātiharṣād anayam asamīkṣyāhitodayam /
children.translated_text: 'From excessive delight in giving, [comes] ruin whose harmful consequences are unforeseen.

children.text: prasīda deva mā maivaṃ na cakṣur dātum arhasi // AJm_2.15 //
children.translated_text: Be gracious, O lord! Not thus! You should not give your eyes!'

children.text: ekasyārthe dvijasyāsya mā naḥ sarvān parākṛthāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For the sake of this one <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, do not reject all of us!

children.text: alaṃ śokāgninā dagdhuṃ sukhasaṃvardhitāḥ prajāḥ // AJm_2.16 //
children.translated_text: Enough! Do not burn with the fire of grief your subjects, reared in happiness.'

children.text: dhanāni lakṣmīpratibodhanāni śrīmanti ratnāni payasvinīr gāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Give [him] riches that awaken <s>Lakṣmī</s>, splendid jewels, milch cows,

children.text: rathān vinītāśvayujaḥ prayaccha madorjitaśrīlalitān dvipāṃś ca // AJm_2.17 //
children.translated_text: Chariots yoked with well-trained horses, and elephants graceful with the beauty of their rut—'

children.text: samuccarannūpuranisvanāni śaratpayodābhyadhikadyutīni /
children.translated_text: 'Mansions resounding with anklet-chimes, more radiant than autumn clouds,

children.text: gṛhāṇi sarvartusukhāni dehi mā dāḥ svacakṣur jagadekacakṣuḥ // AJm_2.18 //
children.translated_text: Comfortable in all seasons—give [these]! Do not give your own eyes, O sole eye of the world!'

body.text: vimṛśyatām api ca tāvan mahārāja /
body.translated_text: 'And please consider this, O great king:

children.text: anyadīyaṃ kathaṃ nāma cakṣur anyatra yojyate /
children.translated_text: How can one person's eye be fitted to another?

children.text: atha daivaprabhāvo 'yaṃ tvaccakṣuḥ kim apekṣate // AJm_2.19 //
children.translated_text: And if this is a divine miracle, what need has it for your eyes?'

body.text: api ca deva /
body.translated_text: 'Moreover, O lord:

children.text: cakṣuṣā kiṃ daridrasya parābhyudayasākṣiṇā /
children.translated_text: What use are eyes to a poor man—merely a witness to others' prosperity?

children.text: dhanam eva yato dehi deva mā sāhasaṃ kṛthāḥ // AJm_2.20 //
children.translated_text: Therefore give wealth, O lord! Do not commit this rash act!'

body.text: atha sa rājā tān amātyān sānunayamadhurākṣaram ity uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then that king spoke to his ministers with words gentle and sweet:

children.text: adāne kurute buddhiṃ dāsyāmīty abhidhāya yaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He who, having said "I shall give," then sets his mind on not giving—

children.text: sa lobhapāśaṃ prabhraṣṭam ātmani pratimuñcati // AJm_2.21 //
children.translated_text: Fastens upon himself the fallen noose of greed.'

children.text: dāsyāmīti pratijñāya yo 'nyathā kurute manaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He who, having promised "I shall give," then turns his mind otherwise—

children.text: kārpaṇyāniścitamateḥ kaḥ syāt pāpataras tataḥ // AJm_2.22 //
children.translated_text: Who could be more sinful than one of such irresolute mind, given to miserliness?'

children.text: sthirīkṛtyārthinām āśāṃ dāsyāmīti pratijñayā /
children.translated_text: 'Having made firm the hope of petitioners with the promise "I shall give"—

children.text: visaṃvādanarūkṣasya vacaso nāsti niṣkrayaḥ // AJm_2.23 //
children.translated_text: There is no atonement for the harsh word of betrayal.'

body.text: yad api coktaṃ devatānubhāvād eva cakṣur asya kiṃ na saṃbhavatīty atrāpi śrūyatām /
body.translated_text: 'And as for what was said—"Could not his sight be restored by divine power alone?"—hear my answer to this as well:

children.text: naikakāraṇasādhyatvaṃ kāryāṇāṃ nanu dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: Is it not seen that effects require more than a single cause?

children.text: kāraṇāntarasāpekṣaḥ syād daivo 'pi vidhir yataḥ // AJm_2.24 //
children.translated_text: For even a divine dispensation may depend upon some other condition.'

body.text: tan me dānātiśayavighnāya vyāyantuṃ nārhanti bhavanta iti // amātyā ūcuḥ / dhanadhānyaratnādi devo dātum arhati na svacakṣur iti vijñāpitam asmābhiḥ / tan na devaṃ vayam atīrthe pratārayāmaḥ // rājovāca /
body.translated_text: 'Therefore you should not strive to obstruct my supreme act of giving.' The ministers said: 'We have humbly submitted that the lord should give wealth, grain, gems, and the like—not his own eyes. We do not mislead the lord without cause.' The king said:

children.text: yad eva yācyeta tad eva dadyān nānīpsitaṃ prīṇayatīha dattam /
children.translated_text: 'One should give precisely what is asked for; what is given unasked does not satisfy.

children.text: kim uhyamānasya jalena toyair dāsyāmy ataḥ prārthitam artham asmai // AJm_2.25 //
children.translated_text: What use is more water to one being carried away by a flood? Therefore I shall give him the very thing he requests.'

body.text: atha tasya rājño rūḍhataraviśrambhapraṇayaḥ snehāvegād anapekṣitopacāro 'mātyamukhyas taṃ rājānam ity uvāca / mā tāvad bhoḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the chief minister, whose intimate affection [for the king] had grown deep, disregarding formality in the urgency of his love, addressed the king: 'Stay, sir!'

children.text: yā nālpena tapaḥsamādhividhinā saṃprāpyate kena cid yām āsādya ca bhūribhir makhaśataiḥ kīrtiṃ divaṃ cāpnuyāt /
children.translated_text: 'That kingship which no one attains by a small measure of austerity and meditation, having attained which one could gain fame and heaven through abundant hundreds of sacrifices—

children.text: saṃprāptām atipatya tāṃ nṛpatitāṃ śakrarddhivispardhinīṃ kiṃ dṛṣṭvā nayane praditsati bhavān ko 'yaṃ kutastyo vidhiḥ // AJm_2.26 //
children.translated_text: Having obtained that kingship, rivaling <s>Śakra</s>'s prosperity, why do you wish to give away your eyes? What is this custom? Whence does it come?'

children.text: labdhāvakāśas tridaśeṣu yajñaiḥ kīrtyā samantād avabhāsamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having gained a place among the gods through sacrifices, shining all around with fame,

children.text: narendracūḍādyutirañjitāṅghriḥ kiṃ lipsamāno nu dadāsi cakṣuḥ // AJm_2.27 //
children.translated_text: Your feet adorned by the luster of the diadems of [subordinate] kings—what are you seeking to gain by giving your eyes?'

body.text: atha sa rājā tam amātyaṃ sānunayam ity uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then that king spoke to his minister gently:

children.text: nāyaṃ yatnaḥ sārvabhaumatvam āptuṃ naiva svargaṃ nāpavargaṃ na kīrtim /
children.translated_text: 'This effort is not to attain universal sovereignty, nor heaven, nor liberation, nor fame.

children.text: trātuṃ lokān ity ayaṃ tv ādaro me yācñākleśo mā ca bhūd asya moghaḥ // AJm_2.28 //
children.translated_text: Rather, my concern is to save the world—and may this man's trouble in asking not be in vain!'

body.text: atha sa rājā nīlotpaladalarucirakānti nayanam ekaṃ vaidyaparidṛṣṭena vidhinā śanakair akṣatam utpāṭya parayā prītyā cakṣuryācanakāya prāyacchat / atha śakro devendras tādṛśam ṛddhyabhisaṃskāraṃ cakre yathā dadarśa sa rājā saparijanas tat tasya cakṣuś cakṣuḥsthāne pratiṣṭhitam / athonmiṣitaikacakṣuṣaṃ cakṣuryācanakam abhisamīkṣya sa rājā parameṇa harṣeṇāpūryamāṇahṛdayo dvitīyam apy asmai nayanaṃ prāyacchat //
body.translated_text: Then that king, having carefully extracted one eye—beautiful as a dark lotus petal—without damage, by a procedure supervised by physicians, gave it with supreme joy to the eye-petitioner. Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, performed such a miraculous transformation that the king, together with his retinue, saw that eye established in the [<s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s] eye-socket. Then, seeing the eye-petitioner with one eye now opened, the king, his heart overflowing with the utmost joy, gave him his second eye as well.

children.text: tataḥ sa rājā nayane pradāya vipadmapadmākaratulyavaktraḥ /
children.translated_text: Then that king, having given [his] eyes — his face like a lotus-pond without lotuses —

children.text: paurair asādhāraṇatuṣṭir āsīt samagracakṣur dadṛśe dvijaś ca // AJm_2.29 //
children.translated_text: among the citizens there was extraordinary [feeling]; and the twice-born [brahmin] saw with complete sight.

children.text: antaḥpure 'tha manujādhipateḥ pure ca śokāśrubhir vasumatī siṣice samantāt /
children.translated_text: Then in the inner palace and in the city of the lord of men, the earth was sprinkled on all sides with tears of grief.

children.text: śakras tu vismayam avāpa parāṃ ca tuṣṭiṃ saṃbodhaye nṛpam akampyamatiṃ samīkṣya // AJm_2.30 //
children.translated_text: But <s>Śakra</s>, observing the king of unshakeable resolve, attained wonder and supreme delight, [thinking] 'I shall awaken him.'

body.text: atha śakrasya vismayāvarjitahṛdayasyaitad ity abhavat /
body.translated_text: Then in the heart of <s>Śakra</s>, won over by wonder, this [thought] arose:

children.text: aho dhṛtir aho sattvam aho sattvahitaiṣitā /
children.translated_text: 'Oh, what fortitude! Oh, what courage! Oh, what desire for the welfare of beings!

children.text: pratyakṣam api karmedaṃ karotīva vicāraṇām // AJm_2.31 //
children.translated_text: Even this deed, though witnessed directly, causes one to reflect [in disbelief].'

body.text: tan nāyam āścaryasattvaś ciram imaṃ parikleśam anubhavitum arhati yataḥ prayatiṣye cakṣur asyopāyapradarśanād upapādayitum // atha tasya rājñaḥ kramāt saṃrūḍhanayanavraṇasyāvagītapratanūbhūtāntaḥpurapaurajānapadaśokasya pravivekakāmatvād udyānapuṣkariṇyās tīre kusumabhārānatataruvaranicite mṛdusurabhiśiśirasukhapavane madhukaragaṇopakūjite paryaṅkeṇa niṣaṇṇasya śakro devendraḥ purastāt prādurabhavat / ka eṣa iti ca rājñā paryanuyukto 'bravīt /
body.translated_text: 'Therefore this one of wondrous courage does not deserve to experience this affliction for long, since I shall strive to restore his sight by showing him the means.' Now, when that king's eye-wounds had gradually healed, and the grief of the inner palace, city-dwellers, and country-folk had gradually thinned and waned, desiring solitude, he sat on the bank of a garden-lake, crowded with fine trees bowed under the weight of blossoms, in a gentle, fragrant, cool, pleasant breeze humming with swarms of bees, seated on a couch. <s>Śakra</s>, king of the gods, appeared before him. Asked by the king, 'Who is this?' he said:

body.text: śakro 'ham asmi devendras tvatsamīpam upāgataḥ /
body.translated_text: 'I am <s>Śakra</s>, king of the gods, come into your presence.'

body.text: svāgatam / ājñāpyatāṃ kenārtha iti / sa upacārapuraḥsaram ukto rājānaṃ punar uvāca /
body.translated_text: 'Welcome! Command [me] — with what purpose [have you come]?' Thus addressed with courteous formality, he spoke again to the king:

body.text: varaṃ vṛṇīṣva rājarṣe yad icchasi tad ucyatām // AJm_2.32 //
body.translated_text: 'Choose a boon, O royal sage; say what you desire.'

body.text: atha sa rājā pradānasamucitatvād anabhyastayācñākārpaṇyamārgo dhṛtyāvismayaśauṭīryam uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then that king, being accustomed to giving rather than receiving, unfamiliar with the cringing path of begging, spoke with fortitude, without astonishment, and with grace:

children.text: prabhūtaṃ me dhanaṃ śakra śaktimac ca mahad balam /
children.translated_text: 'My wealth is abundant, O <s>Śakra</s>, and great and mighty is my power.

children.text: andhabhāvāt tv idānīṃ me mṛtyur evābhirocate // AJm_2.33 //
children.translated_text: But now, because of my blindness, death alone appeals to me.

children.text: kṛtvāpi paryāptamanorathānāṃ prītiprasādādhikalocanāni /
children.translated_text: Since I cannot see the faces of supplicants whose wishes have been fulfilled —

children.text: mukhāni paśyāmi na yācakānāṃ yat tena mṛtyur dayito mamendra // AJm_2.34 //
children.translated_text: faces [lit up] with eyes brimming with joy and gratitude — for that reason, O <s>Indra</s>, death is dear to me.'

body.text: śakra uvāca / alam anena te vyavasāyena / satpuruṣā evedṛśāny anuprāpnuvanti/ api ca pṛcchāmi tāvad bhavantam /
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: 'Enough of this resolve of yours! Only virtuous ones attain such things. But let me ask you a question:

children.text: imām avasthāṃ gamitasya yācakaiḥ kathaṃ nu te saṃprati teṣu mānasam /
children.translated_text: Brought to this condition by supplicants — what now is your disposition toward them?

children.text: pracakṣva tat tāvad alaṃ nigūhituṃ vrajec ca saṃpratyayanīyatāṃ yathā // AJm_2.35 //
children.translated_text: Declare that; enough of concealment! And let it become credible.'

body.text: rājovāca / ko 'yam asmān vikatthayitum atrabhavato nirbandhaḥ / api ca devendra śrūyatām /
body.translated_text: The king said: 'What is this insistence of the honored one to test us? But hear, O king of the gods!

children.text: tadaiva caitarhi ca yācakānāṃ vacāṃsi yācñāniyatākṣarāṇi /
children.translated_text: Then as now, the words of supplicants — their syllables shaped by entreaty —

children.text: āśīrmayāṇīva mama priyāṇi yathā tathodetu mamaikam akṣi // AJm_2.36 //
children.translated_text: are dear to me as if they were blessings. As truly as this is so, let one eye arise for me.'

body.text: atha tasya rājñaḥ satyādhiṣṭhānabalāt puṇyopacayaviśeṣāc ca vacanasamanantaram evendranīlaśakalākrāntamadhyam iva nīlotpaladalasadṛśam ekaṃ cakṣuḥ prādurabhūt / prādurbhūte ca tasmin nayanāścarye pramuditamanāḥ sa rājā punar api śakram uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then, through the power of that king's truth-resolve (<s>satyādhiṣṭhāna</s>) and through the special accumulation of merit, immediately after his words, a single eye appeared — as if its center were invaded by a fragment of sapphire, resembling a blue lotus petal. And when that wondrous eye had appeared, the king, his mind overjoyed, spoke again to <s>Śakra</s>:

children.text: yaś cāpi māṃ cakṣur ayācataikaṃ tasmai mudā dve nayane pradāya /
children.translated_text: 'To him who asked me for a single eye, having joyfully given both eyes,

children.text: prītyutsavaikāgramatir yathāsaṃ dvitīyam apy akṣi tathā mamāstu // AJm_2.37 //
children.translated_text: my mind wholly absorbed in the festival of love — as truly as that was so, let a second eye also appear for me.'

body.text: athābhivyāhārasamanantaram eva tasya rājño vispardhamānam iva tena nayanena dvitīyaṃ cakṣuḥ prādurabhūt /
body.translated_text: Then, immediately upon his utterance, a second eye appeared for that king, as if vying with the first.

children.text: tataś cakampe sadharādharā dharā vyatītya velāṃ prasasāra sāgaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the earth with its mountains and valleys trembled; the ocean surged beyond its shore;

children.text: prasaktagambhīramanojñanisvanāḥ prasasvanur dundubhayo divaukasām // AJm_2.38 //
children.translated_text: the divine drums of the celestial beings resounded with deep and pleasing tones.

children.text: prasādaramyaṃ dadṛśe vapur diśāṃ rarāja śuddhyā śaradīva bhāskaraḥ /
children.translated_text: The form of the quarters appeared lovely with serenity; the sun shone with the purity of autumn.

children.text: paribhramac candanacūrṇarañjitaṃ papāta citraṃ kusumaṃ nabhastalāt // AJm_2.39 //
children.translated_text: Variegated flowers, tinted with sandalwood powder, rained down, whirling, from the sky.

children.text: samāyayur vismayaphullalocanā divaukasas tatra sahāpsarogaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: The celestial beings arrived there together with hosts of <s>Apsarases</s>, their eyes wide with wonder.

children.text: vavau manojñātmaguṇaḥ samīraṇo manaḥsu harṣo jagatāṃ vyajṛmbhata // AJm_2.40 //
children.translated_text: A breeze blew, possessing pleasant qualities; joy expanded in the hearts of all beings.

children.text: udīritā harṣaparītamānasair maharddhibhir bhūtagaṇaiḥ savismayaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Uttered by hosts of mighty beings with minds enveloped in joy and wonder,

children.text: nṛpasya karmātiśayastavāśrayāḥ samantataḥ śuśruvire giraḥ śubhāḥ // AJm_2.41 //
children.translated_text: auspicious words — the vehicle of praise for the king's extraordinary deed — were heard from all directions:

children.text: aho bataudāryam aho kṛpālutā viśuddhatā paśya yathāsya cetasaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Oh, what generosity! Oh, what compassion! See how pure is his heart!

children.text: aho svasaukhyeṣu nirutsukā matir namo 'stu te 'tyadbhutadhairyavikrama // AJm_2.42 //
children.translated_text: Oh, how indifferent is his mind to his own pleasures! Homage to you, O one of utterly wondrous fortitude and valor!

children.text: sanāthatāṃ sādhu jagad gataṃ tvayā punar vibuddhekṣaṇapaṅkajaśriyā /
children.translated_text: The world has truly regained its protectedness through the lotus-beauty of your reopened eyes.

children.text: amogharūpā bata puṇyasaṃcayāś cirasya dharmeṇa khalūrjitaṃ jitam // AJm_2.43 //
children.translated_text: Indeed, accumulations of merit are never fruitless! Assuredly, by righteousness, the enduring victory is won.'

body.text: atha śakraḥ sādhu sādhv ity enam abhisaṃrādhya punar uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, having delighted him with 'Well done, well done!,' spoke again:

children.text: na no na vidito rājaṃs tava śuddhāśayāśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Not unknown to us, O king, is the pure intention of your mind.

children.text: evaṃ tu pratidatte te mayeme nayane nṛpa // AJm_2.44 //
children.translated_text: Even so, O king, these eyes are bestowed upon you by me as [my] gift in return.

children.text: samantād yojanaśataṃ śailair api tiraskṛtam /
children.translated_text: A hundred <s>yojanas</s> in every direction, even [what is] hidden by mountains —

children.text: draṣṭum avyāhatā śaktir bhaviṣyaty anayoś ca te // AJm_2.45 //
children.translated_text: the unobstructed power to see shall belong to these [eyes] of yours.'

body.text: ity uktvā śakras tatraivāntardadhe // atha bodhisattvo vismayapraharṣāpūrṇamanobhir mandamandanimeṣapravikasitanayanair amātyair anuyātaiḥ pauraiś cābhivīkṣyamāṇo jayāśīrvacanapuraḥsaraiś ca brāhmaṇair abhinandyamānaḥ puravaram ucchritadhvajavicitrapatākaṃ pravitanyamānābhyudayaśobham abhigamya parṣadi niṣaṇṇaḥ sabhājanārtham abhigatasyāmātyapramukh

children.text: y
children.translated_text: together with

children.text: asya brāhmaṇavṛddhapaurajanasyaivam ātmopanāyikaṃ dharmaṃ deśayām āsa /
children.translated_text: the brahmin-elders and leading citizens, he taught the <s>Dharma</s> by way of personal experience thus:

body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, <s>Śakra</s> vanished right there. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, gazed upon by ministers who followed with minds filled with wonder and joy, their eyes slowly blinking open in amazement, and by citizens, and welcomed by brahmins with words of victorious blessing, approaching the chief city adorned with raised banners and colorful flags, resplendent with unfolding prosperity, seated himself in the assembly. To the assembly that had come to pay homage, led by the chief ministers,

children.text: ko nāma loke śithilādaraḥ syāt kartuṃ dhanair arthijanapriyāṇi /
children.translated_text: 'Who in the world could be slack in zeal to do pleasing things for supplicants with wealth —

children.text: divyaprabhāve nayane mameme pradānapuṇyopanate samīkṣya // AJm_2.46 //
children.translated_text: seeing these eyes of mine, of divine power, obtained through the merit of giving?

children.text: anekaśailāntaritaṃ yojanānāṃ śatād api /
children.translated_text: Even from a hundred <s>yojanas</s> away, hidden by many mountains,

children.text: adūrasthitavispaṣṭaṃ dṛśyaṃ paśyāmi sarvataḥ // AJm_2.47 //
children.translated_text: I see all visible things on every side, as clearly as if standing nearby.

children.text: parānukampāvinayābhijātād dānāt paraḥ ko 'bhyudayābhyupāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: What greater means to prosperity is there than giving, born from compassion for others and from discipline?

children.text: yan mānuṣaṃ cakṣur ihaiva dattvā prāptaṃ mayāmānuṣadivyacakṣuḥ // AJm_2.48 //
children.translated_text: For, having given mere human sight right here, I have obtained superhuman, divine sight.

children.text: etad viditvā śibayaḥ pradānair bhogena cārthān saphalīkurudhvam /
children.translated_text: Knowing this, O <s>Śibis</s>, make your wealth fruitful through giving and through enjoyment!

children.text: loke parasminn iha caiṣa panthāḥ kīrtipradhānasya sukhodayasya // AJm_2.49 //
children.translated_text: This is the path — in this world and in the next — to the arising of happiness whose chief [ingredient] is fame.

children.text: dhanasya niḥsāralaghoḥ sa sāro yad dīyate lokahitonmukhena /
children.translated_text: The essence of wealth — [which is itself] essenceless and light — is that which is given by one who faces the welfare of the world.

children.text: nidhānatāṃ yāti hi dīyamānam adīyamānaṃ nidhanaikaniṣṭham // AJm_2.50 //
children.translated_text: For what is given becomes a treasure; what is not given ends only in destruction.'

body.text: tad evaṃ duṣkaraśatasamudānīto 'yam asmadarthaṃ tena bhagavatā saddharma iti satkṛtya śrotavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, since this True <s>Dharma</s> was brought forth for our sake by that <s>Bhagavān</s> through hundreds of difficult deeds, it should be heard with respect.

body.text: tathāgatamāhātmye pūrvavac ca karuṇāvarṇe 'pi vācyam ihaiva puṇyaphalapradarśane caivaṃ satkṛtyopacitāni puṇyānīhaiva puṣpamātram ātmaprabhāvasya kīrtisaṃtatimanoharaṃ pradarśayantīti //
body.translated_text: This [story] may also be told in [illustrating] the greatness of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and as before in depicting compassion. And here, in demonstrating the fruit of merit: 'Merits accumulated with reverence display here, like a mere flower, the captivating stream of fame of one's own spiritual power.'

body.text: śibijātakaṃ dvitīyam //
body.translated_text: The <s>Śibi Jātaka</s>, the second.

children.text: 3. Kulmāṣapiṇḍījātakam
children.translated_text: 3. The <s>Kulmāṣapiṇḍī Jātaka</s> (The Lump of Boiled Grain).

body.text: cittaprasādodgataṃ pātrātiśayapratipāditaṃ ca nālpakaṃ nāma dānam asti vipākamahattvāt //
body.translated_text: A gift that arises from faith of the heart and is offered to an extraordinarily worthy recipient is never 'small' — because of the greatness of its fruition.

body.text: tadyathānuśrūyate / bodhisattvabhūtaḥ kilāyaṃ bhagavān kośalādhipatir babhūva / tasyotsāhamantraprabhāvaśaktisaṃpatprabhṛtīnāṃ prakarṣiṇām api rājaguṇānāṃ vibhūtim atiśiśye daivasaṃpadguṇaśobhā /
body.translated_text: So it is heard: this <s>Bhagavān</s>, when he was the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, was the lord of <s>Kośala</s>. The splendor of his divine endowments surpassed the magnificence of even his preeminent royal qualities — energy, counsel, power, strength, and the like.

children.text: guṇās tasyādhikaṃ rejur daivasaṃpadvibhūṣaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: His virtues, adorned by his divine endowments, shone all the more,

children.text: kiraṇā iva candrasya śaradunmīlitaśriyaḥ // AJm_3.1 //
children.translated_text: like the rays of the moon whose beauty is unveiled in autumn.

children.text: tatyāja dṛptān api tasya śatrūn rakteva reme tadapāśriteṣu /
children.translated_text: His royal fortune (<s>Śrī</s>), conforming to [his] anger and favor toward other kings, abandoned even his proud enemies,

children.text: ity āsa tasyānyanarādhipeṣu kopaprasādānuvidhāyinī śrīḥ // AJm_3.2 //
children.translated_text: yet, as if enamored, delighted in those who took refuge with him.

children.text: dharmātmakatvān na ca nāma tasya paropatāpāśivam āsa cetaḥ /
children.translated_text: And because of his righteous nature, his mind harbored no inauspicious [thoughts of] harming others.

children.text: bhṛtyānurāgas tu tathā jajṛmbhe dviṣatsu lakṣmīr na yathāsya reme // AJm_3.3 //
children.translated_text: Indeed, devotion to his servants expanded to such a degree that his fortune did not delight [equally] among his enemies.

body.text: so 'nantarātītāṃ svāṃ jātim anusasmāra / tadanusmaraṇāc ca samupajātasaṃvego viśeṣavattaraṃ śramaṇabrāhmaṇakṛpaṇavanīpakebhyaḥ sukhahetunidānaṃ dānam adāt / śīlasaṃvaraṃ cānavaraṃ poṣadhaniyamaṃ ca parvadivaseṣu samādade / abhīkṣṇaṃ ca rājaparṣadi svasmiṃś cāntaḥpure puṇyaprabhāvodbhāvanāl lokaṃ śreyasi niyoktukāmaḥ pratītahṛdayo gāthādvayam iti niyatārthaṃ babhāṣe /
body.translated_text: He recalled his own immediately preceding birth. And from that recollection, with religious urgency arisen, he gave gifts with even greater distinction to ascetics, brahmins, the poor, and wanderers — gifts that were the cause and source of happiness. He also undertook the restraint of moral conduct without fail, and the observance of the <s>poṣadha</s> (fast-day) vow on festival days. And frequently, in the royal assembly and in his own inner palace, wishing to direct the people toward the good by demonstrating the power of merit, with a confident heart, he spoke a pair of verses of fixed meaning thus:

children.text: na sugataparicaryā vidyate svalpikāpi pratanuphalavibhūtir yac chrutaṃ kevalaṃ prāk /
children.translated_text: 'There is no service to the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) so small that its fruition is meager — so was formerly heard [by me] merely [through others].

children.text: tad idam alavaṇāyāḥ śuṣkarūkṣāruṇāyāḥ phalavibhavamahattvaṃ paśya kulmāṣapiṇḍyāḥ // AJm_3.4 //
children.translated_text: But now behold the greatness of the fruition of this lump of boiled grain (<s>kulmāṣapiṇḍī</s>) — saltless, dry, coarse, and red!'

children.text: rathaturagavicitraṃ mattanāgendralīlaṃ balam akṛśam idaṃ me medinī kevalā ca /
children.translated_text: 'This army of mine — resplendent with chariots and horses, sporting with lordly rutting elephants — no meager force; and the earth itself.

children.text: bahu dhanam anuraktā śrīr udārāś ca dārāḥ phalasamudayaśobhāṃ paśya kulmāṣapiṇḍyāḥ // AJm_3.5 //
children.translated_text: Abundant wealth, devoted royal fortune, and noble wives: behold the splendor of the accumulated fruit of that lump of boiled grain!'

body.text: tam amātyā brāhmaṇavṛddhāḥ pauramukhyāś ca kautūhalāpūrṇamanaso 'pi na prasahante sma paryanuyoktuṃ kim abhisamīkṣya mahārājo gāthādvayam idam abhīkṣṇaṃ bhāṣata iti // atha tasya rājño vāllabhyād avyāhatataraviśrambhapraṇayaprasādā devī samutpannakautūhalā saṃkathāprastāvāgataṃ parṣadi paryapṛcchad enam /
body.translated_text: Ministers, brahmin-elders, and leading citizens, though their minds were filled with curiosity, did not dare to ask directly: 'With what in mind does the great king speak this pair of verses so frequently?' Then his queen, whose trust, affection, and grace were even more unrestrained due to the king's love, when curiosity arose in her, on an occasion of conversation in the assembly, asked him:

children.text: niyatam iti narendra bhāṣase hṛdayagatāṃ mudam udgirann iva /
children.translated_text: 'You speak [these verses], O lord of men, as one fixed [in conviction], as if pouring forth a joy lodged in your heart.

children.text: bhavati mama kutūhalākulaṃ hṛdayam idaṃ kathitena tena te // AJm_3.6 //
children.translated_text: By that speech of yours, this heart of mine becomes agitated with curiosity.

children.text: tad arhati śrotum ayaṃ jano yadi pracakṣva tat kiṃ nv iti bhāṣase nṛpa /
children.translated_text: If this person deserves to hear, then tell us, O king — why do you speak thus?

children.text: rahasyam evaṃ ca na kīrtyate kva cit prakāśam asmāc ca mayāpi pṛcchyate // AJm_3.7 //
children.translated_text: A secret is not proclaimed anywhere in the open, and therefore it is asked by me [in private].'

body.text: atha sa rājā prītyatisnigdhayā dṛṣṭyā samavekṣya devīṃ smitapravikasitavadana uvāca //
body.translated_text: Then that king, regarding the queen with a gaze exceedingly tender with affection, his face blossoming with a smile, spoke:

children.text: avibhāvyanimittārthaṃ śrutvodgāram imaṃ mama /
children.translated_text: 'Having heard this utterance of mine, whose cause and purpose are unclear,

children.text: na kevalaṃ tavaivātra kautūhalacalaṃ manaḥ // AJm_3.8 //
children.translated_text: it is not your mind alone that is stirred with curiosity here.

children.text: samagram apy etad amātyamaṇḍalaṃ kutūhalāghūrṇitalolamānasam /
children.translated_text: This entire circle of ministers too, their minds swaying and restless with curiosity,

children.text: puraṃ ca sāntaḥpuram atra tena me niśamyatāṃ yena mayaivam ucyate // AJm_3.9 //
children.translated_text: and the city too, together with the inner palace — therefore let it be heard from me why I speak thus.

children.text: svapnaprabuddha iva jātim anusmarāmi yasyām ihaiva nagare bhṛtako 'ham āsam /
children.translated_text: As if awakened from a dream, I recall a birth in which, in this very city, I was a hired servant —

children.text: śīlānvito 'pi dhanamātrasamucchritebhyaḥ karmābhirādhanasamārjitadīnavṛttiḥ // AJm_3.10 //
children.translated_text: though endowed with good conduct, yet earning a wretched livelihood through serving those elevated merely by wealth.

children.text: so 'haṃ bhṛtiṃ paribhavaśramadainyaśālāṃ trāṇāśayā svayam avṛttibhayād vivikṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: I, wishing to escape from my wages — that abode of humiliation, toil, and wretchedness — hoping for protection, fearful of destitution,

children.text: bhikṣārthinaś ca caturaḥ śramaṇān apaśyaṃ vaśyendriyān anugatān iva bhikṣulakṣmyā // AJm_3.11 //
children.translated_text: then saw four ascetics seeking alms, with senses controlled, as if attended by the grace of mendicancy.

children.text: tebhyaḥ prasādamṛdunā manasā praṇamya kulmāṣamātrakam adāṃ prayataḥ svagehe /
children.translated_text: Bowing to them with a heart softened by faith, devoutly in my own home, I gave them a mere lump of boiled grain.

children.text: tasyāṅkurodaya ivaiṣa yad anyarājacūḍāprabhāś caraṇareṇuṣu me niṣiktāḥ // AJm_3.12 //
children.translated_text: The sprouting of that [seed] is this: that the crest-jewel lustre of other kings is showered upon the dust of my feet.

children.text: tad etad abhisaṃdhāya mayaivaṃ devi kathyate /
children.translated_text: With this in mind, O queen, I speak thus.

children.text: puṇyair na ca labhe tṛptim arhatāṃ darśanena ca // AJm_3.13 //
children.translated_text: And I never obtain satiety — either with [making] merit, or with seeing the worthy ones.'

body.text: atha devī praharṣavismayaviśālatarākṣī sabahumānam udīkṣamāṇā rājānam uvāca / upapannarūpaḥ puṇyānām ayam evaṃvidho vipākābhyudayaviśeṣaḥ / puṇyaphalapratyakṣiṇaś ca mahārājasya yad ayaṃ puṇyeṣv ādaraḥ / tad evam eva pāpapravṛttivimukhaḥ piteva prajānāṃ samyakparipālanasumukhaḥ puṇyaguṇārjanābhimukhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the queen, her eyes widened with delight and wonder, looking respectfully at the king, said: "This is the natural form of the extraordinary ripening of merits. And the great king's devotion to meritorious deeds is fitting, since he has seen the fruits of merit with his own eyes. Therefore, thus turned away from the course of sin, like a father well-disposed to the proper protection of his subjects, let him be devoted to the acquisition of meritorious qualities."

children.text: yaśaḥśriyā dānasamṛddhayā jvalan pratiṣṭhitājñaḥ pratirājamūrdhasu /
children.translated_text: "Blazing with the glory of fame and the abundance of generosity, with your authority established upon the heads of rival kings,

children.text: samīraṇākuñcitasāgarāmbarāṃ ciraṃ mahīṃ dharmanayena pālaya // AJm_3.14 //
children.translated_text: long may you protect the earth, girdled by the wind-rippled ocean, through the way of <s>Dharma</s>." [AJm 3.14]

body.text: rājovāca / kiṃ hy etad devi na syāt /
body.translated_text: The king said: "How, O queen, could it be otherwise?"

children.text: so 'haṃ tam eva punar āśrayituṃ yatiṣye śreyaḥpathaṃ samabhilakṣitaramyacihnam /
children.translated_text: "I shall strive again to follow that very path of well-being, marked with clearly visible and beautiful signs."

children.text: lokaḥ praditsati hi dānaphalaṃ niśamya dāsyāmy ahaṃ kim iti nātmagataṃ niśāmya // AJm_3.15 //
children.translated_text: "When the world, hearing of the fruit of giving, desires to give — shall I not give, having considered what is within my own means?" [AJm 3.15]

body.text: atha sa rājā devīṃ devīm iva śriyā jvalantīm atisnigdham avekṣya śrīsaṃpattihetukutūhalahṛdayaḥ punar uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then the king, looking with great affection at the queen who blazed with beauty like a goddess, his heart curious about the cause of such royal fortune, spoke again:

children.text: candralekheva tārāṇāṃ strīṇāṃ madhye virājase /
children.translated_text: "Like a crescent moon among the stars, you shine among women —

children.text: akṛthāḥ kiṃ nu kalyāṇi karmātimadhurodayam // AJm_3.16 //
children.translated_text: what supremely sweet-fruiting deed did you perform, O auspicious one?" [AJm 3.16]

body.text: devy uvāca / asti deva kiṃ cid aham api pūrvajanmavṛttam anusmarāmīti/ kathaya kathayedānīm iti ca sādaraṃ rājñā paryanuyuktovāca /
body.translated_text: The queen said: "There is, O lord, something of my previous birth that I too recall." And when the king earnestly urged, "Tell it, tell it now," she spoke:

children.text: bālye 'nubhūtam iva tat samanusmarāmi dāsī satī yad aham uddhṛtabhaktam ekam /
children.translated_text: "I recall it as if experienced in childhood — that being a slave-woman, I gave a single portion of leftover food

children.text: kṣīṇāsravāya munaye vinayena dattvā supteva tatra samavāpam iha prabodham // AJm_3.17 //
children.translated_text: to an <s>Arhat</s> sage whose defilements were destroyed, with reverence, and as if falling asleep there, I awoke here." [AJm 3.17]

children.text: etat smarāmi kuśalaṃ naradeva yena tvannāthatām upagatāsmi samaṃ pṛthivyā /
children.translated_text: "I remember this meritorious act, O lord of men, by which I have come under your protection together with the earth —

children.text: kṣīṇāsraveṣu na kṛtaṃ tanu nāma kiṃ cid ity uktavān asi yathaiva munis tathaiva // AJm_3.18 //
children.translated_text: 'Nothing done for those whose defilements are destroyed is small' — just as the sage declared, so indeed it is." [AJm 3.18]

body.text: atha sa rājā puṇyaphalapradarśanāt puṇyeṣu samutpāditabahumānām abhiprasannamanasaṃ pariṣadaṃ vismayaikāgrām avetya niyatam īdṛśaṃ kiṃ cit samanuśaśāsa /
body.translated_text: Then the king, perceiving that the assembly had been inspired with great respect for meritorious deeds through this demonstration of the fruits of merit, that their minds were pleased, and that they were focused with wonder — he surely instructed them with something like this:

children.text: alpasyāpi śubhasya vistaram imaṃ dṛṣṭvā vipākaśriyaḥ syāt ko nāma na dānaśīlavidhinā puṇyakriyātatparaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Having seen this vast extent of the splendor of ripening from even a small good deed, who would not be devoted to meritorious activity through the practice of giving and morality?

children.text: naivaṃ draṣṭum api kṣamaḥ sa puruṣaḥ paryāptavitto 'pi san yaḥ kārpaṇyatamisrayāvṛtamatir nāpnoti dānair yaśaḥ // AJm_3.19 //
children.translated_text: That man is not even fit to be seen who, though possessed of sufficient wealth, with mind enveloped in the darkness of miserliness, does not attain fame through gifts." [AJm 3.19]

children.text: tyaktavyaṃ vivaśena yan na ca tathā kasmai cid arthāya yat tan nyāyena dhanaṃ tyajan yadi guṇaṃ kaṃ cit samudbhāvayet /
children.translated_text: "That which must be abandoned helplessly and which serves no purpose for anyone — if one who gives up wealth in a just manner thereby produces some virtue,

children.text: ko 'sau tatra bhajeta matsarapathaṃ jānan guṇānāṃ rasaṃ prītyādyā vividhāś ca kīrtyanusṛtā dānapratiṣṭhā guṇāḥ // AJm_3.20 //
children.translated_text: who knowing the taste of virtues would pursue the path of envy in that matter? Delight and other varied qualities arising from fame are the established rewards of giving." [AJm 3.20]

children.text: dānaṃ nāma mahānidhānam anugaṃ caurādyasādhāraṇaṃ dānaṃ matsaralobhadoṣarajasaḥ prakṣālanaṃ cetasaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Giving is indeed a great treasure that follows one, not shared with thieves and the like; giving is the washing of the mind from the dust of envy, greed, and fault;

children.text: saṃsārādhvapariśramāpanayanaṃ dānaṃ sukhaṃ vāhanaṃ dānaṃ naikasukhopadhānasumukhaṃ sanmitram ātyantikam // AJm_3.21 //
children.translated_text: giving is a comfortable vehicle for removing the fatigue of the road of <s>saṃsāra</s>; giving is a true and eternal friend, disposed to providing manifold comforts." [AJm 3.21]

children.text: vibhavasamudayaṃ vā dīptam ājñāguṇaṃ vā tridaśapuranivāsaṃ rūpaśobhāguṇaṃ vā /
children.translated_text: "Whether one desires a great accumulation of wealth, or brilliant authority, or residence in the city of the gods, or the excellence of beauty —

children.text: yad abhilaṣati sarvaṃ tat samāpnoti dānād iti parigaṇitārthaḥ ko na dānāni dadyāt // AJm_3.22 //
children.translated_text: all that one desires is obtained through giving — knowing this, who would not give gifts?" [AJm 3.22]

children.text: sārādānaṃ dānam āhur dhanānām aiśvaryāṇāṃ dānam āhur nidānam /
children.translated_text: "They call giving the essence of wealth; they call giving the source of sovereignty;

children.text: dānaṃ śrīmat sajjanatvāvadānaṃ nālpaprajñaiḥ pāṃsudānaṃ sudānam // AJm_3.23 //
children.translated_text: giving is a glorious act of noble character — the lesser-minded cannot make a worthy gift." [AJm 3.23]

body.text: atha sā parṣat tasya rājñas tadgrāhakaṃ vacanaṃ sabahumānam abhinandya pradānādiguṇapratipattyabhimukhī babhūva //
body.translated_text: Then that assembly, having respectfully applauded the king's persuasive words, became inclined toward the practice of virtues such as generosity.

body.text:
tad evaṃ cittaprasādodgataṃ pātrātiśayapratipāditaṃ ca nālpakaṃ nāma dānam asti vipākamahattvād iti
prasannacittenānuttare puṇyakṣetra āryasaṃghe dānaṃ dadatā parā prītir utpādyā / adūre mamāpy evaṃvidhā ato viśiṣṭataraś ca saṃpattaya iti //
body.translated_text: Thus, giving that arises from the purity of mind and is enhanced by the excellence of the recipient is never small, due to the greatness of its ripening — therefore, by one who gives with a serene mind to the unsurpassed field of merit, the Noble <s>Saṅgha</s>, supreme joy should be cultivated. 'For me too, such and even more excellent fortunes are near at hand.'

body.text: kulmāṣapiṇḍījātakaṃ tṛtīyam //
body.translated_text: This concludes the third story, the <s>Kulmāṣapiṇḍī-jātaka</s> (The Story of the Lentil-Cake).

children.text: 4. Śreṣṭhijātakam
children.translated_text: 4. The <s>Śreṣṭhi-jātaka</s> (The Story of the Merchant)

children.text: atyayam apy avigaṇayya ditsanti satpuruṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: Noble persons desire to give even disregarding danger to themselves —

children.text: kena nāma svasthena na dātavyaṃ syāt //
children.translated_text: what person in good health would there be who should not give?

body.text: tadyathānuśrūyate / bodhisattvabhūtaḥ kilāyaṃ bhagavān bhāgyātiśayaguṇād utthānasaṃpadā cādhigatavipuladhanasamṛddhir aviṣamavyavahāraśīlatvāl lokabahumānaniketabhūta udārābhijanavān anekavidyākalāvikalpādhigamavimalataramatir guṇamāhātmyād rājñā samupahṛtasaṃmānaḥ pradānaśīlatvāl lokasādhāraṇavibhavaḥ śreṣṭhī babhūva /
body.translated_text: Thus it is heard: <s>Bhagavān</s>, when he was a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, by the abundance of his fortune and by the excellence of his enterprise, having acquired vast wealth and prosperity, being of honest dealings and thus a dwelling-place for public esteem, of noble birth, with a mind made pure by the mastery of many arts and sciences, honored by the king on account of the greatness of his virtues, and with his possessions shared with all people due to his habit of giving — he became a merchant (<s>śreṣṭhin</s>).

children.text: arthibhiḥ prītahṛdayaiḥ kīrtyamānam itas tataḥ /
children.translated_text: By supplicants with delighted hearts, proclaimed here and there,

children.text: tyāgaśauryonnataṃ nāma tasya vyāpa diśo daśa // AJm_4.1 //
children.translated_text: his name, exalted by generosity and valor, spread to the ten directions. [AJm 4.1]

children.text: dadyān na dadyād iti tatra nāsīd vicāradolācalamānaso 'rthī /
children.translated_text: There was no supplicant whose mind wavered on the pendulum of deliberation, 'Will he give or will he not give?'

children.text: khyātāvadāne hi babhūva tasmin viśrambhadhṛṣṭapraṇayo 'rthivargaḥ // AJm_4.2 //
children.translated_text: For in him, whose generosity was renowned, the crowd of supplicants was bold with the confidence of trust. [AJm 4.2]

children.text: nāsau jugopātmasukhārtham arthaṃ na spardhayā lobhaparābhavād vā /
children.translated_text: He did not guard his wealth for his own happiness, nor from rivalry, nor from the defeat of greed;

children.text: sa tv arthiduḥkhaṃ na śaśāka soḍhuṃ nāstīti vaktuṃ ca tato jugopa // AJm_4.3 //
children.translated_text: but he could not endure the suffering of supplicants, nor say 'There is none' — and therefore he guarded it. [AJm 4.3]

body.text: atha kadā cit tasya mahāsattvasya bhojanakāle snātānuliptasya kuśalasūdopakalpite samupasthite varṇagandharasasparśādiguṇasamudite vicitre bhakṣyabhojyādividhau tatpuṇyasaṃbhāravivṛddhikāmo jñānāgninirdagdhasarvakleśendhanaḥ pratyekabuddhas tadgṛham abhijagāma bhikṣārthī / samupetya ca dvārakoṣṭhake vyatiṣṭhata /
