body.translated_text: Then one day, at mealtime for that great being, when he had bathed and was anointed, and a varied meal of eatables and delicacies was prepared and presented by expert cooks, endowed with excellence of color, fragrance, taste, and touch — a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, who had burned the fuel of all defilements with the fire of knowledge, came to his house seeking alms, desiring to increase the store of his merit. Having approached, he stood at the entrance-hall.

children.text: aśaṅkitācañcaladhīrasaumyam avekṣamāṇo yugamātram urvyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Gazing at the earth for just a moment, with a look that was fearless, unflickering, composed, and gentle —

children.text: tatrāvatasthe praśamābhijātaḥ sa pātrasaṃsaktakarāgrapadmaḥ // AJm_4.4 //
children.translated_text: he stood there, born of tranquility, with the lotus-tips of his fingers touching the alms-bowl. [AJm 4.4]

body.text: atha māraḥ pāpīyān bodhisattvasya tāṃ dānasaṃpadam amṛṣyamāṇas tadvighnārtham antarā ca taṃ bhadantam antarā ca dvāradehalīṃ jvālākarālodaram anekapauruṣam atigambhīraṃ bhayānakadarśanaṃ pratibhayanirghoṣaṃ narakam abhinirmame visphuradbhir anekair janaśatair ācitam // atha bodhisattvaḥ pratyekabuddhaṃ bhikṣārthinam abhigatam ālokya patnīm uvāca / bhadre svayam āryāya piṇḍapātaṃ dehīti / sā tathety asmai pratiśrutya praṇītaṃ bhakṣyabhojyam ādāya prasthitā / narakam ālokya dvārasamīpād bhayaviṣādacañcalākṣī sahasā nyavartata / kim etad iti ca bhartrā paryanuyuktā samāpatitasādhvasāpihitakaṇṭhī tat kathaṃ cid asya kathayām āsa // atha bodhisattvaḥ katham ayam āryo madgṛhād anavāptabhikṣa eva pratiyāsyatīti sasaṃbhramas tat tasyāḥ kathitam anādṛtya svayam eva praṇītaṃ bhakṣyabhojyam ādāya tasya mahātmanaḥ piṇḍapātaṃ pratipādayitukāmo dvārakoṣṭhakasamīpam abhigatas tam atibhīṣaṇam antarā narakaṃ dadarśa / tasya kiṃ svid idam iti samutpatitavitarkasya māraḥ pāpīyān bhavanabhitter niṣpatya saṃdṛśyamānadivyādbhutavapur antarikṣe sthitvā hitakāma iva nāmābravīt / gṛhapate mahārauravo nāmāyaṃ mahānarakaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then wicked <s>Māra</s>, unable to tolerate that excellence of giving of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, for the purpose of obstructing it, created between that venerable one and the doorstep a hell — its interior blazing with terrible flames, many persons deep, exceedingly profound, terrifying to behold, with frightful roaring sounds, filled with many hundreds of writhing beings. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, seeing the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> who had come seeking alms, said to his wife:

children.text: arthipraśaṃsāvacanapralubdhā hiṃsanti dānavyasanena ye 'rthān /
children.translated_text: "Those who, enticed by the flattering words of supplicants, destroy their wealth through the vice of giving —

children.text: śaratsahasrāṇi bahūni teṣām asmin nivāso 'sulabhapravāsaḥ // AJm_4.5 //
children.translated_text: their residence in this [hell], a place of hard-won escape, lasts for many thousands of autumns." [AJm 4.5]

children.text: arthas trivargasya viśeṣahetus tasmin hate kena hato na dharmaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Wealth is the special cause of the three aims of life; when it is destroyed, how is <s>Dharma</s> not destroyed?

children.text: dharmaṃ ca hatvārthanibarhaṇena kathaṃ nu na syān narakapratiṣṭhaḥ // AJm_4.6 //
children.translated_text: And having destroyed <s>Dharma</s> through the annihilation of wealth, how could one not be established in hell?" [AJm 4.6]

children.text: dānaprasaṅgena ca dharmamūlaṃ ghnatā tvayārthaṃ yad akāri pāpam /
children.translated_text: "And the sin committed by you in destroying wealth, the root of <s>Dharma</s>, through the occasion of giving —

children.text: tvām attum abhyudgatam etad asmāj jvālograjihvaṃ narakāntakāsyam // AJm_4.7 //
children.translated_text: this mouth of the end of hell, with tongues of flame reaching upward, has risen from here to devour you." [AJm 4.7]

children.text: tat sādhu dānād viniyaccha buddhim evaṃ hi sadyaḥ patanaṃ na te syāt /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, wisely restrain your mind from giving — thus you shall not fall immediately.

children.text: viceṣṭamānaiḥ karuṇaṃ rudadbhir mā dātṛbhir gāḥ samatām amībhiḥ // AJm_4.8 //
children.translated_text: Do not become equal to these givers who writhe and weep piteously!" [AJm 4.8]

children.text: pratigrahītā tu jano 'bhyupaiti nivṛttadānāpanayaḥ suratvam /
children.translated_text: "But the recipient of gifts attains the world of the lord of gods, free from the harm of giving that has ceased.

children.text: tat svargamārgāvaraṇād viramya dānodyamāt saṃyamam āśrayasva // AJm_4.9 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, desisting from the obstruction of the path to heaven, withdrawing from the effort of giving, take up self-restraint!" [AJm 4.9]

body.text: atha bodhisattvo nūnam asyaitad durātmano maddānavighnāya viceṣṭitam ity avagamya svasattvāvaṣṭambhadhīravinayamadhurākṣarāvicchedaṃ niyatam ity avocad enam /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, understanding that 'surely this is the machination of that evil one for obstructing my giving,' with the composure born of reliance on his own nature, in words that were gentle, brave, and uninterrupted, he certainly spoke thus to him:

children.text: asmaddhitāvekṣaṇadakṣiṇena vidarśito 'yaṃ bhavatāryamārgaḥ /
children.translated_text: "This noble path has been shown by your honor, skilled in looking after our welfare;

children.text: yuktā viśeṣeṇa ca daivateṣu parānukampānipuṇā pravṛttiḥ // AJm_4.10 //
children.translated_text: and a disposition skilled in compassion for others is especially fitting among divine beings." [AJm 4.10]

children.text: doṣodayāt pūrvam anantaraṃ vā yuktaṃ tu tacchāntipathena gantum /
children.translated_text: "But before the arising of evil or immediately after, it is proper to proceed by the path of its pacification;

children.text: gate prayāmaṃ hy apacāradoṣair vyādhau cikitsāpraṇayo vighātaḥ // AJm_4.11 //
children.translated_text: for when a disease has progressed far through the faults of misconduct, the desire for treatment is futile." [AJm 4.11]

children.text: idaṃ ca dānavyasanaṃ madīyaṃ śaṅke cikitsāviṣayavyatītam /
children.translated_text: "And this vice of giving of mine — I suspect it has passed beyond the scope of treatment;

children.text: tathā hy anādṛtya hitaiṣitāṃ te na me manaḥ saṃkucati pradānāt // AJm_4.12 //
children.translated_text: for even disregarding your well-wishing counsel, my mind does not shrink from giving." [AJm 4.12]

children.text: dānād adharmaṃ ca yad ūcivāṃs tvam arthaṃ ca dharmasya viśeṣahetum /
children.translated_text: "And as for your saying that <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) comes from giving, and that wealth is the special cause of <s>Dharma</s> —

children.text: tan mānuṣī neyam avaiti buddhir dānād ṛte dharmapatho yathārthaḥ // AJm_4.13 //
children.translated_text: this human understanding does not perceive that; the path of <s>Dharma</s> is truly through giving, not otherwise." [AJm 4.13]

children.text: nidhīyamānaḥ sa tu dharmahetuś cauraiḥ prasahyātha vilupyamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: "For that [wealth], stored as the cause of <s>Dharma</s>, is forcibly plundered by thieves,

children.text: oghodarāntarvinimagnamūrtir hutāśanasyāśanatāṃ gato vā // AJm_4.14 //
children.translated_text: or submerged in form within a flooding stream, or gone to serve as food for fire." [AJm 4.14]

children.text: yac cārthadātā narakaṃ prayāti pratigrahītā tu surendralokam /
children.translated_text: "And as for [your claim] that the giver of wealth goes to hell while the recipient goes to the world of <s>Indra</s> —

children.text: vivardhitas tena ca me tvayāyaṃ dānodyamaḥ saṃyamayiṣyatāpi // AJm_4.15 //
children.translated_text: by this very argument you have increased my zeal for giving, though you wished to restrain it!" [AJm 4.15]

children.text: ananyathā cāstu vacas tavedaṃ svargaṃ ca me yācanakā vrajantu /
children.translated_text: "And let your words be just so! And let my supplicants go to heaven!

children.text: dānaṃ hi me lokahitārtham iṣṭaṃ nedaṃ svasaukhyodayasādhanāya // AJm_4.16 //
children.translated_text: For my giving is desired for the benefit of the world, not as a means for producing my own happiness." [AJm 4.16]

body.text: atha māraḥ punar api bodhisattvaṃ hitaiṣīva dhīrahastenovāca /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> again spoke to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, as if with goodwill, with a steady hand:

children.text: hitoktim enāṃ mama cāpalaṃ vā samīkṣya yenecchasi tena gaccha /
children.translated_text: "Having considered this well-meaning advice of mine, or my impetuosity — go by whichever [path] you wish.

children.text: sukhānvito vā bahumānapūrvaṃ smartāsi māṃ vipratisāravān vā // AJm_4.17 //
children.translated_text: Either you will remember me with gratitude, accompanied by happiness, or with remorse." [AJm 4.17]

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca / mārṣa marṣayatu bhavān /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: "Sir, may your honor forgive me."

children.text: kāmaṃ patāmi narakaṃ sphuradugravahniṃ jvālāvalīḍhaśithilāvanatena mūrdhnā /
children.translated_text: "I would willingly fall into hell with its blazing, fierce fire, with my head bowed low, licked by garlands of flame —

children.text: na tv arthināṃ praṇayadarśitasauhṛdānāṃ saṃmānakālam avamānanayā hariṣye // AJm_4.18 //
children.translated_text: but I shall not rob of their moment of honor the supplicants who have shown me their friendship and trust." [AJm 4.18]

body.text: ity uktvā bodhisattvaḥ svabhāgyabalāvaṣṭabdho jānānaś ca niratyayatāṃ dānasya nivāraṇaikarasam avadhūya svajanaparijanaṃ sādhvasānabhibhūtamatir abhivṛddhadānābhilāṣo narakamadhyena prāyāt /
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, supported by the strength of his own merit, and knowing the harmlessness of giving, shaking off his household and retinue whose minds were overwhelmed with terror — that one whose sole pleasure was in refusing to be deterred — with his desire for giving increased, he advanced through the midst of the hell.

children.text: puṇyānubhāvād atha tasya tasminn apaṅkajaṃ paṅkajam udbabhūva /
children.translated_text: Then, by the power of his merit, in that [hell] there arose an immaculate lotus —

children.text: avajñayevāvajahāsa māraṃ yac chuklayā kesaradantapaṅktyā // AJm_4.19 //
children.translated_text: which, with its white row of filament-teeth, seemed to laugh at <s>Māra</s> with contempt. [AJm 4.19]

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ padmasaṃkrameṇa svapuṇyātiśayanirjātenābhigamya pratyekabuddhaṃ prasādasaṃharṣāpūrṇahṛdayaḥ piṇḍapātam asmai prāyacchat //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, crossing on that lotus which had sprung forth from the preeminence of his merit, having approached the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, his heart overflowing with faith and delight, gave him the alms-food.

children.text: manaḥprasādapratibodhanārthaṃ tasyātha bhikṣur viyad utpapāta /
children.translated_text: Then, in order to awaken clarity of mind in him, the monk flew up into the sky.

children.text: varṣañ jvalaṃś caiva sa tatra reje savidyududdyotapayodalakṣmyā // AJm_4.20 //
children.translated_text: Raining [flowers] and blazing, he shone there with the splendor of a cloud with flashing lightning. [AJm 4.20]

children.text: avamṛditamanorathas tu māro dyutiparimoṣam avāpya vaimanasyāt /
children.translated_text: But <s>Māra</s>, his desires crushed, having suffered the robbery of his radiance, from despondency

children.text: tam abhimukham udīkṣituṃ na sehe saha narakeṇa tatas tirobabhūva // AJm_4.21 //
children.translated_text: could not bear to look toward him face to face; together with his hell, he thereupon disappeared. [AJm 4.21]

body.text: tat kim idam upanītam / evam

children.text: atyayam apy avigaṇayya ditsanti satpuruṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: Virtuous persons are willing to give even at the cost of transgression.

children.text: kena nāma svasthena na dātavyaṃ syād iti
children.translated_text: What person at ease would not give? And thus—

children.text: na sattvavantaḥ śakyante bhayād apy agatiṃ gamayitum ity evam apy upaneyam //
children.translated_text: those of true courage cannot be made to deviate [from their path] even by fear. This too should be drawn [as a lesson].

body.translated_text: So what has been conveyed by this? Thus:

body.text: śreṣṭhijātakaṃ caturtham //
body.translated_text: The fourth [story], the <s>Jātaka</s> of the Merchant.

children.text: 5. Aviṣahyaśreṣṭhijātakam
children.translated_text: 5. The <s>Jātaka</s> of the Merchant <s>Aviṣahya</s>

body.text: na vibhavakṣayāśaṅkayā samṛddhyāśayā vā pradānavaidhuryam upayānti satpuruṣāḥ //
body.translated_text: Virtuous persons do not fall into laxity in giving out of apprehension about the loss of wealth or out of desire for prosperity.

body.text: tadyathānuśrūyate / bodhisattvaḥ kila tyāgaśīlakulavinayaśrutajñānāvismayādiguṇasamudito dhanadāyamāno vibhavasaṃpadā sarvātithitvād anuparatadānasattro lokahitārthapravṛtto dāyakaśreṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhī babhūva / mātsaryādidoṣāviṣahyo 'viṣahya iti prakāśanāmā /
body.translated_text: As tradition relates: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, it is said, endowed with a constellation of virtues such as generosity, moral conduct, family discipline, learning, knowledge, and wonder, radiant with the splendor of wealth, through his universal hospitality and unceasing festival of giving, engaged in the welfare of the world, was a foremost donor, a merchant. His name was known as <s>Aviṣahya</s> ('Unbearable'), because avarice and other faults could not endure [in his presence].

children.text: iṣṭārthasaṃpattivimarśanāśāt prītiprabodhasya viśeṣahetuḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of the destruction of anxiety regarding the attainment of desired goals, he was a special cause for the awakening of joy;

children.text: yathārthināṃ darśanam āsa tasya tathārthināṃ darśanam āsa tasya // AJm_5.1 //
children.translated_text: thus the sight of him was [welcome] to supplicants, as the sight of supplicants was [welcome] to him. [AJm 5.1]

children.text: dehīti yācñāniyatārtham ukto nāstīti nāsau gadituṃ śaśāka /
children.translated_text: When addressed with the word 'Give!' by one whose purpose was fixed upon asking, he was never able to utter 'I have not';

children.text: hṛtāvakāśā hi babhūva citte tasyārthasaktiḥ kṛpayā mahatyā // AJm_5.2 //
children.translated_text: for in his mind, attachment to wealth had its place taken away by his great compassion. [AJm 5.2]

children.text: tasyārthibhir nirhriyamāṇasāre gṛhe babhūvābhyadhikaḥ praharṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: As supplicants carried away the essence of his household, his delight grew ever greater;

children.text: viveda sa hy ugraghanān anarthān akāraṇakṣipravināśino 'rthān // AJm_5.3 //
children.translated_text: for he perceived that wealth is subject to severe and causeless calamities, and is swiftly destroyed without reason. [AJm 5.3]

children.text: bhavanti lokasya ca bhūyasārthā lobhāśrayā durgatimārgasārthāḥ /
children.translated_text: The riches of the world at large, harbored in greed, become caravans on the road to evil destinies;

children.text: parātmanor abhyudayāvahatvād arthās tadīyās tu babhur yathārthāḥ // AJm_5.4 //
children.translated_text: but his riches were truly worthwhile, since they brought prosperity to both others and himself. [AJm 5.4]

body.text: atha tasya mahāsattvasya yathābhilaṣitair akliṣṭaiḥ śiṣṭopacāravibhūṣaṇair vipulair arthavisargair yācanakajanaṃ samantataḥ saṃtarpayataḥ pradānaudāryaśravaṇād vismayāvarjitamanāḥ śakro devendraḥ pradānasthiraniścayatām asya jijñāsamānaḥ pratyahaṃ dhanadhānyaratnaparicchadajātaṃ tat tad antardhāpayām āsa / api nāmāyaṃ vibhavaparikṣayāśaṅkayā mātsaryāya pratāryeteti / pradānādhimuktasya tu punar mahāsattvasya
body.translated_text: Now, as this great being was satisfying the community of supplicants on all sides with effortless, generous, vast disbursements of wealth adorned with the courtesies proper to the well-mannered, <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, his mind captivated with wonder at hearing of his munificent generosity, wishing to test the firmness of his resolve in giving, began day by day to cause his stores of wealth, grain, jewels, and possessions to disappear—thinking: 'Perhaps this one, through apprehension about the loss of his wealth, will be turned to avarice.' But for the great being, devoted to giving,

children.text: yathā yathā tasya vineśur arthāḥ sūryābhisṛṣṭā iva toyaleśāḥ /
children.translated_text: as his riches vanished, like drops of water released by the sun,

children.text: tathā tathaitān vipulaiḥ pradānair gṛhāt pradīptād iva nirjahāra // AJm_5.5 //
children.translated_text: so did he cast them forth from his house with lavish gifts, as from a house on fire. [AJm 5.5]

body.text: atha śakro devendras tyāgaparāyaṇam eva taṃ mahāsattvam avetya prakṣīyamāṇavibhavasāram api vismitataramatis tasyaikarātreṇa sarvaṃ vibhavasāram antardhāpayām āsānyatra rajjukuṇḍalakād dātrāc caikasmāt // atha bodhisattvaḥ prabhātāyāṃ rajanyāṃ yathocitaṃ prativibuddhaḥ paśyati sma dhanadhānyaparicchadaparijanarddhiśūnyaṃ niṣkūjadīnaṃ svabhavanaṃ rākṣasair ivodvāsitam anabhirāmadarśanaṃ kim idam iti ca samutthitavitarkaḥ samanuvicaraṃs tad rajjukuṇḍalakaṃ dātraṃ ca kevalam atra dadarśa / tasya cintā prādurabhavat / yadi tāvat kena cid yācitum anucitavacasā svavikramopajīvinā madgṛhe praṇaya evaṃ darśitaḥ sūpayuktā eva me 'rthāḥ / atha tv idānīṃ madbhāgyadoṣād ucchrayam asahamānāḥ kena cid anupayuktā eva vidrutās tat kaṣṭam /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, perceiving that the great being remained devoted to generosity even as the essence of his wealth was dwindling, with his mind even more astonished, in a single night caused all his wealth to disappear—except for one sickle and one length of rope. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having awakened in the proper manner when dawn broke, beheld his own mansion—empty of wealth, grain, possessions, servants, and prosperity, miserably silent, unpleasant to look upon, as if evicted by <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons)—and wondering 'What is this?', reflecting as he arose, he saw only that rope and sickle there. A thought occurred to him: 'If someone has presumed upon the intimacy of my household with improper words, one who lives by his own prowess, to ask [for these things]—then my wealth has been well-used indeed. But if, on the other hand, through a fault in my fortune, unable to endure their elevation, they have scattered of their own accord, unused by anyone—that is lamentable!'

children.text: calaṃ sauhṛdam arthānāṃ viditaṃ pūrvam eva me /
children.translated_text: 'The fickleness of wealth's friendship was known to me before;

children.text: arthinām eva pīḍā tu dahaty atra mano mama // AJm_5.6 //
children.translated_text: but the suffering of the supplicants—that alone burns my mind.' [AJm 5.6]

children.text: pradānasatkārasukhocitāś ciraṃ viviktam arthair abhigamya madgṛham /
children.translated_text: 'Those supplicants of mine, long accustomed to the pleasure of generous hospitality, upon reaching my house now empty of wealth—

children.text: kathaṃ bhaviṣyanti nu te mamārthinaḥ pipāsitāḥ śuṣkam ivāgatā hradam // AJm_5.7 //
children.translated_text: how will they fare? Like thirsty ones who have come to a dried-up lake!' [AJm 5.7]

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ svadhairyāvaṣṭambhād anāsvāditaviṣādadainyas tasyām apy avasthāyām anabhyastayācñākramatvāt parān yācituṃ paricitān api na prasehe / evaṃ duṣkaraṃ yācitum iti tasya bhūyasī yācanakajaneṣv anukampā babhūva// atha sa mahātmā yācanakajanasvāgatādikriyāvekṣayā svayam eva tad rajjukuṇḍalakaṃ dātraṃ ca parigṛhya pratyahaṃ tṛṇavikrayopalabdhayā vibhavamātrayārthijanapraṇayasaṃmānanaṃ cakāra // atha śakro devendras tasyemām aviṣāditāṃ parame 'pi dāridrye pradānābhimukhatāṃ cāvekṣya savismayabahumānaḥ saṃdṛśyamānadivyādbhutavapur antarikṣe sthitvā dānād vicchandayaṃs taṃ mahāsattvam uvāca / gṛhapate /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, sustained by his own fortitude, having not tasted the wretchedness of despair, even in that condition, because he had no practice in the ways of begging, could not bring himself to ask anything even of those he knew well. 'So difficult it is to beg!'—and thus his compassion for the supplicant folk grew all the more. Then that great soul, out of concern for the customary welcome and other courtesies due to supplicants, himself taking up that rope and sickle, each day, with the meager means obtained from selling grass, maintained his respectful hospitality toward the supplicant folk. Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, observing his undaunted orientation toward giving even in the most extreme poverty, full of wonder and reverence, standing in the sky with his divine and wondrous form made visible, and seeking to dissuade the great being from giving, said: 'O householder!'

children.text: suhṛnmanastāpakarīm avasthām imām upetas tvam atipradānaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Through excessive giving, you have reached this condition which causes grief to the hearts of friends—

children.text: na dasyubhir naiva jalānalābhyāṃ na rājabhiḥ saṃhriyamāṇavittaḥ // AJm_5.8 //
children.translated_text: your wealth being seized not by thieves, not by water or fire, not by kings.' [AJm 5.8]

children.text: tat tvā hitāvekṣitayā bravīmi niyaccha dānavyasanānurāgam /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, looking to your welfare, I tell you: restrain your fondness for the vice of giving.'

children.text: itthaṃgataḥ sann api cen na dadyā yāyāḥ punaḥ pūrvasamṛddhiśobhām // AJm_5.9 //
children.translated_text: 'Even having reached this state, if you were not to give, you would return to your former splendor of prosperity.' [AJm 5.9]

children.text: śaśvat kṛśenāpi parivyayeṇa kālena dṛṣṭvā kṣayam añjanānām /
children.translated_text: 'Having observed over time the exhaustion of even collyrium through constant small expenditure,

children.text: cayena valmīkasamucchrayāṃś ca vṛddhyarthinaḥ saṃyama eva panthāḥ // AJm_5.10 //
children.translated_text: and the ant-hill heights [attained] through accumulation—restraint is indeed the path for those who seek increase.' [AJm 5.10]

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ pradānābhyāsamāhātmyaṃ vidarśayañ chakram uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, demonstrating the greatness of the practice of giving, said to <s>Śakra</s>:

children.text: anāryam āryeṇa sahasranetra suduṣkaraṃ suṣṭhv api durgatena /
children.translated_text: 'O Thousand-eyed One (<s>Śakra</s>), it is ignoble for a noble one, and extremely difficult for one in poverty, however proper [the advice may be]—'

children.text: mā caiva tad bhūn mama śakra vittaṃ yatprāptihetoḥ kṛpaṇāśayaḥ syām // AJm_5.11 //
children.translated_text: 'And may I never, O <s>Śakra</s>, have that wealth for whose attainment I would become one of wretched disposition!' [AJm 5.11]

children.text: icchanti yācñāmaraṇena gantuṃ duḥkhasya yasya pratikāramārgam /
children.translated_text: 'Those who, by the death of begging, wish to find a remedy for suffering—'

children.text: tenāturān kaḥ kulaputramānī nāstīti śuṣkāśaninābhihanyāt // AJm_5.12 //
children.translated_text: 'what man of noble birth-pride would strike them with the dry thunderbolt of "I have not"?' [AJm 5.12]

children.text: tan madvidhaḥ kiṃ svid upādadīta ratnaṃ dhanaṃ vā divi vāpi rājyam /
children.translated_text: 'Then what would one such as I accept—jewels, wealth, or even sovereignty in heaven—'

children.text: yācñābhitāpena vivarṇitāni prasādayen nārthimukhāni yena // AJm_5.13 //
children.translated_text: 'by which I could not brighten the faces of supplicants, made pale by the torment of begging?' [AJm 5.13]

children.text: mātsaryadoṣopacayāya yaḥ syān na tyāgacittaṃ paribṛṃhayed vā /
children.translated_text: 'Wealth that would increase the flaw of avarice or would not nourish the spirit of generosity—'

children.text: sa tyāgam evārhati madvidhebhyaḥ parigrahacchadmamayo vighātaḥ // AJm_5.14 //
children.translated_text: 'such [wealth] deserves only to be given away by one such as me; acquisition [of it] is destruction in the guise of possession.' [AJm 5.14]

children.text: vidyullatānṛttacale dhane ca sādhāraṇe naikavighātahetau /
children.translated_text: 'When wealth is as unstable as a dancing lightning-flash, shared by all, a cause of many afflictions—'

children.text: dāne nidāne ca sukhodayānāṃ mātsaryam āryaḥ ka ivāśrayeta // AJm_5.15 //
children.translated_text: 'in giving, the source of the arising of happiness—what noble person would resort to avarice?' [AJm 5.15]

children.text: tad darśitā śakra mayi svateyaṃ hitābhidhānād anukampito 'smi /
children.translated_text: 'Your own [kindness] has been shown to me, O <s>Śakra</s>; I am honored by your beneficial words.'

children.text: svabhyastaharṣaṃ tu manaḥ pradānais tadutpathe kena dhṛtiṃ labheta // AJm_5.16 //
children.translated_text: 'But how could a mind accustomed to the joy of giving find composure on the wrong path?' [AJm 5.16]

children.text: na cātra manyor anuvṛttimārge cittaṃ bhavān arhati saṃniyoktum /
children.translated_text: 'And you should not yoke my mind to the path of pursuing anger here;'

children.text: na hi svabhāvasya vipakṣadurgam āroḍhum alpena balena śakyam // AJm_5.17 //
children.translated_text: 'for one cannot ascend the fortress of the enemy of one's own nature with a small force.' [AJm 5.17]

body.text: śakra uvāca / gṛhapate / paryāptavibhavasya paripūrṇakośakoṣṭhāgārasya samyakpravṛttavividhavipulakarmāntasya virūḍhāyater loke vaśīkṛtaiśvaryasyāyaṃ kramo nemāṃ daśām abhiprapannasya / paśya /
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: 'O householder! This course [of action] is proper for one of ample means, with full treasuries and storehouses, with various and extensive enterprises well in motion, with growing income, with lordship established in the world—not for one who has arrived at this condition. Behold:'

children.text: svabuddhivispandasamāhitena vā yaśo'nukūlena kulocitena vā /
children.translated_text: 'Whether by an effort initiated by one's own intelligence, or in a manner befitting one's lineage, or one favorable to fame—'

children.text: samṛddhim ākṛṣya śubhena karmaṇā sapatnatejāṃsy abhibhūya bhānuvat // AJm_5.18 //
children.translated_text: 'having attracted prosperity by meritorious action, overpowering the brilliance of rivals like the sun—' [AJm 5.18]

children.text: jane prasaṅgena vitatya saṃnatiṃ prabodhya harṣaṃ sasuhṛtsu bandhuṣu /
children.translated_text: 'having gradually spread one's reputation among people, having awakened joy among friends and kinsmen—'

children.text: avāptasaṃmānavidhir nṛpād api śriyā pariṣvakta ivābhikāmyayā // AJm_5.19 //
children.translated_text: 'having obtained the honor of procedure even from the king, as if embraced by desirable <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune)—' [AJm 5.19]

children.text: atha pradāne pravijṛmbhitakramaḥ sukheṣu vā naiti janasya vācyatām /
children.translated_text: 'then, if one expands one's course of giving or enjoyments, one does not fall into people's censure;'

children.text: ajātapakṣaḥ kham ivārurukṣayā vighātabhāk kevalayā tu ditsayā // AJm_5.20 //
children.translated_text: 'but one who, with mere desire to give, like one without wings wishing to fly—meets only with failure.' [AJm 5.20]

children.text: yato dhanaṃ saṃyamanaibhṛtāśrayād upārjyatāṃ tāvad alaṃ praditsayā /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, let wealth first be earned through a foundation sustained by restraint—enough of this desire to give!'

children.text: anāryatāpy atra ca nāma kā bhaven na yat pradadyād vibhaveṣv abhāviṣu // AJm_5.21 //
children.translated_text: 'And what ignoble thing would there be in this—that one does not give when wealth is not yet at hand?' [AJm 5.21]

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca / alam atinirbandhenātrabhavataḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Enough of your excessive insistence, sir!'

children.text: ātmārthaḥ syād yasya garīyān parakāryāt tenāpi syād deyam anādṛtya samṛddhim /
children.translated_text: 'Even one for whom self-interest is greater than the welfare of others should give, disregarding prosperity;'

children.text: naiti prītiṃ tāṃ hi mahatyāpi vibhūtyā dānais tuṣṭiṃ lobhajayād yām upabhuṅkte // AJm_5.22 //
children.translated_text: 'for one does not attain that joy from even great affluence which one enjoys from giving, through the conquest of greed.' [AJm 5.22]

children.text: naiti svargaṃ kevalayā yac ca samṛddhyā dānenaiva khyātim avāpnoti ca puṇyām /
children.translated_text: 'One does not go to heaven by prosperity alone; and by giving alone does one obtain virtuous fame.'

children.text: mātsaryādīn nābhibhavaty eva ca doṣāṃs tasyā hetor dānam ataḥ ko na bhajeta // AJm_5.23 //
children.translated_text: 'It does not overcome faults such as avarice and the rest. Therefore, for the sake of that [prosperity], who would not resort to giving?' [AJm 5.23]

children.text: trātuṃ lokān yas tu jarāmṛtyuparītān apy ātmānaṃ ditsati kāruṇyavaśena /
children.translated_text: 'But he who, out of compassion, wishes to give even himself to protect beings beset by old age and death—'

children.text: yo nāsvādaṃ vetti sukhānāṃ paraduḥkhaiḥ kas tasyārthas tvadgatayā syād api lakṣmyā // AJm_5.24 //
children.translated_text: 'he who knows no relish for pleasures because of others' suffering—what use would wealth, even of your kind, be to him?' [AJm 5.24]

body.text: api ca devendra /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O lord of the gods:

children.text: saṃpattir iva vittānām adhruvā sthitir āyuṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Like the fortune of riches, the duration of life too is impermanent;'

children.text: iti yācanakaṃ labdhvā na samṛddhir avekṣyate // AJm_5.25 //
children.translated_text: 'therefore, having obtained a supplicant, one should not look to prosperity.' [AJm 5.25]

children.text: eko rathaś ca bhuvi yad vidadhāti vartma tenāparo vrajati dhṛṣṭataraṃ tathānyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'One chariot lays a track upon the earth; another follows it boldly, and then yet another.'

children.text: kalyāṇam ādyam imam ity avadhūya mārgaṃ nāsatpathapraṇayane ramate mano me // AJm_5.26 //
children.translated_text: 'Knowing this first [path] to be the auspicious one—my mind does not delight in fondness for the wrong path, casting aside this road.' [AJm 5.26]

children.text: arthaś ca vistaram upaiṣyati cet punar me hartā manāṃsi niyamena sa yācakānām /
children.translated_text: 'And if my wealth should again grow vast, it will surely capture the hearts of supplicants by its discipline;'

children.text: evaṃgate 'pi ca yathāvibhavaṃ pradāsye mā caiva dānaniyame pramadiṣma śakra // AJm_5.27 //
children.translated_text: 'and even in this condition, I shall give according to my means. And let us never be negligent in the vow of giving, O <s>Śakra</s>!' [AJm 5.27]

body.text: ity ukte śakro devendraḥ samabhiprasāditamanāḥ sādhu sādhv ity enam abhisaṃrādhya sabahumānasnigdham avekṣamāṇa uvāca /
body.translated_text: When this was said, <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, his mind thoroughly gladdened, praising him with 'Excellent! Excellent!', gazing upon him with reverence and affection, said:

children.text: yaśaḥsapatnair api karmabhir janaḥ samṛddhim anvicchati nīcadāruṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'People seek prosperity through actions that rival fame, yet are mean and cruel—'

children.text: svasaukhyasaṅgād anapekṣitātyayaḥ pratāryamāṇaś capalena cetasā // AJm_5.28 //
children.translated_text: 'heedless of their own destruction, out of attachment to their own pleasure, deceived by their fickle minds.' [AJm 5.28]

children.text: acintayitvā tu dhanakṣayaṃ tvayā svasaukhyahāniṃ mama ca pratāraṇām /
children.translated_text: 'But by you, without thought for the loss of wealth, for the loss of your own happiness, or for my deception—'

children.text: parārthasaṃpādanadhīracetasā mahattvam udbhāvitam ātmasaṃpadaḥ // AJm_5.29 //
children.translated_text: 'with a mind resolute in accomplishing the welfare of others, the greatness of self-worth has been revealed.' [AJm 5.29]

children.text: aho bataudāryaviśeṣabhāsvataḥ pramṛṣṭamātsaryatamisratā hṛdaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Ah! Of one radiant with the excellence of generosity, whose heart's darkness of avarice has been wiped away—'

children.text: pradānasaṃkocavirūpatāṃ gataṃ dhane pranaṣṭe 'pi na yat tadāśayā // AJm_5.30 //
children.translated_text: 'even when wealth is lost, that [heart] has not assumed the ugliness of contraction in giving, through the force of that disposition!' [AJm 5.30]

children.text: na cātra citraṃ paraduḥkhaduḥkhinaḥ kṛpāvaśāl lokahitaiṣiṇas tava /
children.translated_text: 'And here there is nothing wonderful: for you who suffer at others' suffering, who through compassion desire the welfare of the world—'

children.text: himāvadātaḥ śikharīva vāyunā na yat pradānād asi kampito mayā // AJm_5.31 //
children.translated_text: 'that you were not shaken from giving by me, like a peak white with snow [shaken] by the wind.' [AJm 5.31]

children.text: yaśaḥ samudbhāvayituṃ parīkṣayā dhanaṃ tavedaṃ tu nigūḍhavān aham /
children.translated_text: 'In order to make your fame shine forth, through a test, I had concealed this wealth of yours;'

children.text: maṇir hi śobhānugato 'py ato 'nyathā na saṃspṛśed ratnayaśomahārghatām // AJm_5.32 //
children.translated_text: 'for a gem, even though naturally lustrous, would not otherwise touch the great value of the fame of being [recognized as] a jewel.' [AJm 5.32]

children.text: ataḥ pradānair abhivarṣa yācakān hradān mahāmegha ivābhipūrayan /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, rain upon the supplicants with your gifts, like a great cloud filling lakes!'

children.text: dhanakṣayaṃ nāpsyasi matparigrahād idaṃ kṣamethāś ca viceṣṭitaṃ mama // AJm_5.33 //
children.translated_text: 'You shall not experience loss of wealth under my protection; and may you pardon this conduct of mine.' [AJm 5.33]

body.text: ity enam abhisaṃrādhya śakras tac cāsya vibhavasāram upasaṃhṛtya kṣamayitvā ca tatraivāntardadhe //
body.translated_text: Having thus gladdened him, <s>Śakra</s>, having restored the essence of his wealth, asked forgiveness, and disappeared right there.

body.text: tad evaṃ na vibhavakṣayāpekṣayā samṛddhyāśayā vā pradānavaidhuryam upayānti satpuruṣā iti //
body.translated_text: Thus, virtuous persons do not fall into laxity in giving, neither out of concern for loss of wealth nor out of desire for prosperity.

body.text: aviṣahyaśreṣṭhijātakaṃ pañcamam //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth, the <s>Aviṣahyaśreṣṭhi-Jātaka</s>.

children.text: 6. Śaśajātakam
children.translated_text: 6. The <s>Śaśa-Jātaka</s> (Hare Story).

children.text: tiryaggatānām api mahāsattvānāṃ śaktyanurūpā dānapravṛttir dṛṣṭā /
children.translated_text: Even among great beings born in animal form, generosity proportionate to their capacity has been observed.

children.text: kena nāma manuṣyabhūtena na dātavyaṃ syāt //
children.translated_text: What person born as a human, then, should fail to give?

body.text: tadyathānuśrūyate / kasmiṃś cid araṇyapradeśe manojñavīruttṛṇatarunicite puṣpaphalavati vaiḍūryanīlaśucisalilavāhinyā saritā vibhūṣitaparyante mṛduśādvalāstaraṇa

children.text: sukhasaṃsparśadarśanīya
children.translated_text: pleasant to touch and beautiful to behold,

children.text: dharaṇitale tapasvijanavicarite bodhisattvaḥ śaśo babhūva /
children.translated_text: Frequented by ascetics, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was born as a hare.

body.translated_text: As is traditionally heard: In a certain forest region, thickly covered with charming shrubs, grass, and trees, bearing flowers and fruits, its borders adorned by a river carrying waters pure as <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl) blue, with a ground of soft meadow-turf

children.text: sa sattvayogād vapuṣaś ca saṃpadā balaprakarṣād vipulena caujasā /
children.translated_text: By his strength of being, his bodily perfection, his preeminent power, and his vast energy,

children.text: atarkitaḥ kṣudramṛgair aśaṅkitaś cacāra tasmin mṛgarājalīlayā // AJm_6.1 //
children.translated_text: Unsuspected and unafraid among the smaller animals, he moved through that [forest] with the grace of a lion.

children.text: svacarmājinasaṃvītaḥ svatanūruhavalkalaḥ /
children.translated_text: Clothed in his own skin as a hide-garment, with his own body-hair as bark-cloth,

children.text: munivat tatra śuśubhe tuṣṭacittas tṛṇāṅkuraiḥ // AJm_6.2 //
children.translated_text: He shone there like a sage, content in heart with [mere] shoots of grass.

children.text: tasya maitryavadātena manovākkāyakarmaṇā /
children.translated_text: Through his conduct of body, speech, and mind, radiant with loving-kindness,

children.text: āsur jihmitadaurātmyāḥ prāyaḥ śiṣyasukhā mṛgāḥ // AJm_6.3 //
children.translated_text: The [other] animals, their wickedness subdued, were for the most part as docile as disciples.

body.text: tasya guṇātiśayasaṃbhṛtena snehagauraveṇa viśeṣavattaram avabaddhahṛdayās trayaḥ sahāyā babhūvur udraḥ śṛgālo vānaraś ca / te parasparasaṃbandhanibaddhasnehā iva bāndhavā anyonyapraṇayasaṃmānavirūḍhasauhṛdā iva ca suhṛdaḥ saṃmodamānās tatra viharanti sma / tiryaksvabhāvavimukhāś ca prāṇiṣu dayānuvṛttyā laulyapraśamād vismṛtasteyapravṛttyā ca dharmānurodhinyā ca vṛttyā paṭuvijñānatvād vinayaniyamadhīrayā ca ceṣṭayā devatānām api vismayanīyā babhūvuḥ /
body.translated_text: Bound in heart especially close to him by an affection and reverence born of his surpassing virtues, three companions he had: an otter, a jackal, and a monkey. They, their friendship bound by mutual connection like kinsmen, their goodwill grown through mutual esteem and honor like true friends, lived there in delight. Turning away from the nature of animals—through compassion toward creatures, through the calming of covetousness, through having forgotten the habit of stealing, through conduct conforming to <s>Dharma</s>, and through behavior steady with the discipline of training, owing to their keen intelligence—they became a wonder even to the gods.

children.text: sukhānulome guṇabādhini krame guṇānukūle ca sukhoparodhini /
children.translated_text: When the path is agreeable to pleasure yet obstructs virtue, and when it favors virtue yet impedes pleasure,

children.text: naro 'pi tāvad guṇapakṣasaṃśrayād virājate kiṃ bata tiryagākṛtiḥ // AJm_6.4 //
children.translated_text: Even a human being shines by embracing the side of virtue—how much more so one in an animal form!

children.text: abhūt sa teṣāṃ tu śaśākṛtiḥ kṛtī parānukampāpratipadgurur guruḥ /
children.translated_text: That hare-formed one, accomplished, was their <s>guru</s>, venerable as a guide on the path of compassion for others;

children.text: svabhāvasaṃpac ca guṇakramānugā yaśo yad eṣāṃ suralokam apy agāt // AJm_6.5 //
children.translated_text: And since his natural excellence followed the course of virtue, their fame reached even the world of the gods.

body.text: atha kadā cit sa mahātmā sāyāhnasamaye dharmaśravaṇārtham abhigataiḥ sabahumānam upāsyamānas taiḥ sahāyaiḥ paripūrṇaprāyamaṇḍalam ādityaviprakarṣād vyavadāyamānaśobhaṃ rūpyadarpaṇam iva tsaruvirahitam īṣatpārśvāpavṛttabimbaṃ śuklapakṣacaturdaśīcandramasamuditam abhivīkṣya sahāyān uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then once, that great soul, at the evening hour, being reverently attended by those companions who had come to hear the <s>Dharma</s>, seeing the moon of the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight rising—its disc nearly full, its beauty clarified by the withdrawal of the sun, like a silver mirror without its handle, its orb slightly turned to one side—spoke to his companions:

children.text: asāv āpūrṇaśobhena maṇḍalena hasann iva /
children.translated_text: 'With his disc full of beauty, as if laughing,

children.text: nivedayati sādhūnāṃ candramāḥ poṣadhotsavam // AJm_6.6 //
children.translated_text: The moon announces to the virtuous the <s>Poṣadha</s> (observance-day) festival.'

body.text: tad vyaktaṃ śvaḥ pañcadaśī yato bhavadbhiḥ poṣadhaniyamam abhisaṃpādayadbhir nyāyopalabdhenāhāraviśeṣena kālopanatam atithijanaṃ pratipūjya prāṇasaṃdhāraṇam anuṣṭheyam / paśyantu bhavantaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Clearly, tomorrow is the fifteenth—therefore you, while observing the <s>Poṣadha</s> restraints, should honor any guest who appears at the proper time with a special offering of food lawfully obtained, and then maintain your own lives. Consider, sirs:'

children.text: yat saṃprayogā virahāvasānāḥ samucchrayāḥ pātavirūpaniṣṭhāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Unions end in separation; elevations end in downfall;

children.text: vidyullatābhaṅguralolam āyus tenaiva kāryo dṛḍham apramādaḥ // AJm_6.7 //
children.translated_text: Life is as wavering and fickle as a streak of lightning—therefore one must be earnestly vigilant.'

children.text: dānena śīlābharaṇena tasmāt puṇyāni saṃvardhayituṃ yatadhvam /
children.translated_text: 'Through generosity, therefore, and through the ornament of moral conduct,

children.text: vivartamānasya hi janmadurge lokasya puṇyāni parā pratiṣṭhā // AJm_6.8 //
children.translated_text: Strive to increase your merits; for beings revolving in the perilous path of birth, merit is the supreme foundation.'

children.text: tārāgaṇānām abhibhūya lakṣmīṃ vibhāti yat kāntiguṇena somaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'That the moon outshines the splendor of the host of stars by the quality of his beauty,

children.text: jyotīṃṣi cākramya sahasraraśmir yad dīpyate puṇyaguṇocchrayaḥ saḥ // AJm_6.9 //
children.translated_text: And that the thousand-rayed sun blazes overwhelming [all other] lights—that is the exaltation of the quality of merit.'

children.text: dṛptasvabhāvāḥ sacivā nṛpāś ca puṇyaprabhāvāt pṛthivīśvarāṇām /
children.translated_text: 'That proud-natured ministers and kings, through the power of merit of earth's sovereigns,

children.text: sadaśvavṛttyā hatasarvagarvāḥ prītā ivājñādhuram udvahanti // AJm_6.10 //
children.translated_text: With all their pride destroyed as if by the behavior of a fine horse, willingly bear the yoke of obedience.'

children.text: puṇyair vihīnān anuyāty alakṣmīr vispandamānān api nītimārge /
children.translated_text: 'Misfortune follows those devoid of merit, even as they stir upon the path of statecraft;

children.text: puṇyādhikaiḥ sā hy avabhartsyamānā paryety amarṣād iva tadvipakṣān // AJm_6.11 //
children.translated_text: For she [misfortune], being rebuked by those rich in merit, pursues their opponents as if in anger.'

children.text: duḥkhapratiṣṭhād ayaśo'nubandhād apuṇyamārgād uparamya tasmāt /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, desisting from the path of demerit, whose foundation is suffering and whose companion is infamy,

children.text: śrīmatsu saukhyodayasādhaneṣu puṇyaprasaṅgeṣu matiṃ kurudhvam // AJm_6.12 //
children.translated_text: Set your minds upon the auspicious occasions of merit, which are glorious and the means of producing happiness.'

body.text: te tathety asyānuśāsanīṃ pratigṛhyābhivādya pradakṣiṇīkṛtya cainaṃ svaṃ svam ālayam abhijagmuḥ / aciragateṣu ca teṣu sahāyeṣu sa mahātmā cintām āpede /
body.translated_text: Saying 'So be it,' they accepted his instruction, bowed to him, circumambulated him, and went each to their own dwelling. And when those companions had not long departed, that great soul fell into reflection:

children.text: atither abhyupetasya saṃmānaṃ yena tena vā /
children.translated_text: 'Each of these has the power to honor a guest who arrives

children.text: vidhātuṃ śaktir asty eṣām atra śocyo 'ham eva tu // AJm_6.13 //
children.translated_text: With one thing or another—but it is I alone who am to be pitied here.'

children.text: asmaddantāgravicchinnāḥ paritiktās tṛṇāṅkurāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Blades of grass, cut by the tips of our teeth, are bitter;

children.text: śakyā nātithaye dātuṃ sarvathā dhig aśaktitām // AJm_6.14 //
children.translated_text: They cannot possibly be given to a guest—shame upon powerlessness in every way!'

children.text: ity asāmarthyadīnena ko nv artho jīvitena me /
children.translated_text: 'What use is life to me, miserable from this incapacity,

children.text: ānandaḥ śokatāṃ yāyād yasyaivam atithir mama // AJm_6.15 //
children.translated_text: When my joy would turn to sorrow if a guest were to come to me thus?'

body.text: tat kutredānīm idam atithiparicaryāvaiguṇyān niḥsāraṃ śarīrakam utsṛjyamānaṃ kasya cid upakārāya syād iti vimṛśan sa mahātmā smṛtiṃ pratilebhe / aye /
body.translated_text: 'Then where, in some way, might this worthless little body, cast aside because of its unfitness for the duty of hospitality, be of service to someone?' Reflecting thus, that great soul regained his presence of mind: 'Aha!'

children.text: svādhīnasulabham etan niravadyaṃ vidyate mamaiva khalu /
children.translated_text: 'This body-treasure of mine, easily available and within my own power, is free from fault,

children.text: atithijanapratipūjanasamartharūpaṃ śarīradhanam // AJm_6.16 //
children.translated_text: And exists in a form capable of honoring a guest.'

body.text: tat kim ahaṃ viṣīdāmi /
body.translated_text: 'Then why should I despond?'

children.text: samadhigatam idaṃ mayātitheyaṃ hṛdaya vimuñca yato viṣādadainyam /
children.translated_text: 'I have found my offering for a guest—O heart, abandon this wretchedness of despair!

children.text: samupanatam anena satkariṣyāmy aham atithipraṇayaṃ śarīrakeṇa // AJm_6.17 //
children.translated_text: With this little body, I shall honor the gift of hospitality that has presented itself.'

body.text: iti viniścitya sa mahāsattvaḥ param iva lābham adhigamya paramaprītamanās tatrāvatasthe /
body.translated_text: Having thus resolved, that great being, as if having obtained the highest gain, remained there with his mind supremely delighted.

children.text: vitarkātiśayas tasya hṛdi saṃpravijṛmbhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The extraordinary intensity of his resolution, having swelled in his heart,

children.text: āviścakre prabhāvaṃ ca prasādaṃ ca divaukasām // AJm_6.18 //
children.translated_text: Manifested both its power and its grace to the celestial beings.

children.text: tataḥ praharṣād iva sācalā calā mahī babhūvānibhṛtārṇavāṃśukā /
children.translated_text: Then, as if from joy, the earth with its mountains trembled, with the waters of its oceans agitated;

children.text: vitastaruḥ khe suradundubhisvanā diśaḥ prasādābharaṇāś cakāśire // AJm_6.19 //
children.translated_text: The sky became filled with the sound of divine drums, and the quarters shone as if adorned with serenity.

children.text: prasaktamandrastanitaprahāsinas taḍitpinaddhāś ca ghanāḥ samantataḥ /
children.translated_text: Clouds all around, thundering deeply as if laughing, wrapped in lightning,

children.text: parasparāśleṣavikīrṇareṇubhiḥ prasaktam enaṃ kusumair avākiran // AJm_6.20 //
children.translated_text: Showered flowers upon him continuously, the pollen scattered by their mutual embrace.

children.text: samudvahan dhīragatiḥ samīraṇaḥ sugandhi nānādrumapuṣpajaṃ rajaḥ /
children.translated_text: The steady-moving breeze, carrying the fragrant pollen born from the flowers of various trees,

children.text: mudā pravṛddhair avibhaktabhaktibhis tam arcayām āsa kṛśāṃśukair iva // AJm_6.21 //
children.translated_text: Seemed to worship him joyfully with thin garments, as it were, of undivided devotion.

body.text: tad upalabhya pramuditavismitamanobhir devatābhiḥ samantataḥ parikīrtyamānaṃ tasya vitarkādbhutaṃ samāpūryamāṇavismayakautūhalena manasā tasya mahāsattvasya bhāvajijñāsayā dvitīye 'hani gaganatalamadhyam abhilaṅghamāne paṭutarakiraṇaprabhāve savitari prasphuritamarīcijālavasanāsu bhāsvarātapavisarāvaguṇṭhitāsv anālokanakṣamāsu dikṣu saṃkṣipyamāṇacchāyeṣv abhivṛddhacīrīvirāvonnāditeṣu vanāntareṣu vicchidyamānapakṣisaṃpāteṣu gharmaklamāpītotsāheṣv adhvageṣu śakro devānām adhipatir brāhmaṇarūpī bhūtvā mārgapranaṣṭa ivādhvagaḥ kṣuttarṣaśramaviṣādadīnakaṇṭhaḥ sasvaraṃ prarudann avidūre teṣāṃ vicukrośa /
body.translated_text: Perceiving this, with minds delighted and amazed, the deities praising his wondrous resolution from all sides—with a mind filling with wonder and curiosity, wishing to test the true nature of that great being—on the second day, when the sun was traversing the middle of the sky's surface with even sharper rays, when the directions, veiled by shimmering heat-haze garments, were blinding with the spread of blazing light, when the shadows were shrinking, when the forest interiors resounded with the heightened shrill cries of crickets, when the flights of birds had ceased, when travelers were drained of energy by the oppression of heat—<s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, assumed the form of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, appearing as a traveler lost on the road, his voice hoarse with hunger, thirst, fatigue, and despair, weeping aloud, and cried out not far from them:

children.text: ekaṃ sārthāt paribhraṣṭaṃ bhramantaṃ gahane vane /
children.translated_text: 'One who has strayed from his caravan, wandering in the depths of the forest,

children.text: kṣucchramaklāntadehaṃ māṃ trātum arhanti sādhavaḥ // AJm_6.22 //
children.translated_text: My body exhausted from hunger, fatigue, and weariness—the virtuous should rescue me!'

children.text: mārgāmārgajñānaniścetanaṃ māṃ diksaṃmohāt kvāpi gacchantam ekam /
children.translated_text: 'Unable even to discern path from non-path, going somewhere alone in my confusion of directions,

children.text: kāntāre 'smin gharmatarṣaklamārtaṃ mābhaiḥśabdaiḥ ko 'tra māṃ hlādayeta // AJm_6.23 //
children.translated_text: Afflicted by heat, thirst, and weariness in this wilderness—who here would gladden me with words of 'Fear not!'?'

body.text: atha te mahāsattvās tena tasyātikaruṇenākranditaśabdena samākampitahṛdayāḥ sasaṃbhramadrutataragatayas taṃ deśam abhijagmuḥ / mārgapranaṣṭādhvagadīnadarśanaṃ cainam abhisamīkṣya samabhigamyopacārapuraḥsaraṃ samāśvāsayanta ūcuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then those great beings, their hearts shaken by that most piteous cry of his, rushing with increased haste and agitation, came to that place. And seeing the wretched appearance of the traveler who had lost his way, they approached him and, preceded by courteous attentions, comforted him and said:

children.text: kāntāre vipranaṣṭo 'ham ity alaṃ saṃbhrameṇa te /
children.translated_text: '"I am lost in the wilderness"—enough of your alarm!

children.text: svasya śiṣyagaṇasyeva samīpe vartase hi naḥ // AJm_6.24 //
children.translated_text: You are now in our presence, as if among your own group of disciples.'

children.text: tad adya tāvad asmākaṃ paricaryāpratigrahāt /
children.translated_text: 'So today, by accepting our service,

children.text: vidhāyānugrahaṃ saumya śvo gantāsi yathepsitam // AJm_6.25 //
children.translated_text: Bestow your favor upon us, gentle sir, and tomorrow you shall go as you wish.'

body.text: athodras tasya tūṣṇīṃbhāvād anumatam upanimantraṇam avetya harṣasaṃbhramatvaritagatiḥ sapta rohitamatsyān samupanīyāvocad enam /
body.translated_text: Then the otter, understanding from the guest's silence that the invitation was accepted, went swiftly in the haste of delight and brought seven <s>rohita</s> fish, and said to him:

children.text: mīnāribhir vismaraṇojjhitā vā trāsotplutā vā sthalam abhyupetāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Either forgotten and abandoned by fishermen, or having leapt to shore in fright,

children.text: khedaprasuptā iva sapta matsyā labdhā mayaitān nivaseha bhuktvā // AJm_6.26 //
children.translated_text: These seven fish, lying as if asleep from exhaustion, were found by me—eat them and stay here.'

body.text: atha śṛgālo 'py enaṃ yathopalabdham annajātam upahṛtya praṇāmapuraḥsaraṃ sādaram uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then the jackal too, bringing such food as he had found and offering it with a respectful bow, said courteously:

children.text: ekāṃ ca godhāṃ dadhibhājanaṃ ca kenāpi saṃtyaktam ihādhyagaccham /
children.translated_text: 'A single monitor lizard and a pot of yogurt, abandoned here by someone, I have found;

children.text: tan me hitāvekṣitayopayujya vane 'stu te 'smin guṇavāsa vāsaḥ // AJm_6.27 //
children.translated_text: Please use them, looking upon my welfare—and may your stay in this forest be one of virtue.'

body.text: ity uktvā prītamanās tad asmai samupajahāra // atha vānaraḥ paripākaguṇāt samupajātamārdavāni manaḥśilācūrṇarañjitānīvātipiñjarāṇy atiraktabandhanamūlāni piṇḍīkṛtāny āmraphalāny ādāya sāñjalipragraham enam uvāca /
body.translated_text: Having said this, delighted in mind, he presented it to him. Then the monkey, bringing mango fruits that had acquired softness from ripeness, exceedingly golden as if tinted with <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) powder, with very red stems at their base, gathered into a heap, said to him with palms joined in offering:

children.text: āmrāṇi pakvāny udakaṃ manojñaṃ chāyāś ca satsaṃgamasaukhyaśītāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Ripe mangoes, delightful water, and shade cool with the pleasure of good company—

children.text: ity asti me brahmavidāṃ variṣṭha bhuktvaitad atraiva tavāstu vāsaḥ // AJm_6.28 //
children.translated_text: These I have, O best of knowers of <s>Brahman</s>—eat this, and let your stay be here.'

body.text: atha śaśo 'bhisṛtyainam upacārakriyānantaraṃ sabahumānam udīkṣamāṇaḥ svena śarīreṇopanimantrayām āsa /
body.translated_text: Then the hare, approaching him, after the courtesies had been performed, gazing upon him respectfully, invited him with his own body:

children.text: na santi mudgā na tilā na taṇḍulā vane 'bhivṛddhasya śaśasya ke ca na /
children.translated_text: 'I have no lentils, no sesame, no rice—and what else does a hare raised in the forest possess?

children.text: śarīram etat tv analābhisaṃskṛtaṃ mamopayujyādya tapovane vasa // AJm_6.29 //
children.translated_text: But this body of mine, prepared by fire, please use it, and live today in this grove of austerities.'

children.text: yad asti yasyepsitasādhanaṃ dhanaṃ sa tan niyuṅkte 'rthijanāgamotsave /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever wealth one has that serves to fulfill one's desires, that one employs at the festival of a supplicant's arrival;

children.text: na cāsti dehād adhikaṃ ca me dhanaṃ pratīccha sarvasvam idaṃ yato mama // AJm_6.30 //
children.translated_text: And I have no wealth greater than my body—therefore accept this, my all.'

body.text: śakra uvāca /
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said:

children.text: anyasyāpi vadhaṃ tāvat kuryād asmadvidhaḥ katham /
children.translated_text: 'One like me would never kill even another [creature]—

children.text: iti darśitasauhārde kathā kaiva bhavadvidhe // AJm_6.31 //
children.translated_text: How then could there be any talk [of killing oneself] for one of your demonstrated goodwill?'

body.text: śaśa uvāca / upapannarūpam idam āsannānukrośe brāhmaṇye / tad ihaiva tāvad bhavān āstām asmadanugrahāpekṣayā yāvat kutaś cid ātmānugrahopāyam āsādayāmīti // atha śakro devānām indras tasya bhāvam avetya taptatapanīyavarṇaṃ sphuratpratanujvālaṃ vikīryamāṇavisphuliṅgaprakaraṃ nirdhūmam aṅgārarāśim abhinirmame // atha śaśaḥ samantato vilokayaṃs tam agniskandhaṃ dadarśa / dṛṣṭvā ca prītamanāḥ śakram uvāca / samadhigato 'yaṃ mayātmānugrahopāyaḥ / tad asmaccharīropabhogāt saphalām anugrahāśāṃ me kartum arhasi / paśya mahābrāhmaṇa /
body.translated_text: The hare said: 'This is fitting from a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> given to ready compassion. Then please stay right here, sir, in expectation of my favor, while I find somewhere the means to serve myself.' Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, understanding his intention, created a heap of glowing embers—golden as heated gold, with slender quivering flames, scattering sparks, smokeless. Then the hare, looking around on all sides, saw that mass of fire. And seeing it, his mind delighted, he said to <s>Śakra</s>: 'I have found the means to serve myself. Please make my hope of favor fruitful by partaking of my body. Behold, O great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>:'

children.text: deyaṃ ca ditsāpravaṇaṃ ca cittaṃ bhavadvidhenātithinā ca yogaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Something to give, a mind inclined to giving, and the arrival of a guest like you—

children.text: nāvāptum etad dhi sukhena śakyaṃ tat syād amoghaṃ bhavadāśrayān me // AJm_6.32 //
children.translated_text: This is truly not easy to obtain—therefore, may it not be in vain through your grace.'

body.text: ity anunīya saṃmānanādarātithipriyatayā cainam abhivādya /
body.translated_text: Having thus entreated him, and having bowed to him with the earnestness and respect of one who delights in honoring guests,

children.text: tataḥ sa taṃ vahnim abhijvalantaṃ nidhiṃ dhanārthī sahaseva dṛṣṭvā /
children.translated_text: Then he, seeing that blazing fire like a treasure-seeker suddenly seeing a hoard of wealth,

children.text: pareṇa harṣeṇa samāruroha toyaṃ hasatpadmam ivaikahaṃsaḥ // AJm_6.33 //
children.translated_text: Leapt upon it with supreme joy, like a single swan upon a lake of water adorned with laughing lotuses.

body.text: tad dṛṣṭvā paramavismayāvarjitamatir devānām adhipatiḥ svam eva vapur āsthāya divyakusumavarṣapuraḥsarībhir manaḥśrutisukhābhir vāgbhir abhipūjya taṃ mahāsattvaṃ kamalapalāśalakṣmīsamṛddhābhyāṃ bhāsurāṅgulivibhūṣaṇālaṃkṛtābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ svayam eva cainaṃ parigṛhya tridaśebhyaḥ saṃdarśayām āsa / paśyantv atrabhavantas tridaśālayanivāsino devāḥ samanumodantāṃ cedam ativismayanīyaṃ karmāvadānam asya mahāsattvasya /
body.translated_text: Seeing that, the lord of the gods, his mind captivated with supreme wonder, assuming his own form, honoring that great being with words that preceded showers of divine flowers and that were delightful to the mind and ear — with his own two hands, resplendent with the beauty of lotus petals and adorned with shining finger-ornaments, he took him up and displayed him to the gods: "Behold —"

children.text: tyaktaṃ batānena yathā śarīraṃ niḥsaṅgam adyātithivatsalena /
children.translated_text: "How this body was given up by him today, without attachment, the one who is devoted to guests!

children.text: nirmālyam apy evam akampamānā nālaṃ parityaktum adhīrasattvāḥ // AJm_6.34 //
children.translated_text: Even a worthless garland — those of irresolute nature are incapable of giving up without trembling." [AJm 6.34]

children.text: jātiḥ kveyaṃ tadvirodhi kva cedaṃ tyāgaudāryaṃ cetasaḥ pāṭavaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: "What is this birth [as an animal], and how contrary to it are this magnificence of renunciation, this breadth of mind!

children.text: vispaṣṭo 'yaṃ puṇyamandādarāṇāṃ pratyādeśo devatānāṃ nṛṇāṃ ca // AJm_6.35 //
children.translated_text: This is a clear rebuke to those gods and men who have but scant regard for merit." [AJm 6.35]

children.text: aho bata guṇābhyāsavāsitāsya yathā matiḥ /
children.translated_text: "Ah, how his mind is perfumed by the practice of virtues!

children.text: aho sadvṛttavātsalyaṃ kriyaudāryeṇa darśitam // AJm_6.36 //
children.translated_text: Ah, the devotion to noble conduct demonstrated by the magnificence of his deed!" [AJm 6.36]

body.text: atha śakras tatkarmātiśayavikhyāpanārthaṃ lokahitāvekṣī śaśabimbalakṣaṇena vaijayantasya prāsādavarasya sudharmāyāś ca devasabhāyāḥ kūṭāgārakarṇike candramaṇḍalaṃ cābhyalaṃcakāra /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, looking to the welfare of the world, in order to make known the excellence of that deed, adorned the moon-disc and the peak-chamber of the supreme palace <s>Vaijayanta</s> and of the divine assembly-hall <s>Sudharmā</s> with the mark of the hare's image.

children.text: saṃpūrṇe 'dyāpi tad idaṃ śaśabimbaṃ niśākare /
children.translated_text: To this day, this image of the hare in the full night-maker

children.text: chāyāmayam ivādarśe rājate 'bhivirājate // AJm_6.37 //
children.translated_text: shines and gleams, like a reflection of shadow in a mirror. [AJm 6.37]

children.text: tataḥ prabhṛti lokena kumudākarahāsanaḥ /
children.translated_text: From that time forth, the moon, who causes the water-lilies to smile,

children.text: kṣaṇadātilakaś candraḥ śaśāṅka iti kīrtyate // AJm_6.38 //
children.translated_text: the ornament of the night, is celebrated by the world as '<s>Śaśāṅka</s>' (hare-marked). [AJm 6.38]

body.text: tad evaṃ tiryaggatānām api mahāsattvānāṃ śaktyanurūpā dānapravṛttir dṛṣṭā / kena nāma manuṣyabhūtena na dātavyaṃ syāt //
body.translated_text: Thus, even among great beings born in animal form, the practice of giving according to their ability has been observed — what human being could there be who should not give?

body.text: tathā tiryaggatā api guṇavātsalyāt saṃpūjyante sadbhir iti guṇeṣv ādaraḥ kārya ity evam apy upaneyam //
body.translated_text: Also, it should be understood thus: even those born as animals are honored by the virtuous on account of their devotion to virtue — therefore regard for virtues should be cultivated.

body.text: śaśajātakaṃ ṣaṣṭham //
body.translated_text: This concludes the sixth story, the <s>Śaśa-jātaka</s> (The Hare Story).

children.text: 7. Agastyajātakam
children.translated_text: 7. The <s>Agastya-jātaka</s> (The Story of Agastya)

body.text: tapovanasthānām apy alaṃkāras tyāgaśauryaṃ prāg eva gṛhasthānām //
body.translated_text: The magnificence of renunciation is an ornament even for those dwelling in a hermitage — how much more so for householders!

body.text: tadyathānuśrūyate / bodhisattvabhūtaḥ kilāyaṃ bhagavāṃl lokahitārthaṃ saṃsārādhvani vartamānaś cāritraguṇaviśuddhyabhilakṣitaṃ kṣititalatilakabhūtam anyatamaṃ mahad brāhmaṇakulaṃ gaganatalam iva śaradamalaparipūrṇamaṇḍalaś candramāḥ samudyann evābhyalaṃcakāra / sa yathākramaṃ śrutismṛtivihitān avāpya jātakarmādīn saṃskārān adhītya sāṅgān vedān kṛtsnaṃ vyāpya vidvadyaśasā manuṣyalokaṃ guṇapriyair dātṛbhir abhyarthya pratigrāhyamāṇavibhavatvāt parāṃ dhanasamṛddhim adhijagāma /
body.translated_text: Thus it is heard: <s>Bhagavān</s>, when he was a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, traveling on the road of <s>saṃsāra</s> for the benefit of the world, graced a certain great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> family — distinguished for its purity of virtuous conduct, a jewel upon the surface of the earth — just as the moon, with its orb full and spotless in autumn, graces the sky by its very rising. He, in due course, having obtained the rites prescribed by scripture and tradition —

children.text: sa bandhumitrāśritadīnavargaṃ saṃmānanīyān atithīn gurūṃś ca /
children.translated_text: he gladdened his kinsmen, friends, dependents, the poor, honored guests, and teachers with that prosperity,

children.text: prahlādayām āsa tayā samṛddhyā deśān mahāmegha ivābhivarṣan // AJm_7.1 //
children.translated_text: pouring down upon the regions like a great cloud. [AJm 7.1]

children.text: vidvattayā tasya yaśaḥ prakāśaṃ tat tyāgaśauryād adhikaṃ cakāśe /
children.translated_text: His fame, bright with learning, shone even more through the magnificence of his renunciation —

children.text: niśākarasyeva śaradviśuddhaṃ samagrabhāvād adhikānti bimbam // AJm_7.2 //
children.translated_text: like the full orb of the moon, pure in autumn, shining with greater beauty because of its completeness. [AJm 7.2]

body.text: atha sa mahātmā kukāryavyāsaṅgadoṣasaṃbādhaṃ pramādāspadabhūtaṃ dhanārjanarakṣaṇaprasaṅgavyākulam upaśamavirodhi vyasanaśaraśatalakṣyabhūtam aparyantakarmāntānuṣṭhānapariśramam atṛptijanakaṃ kṛśāsvādaṃ gārhasthyam avetya taddoṣaviviktasukhāṃ ca dharmapratipattyanukūlāṃ mokṣadharmārambhādhiṣṭhānabhūtāṃ pravrajyām anupaśyan mahatīm api tāṃ dhanasamṛddhim aparikleśādhigatāṃ lokasaṃnatimanoharāṃ tṛṇavad apāsya tāpasapravrajyāvinayaniyamaparo babhūva / pravrajitam api taṃ mahāsattvaṃ yaśaḥprakāśatvāt pūrvasaṃstavānusmaraṇāt saṃbhāvitaguṇatvāt praśamābhilakṣitatvāc ca śreyo'rthī janas tadguṇagaṇāvarjitamatis tathaivābhijagāma / sa taṃ gṛhijanasaṃsargaṃ pravivekasukhapramāthinaṃ vyāsaṅgavikṣepāntarāyakaram abahumanyamānaḥ pravivekābhirāmatayā dakṣiṇasamudramadhyāvagāḍham indranīlabhedābhinīlavarṇair anilabalākalitair ūrmimālāvilāsair ācchuritaparyantaṃ sitasikatāstīrṇabhūmibhāgaṃ puṣpaphalapallavālaṃkṛtaviṭapair nānātarubhir upaśobhitaṃ vimalasalilāśayapratīraṃ kārādvīpam adhyāsanād āśramapadaśriyā saṃyojayām āsa /
body.translated_text: Then that great soul, perceiving household life to be crowded with the faults of entanglement in bad deeds, a breeding ground for negligence, troubled by the concern for acquiring and protecting wealth, hostile to tranquility, a target for the hundred arrows of vice, wearying with the toil of endless undertakings, unsatisfying and thin in its pleasures — and perceiving the happiness of forest life, free from those faults, favorable to the practice of <s>Dharma</s>, the foundation for the commencement of the path to liberation —

children.text: sutanus tapasā tatra sa reje tapasātanuḥ /
children.translated_text: slender in body through austerity, he shone there, though slender in his bodily frame —

children.text: navaś candra iva vyomni kāntatvenākṛśaḥ kṛśaḥ // AJm_7.3 //
children.translated_text: like a new moon in the sky, attractive despite being thin. [AJm 7.3]

children.text: praśamanibhṛtaceṣṭitendriyo vrataniyamaikaraso vane vasan /
children.translated_text: With senses calmed and restrained in their activity, his sole delight in the observance of vows, dwelling in the forest —

children.text: munir iti tanubuddhiśaktibhir mṛgavihagair api so 'nvagamyata // AJm_7.4 //
children.translated_text: he was recognized as a sage even by the deer and birds, whose powers of understanding are slight. [AJm 7.4]

body.text: atha sa mahātmā pradānocitatvāt tapovane 'pi nivasan kālopanatam atithijanaṃ yathāsaṃnihitena mūlaphalena śucinā salilena hṛdyābhiś ca svāgatāśīrvādapeśalābhis tapasvijanayogyābhir vāgbhiḥ saṃpūjayati sma / atithijanopayuktaśeṣeṇa ca yātrāmātrārtham abhyavahṛtena vanyenāhāreṇa vartayām āsa // tasya tapaḥprakarṣāt pravisṛtena yaśasā samāvarjitahṛdayaḥ śakro devānām indraḥ sthairyajijñāsayā tasya mahāsattvasya tasminn araṇyāyatane tāpasajanopabhogayogyaṃ mūlaphalam anupūrveṇa sarvam antardhāpayām āsa / bodhisattvo 'pi dhyānaprasṛtamānasatayā saṃtoṣaparicayād anadhimūrchitatvād āhāre śarīre cānabhiṣvaṅgān na tadantardhānahetuṃ manasi cakāra / sa taruṇāni tarupallavāny adhiśrāya tair āhāraprayojanam abhiniṣpādyāparitṛṣyamāṇa āhāraviśeṣānutsukaḥ svasthamatis tathaiva vijahāra /
body.translated_text: Then that great soul, being accustomed to giving, even while dwelling in the hermitage, would honor the guests who came at the appointed time with such roots and fruits as were available, with pure water, and with pleasant words befitting an ascetic, graciously said as words of welcome and blessing. And he sustained himself with forest food eaten merely for the purpose of subsistence, being the remainder after the guests had partaken.

children.text: na kva cid durlabhā vṛttiḥ saṃtoṣaniyatātmanām /
children.translated_text: Livelihood is nowhere difficult to obtain for those of self-controlled nature, established in contentment —

children.text: kutra nāma na vidyante tṛṇaparṇajalāśayāḥ // AJm_7.5 //
children.translated_text: where indeed are grass, leaves, and water-courses not to be found? [AJm 7.5]

body.text: vismitataramanās tu śakro devendras tasya tenāvasthānena sthirataraguṇasaṃbhāvanas tatparīkṣānimittaṃ tasminn araṇyavanapradeśe nidāghakālānila iva samagraṃ vīruttṛṇatarugaṇaṃ parṇasamṛddhyā viyojayām āsa // atha bodhisattvaḥ pratyārdratarāṇi śīrṇaparṇāni samāhṛtya tair udakasvinnair anutkaṇṭhitamatir vartayamāno dhyānasukhaprīṇitamanās tatrāmṛtatṛpta iva vijahāra /
body.translated_text: But <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, his mind filled with ever-greater wonder, recognizing the firmness of his qualities through that mode of life, and for the purpose of testing him, in that forest region, like a hot-season wind, stripped all the shrubs, grasses, and trees of their leafy abundance. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, gathering the still-moist fallen leaves and softening them in water, with an undisturbed mind —

children.text: avismayaḥ śrutavatāṃ samṛddhānām amatsaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Lack of amazement among the learned, lack of envy among the wealthy,

children.text: saṃtoṣaś ca vanasthānāṃ guṇaśobhāvidhiḥ paraḥ // AJm_7.6 //
children.translated_text: and contentment among forest-dwellers — these are the supreme principles of virtuous beauty. [AJm 7.6]

body.text: atha śakras tena tasyādbhutarūpeṇa saṃtoṣasthairyeṇa samabhivṛddhavismayaḥ sāmarṣa iva tasya mahāsattvasya vratakāle hutāgnihotrasya parisamāptajapasyātithijanadidṛkṣayā diśo vyavalokayato brāhmaṇarūpam āsthāyātithir iva nāma purastāt prādurabhūt / prītamanāḥ samabhigamya cainaṃ bodhisattvaḥ svāgatādipriyavacanapuraḥsareṇāhārakālanivedanenopanimantrayām āsa / tūṣṇīṃbhāvāt tu tasyānumatam upanimantraṇam avetya sa mahātmā
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, his wonder increased by that extraordinary steadfastness of contentment, as if with indignation, at the time of the great being's vow-observance — when the oblation-fire had been offered, the recitation completed, and he was looking in all directions eager to see a guest — assumed the form of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and appeared before him like a guest. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with delighted mind, approached him with words of welcome and —

children.text: ditsāprakarṣavikasannayanāsyaśobhaḥ snigdhair manaḥśrutiharair abhinandya vākyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: with the beauty of eyes and face blossoming with the ardor of the desire to give, having greeted him with affectionate words that delighted the mind and ear,

children.text: kṛcchropalabdham api tac chrapaṇaṃ samastaṃ tasmai dadau svayam abhūc ca mudaiva tṛptaḥ // AJm_7.7 //
children.translated_text: he gave him all that food obtained with such difficulty, and was himself satisfied by joy alone. [AJm 7.7]

body.text: sa tathaiva praviśya dhyānāgāraṃ tenaiva prītiprāmodyena tad ahorātram atināmayām āsa // atha śakras tasya dvitīye tṛtīye cāhani tathaiva vratakāle purataḥ prādurabhūt / so 'pi cainaṃ pramuditataramanās tathaiva pratipūjayām āsa/
body.translated_text: He then entered the meditation-chamber and passed that day and night in that very state of joy and delight. Then <s>Śakra</s> appeared before him in the same manner at the time of his vow-observance on the second and third days. And he, with ever more delighted mind, honored him in the same manner.

children.text: dānābhilāṣaḥ sādhūnāṃ kṛpābhyāsavivardhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The desire for giving among the virtuous, nourished by the practice of compassion,

children.text: naiti saṃkocadīnatvaṃ duḥkhaiḥ prāṇāntikair api // AJm_7.8 //
children.translated_text: does not dwindle into the meanness of contraction, even through suffering that threatens life itself. [AJm 7.8]

body.text: atha śakraḥ paramavismayāviṣṭahṛdayas tapaḥprakarṣād asya prārthanāmātrāpekṣaṃ tridaśapatilakṣmīsaṃparkam avagamya samutpatitabhayāśaṅkaḥ svam eva vapur divyādbhutaśobham abhiprapadya tapaḥprayojanam enaṃ paryapṛcchat /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, his heart filled with supreme wonder, understanding that through the excellence of his austerity, the splendor of the lord of the thirty gods awaited merely his wish, and alarmed by the apprehension that had arisen, assuming his own form of divine and wonderful beauty, asked him about the purpose of his austerity:

children.text: bandhūn priyān aśrumukhān vihāya parigrahān saukhyaparigrahāṃś ca /
children.translated_text: "Having left behind kinsmen and loved ones with tear-stained faces, and possessions, and the embrace of pleasures,

children.text: āśāṅkuśaṃ nu vyavasṛjya kutra tapaḥparikleśam imaṃ śrito 'si // AJm_7.9 //
children.translated_text: having cast away the goad of desire — to what end have you resorted to this painful austerity? [AJm 7.9]

children.text: sukhopapannān paribhūya bhogāñ chokāturaṃ bandhujanaṃ ca kṛtvā /
children.translated_text: "Disdaining enjoyments that are easily available, and making your kinsmen distressed with grief —

children.text: na hetunālpena hi yānti dhīrāḥ sukhoparodhīni tapovanāni // AJm_7.10 //
children.translated_text: for it is not for a trivial reason that the resolute betake themselves to hermitages that obstruct pleasure. [AJm 7.10]

children.text: vaktavyam etan mayi manyase cet kautūhalaṃ no 'rhasi tad vinetum /
children.translated_text: "If you deem this fit to be told to me, you should gratify our curiosity —

children.text: kiṃ nāma tad yasya guṇaśraveṇa vaśīkṛtaivaṃ bhavato 'pi buddhiḥ // AJm_7.11 //
children.translated_text: what is that thing, by hearing of whose qualities even your understanding has been so captivated?" [AJm 7.11]

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca / śrūyatāṃ mārṣa yannimitto 'yaṃ mama prayatnaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: "Hear, sir, the purpose for which this effort of mine is undertaken."

children.text: punaḥpunarjātir atīva duḥkhaṃ jarā vipad vyādhivirūpatā ca /
children.translated_text: "Birth again and again, extreme suffering, old age, calamity, disease, and disfigurement,

children.text: martavyam ity ākulatā ca buddher lokān atas trātum iha sthito 'smi // AJm_7.12 //
children.translated_text: and the confusion of mind from the thought 'I must die' — to save the world from these, I stand here." [AJm 7.12]

body.text: atha śakro nāyam asmadgatāṃ śriyaṃ kāmayata iti samāśvāsitahṛdayaḥ subhāṣitena tena cābhiprasāditamatir yuktam ity abhipūjya tad asya vacanaṃ varapradānena bodhisattvam upanimantrayām āsa /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, his heart reassured that 'this one does not desire the sovereignty that belongs to me,' and his mind pleased by that eloquent speech, said 'It is fitting!' in approval of his words, and invited the <s>Bodhisattva</s> by offering a boon:

children.text: atra te tāpasajanapratirūpe subhāṣite /
children.translated_text: "In this eloquent speech of yours, worthy of the manner of ascetics —

children.text: dadāmi kāśyapa varaṃ tad vṛṇīṣva yad icchasi // AJm_7.13 //
children.translated_text: I give you a boon, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>; choose whatever you desire." [AJm 7.13]

body.text: atha bodhisattvo bhavasukheṣv anāsthaḥ prārthanām eva duḥkham avagacchan sātmībhūtasaṃtoṣaḥ śakram uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, without attachment to the pleasures of existence, understanding that desire itself is suffering, established in contentment that had become part of his nature, said to <s>Śakra</s>:

children.text: dātum icchasi cen mahyam anugrahakaraṃ varam /
children.translated_text: "If you wish to give me a boon that brings benefit,

children.text: vṛṇe tasmād aham imaṃ devānāṃ pravaraṃ varam // AJm_7.14 //
children.translated_text: then I choose from the lord of the gods this supreme boon: [AJm 7.14]

children.text: dārān mano'bhilaṣitāṃs tanayān prabhutvam arthān abhīpsitaviśālatarāṃś ca labdhvā /
children.translated_text: "Having obtained wives desired by the mind, sons, sovereignty, and wealth of the most abundant kind wished for —

children.text: yenābhitaptamatir eti na jātu tṛptiṃ lobhānalaḥ sa hṛdayaṃ mama nābhyupeyāt // AJm_7.15 //
children.translated_text: by which the tormented mind never attains satisfaction — may the fire of greed not approach my heart." [AJm 7.15]

body.text: atha śakras tasya tayā saṃtoṣapravaṇamānasatayā subhāṣitābhivyañjitayā bhūyasyā mātrayā saṃprasāditamatiḥ punar bodhisattvaṃ

children.text: sādhu
children.translated_text: "Excellent!

children.text: sādhv iti praśasya vareṇopacchandayām āsa /
children.translated_text: Excellent!" — praising him thus, he offered another boon:

body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, his mind pleased to an even greater degree by that contentment-inclined disposition, revealed through that eloquent speech —

children.text: atrāpi te munijanapratirūpe subhāṣite /
children.translated_text: "In this too, your eloquent speech, worthy of the manner of sages —

children.text: pratiprābhṛtavat prītyā prayacchāmy aparaṃ varam // AJm_7.16 //
children.translated_text: with joy, like a return-gift, I grant you yet another boon." [AJm 7.16]

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ kleśaviyogasyaiva durlabhatām asya pradarśayan varayācñāpadeśena punar apy asmai dharmaṃ deśayām āsa /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, demonstrating to him the very difficulty of freedom from defilements, under the pretext of requesting a boon, taught him the <s>Dharma</s> once again:

children.text: dadāsi me yadi varaṃ sadguṇāvāsa vāsava /
children.translated_text: "If you give me a boon, O <s>Vāsava</s> (Indra), abode of noble qualities,

children.text: vṛṇe tenedam aparaṃ devendrānavaraṃ varam // AJm_7.17 //
children.translated_text: then I choose this further boon, no less than one from the lord of the gods: [AJm 7.17]

children.text: arthād api bhraṃśam avāpnuvanti varṇaprasādād yaśasaḥ sukhāc ca /
children.translated_text: "By which beings, when overcome as if by an enemy, lose their wealth, the luster of their reputation, their fame, and their happiness —

children.text: yenābhibhūtā dviṣateva sattvāḥ sa dveṣavahnir mama dūrataḥ syāt // AJm_7.18 //
children.translated_text: may that fire of hatred be far from me." [AJm 7.18]

body.text: tac chrutvā śakro devānām adhipatir vismayavaśāt sādhv ity enaṃ sabahumānam abhipraśasya punar uvāca /
body.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, out of wonder, praised him with 'Excellent!', with great respect, and said again:

children.text: sthāne pravrajitān kīrtir anurakteva sevate /
children.translated_text: 'Justly does fame attend the renunciants, as if devoted [to them];'

children.text: tad varaṃ pratigṛhṇīṣva mad atrāpi subhāṣite // AJm_7.19 //
children.translated_text: 'therefore accept a boon from me in this matter too—well-spoken one!' [AJm 7.19]

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ kleśaprātikūlyāt kliṣṭasattvasaṃparkavigarhāṃ varasaṃpratigrahāpadeśena kurvann ity uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, on account of his aversion to the afflictions, making a censure of association with afflicted beings under the pretext of accepting a boon, spoke thus:

children.text: śṛṇuyām api naiva jātu bālaṃ na ca vīkṣeya na cainam ālapeyam /
children.translated_text: 'May I never even hear a fool, nor look upon one, nor speak to one,

children.text: na ca tena nivāsakhedaduḥkhaṃ samupeyāṃ varam ity ahaṃ vṛṇe tvām // AJm_7.20 //
children.translated_text: nor suffer the pain of the misery of dwelling with one—this is the boon I choose from you.' [AJm 7.20]

body.text: śakra uvāca /
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said:

children.text: anukampyo viśeṣeṇa satām āpadgato nanu /
children.translated_text: 'Is not one who has fallen into calamity especially deserving of compassion from the virtuous?'

children.text: āpadāṃ mūlabhūtatvād bālyaṃ cādhamam iṣyate // AJm_7.21 //
children.translated_text: 'And foolishness is considered the worst [calamity], since it is the root of all calamities.' [AJm 7.21]

children.text: karuṇāśrayabhūtasya bālasyāsya viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Of a fool, especially one who is an object of compassion—'

children.text: kṛpālur api san kasmān na darśanam apīcchasi // AJm_7.22 //
children.translated_text: 'why, even though you are compassionate, do you not wish even for the sight [of such a one]?' [AJm 7.22]

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca / agatyā mārṣa / paśyatv atrabhavān /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Out of helplessness, sir. Let your honor observe:'

children.text: kathaṃ cid api śakyeta yadi bālaś cikitsitum /
children.translated_text: 'If a fool could somehow be cured,'

children.text: taddhitodyoganiryatnaḥ kathaṃ syād iti madvidhaḥ // AJm_7.23 //
