children.translated_text: 'how could one such as I, striving earnestly for his welfare, [not wish to see him]?' [AJm 7.23]

body.text: itthaṃ caiṣa cikitsāprayogasyāpātram iti gṛhyatām /
body.translated_text: 'And consider that this one is truly unfit for the application of a cure:'

children.text: sunayavad anayaṃ nayaty ayaṃ param api cātra niyoktum icchati /
children.translated_text: 'He leads others astray like sound policy leading them along the wrong path, and wishes to employ others in the same;'

children.text: anucitavinayārjavakramo hitam api cābhihitaḥ prakupyati // AJm_7.24 //
children.translated_text: 'and when told what is beneficial, in a manner unsuited to the sequence of discipline and uprightness, he becomes angry.' [AJm 7.24]

children.text: iti paṇḍitamānamohadagdhe hitavādiṣv api roṣarūkṣabhāve /
children.translated_text: 'Thus, toward one burned by the delusion of the pride of learning, harsh in disposition even toward those who speak for his welfare,'

children.text: rabhase vinayābhiyogamāndyād vada kas tatra hitārpaṇābhyupāyaḥ // AJm_7.25 //
children.translated_text: 'rash from sluggishness in the application of discipline—tell me, what is the means of conferring benefit there?' [AJm 7.25]

children.text: ity agatyā suraśreṣṭha karuṇāpravaṇair api /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, out of helplessness, O best of gods, even by those inclined to compassion,'

children.text: bālyād adravyabhūtasya na darśanam apīṣyate // AJm_7.26 //
children.translated_text: 'not even the sight is desired of a fool, who is a hopeless case because of his foolishness.' [AJm 7.26]

body.text: tac chrutvā śakraḥ sādhu sādhv ity enam abhinandya subhāṣitaparitoṣitamatiḥ punar uvāca /
body.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Śakra</s>, praising him with 'Excellent! Excellent!', his mind gratified by the well-spoken words, said again:

children.text: na subhāṣitaratnānām arghaḥ kaś ca na vidyate /
children.translated_text: 'There is no price whatsoever for the jewels of well-spoken words;'

children.text: kusumāñjalivat prītyā dadāmy atra tu te varam // AJm_7.27 //
children.translated_text: 'but with joy, like an offering of flowers, I give you a boon here.' [AJm 7.27]

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ sarvāvasthasukhatāṃ sajjanasya pradarśayañ chakram uvāca/
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, demonstrating the happiness of the virtuous person in every condition, said to <s>Śakra</s>:

children.text: vīkṣeya dhīraṃ śṛṇuyāṃ ca dhīraṃ syān me nivāsaḥ saha tena śakra /
children.translated_text: 'May I see the steadfast, may I hear the steadfast, may my dwelling be with the steadfast, O <s>Śakra</s>;'

children.text: saṃbhāṣaṇaṃ tena sahaiva bhūyād etad varaṃ devavara prayaccha // AJm_7.28 //
children.translated_text: 'may I have conversation with the steadfast—grant this boon, O best of gods!' [AJm 7.28]

body.text: śakra uvāca / atipakṣapāta iva khalu te dhīraṃ prati / tad ucyatām /
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: 'You have an excessive partiality toward the steadfast indeed. Tell me then:'

children.text: kiṃ nu dhīras tavākārṣīd vada kāśyapa kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: 'What indeed has the steadfast one done for you? Tell the reason, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>!'

children.text: adhīra iva yenāsi dhīradarśanalālasaḥ // AJm_7.29 //
children.translated_text: 'Why is it that, as if unsteady yourself, you are longing for the sight of the steadfast?' [AJm 7.29]

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ sajjanamāhātmyam asya pradarśayann uvāca / śrūyatāṃ mārṣa yena me dhīradarśanam evābhilaṣati matiḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, demonstrating to him the greatness of the virtuous, said: 'Listen, sir, to the reason my mind desires only the sight of the steadfast:'

children.text: vrajati guṇapathena ca svayaṃ nayati parān api tena vartmanā /
children.translated_text: 'He himself walks the path of virtue and leads others too along that road;'

children.text: vacanam api na rūkṣam akṣamāṃ janayati tasya hitopasaṃhitam // AJm_7.30 //
children.translated_text: 'even his speech, which is not harsh, connected with what is beneficial, does not engender intolerance.' [AJm 7.30]

children.text: aśaṭhavinayabhūṣaṇaḥ sadā hitam iti lambhayituṃ sa śakyate /
children.translated_text: 'Adorned with genuine discipline, he can always be made to accept what is beneficial—'

children.text: iti mama guṇapakṣapātinī namati matir guṇapakṣapātini // AJm_7.31 //
children.translated_text: 'thus my mind, partial to virtue, bows to one who is partial to virtue.' [AJm 7.31]

body.text: athainaṃ śakraḥ sādhūpapannarūpam idam iti cābhinandya samabhivṛddhaprasādaḥ punar vareṇopanimantrayām āsa /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, praising him with 'This is indeed fitting for a virtuous person!', his pleasure having grown further, invited him again with a boon:

children.text: kāmaṃ saṃtoṣasātmatvāt sarvatra kṛtam eva te /
children.translated_text: 'Since, through the nature of contentment, everything is already accomplished for you everywhere;'

children.text: madanugrahabuddhyā tu grahītuṃ varam arhasi // AJm_7.32 //
children.translated_text: 'but with the thought of showing my favor, please accept a boon.' [AJm 7.32]

children.text: upakārāśayā bhaktyā śaktyā caiva samastayā /
children.translated_text: 'For the non-acceptance of affection offered with a benevolent intention, with devotion, and with all one's might,'

children.text: prayuktasyātiduḥkho hi praṇayasyāpratigrahaḥ // AJm_7.33 //
children.translated_text: 'is indeed extremely painful.' [AJm 7.33]

body.text: atha tasya parām upakartukāmatām avetya bodhisattvas tatpriyahitakāmyayā pradānānutarṣaprābalyam asmai prakāśayann uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then, perceiving his supreme desire to help, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, wishing what was dear and beneficial to him, revealing to him the overriding power of his thirst for giving, said:

children.text: tvadīyam annaṃ kṣayadoṣavarjitaṃ manaś ca ditsāparitoṣapeśalam /
children.translated_text: 'May your food, free from the fault of exhaustion, be mine; and a mind refined with the satisfaction of the desire to give;'

children.text: viśuddhaśīlābharaṇāś ca yācakā mama syur etāṃ varasaṃpadaṃ vṛṇe // AJm_7.34 //
children.translated_text: 'and may supplicants adorned with pure conduct be mine—this treasure of boons I choose.' [AJm 7.34]

body.text: śakra uvāca / subhāṣitaratnākaraḥ khalv atrabhavān / api ca /
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: 'Your honor is indeed an ocean of well-spoken jewels. Furthermore:'

children.text: yad abhiprārthitaṃ sarvaṃ tat tathaiva bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: 'All that you have prayed for shall come to be exactly so;'

children.text: dadāmi ca punas tubhyaṃ varam asmin subhāṣite // AJm_7.35 //
children.translated_text: 'and I give you yet another boon for this well-spoken [word].' [AJm 7.35]

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: varaṃ mamānugrahasaṃpadākaraṃ dadāsi cet sarvadivaukasāṃ vara /
children.translated_text: 'If you give a boon that is a mine of the treasure of your favor, O best of all celestials—'

children.text: na mābhyupeyāḥ punar ity abhijvalann imaṃ varaṃ daityanisūdanaṃ vṛṇe // AJm_7.36 //
children.translated_text: '"May you never come to me again"—blazing [with resolve], I choose this boon, O slayer of demons!' [AJm 7.36]

body.text: atha śakraḥ sāmarṣavad enam ativismayamāna uvāca / mā tāvad bhoḥ /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, as if indignant, exceedingly astonished, said: 'Wait a moment, sir!'

children.text: japavratejyāvidhinā tapaḥśramair jano 'yam anvicchati darśanaṃ mama /
children.translated_text: 'Through the rite of prayer, vows, and sacrifice, through the labors of austerity, people seek my audience;'

children.text: bhavān punar necchati kena hetunā varapraditsābhigatasya me sataḥ // AJm_7.37 //
children.translated_text: 'yet you do not wish it! For what reason—when I, present before you, wish to grant a boon?' [AJm 7.37]

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca / alaṃ te manyupraṇayena / samanuneṣyāmy aham atrabhavantaṃ devarājam / na hy asāv adākṣiṇyānuvṛttir nāpy abahumānaviceṣṭitam asamavadhānakāmyatā vā bhavataḥ / kiṃ tu

children.text: nirīkṣya te rūpam amānuṣādbhutaṃ prasannakānti jvalitaṃ ca tejasā /
children.translated_text: 'Having beheld your form, superhuman, wondrous, of serene beauty, and blazing with splendor—'

children.text: bhavet pramādas tapasīti me bhayaṃ prasādasaumyād api darśanāt tava // AJm_7.38 //
children.translated_text: 'my fear is that there might arise negligence in austerity, even from a sight so gracious and gentle as yours.' [AJm 7.38]

body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Enough of your indignation born of affection. I shall appease your honor, the king of the gods. For that [wish of mine] is not a conduct of discourtesy, nor is it an act of disrespect, nor is it a desire for inattention toward you. But—'

body.text: atha śakraḥ praṇamya pradakṣiṇīkṛtya cainaṃ tatraivāntardadhe / prabhātāyāṃ ca rajanyāṃ bodhisattvaḥ śakraprabhāvopahṛtaṃ prabhūtaṃ divyam annapānaṃ dadarśa / śakropanimantraṇāhūtāni cānekāni pratyekabuddhaśatāni vyāyatābaddhaparikarāṃś ca pariveṣaṇasajjān anekān devakumārān /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, having bowed and circumambulated him, disappeared right there. And when dawn broke, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> beheld an abundant, divine provision of food and drink brought by <s>Śakra's</s> power, and many hundreds of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary Buddhas) summoned by <s>Śakra's</s> invitation, and many divine youths with robes firmly fastened, prepared for serving.

children.text: tenānnapānavidhinā sa munir maharṣīn saṃtarpayan mudam udāratamām avāpa /
children.translated_text: That sage, nourishing the great sages with that provision of food and drink, attained the most sublime joy;

children.text: vṛttyā ca tāpasajanocitayābhireme dhyānāpramāṇaniyamena śamena caiva // AJm_7.39 //
children.translated_text: and he delighted in the manner of life befitting a community of ascetics—through <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), the <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables), self-discipline, and tranquility. [AJm 7.39]

body.text: tad evaṃ tapovanasthānām apy alaṃkāras tyāgaśauryaṃ prāg eva gṛhasthānām iti
body.translated_text: Thus, the heroism of generosity is an ornament even for forest-dwellers, how much more for householders. Therefore—

body.text: tyāgaśauryeṇālaṃkartavya evātmā satpuruṣeṇeti dānapatisaṃvarṇanāyām upaneyaṃ

children.text: lobhadveṣabālavigarhāyāṃ kalyāṇamitrasaṃparkaguṇe saṃtoṣakathāyāṃ
children.translated_text: in the censure of greed, hatred, and foolishness, in [teaching] the virtue of association with good friends, in the discourse on contentment,

children.text: tathāgatamāhātmye caivaṃ pūrvajanmasv api subhāṣitaratnātiśayākaraḥ sa bhagavān prāg evābhisaṃbuddha iti //
children.translated_text: and in [illustrating] the greatness of the <s>Tathāgata</s>: 'Even in his former births, that <s>Bhagavān</s> was an overflowing source of well-spoken jewels—how much more so when fully awakened.'

body.translated_text: one should adorn oneself with the heroism of generosity—this should be drawn as a lesson in praise of the lord of giving,

body.text: agastyajātakaṃ saptamam //
body.translated_text: The seventh [story], the <s>Jātaka</s> of <s>Agastya</s>.

children.text: 8. Maitrībalajātakam
children.translated_text: 8. The <s>Jātaka</s> of <s>Maitrībala</s> (Power of Loving-kindness)

body.text: na paraduḥkhāturāḥ svasukham avekṣante mahākāruṇikāḥ //
body.translated_text: Those of great compassion, distressed by the suffering of others, do not look to their own happiness.

body.text: tadyathānuśrūyate / bodhisattvaḥ kila svamāhātmyakāruṇyābhiprapannajagatparitrāṇādhyāśayaḥ pradānadamasaṃyamasauratyādibhir lokānugrahānukūlair guṇātiśayair abhivardhamānaḥ sarvasattvamaitramanā maitrībalo nāma rājā babhūva /
body.translated_text: As tradition relates: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, it is said, whose overriding aspiration was the protection of the world through his own greatness and compassion, growing through surpassingly excellent virtues favorable to the welfare of the world—such as giving, self-control, restraint, and gentleness—was a king named <s>Maitrībala</s> (Power of Loving-kindness), whose mind was friendly toward all beings.

children.text: duḥkhaṃ sukhaṃ vā yad abhūt prajānāṃ tasyāpi rājñas tad abhūt tathaiva /
children.translated_text: Whatever suffering or happiness befell his subjects, that likewise befell that king too;

children.text: ataḥ prajārakṣaṇadakṣiṇo 'sau śastraṃ ca śāstraṃ ca parāmamarśa // AJm_8.1 //
children.translated_text: therefore, skilled in the protection of his subjects, he attended to both arms (<s>śastra</s>) and scriptures (<s>śāstra</s>). [AJm 8.1]

children.text: narendracūḍādhṛtaśāsanasya tasya tv alaṃkāravad āsa śastram /
children.translated_text: For him, whose commands were upheld on the crowns of princes, arms were like an ornament;

children.text: vispaṣṭarūpaṃ dadṛśe ca śāstraṃ nayeṣu lokasya hitodayeṣu // AJm_8.2 //
children.translated_text: and his knowledge of scriptures was clearly visible in policies conducive to the welfare of the world. [AJm 8.2]

children.text: vinigrahapragrahayoḥ pravṛttir dharmoparodhaṃ na cakāra tasya /
children.translated_text: His exercise of punishment and reward did not obstruct <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: hitāśayatvān nayanaipuṇāc ca parīkṣakasyeva pituḥ prajāsu // AJm_8.3 //
children.translated_text: because of the benevolence of his intentions and his skill in governance—like a discerning father toward his children. [AJm 8.3]

body.text: tasyaivaṃ dharmeṇa prajāḥ pālayataḥ satyatyāgopaśamaprajñādibhiś ca parahitapariṇāmanāt saviśeṣodāttakramair bodhisaṃbhāravidhibhir abhivardhamānasya kadā cit kasmiṃś cid aparādhe yakṣāṇām adhipatinā svaviṣayāt pravrājitā ojohārāḥ pañca yakṣāḥ paravadhadakṣās tadviṣayam abhijagmuḥ / vyapagatasarvopadravatvāc ca nityapravṛttavividhotsavaṃ parayā saṃpadā samupetarūpaṃ pramuditatuṣṭapuṣṭajanam abhisamīkṣya taṃ viṣayaṃ tadviṣayanivāsināṃ puruṣāṇām ojāṃsy apahartum eṣām abhilāṣo babhūva /
body.translated_text: While he was thus protecting his subjects through <s>dharma</s>, and growing through the methods of accumulating the requisites of awakening (<s>bodhisaṃbhāra</s>)—distinguished by their surpassingly noble course, [namely] truth, generosity, tranquility, wisdom, and the rest—devoted to the transformation [of merit] for the benefit of others, once, five <s>yakṣas</s> (nature spirits) who were vitality-stealers, skilled in killing others, having been banished from their own territory by the chief of the <s>yakṣas</s> for some offense, came to his realm. And seeing that territory—adorned with constantly ongoing various festivals because all afflictions had ceased, endowed with supreme prosperity, its people joyful, content, and thriving—their desire arose to steal the vitality of the men dwelling in that territory.

children.text: te pareṇāpi yatnena saṃpravṛttāḥ svakarmaṇi /
children.translated_text: Even with the utmost effort, engaged in their own work,

children.text: naiva tadviṣayasthānāṃ hartum ojaḥ prasehire // AJm_8.4 //
children.translated_text: they were utterly unable to steal the vitality of the inhabitants of that territory. [AJm 8.4]

children.text: tasya prabhāvātiśayān nṛpasya mameti yatraiva babhūva buddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of the surpassing power of that king, wherever there arose the thought 'This is mine'—

children.text: saivāsya rakṣā paramāsa tasmād ojāṃsi hartuṃ na viṣehire te // AJm_8.5 //
children.translated_text: that very [thought] was their protection; therefore, they could not steal their vitality. [AJm 8.5]

body.text: yadā ca param api prayatnaṃ kurvanto naiva śaknuvanti sma kasya cit tadviṣayanivāsina ojo 'pahartum athaiṣāṃ parasparam avekṣyaitad abhūt / kiṃ nu khalv idaṃ mārṣāḥ /
body.translated_text: And when, even with the greatest effort, they were unable to steal the vitality of any inhabitant of that territory, then, looking at one another, they reflected: 'What indeed is this, sirs?'

children.text: asmatprabhāvapratighātayogyā vidyātapaḥsiddhimayā viśeṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Distinctions born of sacred knowledge, austerity, and accomplishment, capable of counteracting our power—'

children.text: na santi caiṣām atha cādya sarve vyarthābhidhānatvam upāgatāḥ smaḥ // AJm_8.6 //
children.translated_text: 'these people do not possess [such things]; and yet today we have all become mere bearers of empty names!' [AJm 8.6]

body.text: atha te yakṣā brāhmaṇavarṇam ātmānam abhinirmāya samanucaranto dadṛśuḥ pratyaraṇyacaram anyatamaṃ gopālakaṃ saśādvale chāyādrumamūle sopānatkaṃ saṃniṣaṇṇaṃ sapallavair vanatarukusumair viracitāṃ mālām udvahantaṃ dakṣiṇato vinyastadaṇḍaparaśum ekākinaṃ rajjuvartanavyāpṛtaṃ prakṣveḍitavilāsena gāyantam āsīnaṃ samupetya cainam ūcuḥ / bho gavāṃ saṃrakṣaṇādhikṛta / evaṃ vivikte nirjanasaṃpāte 'sminn araṇye vicarann ekākī kathaṃ na bibheṣīti // sa tān ullokyābravīt / kuto vā bhetavyam iti // yakṣā ūcuḥ / kiṃ tvayā na śrutapūrvā rakṣasāṃ piśācānāṃ vā nisargaraudrā prakṛtiḥ /
body.translated_text: Then those <s>yakṣas</s>, having magically assumed the appearance of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and wandering about, saw a certain cowherd living near the edge of the forest, seated on grassy ground at the root of a shade tree, wearing a turban, bearing a garland fashioned from the blossoms and leaves of forest trees, with his staff and axe placed to the right, alone, occupied with twisting a rope, singing with the grace of whistling, and approaching him, they said: 'Ho, guardian of cattle! Wandering alone in this wilderness, in such a desolate, uninhabited spot—how is it that you are not afraid?' He, looking up at them, replied: 'Of what indeed should one be afraid?' The <s>yakṣas</s> said: 'Have you never before heard of the naturally fierce disposition of <s>rākṣasas</s> and <s>piśācas</s>?'

children.text: sahāyamadhye 'pi hi vartamāno vidyātapaḥsvastyayanair upetaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Even one who is in the midst of companions, equipped with sacred knowledge, austerity, and protective rites—'

children.text: yebhyaḥ kathaṃ cit parimokṣam eti śauryād avajñātabhayo 'pi lokaḥ // AJm_8.7 //
children.translated_text: 'from whom the world, though brave and scornful of danger, barely manages to find some escape—' [AJm 8.7]

children.text: tebhyo nṛmedaḥpiśitāśanebhyaḥ kathaṃ bhayaṃ te 'sti na rākṣasebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'From these devourers of human fat and flesh, the <s>rākṣasas</s>—how is it you have no fear,'

children.text: viviktagambhīrabhayānakeṣu sahāyahīnasya vanāntareṣu // AJm_8.8 //
children.translated_text: 'alone, without companions, in these solitary, deep, and fearsome forest interiors?' [AJm 8.8]

body.text: ity ukte sa gopālakaḥ prahasyainān uvāca /
body.translated_text: When this was said, the cowherd laughed and said to them:

children.text: janaḥ svastyayanenāyaṃ mahatā paripālyate /
children.translated_text: 'This people is protected by a great safeguard;'

children.text: devendrair apy aśakyo 'yaṃ kiṃ punaḥ piśitāśanaiḥ // AJm_8.9 //
children.translated_text: 'even the lords of the gods cannot [overcome] them—how much less the flesh-eaters!' [AJm 8.9]

children.text: tena geha ivāraṇye rātrāv api yathā divā /
children.translated_text: 'Because of him, in the forest as if at home, at night as if in daytime,'

children.text: janānta iva caiko 'pi nirbhayo vicarāmy aham // AJm_8.10 //
children.translated_text: 'and alone as if in the midst of people—I wander without fear.' [AJm 8.10]

body.text: athainaṃ te yakṣāḥ kautūhalaprābalyāt sādaram upavatsayanta ivocuḥ / tat kathaya kathaya tāvad bhadra kīdṛśo 'yaṃ yuṣmākaṃ svastyayanaviśeṣa iti // sa tān prahasann uvāca / śrūyatāṃ yādṛśo 'smākam atyadbhutaḥ svastyayanaviśeṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then those <s>yakṣas</s>, with the intensity of their curiosity, said to him eagerly, as if pressing him for an answer: 'Then tell us, tell us, good sir—what manner of extraordinary safeguard is this of yours?' He, laughing at them, said: 'Listen to the nature of our most wondrous safeguard:'

children.text: kanakagiriśilāviśālavakṣāḥ śaradamalendumanojñavaktraśobhaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'With a chest broad as the rock-face of a golden mountain, with the charming splendor of a face [beautiful] as the autumn's spotless moon,'

children.text: kanakaparighapīnalambabāhur vṛṣabhanibhekṣaṇavikramo narendraḥ // AJm_8.11 //
children.translated_text: 'with long arms thick as golden maces, with the gait and valor of a bull—such is our king!' [AJm 8.11]

body.text: īdṛśo 'smākaṃ svastyayanaviśeṣa ity uktvā sāmarṣavismayas tān yakṣān avekṣamāṇaḥ punar uvāca / āścaryaṃ batedam /
body.translated_text: 'Such is our extraordinary safeguard'—having said this, looking upon those <s>yakṣas</s> with indignant wonder, he spoke again: 'How astonishing is this!'

children.text: evaṃ prakāśo nṛpatiprabhāvaḥ kathaṃ nu vaḥ śrotrapathaṃ na yātaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The power of the king being so manifest, how has it not reached the path of your ears?'

children.text: atyadbhutatvād athavā śruto 'pi bhavatsu vipratyayato na rūḍhaḥ // AJm_8.12 //
children.translated_text: 'Or perhaps, having been heard, because of its extraordinary nature, it has not taken root in you due to disbelief?' [AJm 8.12]

children.text: śaṅke guṇānveṣaṇaviklavo vā deśe jano 'sāv akutūhalo vā /
children.translated_text: 'I suspect that the people there are either distressed in their search for virtues, or that they are without curiosity;'

children.text: vivarjito bhāgyaparikṣayād vā kīrtyā narendrasya yato 'bhyupaitha // AJm_8.13 //
children.translated_text: Or abandoned by fortune's decline, since you have come to this king's [realm].'

body.text: tad asti vo bhāgyaśeṣaṃ yat tādṛśād deśakāntārād ihāgatāḥ stha // yakṣā ūcuḥ / bhadra kiṃkṛto 'yam asya rājñaḥ prabhāvo yad asyāmānuṣā na prasahante viṣayanivāsinaṃ janaṃ hiṃsitum iti / gopālaka uvāca / svamāhātmyādhigataḥ prabhāvo 'yam asmākaṃ mahārājasya / paśyata brāhmaṇāḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Then it is your remaining good fortune that you have arrived here from such a desolate wilderness.' The <s>Yakṣas</s> said: 'Good sir, what is the source of this king's power, that non-human beings cannot overpower the inhabitants of his territory?' The cowherd said: 'This power of our great king is self-attained through his own greatness. Behold, O <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>:'

children.text: maitrī tasya balaṃ dhvajāgraśabalaṃ tv ācāramātraṃ balaṃ nāsau vetti ruṣaṃ na cāha paruṣaṃ samyak ca gāṃ rakṣati /
children.translated_text: 'Loving-kindness is his strength; his army-banner's might is but his conduct alone. He knows not anger, nor does he speak harshly, and he protects the earth rightly.'

children.text: dharmas tasya nayo na nītinikṛtiḥ pūjārtham arthaḥ satām ity āścaryamayo 'pi durjanadhanaṃ garvaṃ ca nālambate // AJm_8.14 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Dharma</s> is his policy, not political cunning; wealth serves to honor the virtuous. Thus, though he is wonderful beyond wonder, he does not grasp at pride—the treasure of the wicked.'

body.text: evamādiguṇaśatasamudito 'yam asmākaṃ svāmī / tenāsya na prasahante viṣayanivāsinaṃ janam upadravāḥ / api ca kiyad ahaṃ vaḥ śakṣyāmi vaktum / nṛpatiguṇaśravaṇakutūhalais tu bhavadbhir nagaram eva yuktaṃ praveṣṭuṃ syāt / tatra hi bhavantaḥ svadharmānurāgād vyavasthitāryamaryādaṃ nityakṣemasubhikṣatvāt pramuditasamṛddham anuddhatodāttaveṣam abhyāgatātithijanaviśeṣavatsalaṃ nṛpatiguṇākṣiptahṛdayaṃ tatkīrtyāśrayāḥ stutīr maṅgalam iva svastyayanam iva ca praharṣād abhyasyantaṃ janaṃ dṛṣṭvā rājño guṇavistaram anumāsyante / satyāṃ ca guṇabahumānodbhāvanāyāṃ taddidṛkṣāyām avaśyaṃ tadguṇapratyakṣiṇo bhaviṣyatheti // atha te yakṣāḥ svaprabhāvapratīghātāt tasmin rājani sā marṣahṛdayā bhāvaprayuktayāpi yuktayā tayā tathyayā guṇakathayā naiva mārdavam upajagmuḥ /
body.translated_text: 'This lord of ours is endowed with hundreds of such qualities. Therefore no calamities overpower the inhabitants of his territory. And how much can I tell you? But if you are curious to hear the king's virtues, it would be fitting for you to enter the city itself. There you will see people who, from devotion to their own <s>dharma</s>, maintain established noble standards, who are joyful and prosperous from perpetual safety and abundance, whose demeanor is dignified without arrogance, who are especially affectionate to arriving guests, whose hearts are captured by the king's qualities, and who, with delight, recite praises celebrating his fame as if they were benedictions and blessings—and from this you will infer the full extent of the king's virtues. And when the esteem for his qualities has been aroused, and the desire to see him [has grown], you will surely become direct witnesses of his qualities.' Then those <s>Yakṣas</s>, resentful at heart because their own power was thwarted in that king's [realm], even by that truthful and well-reasoned account of his virtues, prompted by genuine sentiment, were not moved to softness.

children.text: prāyeṇa khalu mandānām amarṣajvalitaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Indeed, the resentment-inflamed minds of the dull are generally

children.text: yasmin vastuni tatkīrtyā tad viśeṣeṇa dahyate // AJm_8.15 //
children.translated_text: Especially scorched by the fame of that very thing [which thwarts them].

body.text: pradānapriyatāṃ tu samabhivīkṣya rājñas te yakṣās tadapakāracikīrṣavaḥ samabhigamya rājānaṃ saṃdarśanakāle bhojanam ayācanta // atha sa rājā pramuditamanās tadadhikṛtān puruṣān samādideśa / kṣipram abhirucitaṃ bhojanaṃ brāhmaṇebhyo dīyatām iti // atha te yakṣāḥ samupahṛtaṃ rājārham api bhojanaṃ haritatṛṇam iva vyāghrā naiva pratyagṛhṇan naivaṃvidhaṃ bhojanaṃ vayam aśnīma iti / tac chrutvā sa rājā samabhigamyainān abravīt / atha kīdṛśaṃ bhojanaṃ yuṣmākam upaśete / yāvat tādṛśam anviṣyatām iti // yakṣā ūcuḥ /
body.translated_text: But observing the king's love of giving, those <s>Yakṣas</s>, wishing to harm him, approached the king at the time of audience and asked for food. Then the king, his mind delighted, instructed the officials in charge: 'Quickly, let desirable food be given to the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.' But those <s>Yakṣas</s> did not accept the food that was brought, even though it was fit for a king—[rejecting it] as tigers would green grass—saying 'We do not eat food of this kind.' Hearing this, the king approached them and said: 'Then what kind of food suits you? Let such be sought.' The <s>Yakṣas</s> said:

children.text: atyaktoṣmāṇi māṃsāni narāṇāṃ rudhirāṇi ca /
children.translated_text: 'Flesh still warm, and the blood of humans—

children.text: ity annapānaṃ padmākṣa yakṣānām akṣatavrata // AJm_8.16 //
children.translated_text: This, O lotus-eyed one of inviolate vows, is the food and drink of <s>Yakṣas</s>.'

body.text: ity uktvā daṃṣṭrākarālavadanāni dīptapiṅgalakekararaudranayanāni cipiṭavirūpaghoṇāni jvaladanalakapilakeśaśmaśrūṇi sajalajaladharāndhakārākārāṇi vikṛtabhīṣaṇāni svāny eva vapūṃṣi pratyapadyanta / samavekṣya cainān sa rājā piśācāḥ khalv ime na mānuṣās tenāsmadīyam annapānaṃ nābhilaṣantīti niścayam upajagāma //
body.translated_text: Having said this, they assumed their own forms—faces terrible with protruding fangs, eyes fierce and reddish-tawny and rolling, noses flat and deformed, hair and beards tawny-brown as blazing fire, dark in appearance like rain-clouds laden with water—hideous and frightening. And seeing them, the king reached the conclusion: 'These are certainly <s>Piśācas</s> (flesh-eating demons), not humans—that is why they do not desire our food and drink.'

children.text: atha tasya narendrasya prakṛtyā karuṇātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then for that king, compassionate by nature,

children.text: bhūyasī karuṇā teṣu samabhūc chuddhacetasaḥ // AJm_8.17 //
children.translated_text: An even greater compassion arose toward them, from his pure heart.

body.text: karuṇaikatānahṛdayaś ca tān yakṣān anuśocan niyatam īdṛśam arthaṃ cintayām āsa /
body.translated_text: His heart united in compassion alone, grieving for those <s>Yakṣas</s>, he pondered this matter with certainty:

children.text: dayāvatas tāvad idam annapānaṃ sudurlabham /
children.translated_text: 'For those who are compassionate, this food and drink [of human flesh] is extremely difficult to obtain,

children.text: pratyahaṃ ca tad anveṣyaṃ kiṃ nu duḥkham ataḥ param // AJm_8.18 //
children.translated_text: And it must be sought every day—what suffering could be greater than this?'

children.text: nirdayasyāpy aśaktasya vighātaikarasaḥ śramaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For the merciless too, who are powerless, toil whose only taste is destruction; for the powerful too, through habitual harmful practice—what could be more wretched than that?'

children.text: śaktasyāpy ahitābhyāsāt kiṃ svit kaṣṭataraṃ tataḥ // AJm_8.19 //
children.translated_text: 'For these whose very sustenance depends on such food, whose minds are devoid of compassion and steeped in evil—'

children.text: evaṃvidhāhāraparāyaṇānāṃ kāruṇyaśūnyāśivamānasānām /
children.translated_text: 'These who burn their own welfare both here and hereafter—when will their sufferings ever come to an end?'

children.text: pretyeha caiṣāṃ dahatāṃ svam arthaṃ duḥkhāni yāsyanti kadā nu nāśam // AJm_8.20 //
children.translated_text: 'Then how can I now, by providing them food, even for a single day, bring about the cessation of their devotion to harming others?'

body.text: tat katham idānīm aham eṣām āhārasaṃpādanād ekāham api tāvat parahiṃsāpraṇayavighātaṃ kuryām /
body.translated_text: 'For I do not recall ever having made the faces of supplicants who came in need—

children.text: na hi smarāmy arthitayāgatānām āśāviparyāsahataprabhāṇi /
children.translated_text: Faces whose radiance was destroyed by the disappointment of their hopes—

children.text: himānilamlāpitapaṅkajānāṃ samānadainyāni mukhāni kartum // AJm_8.21 //
children.translated_text: Resemble in their wretchedness lotuses withered by frost and wind.'

body.text: bhavatu / dṛṣṭam /
body.translated_text: 'So be it! I see the way:'

children.text: svataḥ śarīrāt sthirapīvarāṇi dāsyāmi māṃsāni saśoṇitāni /
children.translated_text: 'From my own body I shall give firm, abundant flesh together with blood;

children.text: ato 'nyathā ko hi mama kramaḥ syād ity āgateṣv arthiṣu yuktarūpaḥ // AJm_8.22 //
children.translated_text: What other course would be fitting for me when supplicants have arrived?'

children.text: svayaṃmṛtānāṃ hi nirūṣmakāṇi bhavanti māṃsāni viśoṇitāni /
children.translated_text: 'For the flesh of those who have died naturally is cold and bloodless,

children.text: priyāṇi caiṣāṃ na hi tāni samyag bubhukṣayā pīḍitavigrahāṇām // AJm_8.23 //
children.translated_text: And such [flesh] is not truly pleasing to these beings whose bodies are afflicted by hunger.'

body.text: jīvato 'pi ca kuto 'ham anyasmān māṃsam ādāsye mām abhigamya caite tathaiva kṣuttarṣaparikṣāmanayanavadanā niṣphalāśāpraṇayatvād adhikataravighātāturamanasaḥ kathaṃ nāma pratiyāsyanti / tad idam atra prāptakālam /
body.translated_text: 'And even from another living being, how would I take flesh? If these were to come to me and then depart again, their faces gaunt with hunger and thirst, their minds even more distressed from the fruitlessness of their hopeful approach—how could I bear that? Therefore this is the appropriate course here:'

children.text: duṣṭavraṇasyeva sadāturasya kaḍevarasyāsya rujākarasya /
children.translated_text: 'Of this body, like a festering wound, always ailing, essence-less, and a source of pain,

children.text: karomi kāryātiśayopayogād atyartharamyaṃ pratikārakhedam // AJm_8.24 //
children.translated_text: I shall make a supremely delightful remedy through its extraordinary useful application.'

body.text: iti viniścitya sa rājā praharṣodgamāt sphītīkṛtanayanavadanaśobhaḥ svaśarīram upadarśayaṃs tān yakṣān uvāca /
body.translated_text: Having thus resolved, the king, his face and eyes made radiant by the arising of joy, displaying his own body, said to those <s>Yakṣas</s>:

children.text: amūni māṃsāni saśoṇitāni dhṛtāni lokasya hitārtham eva /
children.translated_text: 'These limbs of flesh with blood have been maintained solely for the welfare of the world;

children.text: yady ātitheyatvam upeyur adya mahodayaḥ so 'bhyudayo mama syāt // AJm_8.25 //
children.translated_text: If they were to attain the status of a guest-offering today, that would be my supreme fortune.'

body.text: atha te yakṣā jānanto 'pi rājñas tasyādhyāśayam atyadbhutatvād aśraddadhānā rājānam ūcuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then those <s>Yakṣas</s>, though knowing the king's extraordinary intention, disbelieving because of its extreme wonderfulness, said to the king:

children.text: arthinātmagate duḥkhe yācñādainyena darśite /
children.translated_text: 'When suffering has come upon one's own person, and wretchedness has been displayed through the humiliation of begging—

children.text: jñātum arhati dātaiva prāptakālam ataḥ param // AJm_8.26 //
children.translated_text: The giver himself should know what is appropriate henceforth.'

body.text: atha sa rājā 'numatam idam eṣām iti pramuditamanāḥ sirāmokṣaṇārthaṃ vaidyā ājñāpyantām iti samādideśa // atha tasya rājño 'mātyāḥ svamāṃsaśoṇitapradānavyavasāyam avetya sasaṃbhramāmarṣavyākulahṛdayā vyaktam īdṛśaṃ kaṃ cid arthaṃ snehavaśād ūcuḥ / nārhati devaḥ pradānaharṣātirabhasād anuraktānāṃ prajānāṃ hitāhitakramam anavekṣitum / na caitad aviditaṃ devasya yathā
body.translated_text: Then the king, his mind delighted thinking 'this is their consent,' ordered: 'Let physicians be summoned for the opening of the veins.' Then his ministers, realizing the king's resolve to give his own flesh and blood, with hearts troubled by alarm and indignation, out of affection spoke to him clearly about this matter: 'Your Majesty should not, in the excess of delight at giving, fail to consider the proper order of what is beneficial and harmful to his devoted subjects. Nor is it unknown to Your Majesty that—'

children.text: yad yat prajānām ahitodayāya tat tat priyaṃ mānada rākṣasānām /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever brings harm to the subjects, that is pleasing to the <s>Rākṣasas</s>, O bestower of honor;

children.text: paroparodhārjitavṛttituṣṭir evaṃsvabhāvānagha jātir eṣām // AJm_8.27 //
children.translated_text: Content with livelihood obtained by troubling others—such, O faultless one, is the very nature of their kind.'

children.text: sukheṣv asaktaś ca bibharṣi deva rājyaśriyaṃ lokahitārtham eva /
children.translated_text: 'Unattached to pleasures, you bear the glory of kingship solely for the welfare of the world, O lord;

children.text: svamāṃsadānavyavasāyam asmāt svaniścayonmārgam imaṃ vimuñca // AJm_8.28 //
children.translated_text: Therefore abandon this resolve to give your own flesh, which is a deviation from your [true] purpose.'

children.text: asaṃśayaṃ na prasahanta ete tvadvīryaguptaṃ naravīra lokam /
children.translated_text: 'Without doubt, these [demons] cannot overpower your people, who are protected by your valor;

children.text: anarthapāṇḍityahatās tathā hi nayena vāñchanty anayaṃ prajānām // AJm_8.29 //
children.translated_text: Indeed, afflicted by their skill in mischief, they seek through cunning the harm of your subjects.'

children.text: medovasādyais tridaśā makheṣu prītiṃ hutāśābhihutair vrajanti /
children.translated_text: 'The gods in sacrifices find satisfaction with offerings of fat, marrow, and the like, consecrated by fire;

children.text: satkārapūtaṃ bhavadīyam annaṃ saṃpannam eṣāṃ kila naiva rucyam // AJm_8.30 //
children.translated_text: Yet your own food, purified by honor, rich and excellent—does it not please them at all?'

body.text: kāmaṃ nāsmadvidhajanādheyabuddhayo devapādāḥ svakāryānurāgas tv ayam asmān evam upacārapathād bhraṃśayati / pañcānām amīṣām arthe sakalaṃ jagad anāthīkartavyam iti ko 'yaṃ dharmamārgo devasya / api ca / kiṃkṛteyam asmāsv evaṃ niṣpraṇayatā kena vāsmākaṃ svāmyarthe viniyojyamānāni vinigūḍhapūrvāṇi māṃsaśoṇitāni yad aparikṣīṇeṣv evāmīṣu svāni devo dātum icchatīti // atha sa rājā tān amātyān uvāca /
body.translated_text: 'We are of course not fit to instruct Your Majesty, but this attachment to our own cause makes us deviate thus from the path of propriety. What kind of path of <s>dharma</s> is it for Your Majesty to make the entire world bereft of a protector for the sake of these five? Moreover—what have we done that Your Majesty is so without affection for us? By what [right] should flesh and blood long hidden [within] be devoted to these as our master's purpose, when our [other resources] are not yet exhausted, yet Your Majesty wishes to give of his own?' Then the king said to his ministers:

children.text: saṃvidyamānaṃ nāstīti brūyād asmadvidhaḥ katham /
children.translated_text: 'How could one such as I, when [resources] exist, say "They do not exist"?

children.text: na dadāmīty asabhyaṃ vā vispaṣṭam api yācitaḥ // AJm_8.31 //
children.translated_text: Or "I will not give"—this ignoble [refusal]—even when plainly asked?'

children.text: dharmavyavasthāsu puraḥsaraḥ san svayaṃ vrajeyaṃ yadi kāpathena /
children.translated_text: 'If I, who am a leader in the institutions of <s>dharma</s>, were myself to take the wrong path,

children.text: asmadgatācārapathānugānāṃ bhaved avasthā mama kā prajānām // AJm_8.32 //
children.translated_text: What would be the condition of my subjects, who follow the path of conduct based upon mine?'

children.text: yataḥ prajā eva samīkṣamāṇaḥ sāraṃ śarīrād aham uddhariṣye /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, considering my subjects themselves, I shall extract the essence from this body;

children.text: kaś ca prabhāvo jagadarthasādhur mātsaryahāryālpahṛdo mama syāt // AJm_8.33 //
children.translated_text: And what power dedicated to the world's welfare could be overcome by the pettiness of stinginess?'

body.text: yad api cāsmatpremabahumānāvarjitaṃ praṇayaviśrambhagarbham abhidhīyate bhavadbhiḥ kiṃkṛteyam asmāsv evaṃ niṣpraṇayatā yad aparikṣīṇeṣv eva no māṃsaśoṇiteṣu svāni devo dātum icchatīty atra vo 'nuneṣyāmi / na khalu me yuṣmāsu pratihataviṣayaḥ praṇayamārgo viśrambhavirahāt pariśaṅkāgahanaduravagāho vā / kiṃ tu
body.translated_text: 'And as for what you say, prompted by loving esteem for us, with the intimacy of affectionate trust—"What have we done that Your Majesty is so without affection for us, that he wishes to give of his own when our flesh and blood are not yet exhausted?"—in this I shall reassure you. My path of affection toward you is certainly not obstructed or made impenetrable by suspicion due to lack of trust. But—'

children.text: dhane tanutvaṃ kramaśo gate vā bhāgyānuvṛttyā kṣayam āgate vā /
children.translated_text: 'When wealth has gradually diminished, or has come to exhaustion through the turns of fate,

children.text: vijṛmbhamāṇapraṇayaḥ suhṛtsu śobheta na sphītadhanaḥ kṛśeṣu // AJm_8.34 //
children.translated_text: One who displays swelling affection toward friends who have become poor would not look well if [oneself] wealthy.'

children.text: vivardhiteṣv arthijanārtham eva saṃvidyamāneṣu ca me bṛhatsu /
children.translated_text: 'When my limbs, ample and existing, were nourished and elevated with accumulated flesh precisely for the sake of supplicants,

children.text: gātreṣu māṃsopacayonnateṣu yuṣmāsv api syāt praṇayo virūpaḥ // AJm_8.35 //
children.translated_text: Affection toward you too [at the cost of not giving] would be unseemly.'

children.text: asaṃstutānām api ca kṣameya pīḍāṃ kathaṃ kaiva kathā bhavatsu /
children.translated_text: 'I would endure the suffering even of strangers—how much more so of you!

children.text: svāny eva māṃsāni yato 'smi ditsur māṃ caiva yācanta ime na yuṣmān // AJm_8.36 //
children.translated_text: Since it is my own flesh that I wish to give, and these are asking me, not you.'

body.text: tad alam asmadatisnehād dharmavighnaniḥsādhvasatayā / anucitaḥ khalv ayam atrabhavatām asmadartheṣu samudācāraḥ / mīmāṃsitavyam api ca tāvad etat syāt /

children.text: svārtham annādi ditsantaṃ kathaṃ syāt pratiṣedhayan /
children.translated_text: 'How could one who restrains another wishing to give his own food and the like

children.text: sādhuvṛttir asādhur vā prāg evaivaṃvidhaṃ vidhim // AJm_8.37 //
children.translated_text: Be of virtuous conduct—or not?—let alone in a case such as this.'

body.translated_text: 'So enough of this obstruction of <s>dharma</s> born from excessive affection for us, with no fear [of impropriety]. This conduct of yours in our affairs is truly unfitting. And consider this further:'

body.text: tad alam anenātra vo nirbandhena / nyāyopaparīkṣayā kriyatām asmatsācivyasadṛśam unmārgāvaraṇaṃ manasaḥ / anumodanānuguṇavacasaḥ khalv atrabhavantaḥ śobheran naivam adhīranayanāḥ / kutaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'So enough of this insistence here. With proper examination of justice, perform what befits your role as my ministers: the obstruction of wrong paths of the mind. You gentlemen would look well with words of approbation, not thus with agitated eyes. For:'

children.text: naikopayogasya dhanasya tāvan na pratyahaṃ yācanakā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: 'Supplicants for wealth that has [only] one use do not come every day;

children.text: evaṃvidhas tv arthijano 'dhigantuṃ na daivatārādhanayāpi śakyaḥ // AJm_8.38 //
children.translated_text: But supplicants of this kind cannot be obtained even by propitiating the gods.'

children.text: evaṃvidhe cārthijane 'bhyupete dehe vināśiny asukhāspade ca /
children.translated_text: 'When such a supplicant has arrived, and this body is perishable and not a seat of happiness,

children.text: vimarśamārgo 'py anudāttatā syān mātsaryadainyaṃ tu parā tamisrā // AJm_8.39 //
children.translated_text: Even deliberation would be a lack of generosity; but the wretchedness of miserliness would be utter darkness.'

body.text: tan na māṃ vārayitum arhanty atrabhavanta ity anunīya sa rājā svāṃ parṣadam āhūya vaidyān pañca sirāḥ svaśarīre mokṣayitvā tān yakṣān uvāca /
body.translated_text: So, having reassured his court that they should not restrain him, the king summoned his assembly, had physicians open five veins in his own body, and said to those <s>Yakṣas</s>:

children.text: dharmakarmaṇi sācivyaṃ prītiṃ ca paramāṃ mama /
children.translated_text: 'May you render assistance in this act of <s>dharma</s> and [bring me] supreme joy

children.text: bhavantaḥ kartum arhanti dehasyāsya pratigrahāt // AJm_8.40 //
children.translated_text: By accepting this body of mine.'

body.text: te tathety uktvāñjalipuṭair eva rājño raktacandanarasābhitāmraṃ rudhiraṃ pātum upacakramire /
body.translated_text: Saying 'So be it,' they began to drink the king's blood from their cupped hands—blood coppery-red like the sap of red sandalwood.

children.text: sa pīyamānakṣatajaḥ kṣitīśaḥ kṣapācarair hemavapuś cakāśe /
children.translated_text: That king of the earth, golden-bodied, as his blood was being drunk by those nocturnal beings, shone

children.text: saṃdhyānuraktair jalabhāranamraiḥ payodharair merur ivopagūḍhaḥ // AJm_8.41 //
children.translated_text: Like <s>Meru</s> embraced by rain-clouds, heavy with water and reddened by twilight.

children.text: prītiprakarṣād dhṛtisaṃpadā ca vapurguṇād eva ca tasya rājñaḥ /
children.translated_text: Through the intensity of his joy, his wealth of fortitude, and the very quality of his body,

children.text: mamlau na gātraṃ na mumūrcha cetaḥ saṃcikṣiye na kṣatajaṃ kṣarad vā // AJm_8.42 //
children.translated_text: The king's limbs did not wither, his mind did not faint, and his flowing blood did not cease.

body.text: vinītatarṣaklamās tu te yakṣāḥ paryāptam aneneti rājānam ūcuḥ //
body.translated_text: But those <s>yakṣas</s>, their thirst and weariness removed, said to the king, 'This is enough for us.'

children.text: anekaduḥkhāyatane śarīre sadā kṛtaghne 'pi narādhipasya /
children.translated_text: The king's body, though it is the abode of manifold sufferings and always ungrateful,

children.text: gate 'rthisaṃmānanasādhanatvaṃ harṣānukūlaṃ grahaṇaṃ babhūva // AJm_8.43 //
children.translated_text: Having become the means of honoring supplicants, became something he was delighted to possess.

body.text: atha sa rājā praharṣaprabodhād adhikataranayanavadanaprasādo nīlotpaladalanīlavimalapattraṃ ratnaprabhodbhāsuraruciratsaruṃ niśitaṃ nistriṃśam ādāya svamāṃsāni cchittvā cchittvā tebhyaḥ prāyacchat /
body.translated_text: Then that king, his eyes and face radiant with even greater serenity from the awakening of joy, taking up a sharp sword with an unblemished blade dark as a blue lotus petal and a lovely hilt blazing with the splendor of gems, cut his own flesh piece by piece and gave it to them.

children.text: hriyamāṇāvakāśaṃ tu dānaprītyā punaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: But his mind, its scope being repeatedly carried away by the joy of giving,

children.text: na prasehe manas tasya cchedaduḥkhaṃ vigāhitum // AJm_8.44 //
children.translated_text: Could not bring itself to immerse in the pain of cutting.

children.text: ākṛṣyamāṇaṃ śitaśastrapātaiḥ prītyā punar dūram apāsyamānam /
children.translated_text: Though drawn [toward him] by the strokes of the sharp weapon, the pain was cast far away again by joy—

children.text: khedālasatvād iva tasya duḥkhaṃ manaḥsamutsarpaṇamandam āsīt // AJm_8.45 //
children.translated_text: His suffering was slow to rise into his mind, as if from the torpor of exhaustion.

children.text: sa prītimān eva niśācarāṃs tān saṃtarpayan svaiḥ piśitais tathāsa /
children.translated_text: He, still full of joy, satisfied those night-wanderers (<s>yakṣas</s>) with his own flesh in such a manner

children.text: krūrāṇi teṣām api mānasāni yenāsur āviṣkṛtamārdavāni // AJm_8.46 //
children.translated_text: That even their cruel minds manifested tenderness.

children.text: dharmapriyatvāt karuṇāvaśād vā tyajan parārthe priyam ātmadeham /
children.translated_text: From love of <s>Dharma</s> or under the sway of compassion, one who gives up his dear body for others' sake

children.text: dveṣāgnidagdhāny api mānasāni prasādasāvarṇyanavāni kuryāt // AJm_8.47 //
children.translated_text: Could render even minds burnt by the fire of hatred new with the hue of serenity.

body.text: atha te yakṣās taṃ rājānaṃ svamāṃsotkartanaparaṃ tathaivāskhalitavadanaprasādam avikampyamānaṃ māṃsacchedavedanābhir abhivīkṣya paraṃ prasādaṃ vismayaṃ copajagmuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then those <s>yakṣas</s>, beholding the king devoted to cutting his own flesh, with his facial serenity still unfaltering, unshaken by the pain of flesh being cut, attained the highest serenity and wonder.

children.text: āścaryam adbhutam aho bata kiṃ svid etat satyaṃ na veti samudīrṇavicāraharṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'A wonder! A marvel! Ah, what is this? Is it real or not?'—thus filled with the joy of excited deliberation,

children.text: rājany amarṣam upamṛdya manaḥprasādaṃ tatsaṃstutipraṇatibhiḥ prathayāṃ babhūvuḥ // AJm_8.48 //
children.translated_text: Suppressing their hostility toward the king, they spread abroad mental serenity through praises and prostrations to him.

body.text: alam alaṃ deva / viramyatāṃ svaśarīrapīḍāprasaṅgāt / saṃtarpitāḥ smas tavānayātyadbhutayā yācanakajanamanoharayā pratipattyeti sasaṃbhramāḥ sapraṇāmaṃ vinivārya rājānaṃ prasādāśrupariṣiktavadanāḥ sabahumānam udīkṣamāṇāḥ punar ūcuḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Enough, enough, O lord! Desist from this matter of tormenting your own body! We are satisfied by this extraordinary conduct of yours, which captivates the hearts of supplicants.' Thus, with agitation, bowing and restraining the king, their faces bathed with tears of devotion, gazing upon him with deep reverence, they said again:

children.text: sthāne bhaktivaśena gacchati janas tvatkīrtivācālatāṃ sthāne śrīḥ paribhūya paṅkajavanaṃ tvatsaṃśrayaślāghinī /
children.translated_text: 'Rightly do people, overcome by devotion, become eloquent in [proclaiming] your fame; rightly does <s>Lakṣmī</s>, scorning the lotus groves, boast of her abode in you.

children.text: vyaktaṃ śakrasanāthatām api gatā tvadvīryaguptām imāṃ dyauḥ paśyaty uditaspṛhā vasumatīṃ no ced aho vañcyate // AJm_8.49 //
children.translated_text: Clearly, heaven, having attained equality even with <s>Śakra</s>'s realm, gazes with arisen longing upon this earth, guarded by your valor—otherwise, alas, it is deceived!'

body.text: kiṃ bahunā / evaṃvidhajanābhyupapannaḥ sabhāgyaḥ khalu manuṣyalokaḥ / yuṣmadāyāsābhyanumodanāt tu vayam atra dagdhāḥ / bhavadvidhajanāpāśrayāc chakya itthaṃgatair apy ātmā samuddhartum iti svaduṣkṛtapratīkārāśayā pṛcchāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'What more can be said? The human world is fortunate indeed, being graced by beings like you. But from our approval of your exertion, we are burned here. From taking refuge in beings like you, even those who have fallen to such states can uplift themselves'—with the intention of making amends for their own misdeeds, they asked:

children.text: anādṛtya sukhaprāptām anuraktāṃ nṛpaśriyam /
children.translated_text: 'Disregarding royal splendor—easily won and devoted [to you]—

children.text: kiṃ tad atyadbhutaṃ sthānaṃ pathānena yad icchasi // AJm_8.50 //
children.translated_text: What is that supremely wondrous station that you seek by this path?'

children.text: sarvakṣitipatitvaṃ nu dhaneśatvam athendratām /
children.translated_text: 'Do you desire universal sovereignty, the lordship of wealth, the status of <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: brahmabhūyaṃ vimokṣaṃ vā tapasānena kāṅkṣasi // AJm_8.51 //
children.translated_text: Union with <s>Brahman</s>, or liberation—through this austerity?'

children.text: asya hi vyavasāyasya na dūrataram īpsitam /
children.translated_text: 'For the desired fruit of this effort cannot be far away.

children.text: śrotavyaṃ cet tad asmābhir vaktum arhati no bhavān // AJm_8.52 //
children.translated_text: If it may be heard by us, you should deign to tell us.'

body.text: rājovāca / śrūyatāṃ yadartho 'yaṃ mamābhyudyamaḥ /
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Hear then the purpose of this my endeavor:'

children.text: prayatnalabhyā yad ayatnanāśinī na tṛptisaukhyāya kutaḥ praśāntaye /
children.translated_text: 'Since worldly prosperity is won with effort yet perishes without effort, brings not the happiness of contentment, much less peace,

children.text: bhavāśrayā saṃpad ato na kāmaye surendralakṣmīm api kiṃ batetarām // AJm_8.53 //
children.translated_text: And depends on [continued] existence—therefore I do not desire even the splendor of <s>Surendra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), let alone anything lesser.'

children.text: na cātmaduḥkhakṣayamātrakeṇa me prayāti saṃtoṣapathena mānasam /
children.translated_text: 'Nor does my mind travel the path of contentment merely from the cessation of my own suffering,

children.text: amūn anāthān abhivīkṣya dehinaḥ prasaktatīvravyasanaśramāturān // AJm_8.54 //
children.translated_text: When I behold those helpless embodied beings, afflicted with constant, intense misery and exhaustion.'

children.text: anena puṇyena tu sarvadarśitām avāpya nirjitya ca doṣavidviṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'But through this merit, having attained omniscience and conquered the enemies that are moral faults,

children.text: jarārujāmṛtyumahormisaṃkulāt samuddhareyaṃ bhavasāgarāj jagat // AJm_8.55 //
children.translated_text: May I rescue the world from the ocean of existence, turbulent with the great waves of old age, disease, and death.'

body.text: atha te yakṣāḥ prasādasaṃhṛṣitatanūruhāḥ praṇamya rājānam ūcuḥ / upapannarūpam evaṃvidhasya vyavasāyātiśayasyedaṃ karma / tan na dūre bhavadvidhānām abhiprāyasaṃpad iti niścitamanaso vijñāpayām āsuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then those <s>yakṣas</s>, their body-hair bristling with devotion, having bowed to the king, said: 'This deed is fitting for such an extraordinary resolve. Therefore the fulfillment of intention is not far off for beings like you.' Thus, with minds now certain, they humbly declared:

children.text: kāmaṃ lokahitāyaiva tava sarvo 'yam udyamaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Assuredly, all this your effort is for the welfare of the world alone.

children.text: svahitātyādaras tv eṣa smartum arhasi nas tadā // AJm_8.56 //
children.translated_text: But this is excessive disregard for your own well-being—please remember us then.'

children.text: ajñānāc ca yad asmābhir evam āyāsito bhavān /
children.translated_text: 'And that we, out of ignorance, not seeing even our own good,

children.text: svam apy artham apaśyadbhir mṛṣyatām eva tac ca naḥ // AJm_8.57 //
children.translated_text: Have thus troubled you—please forgive us that as well.'

children.text: ājñām api ca tāvan nas tvam anugrahapaddhatim /
children.translated_text: 'And please deign to give us, with confidence as to your own ministers,

children.text: sacivānām iva sveṣāṃ viśrabdhaṃ dātum arhasi // AJm_8.58 //
children.translated_text: A command that may become a path of grace [for us].'

body.text: atha sa rājā prasādamṛdūkṛtahṛdayān matvainān uvāca / upakāraḥ khalv ayaṃ nāyāso mamety alam atrākṣamāśaṅkayā / api ca /
body.translated_text: Then that king, perceiving that their hearts had been softened by devotion, said to them: 'This was indeed a service to me, not a trouble—enough of your suspicion of displeasure. Moreover:'

children.text: evaṃvidhe dharmapathe sahāyān kiṃ vismariṣyāmy adhigamya bodhim /
children.translated_text: 'How could I forget companions on such a path of <s>Dharma</s> upon attaining awakening (<s>bodhi</s>)?

children.text: yuṣmākam eva prathamaṃ kariṣye vimokṣadharmāmṛtasaṃvibhāgam // AJm_8.59 //
children.translated_text: To you first I shall distribute the nectar of the <s>Dharma</s> of liberation.'

children.text: asmatpriyaṃ cābhisamīkṣamāṇair hiṃsā bhavadbhir viṣavad vivarjyā /
children.translated_text: 'And by you, looking to what pleases me, violence should be shunned like poison,

children.text: lobhaḥ paradravyaparigraheṣu vāg garhitā madyamayaś ca pāpmā // AJm_8.60 //
children.translated_text: As should greed for others' possessions, blameworthy speech, and the sin of intoxication.'

body.text: atha te yakṣās tathety asmai pratiśrutya praṇamya pradakṣiṇīkṛtya cainaṃ tatraivāntardadhire / svamāṃsaśoṇitapradānaniścayasamakālam eva tu tasya mahāsattvasya
body.translated_text: Then those <s>yakṣas</s>, having promised him 'So be it,' having bowed and circumambulated him, vanished right there. But at the very moment of that great being's resolve to give his own flesh and blood—

children.text: vikampamānā bahudhā vasuṃdharā vighūrṇayām āsa suvarṇaparvatam /
children.translated_text: The earth, trembling in many ways, shook the golden mountain (<s>Sumeru</s>);

children.text: prasasvanur dundubhayaś ca tadgatā drumāś ca puṣpaṃ sasṛjur vikampanāt // AJm_8.61 //
children.translated_text: Divine drums sounded there, and trees released flowers from the shaking.

children.text: tad abhravad vyomani māruteritaṃ patatriseneva vitānavat kva cit /
children.translated_text: That [flower-rain], driven by the wind in the sky like a cloud, in some places spread like a canopy, like an army of birds,

children.text: visṛtya mālā grathiteva kutra cit samaṃ samantān nṛpater vyakīryata // AJm_8.62 //
children.translated_text: Scattering loose like a garland in others, strung together in others—it was strewn evenly all around upon the king.

children.text: nivārayiṣyann iva medinīpatiṃ samuddhatāvegatayā mahārṇavaḥ /
children.translated_text: The great ocean, as if trying to restrain the lord of the earth, with swelling velocity,

children.text: jalaiḥ prakṛtyabhyadhikakramasvanaiḥ prayāṇasaujaskavapur vyarocata // AJm_8.63 //
children.translated_text: Shone with its mass of waters surging with a noise exceeding their natural rhythm, as though possessed of the vigor of travel.

children.text: kim etad ity āgatasaṃbhramas tataḥ surādhipas tasya vicintya kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: 'What is this?'—thus alarmed, the lord of the gods (<s>Śakra</s>), having reflected on the cause,

children.text: nṛpātyayāśaṅkitatūrṇam āyayau nṛpālayaṃ śokabhayākulākulam // AJm_8.64 //
children.translated_text: Came swiftly to the royal palace, agitated with the confusion of grief and fear, suspecting the king's demise.

children.text: tathāgatasyāpi tu tasya bhūpater mukhaprasādāt saviśeṣavismayaḥ /
children.translated_text: But finding that king still present, with particular wonder at his facial serenity,

children.text: upetya tatkarma manojñayā girā prasādasaṃharṣavaśena tuṣṭuve // AJm_8.65 //
children.translated_text: He approached and, overcome by the joy of devotion, praised that deed with charming words.

children.text: aho prakarṣo bata sajjanasthiter aho guṇābhyāsavidher udāttatā /
children.translated_text: 'Ah, the excellence of the conduct of the virtuous! Ah, the sublimity of the practice of cultivating virtues!

children.text: aho parānugrahapeśalā matis tvadarpaṇān nāthavatī bata kṣitiḥ // AJm_8.66 //
children.translated_text: Ah, the mind skilled in benefiting others! Having you as her mirror, the earth indeed has a protector!'

body.text: ity abhipraśasyainaṃ śakro devendraḥ sadyaḥkṣatarohaṇasamarthair divyamānuṣyakair auṣadhaviśeṣair nirvedanaṃ yathāpaurāṇaṃ śarīraṃ kṛtvā dākṣiṇyavinayopacāramadhuraṃ pratipūjitas tena rājñā svam āvāsaṃ pratijagāma //
body.translated_text: Having thus praised him, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, using special medicines—both divine and human—capable of instant wound-healing, restored his body to its former state without pain. Then, having been honored in return by that king with courtesies sweet with graciousness and good manners, he returned to his own abode.

body.text:
tad evaṃ paraduḥkhāturā nātmasukham avekṣante mahākāruṇikā iti
ko nāma dhanamātrake 'py avekṣāṃ notsraṣṭum arhatīti dāyakajanasamuttejanāyāṃ vācyaṃ karuṇāvarṇe 'pi tathāgatamāhātmye satkṛtya dharmaśravaṇe ca / yac coktaṃ bhagavatā bahukarāḥ khalv ete pañcakā bhikṣava iti syād etad abhisaṃdhāya / tena hi samayena te pañca yakṣā babhūvuḥ / teṣāṃ bhagavatā yathāpratijñātam eva prathamaṃ dharmāmṛtasaṃvibhāgaḥ kṛta iti //
body.translated_text: Thus, those of great compassion, afflicted by the suffering of others, do not regard their own comfort—thus, who would not be ready to relinquish attachment even to mere wealth? This should be said when encouraging donors, when describing compassion, when [describing] the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s greatness, and when [encouraging] hearing the <s>Dharma</s> with reverence. And as the Blessed One said, 'These five are indeed of great service, O monks'—this might have been said with reference to this [story]. For at that time, those five <s>yakṣas</s> existed. To them, as promised, [the <s>Buddha</s>] first distributed the nectar of the <s>Dharma</s> of liberation.

body.text: maitrībalajātakam aṣṭamam //
body.translated_text: The <s>Maitrībala-jātaka</s> (Story of the Power of Loving-kindness) is the eighth.

children.text: 9. Viśvaṃtarajātakam
children.translated_text: 9. The <s>Viśvaṃtara-jātaka</s> (Story of <s>Viśvaṃtara</s>)

body.text: na bodhisattvacaritaṃ sukham anumoditum apy alpasattvaiḥ prāg evācaritum //
body.translated_text: The conduct of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> is not easy even to appreciate for those of little spirit, let alone to practice.

body.text: tadyathānuśrūyate / sātmībhūtendriyajayaḥ parākramanayavinayasaṃpadā samadhigatavijayaśrīr vṛddhopāsananiyamāt trayyānvīkṣikyor upalabdhārthatattvaḥ svadharmakarmānuraktābhir anudvignasukhocitābhir anuraktābhiḥ prakṛtibhiḥ prakāśyamānadaṇḍanītiśobhaḥ samyakpravṛttavārttāvidhiḥ saṃjayo nāma śibīnāṃ rājā babhūva /
body.translated_text: Thus it is heard in tradition: Having made mastery over the senses his very nature, having attained the glory of victory through the excellence of his valor, statecraft, and good conduct, having understood the truth of the two [sciences of] the three <s>Vedas</s> and logic through the discipline of attending upon elders, his splendor of governance made manifest by devoted subjects content in their duty-bound happiness and free from anxiety—<s>Saṃjaya</s> by name became king of the <s>Śibis</s>.

children.text: guṇodayair yasya nibaddhabhāvā kulāṅganevāsa narādhipaśrīḥ /
children.translated_text: Royal fortune, its devotion bound to him by the arising of his virtues, was like a woman of noble family—

children.text: atarkaṇīyānyamahīpatīnāṃ siṃhābhigupteva guhā mṛgāṇām // AJm_9.1 //
children.translated_text: Unimaginable for other kings, like a cave guarded by a lion for [lesser] animals.

children.text: tapaḥsu vidyāsu kalāsu caiva kṛtaśramā yasya sado 'bhyupetāḥ /
children.translated_text: His counselors, who had exerted themselves in austerities, learning, and the arts, when they came [to his court],

children.text: viśeṣayuktaṃ bahumānam īyuḥ pūjābhir āviṣkriyamāṇasārāḥ // AJm_9.2 //
children.translated_text: Were shown extraordinary honor, their worth revealed through [his] acts of worship.

body.text: tasya

children.text: rājño
children.translated_text: king,

children.text: rājyapratipattyanantaraḥ prathitaguṇagaṇanirantaro viśvaṃtaro nāma putro yuvarājo babhūva / ayam eva sa bhagavāṃs
children.translated_text: immediately after his accession, a son was born as crown prince named <s>Viśvaṃtara</s>, in whom hosts of renowned virtues were unbroken. This was none other than the Blessed

children.text: chākyamunis
children.translated_text: <s>Śākyamuni</s>

children.text: tena samayena /
children.translated_text: at that time.

body.translated_text: Of that

children.text: yuvāpi vṛddhopaśamābhirāmas tejasvy api kṣāntisukhasvabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Though young, he delighted in the tranquility of the elderly; though brilliant, his nature was the bliss of forbearance;

children.text: vidvān api jñānamadānabhijñaḥ śriyā samṛddho 'py avalepaśūnyaḥ // AJm_9.3 //
children.translated_text: Though learned, he was unacquainted with the pride of knowledge; though prosperous in fortune, he was devoid of arrogance.

children.text: dṛṣṭaprayāmāsu ca dikṣu tasya vyāpte ca lokatritaye yaśobhiḥ /
children.translated_text: When the directions were seen to be pervaded [by his fame], and the three worlds were filled with his glories,

children.text: babhūva naivānyayaśolavānāṃ prasartum utsāha ivāvakāśaḥ // AJm_9.4 //
children.translated_text: There was simply no opportunity—nor, it seemed, even the enthusiasm—for the fames of others to spread.

children.text: amṛṣyamāṇaḥ sa jagadgatānāṃ duḥkhodayānāṃ prabhutāvalepam /
children.translated_text: Unable to tolerate the arrogant dominion of the sufferings that beset the world,

children.text: dāneṣuvarṣī karuṇorucāpas tair yuddhasaṃrambham ivājagāma // AJm_9.5 //
children.translated_text: Raining arrow-showers of generosity, with the bow of the splendor of compassion, he entered, as it were, into the frenzy of battle with them.

body.text: sa pratyaham abhigatam arthijanam abhilaṣitādhikair akliṣṭair arthavisargaiḥ priyavacanopacāramanoharair atīva prahlādayām āsa / parvadivaseṣu ca poṣadhaniyamapraśamavibhūṣaṇaḥ śiraḥsnātaḥ śuklakṣaumavāsā himagiriśikharasaṃnikāśaṃ madalekhābhyalaṃkṛtamukhaṃ lakṣaṇavinayajavasattvasaṃpannaṃ gandhahastinaṃ samājñātam aupavāhyaṃ dviradavaram abhiruhya samantato nagarasyābhiniviṣṭāny arthijananipānabhūtāni svāni sattrāgārāṇi pratyavekṣate sma / tathā ca prītiviśeṣam adhijagāma /
body.translated_text: He daily delighted the petitioners who came to him with gifts exceeding their desires, effortless, and charming with the grace of sweet words. On festival days, adorned with the observance of fasting vows and tranquility, bathed, wearing white linen, he would mount his supreme elephant—called <s>Samājñāta</s>, his foremost royal mount—magnificent as a peak of the snowy mountain, its face adorned with rut-marks, endowed with excellent marks, discipline, swiftness, and strength, and inspect from all sides around the city his own charitable establishments, which served as drinking-places for petitioners. And thus he attained a special degree of joy.

children.text: na hi tāṃ kurute prītiṃ vibhūtir bhavanāśritā /
children.translated_text: For wealth stationed in the treasury does not produce that joy

children.text: saṃkrāmyamāṇārthijane saiva dānapriyasya yām // AJm_9.6 //
children.translated_text: Which the very same [wealth], when being transferred to petitioners, produces for one who loves giving.

body.text: atha kadā cit tasyaivaṃvidhaṃ dānaprasaṅgaṃ pramuditahṛdayair arthibhiḥ samantato vikīryamāṇam upalabhyānyatamo bhūmyanantaras tasya rājā śakyo 'yam atisaṃdhātuṃ dānānurāgavaśagatvād iti pratarkya dviradavarāpaharaṇārthaṃ brāhmaṇāṃs tatra praṇidadhe // atha te brāhmaṇā viśvaṃtarasya svāni sattrāgārāṇi pratyavekṣamāṇasya pramodād adhikataranayanavadanaśobhasya jayāśīrvādamukharāḥ samucchritābhiprasāritadakṣiṇāgrapāṇayaḥ purastāt samatiṣṭhanta / sa taṃ vinigṛhya dviradavaram upacārapuraḥsaram abhigamanaprayojanam enān paryapṛcchad ājñāpyatāṃ kenārtha iti // brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then once, a neighboring king, observing this kind of generosity of his being proclaimed all around by delighted petitioners, thinking 'He can be outwitted because of his slavish devotion to giving,' dispatched <s>brāhmaṇas</s> there to steal his foremost elephant. Then those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> stood before <s>Viśvaṃtara</s> as he was inspecting his charitable establishments, his eyes and face shining with even greater beauty from delight, their raised right hands extended forward, their mouths full of victory-blessings. He, reining in his foremost elephant, preceded by courteous attentions, asked them the purpose of their visit: 'Give your command—what do you need?' The <s>brāhmaṇas</s> said:

children.text: amuṣya tava nāgasya gatilīlāvilambinaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Drawn by the virtues of this your elephant, graceful in the play of his gait,

children.text: guṇair arthitvam āyātā dānaśauryāc ca te vayam // AJm_9.7 //
children.translated_text: And by your valor in giving, we have come as petitioners.'

children.text: kailāsaśikharābhasya pradānād asya dantinaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'By giving away this tusker, magnificent as a peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>,

children.text: kuruṣva tāval lokānāṃ vismayaikarasaṃ manaḥ // AJm_9.8 //
children.translated_text: First make the minds of the world saturated with the single <s>rasa</s> of wonder!'

body.text: ity ukte bodhisattvaḥ prītyā samāpūryamāṇahṛdayaś cintām āpede / cirasya khalūdārapraṇayasumukham arthijanaṃ paśyāmi / kaḥ punar artha evaṃvidhena dviradapatinaiṣāṃ brāhmaṇānām / vyaktam ayaṃ lobherṣyādoṣaparyākulamanasaḥ kasyāpi rājñaḥ kārpaṇyaprayogaḥ /
body.translated_text: When this was said, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, his heart being filled with joy, began to think: 'At last I see supplicants approaching with noble affection! What use could these <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> have for such a lord of elephants? Clearly this is the sending by some king whose mind is troubled by the faults of greed and envy, through the device of miserliness —'

children.text: āśāvighātadīnatvaṃ tan mā bhūd asya bhūpateḥ /
children.translated_text: "Let there not be for this king the wretchedness of disappointed hope,

children.text: anādṛtya yaśodharmau yo 'smaddhita ivodyataḥ // AJm_9.9 //
children.translated_text: who, disregarding fame and <s>Dharma</s>, has set out as if for our benefit." [AJm 9.9]

body.text: iti viniścitya sa mahātmā tvaritam avatīrya dviradavarāt pratigṛhyatām iti samudyatakāñcanabhṛṅgāras teṣāṃ purato 'vatasthe //
body.translated_text: Having so decided, that great soul quickly descended from the excellent elephant and, raising a golden water-vessel, stood before them saying 'Accept this!'

children.text: tataḥ sa vidvān api rājaśāstram arthānuvṛttyā gatadharmamārgam /
children.translated_text: Then he, though versed in the science of kingship, with its path of <s>Dharma</s> abandoned through the pursuit of gain,

children.text: dharmānurāgeṇa dadau gajendraṃ nītivyalīkena na saṃcakampe // AJm_9.10 //
children.translated_text: gave the lord of elephants out of devotion to <s>Dharma</s>, and did not tremble at the falsification of statecraft. [AJm 9.10]

children.text: taṃ hemajālarucirābharaṇaṃ gajendraṃ vidyutpinaddham iva śāradam abhrarāśim /
children.translated_text: That lord of elephants, beautiful with ornaments of golden netting, like an autumn mass of clouds wreathed with lightning —

children.text: dattvā parāṃ mudam avāpa narendrasūnuḥ saṃcukṣubhe tu nagaraṃ nayapakṣapātāt // AJm_9.11 //
children.translated_text: having given him, the king's son attained supreme joy; but the city was agitated, through its attachment to policy. [AJm 9.11]

body.text: atha dviradapatipradānaśravaṇāt samudīrṇakrodhasaṃrambhāḥ śibayo brāhmaṇavṛddhā mantriṇo yodhāḥ pauramukhyāś ca kolāhalaṃ samupajanayantaḥ saṃjayaṃ rājānam abhigamya sasaṃbhramāmarṣasaṃrambhāt pariśithilopacārayantraṇam ūcuḥ / kim iyaṃ deva rājyaśrīr vilupyamānaivam apy upekṣyate / nārhati devaḥ svarājyopaplavam evam abhivardhamānaṃ marṣayitum / kim etad iti ca sāvegam uktā rājñā punar enam ūcuḥ / kasmād devo na jānīte /
body.translated_text: Then, upon hearing of the gift of the lord of elephants, the <s>Śibis</s> — elderly <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, ministers, warriors, and leading citizens — their anger inflamed with fury, raising an uproar, approached King <s>Saṃjaya</s> and, from their haste born of agitation and indignation, with only loosely restrained courtesy, said: 'What is this, Your Majesty — is the royal fortune —'

children.text: niṣevya mattabhramaropagītaṃ yasyānanaṃ dānasugandhi vāyuḥ /
children.translated_text: "He whose face the wind serves, fragrant with the scent of giving, accompanied by the humming of the intoxicated bees —

children.text: madāvalepaṃ paravāraṇānām āyāsaduḥkhena vinā pramārṣṭi // AJm_9.12 //
children.translated_text: wipes away the pride of rival elephants without the suffering of exertion. [AJm 9.12]

children.text: yattejasākrāntabalaprabhāvāḥ saṃsuptadarpā iva vidviṣas te /
children.translated_text: "Your enemies, whose strength and power are overcome by its might, their pride put to sleep as it were —

children.text: viśvaṃtareṇaiṣa gajaḥ sa datto rūpī jayas te hriyate 'nyadeśam // AJm_9.13 //
children.translated_text: this elephant has been given away by <s>Viśvaṃtara</s>! Your victory incarnate is being carried to another land! [AJm 9.13]

children.text: gāvaḥ suvarṇaṃ vasanāni bhojyam iti dvijebhyo nṛpa deyarūpam /
children.translated_text: "Cattle, gold, garments, and food — these, O king, are the proper gifts for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>;

children.text: yasmiñ jayaśrīr niyatā dvipendre deyaḥ sa nāmety atidānaśauryam // AJm_9.14 //
children.translated_text: but to say that the lord of elephants, in whom victory is assured, should be given — that is excessive valor in giving! [AJm 9.14]

children.text: nayotpathenainam iti vrajantaṃ kathaṃ samanveṣyati rājalakṣmīḥ /
children.translated_text: "How will royal fortune follow one who walks this deviant path of policy?

children.text: nopekṣaṇaṃ deva tavātra yuktaṃ purāyam ānandayati dviṣas te // AJm_9.15 //
children.translated_text: Indifference is not fitting for you here, O lord, before this [act] delights your enemies." [AJm 9.15]

body.text: tac chrutvā sa rājā putrapriyatvāt kiṃ cit tān eva praty aprītamanāḥ kāryānurodhāt sāvegavad evam ity uktvā samanuneṣyañ chibīn uvāca / jāne dānaprasaṅgavyasanitāṃ nītikramānapekṣāṃ viśvaṃtarasya na caiṣa kramo rājyadhuri saṃniyuktasya / dattaṃ tv anena svaṃ hastinaṃ vāntakalpaṃ kaḥ pratyāhariṣyati / api tu tathāham enaṃ kariṣye yathā dāne mātrāṃ jñāsyati / tad alam atra vaḥ saṃrambheṇeti // śibaya ūcuḥ / na khalu mahārāja paribhāṣaṇāmātrasādhyo 'sminn arthe viśvaṃtara iti // saṃjaya uvāca / atha kim anyad atra mayā śakyaṃ kartum /
body.translated_text: Hearing this, the king, somewhat displeased with them on account of his love for his son, yet driven by the demands of the situation, hastily said 'So be it' and, intending to conciliate the <s>Śibis</s>, said: 'I know <s>Viśvaṃtara</s>'s addiction to the vice of giving, heedless of the norms of policy, and this is not the conduct of one yoked to the burden of kingship. But what has been given —'

children.text: doṣapravṛtter vimukhasya yasya guṇaprasaṅgā vyasanīkriyante /
children.translated_text: "For one who is averse to the course of evil, whose attachment to virtue is treated as vice —

children.text: bandho vadho vātmasutasya tasya kiṃ niṣkrayaḥ syād dviradasya tasya // AJm_9.16 //
children.translated_text: would imprisonment or execution of one's own son be a fitting price for that elephant?" [AJm 9.16]

body.text: tad alam atra vaḥ saṃrambheṇa / nivārayiṣyāmy aham ato viśvaṃtaram iti // atha śibayaḥ samudīrṇamanyavo rājānam ūcuḥ /
body.translated_text: "So enough of your fury in this matter. I shall restrain <s>Viśvaṃtara</s> from this." Then the <s>Śibis</s>, their anger further inflamed, said to the king:

children.text: ko vā vadhaṃ bandhanatāḍanaṃ vā sutasya te rocayate narendra /
children.translated_text: "Who, O lord of men, would approve of the execution, imprisonment, or beating of your son?

children.text: dharmātmakas tv eṣa na rājyabhārakṣobhasya soḍhā karuṇātmakatvāt // AJm_9.17 //
children.translated_text: But this righteous-souled one, because of his compassionate nature, is not fit to bear the burdens of kingship. [AJm 9.17]

children.text: siṃhāsanaṃ tejasi labdhaśabdās trivargasevānipuṇā bhajante /
children.translated_text: "The lion-throne is ascended by those who have gained renown through might, skilled in attending to the three aims of life;

children.text: dharmātirāgān nayanirvyapekṣas tapovanādhyāsanayogya eṣaḥ // AJm_9.18 //
children.translated_text: this one, through excessive devotion to <s>Dharma</s>, heedless of policy, is fit to dwell in a hermitage. [AJm 9.18]

children.text: phalanti kāmaṃ vasudhādhipānāṃ durnītidoṣās tadapāśriteṣu /
children.translated_text: "The faults of bad policy by kings indeed bear fruit upon their dependents;

children.text: sahyās ta eṣāṃ tu tathāpi dṛṣṭā mūloparodhān na tu pārthivānām // AJm_9.19 //
children.translated_text: those are tolerable, as one can see; but those of kings themselves, who would destroy the root, are not. [AJm 9.19]

children.text: kim atra vā bahv abhidhāya niścayas tv ayaṃ śibīnāṃ tvadabhūtyamarṣiṇām /
children.translated_text: "Or why say more? This is the resolve of the <s>Śibis</s>, who cannot endure your family's ruin:

children.text: prayātu vaṅkaṃ tapaso 'bhivṛddhaye nṛpātmajaḥ siddhaniṣevitaṃ girim // AJm_9.20 //
children.translated_text: let the prince depart to Mount <s>Vaṅka</s>, frequented by accomplished sages, for the increase of his austerity." [AJm 9.20]

body.text: atha sa rājā snehapraṇayaviśrambhavaśād anayāpāyadarśinā hitodyatena tena janena pariniṣṭhuram ity abhidhīyamānaḥ prakṛtikopād vrīḍāvanatavadanaḥ putraviyogacintāparigatahṛdayaḥ sāyāsam abhiniśvasya śibīn uvāca / yady eṣa bhavatāṃ nirbandhas tad ekam api tāvad ahorātram asya mṛṣyatām / prabhātāyāṃ rajanyām abhipretaṃ vo 'nuṣṭhātā viśvaṃtara iti / evam astv iti ca pratigṛhītānunayaḥ śibibhiḥ sa rājā kṣattāram uvāca / gacchemaṃ vṛttāntaṃ viśvaṃtarāya nivedayeti / sa tatheti pratiśrutya śokāśrupariṣiktavadano viśvaṃtaraṃ svabhavanagatam upetya śokaduḥkhāvegāt sasvaraṃ rudan pādayor asya nyapatat / api kuśalaṃ rājakulāyeti ca sasaṃbhramaṃ viśvaṃtareṇānuyuktaḥ samavasīdann aviśadapadākṣaram enam uvāca / kuśalaṃ rājakulāyeti / atha kasmād evam adhīro 'sīti ca punar anuyukto viśvaṃtareṇa kṣattā bāṣpavegoparudhyamānagadgadakaṇṭhaḥ śvāsaviskhalitalulitākṣaraṃ śanair ity uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then the king, being told such harsh things by that assembly which, swayed by affection, trust, and loyalty, was well-intentioned though it foresaw calamity — ashamed and with downcast face from the anger of his subjects, his heart seized by the thought of separation from his son, heaving a labored sigh, said to the <s>Śibis</s>: 'If this is your insistence, then one [request] —'

children.text: sāntvagarbhām anādṛtya nṛpājñām apy adakṣiṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Disregarding even the king's command, though couched in conciliation, the ungracious ones —

children.text: rāṣṭrāt pravrājayanti tvāṃ kupitāḥ śibayo nṛpa // AJm_9.21 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Śibis</s>, enraged, O prince, banish you from the kingdom." [AJm 9.21]

body.text: viśvaṃtara uvāca / māṃ śibayaḥ pravrājayanti kupitā iti kaḥ saṃbandhaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Viśvaṃtara</s> said: 'The <s>Śibis</s> banish me in anger — what does it matter?'

children.text: rame na vinayonmārge dveṣmi cāhaṃ pramāditām /
children.translated_text: "I do not delight in the deviant path, and I hate negligence —

children.text: kutra me śibayaḥ kruddhā yan na paśyāmi duṣkṛtam // AJm_9.22 //
children.translated_text: where are the angry <s>Śibis</s> [in comparison], when I see no wrongdoing in myself?" [AJm 9.22]

body.text: kṣattovāca / atyudāratāyām /
body.translated_text: The chamberlain said: 'In your excessive generosity.'

children.text: alobhaśubhrā tvayi tuṣṭir āsīl lobhākulā yācakamānaseṣu /
children.translated_text: "Contentment, bright with non-greed, was in you; greed-troubled contentment was in the minds of the supplicants;

children.text: datte tvayā mānada vāraṇendre dhairyāṇi kopas tv aharac chibīnām // AJm_9.23 //
children.translated_text: when you gave the lord of elephants, O bestower of honor, anger carried away the composure of the <s>Śibis</s>." [AJm 9.23]

children.text: ity atītāḥ svamaryādāṃ rabhasāḥ śibayas tvayi /
children.translated_text: "Thus the <s>Śibis</s>, exceeding their own bounds, impetuously [acted] toward you —

children.text: yena pravrājitā yānti pathā tena kila vraja // AJm_9.24 //
children.translated_text: by the path along which the banished depart, they say you must go." [AJm 9.24]

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ kṛpābhyāsarūḍhāṃ yācanakajanavatsalatāṃ dhairyātiśayasaṃpadaṃ ca svām udbhāvayann uvāca / capalasvabhāvāḥ khalu śibayo 'nabhijñā iva cāsmatsvabhāvasya /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, manifesting his tenderness toward supplicants, grown from the practice of compassion, and the excellence of his extraordinary steadfastness, said: 'The <s>Śibis</s> are indeed fickle by nature and seem unacquainted with my character.'

children.text: dravyeṣu bāhyeṣu ka eva vādo dadyām ahaṃ sve nayane śiro vā /
children.translated_text: "What need even to speak of external possessions? I would give my own eyes or my head!

children.text: imaṃ hi lokārtham ahaṃ bibharmi samucchrayaṃ kiṃ bata vastu bāhyam // AJm_9.25 //
children.translated_text: For I maintain this body for the sake of the world — how much less a mere external thing?" [AJm 9.25]

children.text: yasya svagātrair api yācakānāṃ vacāṃsi saṃpūjayituṃ manīṣā /
children.translated_text: "That one whose resolve is to honor the words of supplicants even with his own limbs —

children.text: bhayān na dadyāt sa iti pratarkaḥ prakāśanā bāliśacāpalasya // AJm_9.26 //
children.translated_text: the supposition that he would not give out of fear is a display of childish fickleness." [AJm 9.26]

children.text: api ca / śibayas tvayaivaṃ vācyā madvacanena /
children.translated_text: "Moreover, tell the <s>Śibis</s> thus, in my name:"

children.text:
naivāham etad yaśase dadāmi na bhūtim icchañ chibayo na lobhāt /
nīcair anāsevita eṣa panthā dātavyam ity eva tato dadāmi // 26' //
children.translated_text: "'I give this neither for fame, nor desiring prosperity, O <s>Śibis</s>, nor from greed; this path is not trodden by the base — I give simply because one should give.' [26']"
