children.text: kāmaṃ māṃ śibayaḥ sarve ghnantu pravrājayantu vā /
children.translated_text: "Let all the <s>Śibis</s> slay me or banish me if they wish —

children.text: na tv evāhaṃ na dāsyāmi gacchāmy eṣa tapovanam // AJm_9.27 //
children.translated_text: but I shall never cease to give! I depart now for the hermitage." [AJm 9.27]

body.text: atha bodhisattvo vipriyaśravaṇaviklavamukhīṃ patnīm uvāca / śruto 'trabhavatyā śibīnāṃ niścayaḥ //

children.text: madry uvāca / śruto deva // viśvaṃtara uvāca /
children.translated_text: <s>Mādrī</s> said: 'I have heard, my lord.' <s>Viśvaṃtara</s> said:

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> said to his wife, whose face was distressed at hearing unpleasant news: 'Has the lady heard the resolve of the <s>Śibis</s>?'

children.text: yad yad asti dhanaṃ kiṃ cid asmatto 'dhigataṃ tvayā /
children.translated_text: "Whatever wealth has been acquired by you from me,

children.text: nidhehi tad anindyāṅgi yac ca te paitṛkaṃ dhanam // AJm_9.28 //
children.translated_text: deposit that, O woman of blameless limbs, together with your paternal wealth." [AJm 9.28]

body.text: madry uvāca / kutraitad deva nidadhāmīti // viśvaṃtara uvāca /
body.translated_text: <s>Mādrī</s> said: 'Where shall I deposit it, my lord?' <s>Viśvaṃtara</s> said:

children.text: śīlavadbhyaḥ sadā dadyā dānaṃ satkāraśībharam /
children.translated_text: "One should always give gifts to the virtuous, laden with honor and respect;

children.text: tathā hi nihitaṃ dravyam ahāryam anugāmi ca // AJm_9.29 //
children.translated_text: for wealth deposited thus cannot be stolen and follows one [to the next life]." [AJm 9.29]

children.text: priyaṃ śvaśurayoḥ kuryāḥ putrayoḥ paripālanam /
children.translated_text: "Do what is pleasing to your parents-in-law; protect the two sons;

children.text: dharma evāpramādaṃ ca śokaṃ madvirahāt tu mā // AJm_9.30 //
children.translated_text: be vigilant in <s>Dharma</s>; and do not grieve on account of separation from me." [AJm 9.30]

body.text: tac chrutvā madrī saṃtaptahṛdayāpi bhartur adhṛtiparihārārtham anādṛtya śokadainyam ity uvāca /
body.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Mādrī</s>, though her heart was burning, for the sake of removing her husband's unsteadiness, disregarding the wretchedness of grief, spoke thus:

children.text: naiṣa dharmo mahārāja yad yāyā vanam ekakaḥ /
children.translated_text: "This is not <s>Dharma</s>, O great king, that you should go to the forest alone;

children.text: tenāham api yāsyāmi yena kṣatriya yāsyasi // AJm_9.31 //
children.translated_text: therefore, wherever you go, O <s>Kṣatriya</s>, I too shall go." [AJm 9.31]

children.text: tvadaṅkaparivartinyā mṛtyur utsava eva me /
children.translated_text: "For me who turns about in your lap, death is indeed a festival;

children.text: mṛtyor duḥkhataraṃ tat syāj jīveyaṃ yat tvayā vinā // AJm_9.32 //
children.translated_text: more painful than death would be if I were to live without you." [AJm 9.32]

body.text: naiva ca khalu me deva vanavāso duḥkha iti pratibhāti / tathā hi /
body.translated_text: "Nor indeed, O lord, does life in the forest seem sorrowful to me. For indeed:"

children.text: nirdurjanāny anupabhuktasarittarūṇi nānāvihaṃgavirutāni mṛgākulāni /
children.translated_text: "Free from wicked people, with untasted rivers and trees, resounding with the cries of various birds, teeming with deer,

children.text: vaiḍūryakuṭṭimamanoharaśādvalāni krīḍāvanādhikasukhāni tapovanāni // AJm_9.33 //
children.translated_text: with charming lawns like floors of beryl — hermitages are more delightful than pleasure-gardens." [AJm 9.33]

body.text: api ca deva /
body.translated_text: "Moreover, O lord:"

children.text: alaṃkrtāv imau paśyan kumārau mālabhāriṇau /
children.translated_text: "Seeing these two princes adorned, wearing garlands,

children.text: krīḍantau vanagulmeṣu na rājyasya smariṣyasi // AJm_9.34 //
children.translated_text: playing among the forest bushes — you will not remember the kingdom." [AJm 9.34]

children.text: ṛtuprayatnaracitā vanaśobhā navā navā /
children.translated_text: "The beauty of the forest, fashioned anew with each season's effort,

children.text: vane tvāṃ ramayiṣyanti saritkuñjāś ca sodakāḥ // AJm_9.35 //
children.translated_text: and the river-bowers with their waters will delight you in the forest." [AJm 9.35]

children.text: citraṃ virutavāditraṃ pakṣiṇāṃ ratikāṅkṣiṇām /
children.translated_text: "The wonderful musical cries of birds desiring love,

children.text: madācāryopadiṣṭāni nṛttāni ca śikhaṇḍinām // AJm_9.36 //
children.translated_text: and the dances of peacocks as if taught by the master of dance himself — [AJm 9.36]

children.text: mādhuryānavagītaṃ ca gītaṃ madhupayoṣitām /
children.translated_text: "and the songs of the bee-women in the forests, unmatched in sweetness,

children.text: vaneṣu kṛtasaṃgītaṃ harṣayiṣyanti te manaḥ // AJm_9.37 //
children.translated_text: performed in concert, will gladden your heart." [AJm 9.37]

children.text: āstīryamāṇāni ca śarvarīṣu jyotsnādukūlena śilātalāni /
children.translated_text: "And on the nights when rock-surfaces are spread with the silk-cloth of moonlight,

children.text: saṃbāhamāno vanamārutaś ca labdhādhivāsaḥ kusumadrumebhyaḥ // AJm_9.38 //
children.translated_text: and the forest breeze, having obtained its dwelling from the flowering trees, caresses you — [AJm 9.38]

children.text: calopalapraskhalitodakānāṃ kalā virāvāś ca saridvadhūnām /
children.translated_text: "and the artful murmuring sounds of the river-brides, whose waters stumble over rolling stones,

children.text: vibhūṣaṇānām iva saṃninādāḥ pramodayiṣyanti vane manas te // AJm_9.39 //
children.translated_text: like the tinkling of ornaments — these will delight your mind in the forest." [AJm 9.39]

body.text: ity anunīyamānaḥ sa dayitayā vanaprayāṇaparyutsukamatir arthijanāvekṣayā mahāpradānaṃ dātum upacakrame // athemāṃ viśvaṃtarapravrājanapravṛttim upalabhya rājakule tumula ākrandaśabdaḥ prādurabhūt / śokaduḥkhāvegān mūrchāparigata iva cārthijano mattonmatta iva ca tat tad bahuvidhaṃ vilalāpa/
body.translated_text: Thus being consoled by his beloved, he, eager in mind for the journey to the forest, began to make a great distribution in consideration of the supplicants. Then, upon learning of this proceeding to banish <s>Viśvaṃtara</s>, a tumultuous cry of lamentation arose in the royal household. And the crowd of supplicants, as if seized by a swoon from the onslaught of sorrow and grief —

children.text: chāyātaroḥ svāduphalapradasya cchedārtham āgūrṇaparaśvadhānām /
children.translated_text: "That the earth as nurse does not feel shame when axes are being swung to fell

children.text: dhātrī na lajjāṃ yad upaiti bhūmir vyaktaṃ tad asyā hatacetanatvam // AJm_9.40 //
children.translated_text: the sheltering tree that gives sweet fruit — surely this shows that she has lost consciousness." [AJm 9.40]

children.text: śītāmalasvādujalaṃ nipānaṃ bibhitsatām asti na cen niṣeddhā /
children.translated_text: "If there is no one to forbid those who would break open the watering-place of cool, clear, sweet water —

children.text: vyarthābhidhānā bata lokapālā viproṣitā vā śrutimātrakaṃ vā // AJm_9.41 //
children.translated_text: then alas, the so-called world-protectors are vainly named, or have departed, or are merely heard of!" [AJm 9.41]

children.text: adharmo bata jāgarti dharmaḥ supto 'thavā mṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Alas, <s>Adharma</s> (unrighteousness) is awake, and <s>Dharma</s> is asleep or dead —

children.text: yatra viśvaṃtaro rājā svasmād rājyān nirasyate // AJm_9.42 //
children.translated_text: when King <s>Viśvaṃtara</s> is cast out from his own kingdom!" [AJm 9.42]

children.text: ko 'narthapaṭusāmarthyo yācñānūrjitavṛttiṣu /
children.translated_text: "Who is this one, skilled in the power of bringing ruin, harsh in his readiness to execute

children.text: asmāsv anaparādheṣu vadhābhyudyamaniṣṭhuraḥ // AJm_9.43 //
children.translated_text: those of us who are innocent, whose livelihood is enriched by supplication?" [AJm 9.43]

body.text: atha bodhisattvo naikaśatasahasrasaṃkhyaṃ maṇikanakarajataparipūrṇakośaṃ vividhadhanadhānyanicayavanti kośakoṣṭhāgārāṇi dāsīdāsayānavāhanavasanaparicchadādi ca sarvam arthibhyo yathārham atisṛjya śokaduḥkhābhibhūtadhairyayor mātāpitroś caraṇān abhipraṇamya saputradāraḥ syandanavaram abhiruhya puṇyāhaghoṣaṇayeva mahato janakāyasyākranditaśabdena puravarān niragacchat / anurāgavaśagam anuyāyinaṃ ca janaṃ śokāśrupariklinnavadanaṃ prayatnād vinivartya svayam eva pragrahān parigṛhya yena vaṅkaḥ parvatas tena prāyāt / vyatītya cāviklavamatir udyānavanaruciramālinaṃ puravaropacāram anupūrveṇa praviralacchāyādrumaṃ vicchidyamānajanasaṃpātaṃ pravicaritamṛgagaṇasaṃbādham asaṃbādhadigālokaṃ cīrīvirāvonnāditam araṇyaṃ pratyapadyata // athainaṃ yadṛcchayābhigatā brāhmaṇā rathavāhāṃs turagān ayācanta //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having given away to supplicants as was fitting his treasury filled with gems, gold, and silver numbering hundreds of thousands, his storehouses and granaries filled with various kinds of wealth and grain, his maidservants, manservants, vehicles, draft animals, garments, and equipment—everything—and having bowed at the feet of his mother and father, whose fortitude was overcome by grief and sorrow, he mounted an excellent chariot with his wife and children, and departed from the city to the loud wailing of the great multitude, as if to cries of benediction. And having with effort turned back the people who followed, enslaved by affection, their faces wet with tears of grief, taking the reins himself, he set out toward <s>Vaṅka</s> mountain. And passing beyond the pleasant garden-groves surrounding the outskirts of the city, with unshaken mind, he gradually entered the wilderness—where the shade-giving trees became sparse, where the flow of people ceased, where herds of wild animals roamed freely, where the view of the open quarters was unobstructed, and which resounded with the shrill cries of crickets. Then <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who had come by chance requested the horses that drew his chariot.

children.text: sa vartamāno 'dhvani naikayojane sahāyahīno 'pi kalatravān api /
children.translated_text: Though on a journey of many leagues, though without companions, though accompanied by his family,

children.text: pradānaharṣād anapekṣitāyatir dadau dvijebhyaś caturas turaṃgamān // AJm_9.44 //
children.translated_text: From the joy of giving, without considering the consequences, he gave the four horses to the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.

body.text: atha bodhisattvasya svayam eva rathadhuryatām upagantukāmasya gāḍhataraṃ parikaram abhisaṃyacchamānasya rohitamṛgarūpiṇaś catvāro yakṣakumārāḥ suvinītā iva sadaśvāḥ svayam eva rathayugaṃ skandhapradeśaiḥ pratyapadyanta / tāṃs tu dṛṣṭvā harṣavismayaviśālatarākṣīṃ madrīṃ bodhisattva uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then, as the <s>Bodhisattva</s> wished to take upon himself the role of chariot-horse and was tightening the harness more firmly, four <s>Yakṣa</s>-princes in the form of red deer, like well-trained fine horses, voluntarily placed their shoulder-regions against the chariot-yoke. And seeing them, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> said to <s>Madrī</s>, whose eyes had widened with delight and wonder:

children.text: tapodhanādhyāsanasatkṛtānāṃ paśya prabhāvātiśayaṃ vanānām /
children.translated_text: 'Behold the surpassing power of these forests, honored by the dwelling of those rich in austerities,

children.text: yatraivam abhyāgatavatsalatvaṃ saṃrūḍhamūlaṃ mṛgapuṃgaveṣu // AJm_9.45 //
children.translated_text: Where such deep-rooted affection for visitors [is found] even among the noblest of deer.'

body.text: madry uvāca /
body.translated_text: <s>Madrī</s> said:

children.text: tavaivāham imaṃ manye prabhāvam atimānuṣam /
children.translated_text: 'I consider this superhuman power to be yours alone;

children.text: rūḍho 'pi hi guṇābhyāsaḥ sarvatra na samaḥ satām // AJm_9.46 //
children.translated_text: For though habitual practice of virtue is established [everywhere], it is not equal among the virtuous in all places.'

children.text: toyeṣu tārāpratibimbaśobhā viśiṣyate yat kumudaprahāsaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'That the beauty of reflected stars in the waters is surpassed by the laughter of night-lilies,

children.text: kautūhalābhiprasṛtā ivendor hetutvam atrāgrakarāḥ prayānti // AJm_9.47 //
children.translated_text: And that the moon's beams, stretching forward as if from curiosity, become the cause of this—'

body.text: iti teṣām anyonyānukūlyāt parasparaṃ priyaṃ vadatām adhvānaṃ gacchatām athāparo brāhmaṇaḥ samabhigamya bodhisattvaṃ rathavaram ayācata /
body.translated_text: Thus, as they spoke agreeably to each other, exchanging pleasant words while traveling, another <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and asked for the excellent chariot.

children.text: tataḥ svasukhaniḥsaṅgo yācakapriyabāndhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then he, without attachment to his own comfort, a dear kinsman to supplicants,

children.text: pūrayām āsa viprasya sa rathena manoratham // AJm_9.48 //
children.translated_text: Fulfilled the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s heart's desire with the chariot.

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ prītamanā rathād avatārya svajanaṃ niryātya rathavaraṃ brāhmaṇāya jālinaṃ kumāram aṅkenādāya padbhyām evādhvānaṃ pratyapadyata / avimanaskaiva ca madrī kṛṣṇājināṃ kumārīm aṅkena parigṛhya pṛṣṭhato 'nvagacchad enam //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, delighted in mind, descended from the chariot, helped down his family, gave the excellent chariot to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, took the prince <s>Jālin</s> on his hip, and set out on the road on foot. And <s>Madrī</s>, not at all dejected, took the princess <s>Kṛṣṇājinā</s> on her hip and followed behind him.

children.text: nimantrayām āsur iva drumās taṃ hṛdyaiḥ phalair ānamitāgraśākhāḥ /
children.translated_text: The trees seemed to invite him with their delightful fruits, their topmost branches bowing down;

children.text: puṇyānubhāvād abhivīkṣamāṇāḥ śiṣyā vinītā iva ca praṇemuḥ // AJm_9.49 //
children.translated_text: And through the power of his merit, gazing upon him, they bowed like well-mannered disciples.

body.text: haṃsāṃsasaṃkṣobhitapaṅkajāni kiñjalkareṇusphuṭapiñjarāṇi prādurbabhūvuś ca sarāṃsi tasya tatraiva yatrābhicakāṅkṣa vāri // AJm_9.50 //
body.translated_text: Lakes appeared for him right there where he wished for water—their lotuses agitated by the wings of geese, golden-tawny with scattered pollen-dust.

children.text: vitānaśobhāṃ dadhire payodāḥ sukhaḥ sugandhiḥ pravavau nabhasvān /
children.translated_text: The clouds bore the beauty of canopies; a pleasant, fragrant breeze blew;

children.text: pariśramakleśam amṛṣyamāṇā yakṣāś ca saṃcikṣipur asya mārgam // AJm_9.51 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>Yakṣas</s>, unable to endure his fatigue and distress, shortened his path.

body.text: iti bodhisattva udyānavanagata iva pādacāravinodanasukham anubhavan mārgaparikhedarasam anāsvādya saputradāraḥ prāpta eva tu vaṅkaparvatam apaśyat / tatra ca puṣpaphalapallavālaṃkṛtasnigdhavividharucirataruvaranicitaṃ madamuditavihagavividharutaninadaṃ pravṛttanṛttabarhigaṇopaśobhitaṃ pravicaritanaikamṛgakulaṃ kṛtaparikaram iva vimalanīlasalilayā saritā kusumarajo'ruṇasukhapavanaṃ tapovanaṃ vanacarakādeśitamārgaḥ praviśya viśvakarmaṇā śakrasaṃdeśāt svayam abhinirmitāṃ manojñadarśanāṃ sarvartusukhāṃ praviviktāṃ parṇaśālām adhyāvasat /
body.translated_text: Thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, experiencing as if in a pleasure-garden the delight of walking, without tasting the weariness of the road, arrived with his wife and children at <s>Vaṅka</s> mountain. There, shown the way by a forest-dweller, he entered an ascetics' grove—densely planted with trees of various beautiful colors, adorned with flowers, fruits, and fresh shoots, resounding with the varied songs of joyful birds, embellished with troops of dancing peacocks, thronged with many herds of deer, encircled by a river of pure blue water—and with a breeze pleasant and reddened by flower-pollen, seemingly prepared [for him]. He took up residence in a leaf-hut that was delightful to behold, comfortable in all seasons, and secluded—built by <s>Viśvakarman</s> himself at <s>Śakra</s>'s command.

children.text: tasmin vane dayitayā paricaryamāṇaḥ śṛṇvann ayatnamadhurāṃś ca sutapralāpān /
children.translated_text: In that forest, attended by his beloved, hearing the effortlessly sweet prattle of his children,

children.text: udyānasaṃstha iva vismṛtarājyacintaḥ saṃvatsarārdham adhikaṃ sa tapaś cacāra // AJm_9.52 //
children.translated_text: As if dwelling in a pleasure-garden, having forgotten all thought of kingship, he practiced austerities for more than half a year.

body.text: atha kadā cin mūlaphalārthaṃ gatāyāṃ rājaputryāṃ putrayoḥ paripālananimittam āśramapadam aśūnyaṃ kurvāṇe rājaputre mārgareṇuparuṣīkṛtacaraṇaprajaṅghaḥ pariśramakṣāmanayanavadano daṇḍakāṣṭhāvabaddhaskandhāvasaktakamaṇḍalur brāhmaṇaḥ patnyā paricārakānayanārthaṃ samarpitadṛḍhasaṃdeśas taṃ deśam abhijagāma / atha bodhisattvaś cirasyārthijanaṃ dṛṣṭvābhigataṃ manaḥpraharṣāt saṃjāyamānanayanavadanaprasādaḥ pratyudgamya svāgatādipriyavacanapuraḥsaraṃ praveśya cainam āśramapadaṃ kṛtātithisatkāram āgamanaprayojanam apṛcchat / atha sa brāhmaṇo bhāryānurāgād utsāritadhairyalajjaḥ pratigrahamātrasajja īdṛśam artham uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then once, when the princess had gone to gather roots and fruits, while the prince was keeping the hermitage occupied for the purpose of watching over the children, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> arrived in that place—his feet and shins roughened by the dust of the road, his face and eyes gaunt from the fatigue of travel, a water-pot suspended from a staff bound over his shoulder—entrusted with firm instructions by his wife to bring back attendants. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, seeing after a long time a supplicant who had come, his face and eyes brightening with the delight of his heart, went forward to meet him, welcomed him with kind words of greeting, led him into the hermitage, performed the hospitality due a guest, and asked the purpose of his visit. Then that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, his composure and shame overcome by desire for his wife, eager only for the gift, spoke of this matter:

children.text: āloko bhavati yataḥ samaś ca mārgo loko 'yaṃ vrajati tato na durgameṇa /
children.translated_text: 'Where you are, there is light, and the path is level; the world does not travel by a difficult way.

children.text: prāyo 'smiñ jagati tu matsarāndhakāre nānyena praṇayapadāni me vahanti // AJm_9.53 //
children.translated_text: But in this world, generally darkened by the blindness of jealousy, my steps of affection do not proceed by any other [path].'

children.text: pradānaśauryorjitayā yaśaḥśriyā gataṃ ca gantavyam aśeṣatas tava /
children.translated_text: 'By the glory of fame won through the valor of giving, you have traversed and must traverse everything completely;

children.text: ato 'smi yācñāśramam abhyupeyivān prayaccha tan me paricārakau sutau // AJm_9.54 //
children.translated_text: Therefore I have come enduring the toil of begging—give me your two children as servants.'

body.text: ity ukte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ
body.translated_text: When this was said, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, that great being—

children.text: dānaprītau kṛtābhyāsaḥ pratyākhyātum aśikṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Practiced in the delight of giving, untrained in refusal,

children.text: dadāmīty avadad dhṛṣṭaṃ dayitau tanayāv api // AJm_9.55 //
children.translated_text: Boldly said 'I give'—even his beloved children.

body.text: svasty astu / tat kim idānīm āsyata iti ca brāhmaṇenābhihitaḥ sa mahāsattvaḥ pradānakathāśravaṇotpatitaviṣādaviplutākṣayoḥ sutayoḥ snehavegenāvalambyamānahṛdayo bodhisattva uvāca /
body.translated_text: 'May all be well! Then why do you now wait?'—thus addressed by the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> with these words whose meaning was unfinished, that great being, his heart seized by the force of affection as the children's eyes widened with the dismay that had arisen upon hearing the talk of giving, spoke:

children.text: dattāv etau mayā tubhyaṃ kiṃ tu mātānayor gatā /
children.translated_text: 'These two have been given by me to you; but their mother has gone

children.text: vanaṃ mūlaphalasyārthe sāyam adyāgamiṣyati // AJm_9.56 //
children.translated_text: Into the forest for roots and fruits—she will return this evening.'

children.text: tayā dṛṣṭāv upāghrātau mālināv abhyalaṃkṛtau /
children.translated_text: 'When she has seen them, smelled them, garlanded and adorned them,

children.text: ihaikarātraṃ viśramya śvo netāsi sutau mama // AJm_9.57 //
children.translated_text: After resting here for one night, you may take my children tomorrow.'

body.text: brāhmaṇa uvāca / alam anenātrabhavato nirbandhena /
body.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> said: 'Enough of this insistence by your honor.'

children.text: gauṇam etad dhi nārīṇāṃ nāma vāmā iti sthitam /
children.translated_text: 'For it is well established that the secondary name of women is "the contrary ones";

children.text: syāc caivaṃ dānavighnas te tena vāsaṃ na rocaye // AJm_9.58 //
children.translated_text: And thus there would be an obstruction to your giving—therefore I do not approve of staying.'

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca / alaṃ dānavighnāśaṅkayā / sahadharmacāriṇī mama sā / yathā vātrabhavate rocate / api ca mahābrāhmaṇa
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Enough of the suspicion that the gift will be obstructed. She is my companion in <s>dharma</s>. As your honor pleases. Moreover, O great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>—'

children.text: sukumāratayā bālyāt paricaryāsv akauśalāt /
children.translated_text: 'Being tender by nature, [still] children, unskilled in service—

children.text: kīdṛśīṃ nāma kuryātāṃ dāsaprītim imau tava // AJm_9.59 //
children.translated_text: What kind of slave's pleasure could these two possibly give you?'

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tv itthaṃgatāv etau śibirājaḥ pitāmahaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'But King <s>Śibi</s>, their grandfather, upon seeing these two in such a condition,

children.text: addhā dadyād yad iṣṭaṃ te dhanaṃ niṣkrayam etayoḥ // AJm_9.60 //
children.translated_text: Would surely give you whatever wealth you desire as their ransom.'

children.text: yatas tadviṣayaṃ sādhu tvam imau netum arhasi /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore it would be good if you take these two to his territory;

children.text: evaṃ hy arthena mahatā dharmeṇa ca sameṣyasi // AJm_9.61 //
children.translated_text: For thus you will come into both great wealth and <s>dharma</s>.'

body.text: brāhmaṇa uvāca / na śakṣyāmy aham āśīviṣadurāsadaṃ vipriyopāyanena rājānam abhigantum /
body.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> said: 'I am not able to approach the king, who is as unapproachable as a venomous serpent, with an unwelcome gift.'

children.text: ācchindyān mad imau rājā daṇḍaṃ vā praṇayen mayi /
children.translated_text: 'The king would seize these two from me, or impose a punishment on me;

children.text: yato neṣyāmy aham imau brāhmaṇyāḥ paricārakau // AJm_9.62 //
children.translated_text: Therefore I shall take these two as servants for my wife.'

body.text: atha bodhisattvo yatheṣṭam idānīm ity aparisamāptārtham uktvā sānunayam anuśiṣya tanayau paricaryānukūlye pratigrahārtham abhiprasārite brāhmaṇasya pāṇau kamaṇḍalum āvarjayām āsa /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having said 'As you wish, then—' with incomplete meaning, and having tenderly instructed his children in obedience to service, poured water from his water-pot into the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s hand, which was extended to receive the gift.

children.text: tasya yatnānurodhena papātāmbu kamaṇḍaloḥ /
children.translated_text: Water fell from his water-pot at his deliberate bidding;

children.text: padmapattrābhitāmrābhyāṃ netrābhyāṃ svayam eva tu // AJm_9.63 //
children.translated_text: But from his eyes, coppery-red as lotus petals, [tears fell] of their own accord.

body.text: atha sa brāhmaṇo lābhātiharṣāt sasaṃbhramākulitamatir bodhisattvatanayāpaharaṇatvarayā saṃkṣiptapadam āśīrvacanam uktvā nirgamyatām ity ājñākarkaśena vacasā kumārāv āśramapadān niṣkrāmayitum ārebhe // atha kumārau viyogaduḥkhātibhāravyathitahṛdayau pitaram abhipraṇamya bāṣpoparudhyamānanayanāv ūcatuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, his mind agitated with the thrill of his gain, in his haste to carry off the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s children, speaking a hastily abbreviated blessing, began to drive the princes out of the hermitage with harsh commanding words: 'Let us go!' Then the two princes, their hearts agonized by the overwhelming weight of the sorrow of separation, bowed to their father, and with eyes obstructed by tears, said:

children.text: ambā ca tāta niṣkrāntā tvaṃ ca nau dātum icchasi /
children.translated_text: 'Mother too has gone out, Father, and you wish to give us away—

children.text: yāvat tām api paśyeva tato dāsyati nau bhavān // AJm_9.64 //
children.translated_text: Let us at least see her—then you may give us.'

body.text: atha sa brāhmaṇaḥ purā mātānayor āgacchaty asya vā putrasnehāt paścāttāpaḥ saṃbhavatīti vicintya padmakalāpam ivānayor hastān ābadhya latayā saṃtarjayan viceṣṭamānau pitaraṃ prati vyāvartitavadanau prakṛtisukumārau kumārau pracakarṣa // atha kṛṣṇājinā kumārī tatpūrvaduḥkhopanipātāt sasvaraṃ rudatī pitaram uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, thinking 'before their mother arrives, or before he repents out of parental affection,' bound their hands like a bunch of lotuses with a creeper, and threatening them, dragged the two children away—struggling, their faces turned back toward their father, tender by nature. Then the princess <s>Kṛṣṇājinā</s>, struck by this sudden affliction, weeping aloud, said to her father:

children.text: ayaṃ māṃ brāhmaṇas tāta latayā hanti nirdayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This merciless <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is beating me with a vine, Father!

children.text: na cāyaṃ brāhmaṇo vyaktaṃ dhārmikā brāhmaṇāḥ kila // AJm_9.65 //
children.translated_text: He is surely not a [true] <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>—for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are said to be righteous!'

children.text: yakṣo 'yaṃ brāhmaṇacchadmā nūnaṃ harati khāditum /
children.translated_text: 'He is a <s>Yakṣa</s> in <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s disguise, surely carrying us off to devour us!

children.text: nīyamānau piśācena tāta kiṃ nāv upekṣase // AJm_9.66 //
children.translated_text: Being taken away by a <s>Piśāca</s> (demon), Father—why do you ignore us?'

body.text: atha jālī kumāro mātaram anuśocann uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then the prince <s>Jālin</s>, grieving for his mother, said:

children.text: naivedaṃ me tathā duḥkhaṃ yad ayaṃ hanti māṃ dvijaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'It is not so much this that pains me—that this <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> beats me;

children.text: nāpaśyam ambāṃ yat tv adya tad vidārayatīva mām // AJm_9.67 //
children.translated_text: But that I did not see Mother today—that tears me apart, as it were.'

children.text: rodiṣyati ciraṃ nūnam ambā śūnye tapovane /
children.translated_text: 'Mother will surely weep for a long time in the empty hermitage,

children.text: putraśokena kṛpaṇā hataśāveva cātakī // AJm_9.68 //
children.translated_text: Wretched with grief for her children, like a <s>cātakī</s> bird whose chick has been killed.'

children.text: asmadarthaṃ samāhṛtya vanān mūlaphalam bahu /
children.translated_text: 'Having gathered many roots and fruits from the forest for our sake,

children.text: bhaviṣyati kathaṃ nv ambā dṛṣṭvā śūnyaṃ tapovanam // AJm_9.69 //
children.translated_text: How will Mother be, seeing the hermitage empty?'

children.text: ime nāv aśvakās tāta hastikā rathakāś ca ye /
children.translated_text: 'These toy horses, elephants, and chariots of ours, Father—

children.text: ato 'rdhaṃ deyam ambāyai śokaṃ tena vineṣyati // AJm_9.70 //
children.translated_text: Half should be given to Mother; by that she will dispel her grief.'

children.text: vandyāsmadvacanād ambā vāryā śokāc ca sarvathā /
children.translated_text: 'Convey our salutations to Mother, and restrain her from grief in every way;

children.text: durlabhaṃ hi punas tāta tava tasyāś ca darśanam // AJm_9.71 //
children.translated_text: For the sight of you and of her, Father, will be rare again.'

children.text: ehi kṛṣṇe mariṣyāvaḥ ko nv artho jīvitena nau /
children.translated_text: 'Come, <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, we shall die—what use is life to us?

children.text: dattāv āvāṃ janitrāsmai brāhmaṇāya dhanaiṣiṇe // AJm_9.72 //
children.translated_text: We have been given away by our father to this wealth-seeking <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.'

body.text: ity uktvā jagmatuḥ // atha bodhisattvas tenātikaruṇena tanayapralāpenākampitamatir api ka idānīṃ dattvānutāpaṃ kariṣyatīti niṣpratīkāreṇa śokāgninā nirdahyamānahṛdayo viṣavegamūrchāparigata iva samuparudhyamānacetās tatraiva niṣasāda / śītānilavyajanapratilabdhasaṃjñaś ca niṣkūjam ivāśramapadaṃ tanayaśūnyam abhivīkṣya bāṣpagadgadasaṃnirudhyamānakaṇṭha ity ātmagatam uvāca /
body.translated_text: Having said this, they departed. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, though his mind was shaken by that most piteous lamentation of his children, [thinking] 'Who, having given, would now feel remorse?'—his heart being burned by an irremediable fire of grief, his consciousness fading as if seized by the swoon of poison—sank down right there. And when he regained consciousness from the fanning of a cool breeze, seeing the hermitage empty and silent, bereft of his children, his throat choked with tears and sobs, he said to himself:

children.text: putrābhidhāne hṛdaye samakṣaṃ praharan mama /
children.translated_text: 'Striking right before my eyes at my heart in the place called "children,"

children.text: nāśaṅkata kathaṃ nāma dhig alajjo bata dvijaḥ // AJm_9.73 //
children.translated_text: How was that shameless wretch of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> not afraid? Shame on him!'

children.text: pattikāv anupānatkau saukumāryāt klamāsahau /
children.translated_text: 'On foot, without shoes, unable to bear fatigue because of their tenderness—

children.text: yāsyataḥ katham adhvānaṃ tasya ca preṣyatāṃ gatau // AJm_9.74 //
children.translated_text: How will they travel the road, having fallen into his servitude?'

children.text: mārgaśramaparimlānau ko 'dya viśrāmayiṣyati /
children.translated_text: 'Wilted from the weariness of the road, who will give them rest today?'

children.text: kṣuttarṣaduḥkābhihatau yāciṣyete kam etya vā // AJm_9.75 //
children.translated_text: Stricken by the suffering of hunger and thirst, whom will they approach to beg?

children.text: mama tāvad idaṃ duḥkhaṃ dhīratāṃ kartum icchataḥ /
children.translated_text: For me, who wishes to be steadfast, this is [merely] suffering.

children.text: kā nv avasthā mama tayoḥ sutayoḥ sukhavṛddhayoḥ // AJm_9.76 //
children.translated_text: But what must be the condition of those two sons of mine, raised in comfort?

children.text: aho putraviyogāgnir nirdahaty eva me manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Alas, the fire of separation from my sons surely burns my heart!

children.text: satāṃ tu dharmaṃ saṃsmṛtya ko 'nutāpaṃ kariṣyati // AJm_9.77 //
children.translated_text: But remembering the <s>dharma</s> of the virtuous, who would give way to remorse?'

body.text: atha madrī vipriyopanipātāśaṃsibhir aniṣṭair nimittair upajanitavaimanasyā mūlaphalāny ādāya kṣiprataram āgantukāmāpi vyāḍamṛgoparudhyamānamārgā ciratareṇāśramapadam upajagāma / ucitāyāṃ ca pratyudgamanabhūmāv ākrīḍasthāneṣu ca tanayāv apaśyantī bhṛśataram arativaśam agāt //
body.translated_text: Now <s>Madrī</s>, her mind distressed by unfavorable omens portending misfortune, taking roots and fruits and wishing to return quickly, was delayed on the path obstructed by wild beasts and predators, and arrived at the hermitage only after a long while. Not seeing her two sons in the accustomed places of greeting and in the play-areas, she fell ever more deeply under the sway of distress.

children.text: anīpsitāśaṅkitajātasaṃbhramā tataḥ sutānveṣaṇacañcalekṣaṇā /
children.translated_text: Then, with alarm born from the apprehension of something unwanted, her eyes darting about in search of her sons,

children.text: prasaktam āhvānam asaṃpratigrahaṃ tayor viditvā vyalapac chucāturā // AJm_9.78 //
children.translated_text: realizing that her continuous calling had gone unanswered, she wailed, afflicted with grief.

children.text: samājavad yat pratibhāti me purā sutapralāpapratināditaṃ vanam /
children.translated_text: 'This forest that previously seemed to me like a festive gathering, resounding with the chatter of my sons —

children.text: adarśanād adya tayos tad eva me prayāti kāntāram ivāśaraṇyatām // AJm_9.79 //
children.translated_text: today, from not seeing those two, that very [forest] seems to me to become a trackless wilderness, devoid of shelter.

body.text: kiṃ nu khalu tau kumārau
body.translated_text: What indeed [has happened to] those two princes?

children.text: krīḍāprasaṅgaśramajātanidrau suptau nu naṣṭau gahane vane vā /
children.translated_text: Are they asleep, overcome by drowsiness born from the exertion of play? Or are they lost in the dense forest?

children.text: cirān madabhyāgamanād atuṣṭau syātāṃ kva cid bālatayā nilīnau // AJm_9.80 //
children.translated_text: Or, displeased at the lateness of my return, have they, in their childishness, hidden somewhere?

children.text: ruvanti kasmāc ca na pakṣiṇo 'py amī samākulās tadvadhasākṣiṇo yadi /
children.translated_text: And why do these birds not cry out — or are they distraught as witnesses to their slaughter?

children.text: taraṃgabhaṅgair avinītakopayā hṛtau nu kiṃ nimnagayātivegayā // AJm_9.81 //
children.translated_text: Or have they been carried away by a river of violent current, unrestrained in its fury, with crashing waves?

body.text: apīdānīṃ me vitathā mithyāvikalpā bhaveyuḥ / api rājaputrāya saputrāya svasti syāt / apy aniṣṭanivedināṃ nimittānāṃ maccharīra eva vipāko bhavet / kiṃ nu khalv idaṃ

children.text: a
children.translated_text: My

children.text: nimittāpavṛttapraharṣam aratitamisrayāvacchādyamānaṃ vidravatīva me hṛdayam / visrasyanta iva me gātrāṇi / vyākulā iva digvibhāgāḥ / bhramatīva cedaṃ paridhvastalakṣmīkaṃ vanam iti // athānupraviśyāśramapadam ekānte nikṣipya mūlaphalam upacārapuraḥsaraṃ bhartāram abhigamya kva dārakāv iti papraccha / atha bodhisattvo jānānaḥ snehadurbalatāṃ mātṛhṛdayasya durnivedyatvāc ca vipriyasya naināṃ kiṃ cid vaktuṃ śaśāka /
children.translated_text: heart, bereft of the joy that would come from the aversion of omens, obscured by the darkness of distress, seems to dissolve. My limbs seem to collapse. The directions of space seem confused. And this forest, its beauty destroyed, seems to whirl about.' Then, entering the hermitage grounds, setting down the roots and fruits in a corner, she approached her husband with courteous formality and asked: 'Where are the children?' Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, knowing the weakness of a mother's heart due to love, and because unwelcome [news] is so hard to convey, was unable to say anything to her.

body.translated_text: May my unfounded false imaginings prove untrue! May the prince and his sons be well! May the fruition of these ill-boding omens fall upon my body alone! What indeed is this?

body.text: janasya hi priyārhasya vipriyākhyānavahninā

children.text: upetya hi
children.translated_text: having approached [them],

children.text: manastāpaḥ saghṛṇena suduṣkaraḥ // AJm_9.82 //
children.translated_text: the mental anguish [inflicted] by one who is compassionate is extremely difficult [to bear].

body.translated_text: For one who is dear and deserving of pleasant [words], by the fire of conveying unpleasant news,

body.text: atha madrī vyaktam akuśalaṃ me putrayor yad ayam evaṃ tūṣṇīṃbhūtaḥ śokadainyānuvṛttyety avadhārya samantataḥ kṣiptacitteva vicintyāśramapadaṃ tanayāv apaśyantī sabāṣpagadgadaṃ punar uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Madrī</s>, determining: 'Clearly, something ill has befallen my sons, since he remains thus silent, following the course of grief and despondency,' searched the hermitage grounds all about as if with a mind thrown in every direction, and not seeing her two sons, spoke again, her voice choked with tears:

children.text: dārakau ca na paśyāmi tvaṃ ca māṃ nābhibhāṣase /
children.translated_text: 'I do not see the children, and you do not speak to me.

children.text: hatā khalv asmi kṛpaṇā vipriyaṃ hi na kathyate // AJm_9.83 //
children.translated_text: Surely I am lost, wretched one! For unpleasant [news] is not being told [to me].'

body.text: ity uktvā śokāgninā parigatahṛdayā chinnamūleva latā nipapāta / patantīm eva caināṃ parigṛhya bodhisattvas tṛṇaśayanam ānīya śītābhir adbhiḥ pariṣicya pratyāgataprāṇāṃ samāśvāsayann uvāca /
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, her heart engulfed by the fire of grief, she fell like a creeper whose root has been cut. Catching her even as she fell, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> brought her to a bed of grass, sprinkled her with cool water, and as her breath returned, consoling her, he said:

children.text: sahasaiva na te madri duḥkham ākhyātavān aham /
children.translated_text: 'I did not tell you this grief suddenly, O <s>Madrī</s>,

children.text: na hi saṃbhāvyate dhairyaṃ manasi snehadurbale // AJm_9.84 //
children.translated_text: for steadfastness is not to be expected in a heart weakened by love.

children.text: jarādāridryaduḥkhārto brāhmaṇo mām upāgamat /
children.translated_text: A brahmin, afflicted by the suffering of old age and poverty, approached me.

children.text: tasmai dattau mayā putrau samāśvasihi mā śucaḥ // AJm_9.85 //
children.translated_text: To him I gave [our] sons. Take comfort! Do not grieve.

children.text: māṃ paśya madri mā putrau paridevīś ca devi mā /
children.translated_text: Look at me, <s>Madrī</s>, not at [our] sons! Do not lament, O queen!

children.text: putraśokasaśalye me prahārṣīr iva mā hṛdi // AJm_9.86 //
children.translated_text: Do not thrust into my heart, already pierced by the arrow of grief for [our] sons, [yet another weapon]!

children.text: yācitena kathaṃ śakyaṃ na dātum api jīvitam /
children.translated_text: When asked, how can one not give — even one's life?

children.text: anumodasva tad bhadre putradānam idaṃ mama // AJm_9.87 //
children.translated_text: Therefore rejoice, O blessed one, in this gift of [our] sons by me.'

body.text: tac chrutvā madrī putravināśaśaṅkāvyathitahṛdayā putrayor jīvitapravṛttiśravaṇāt pratanūbhūtaśokā patyur adhṛtiparihārārthaṃ pramṛjya nayane savismayam udīkṣamāṇā bhartāram uvāca / āścaryam / kiṃ bahunā /
body.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Madrī</s>, her heart troubled by fear of [her] sons' destruction, yet with her grief diminished by hearing that her sons were still alive, wiping her eyes in order to relieve her husband's distress, gazing at him with wonder, said: 'How marvelous! To say more:',

children.text: nūnaṃ vismayavaktavyacetaso 'pi divaukasaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Surely even the celestial beings, whose hearts are susceptible to wonder,

children.text: yad ity alabdhaprasaras tava cetasi matsaraḥ // AJm_9.88 //
children.translated_text: [must acknowledge] that selfishness finds no scope in your heart.'

children.text: tathā hi dikṣu prasṛtapratisvanaiḥ samantato daivatadundubhisvanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For with sounds of divine drums resounding in all directions, with echoes spreading to every quarter,

children.text: prasaktavispaṣṭapadākṣaraṃ nabhas tavaiva kīrtiprathanādarād abhūt // AJm_9.89 //
children.translated_text: the sky, with its clearly audible syllables and words, became [an instrument] zealously proclaiming your fame.'

children.text: prakampiśailendrapayodharā dharā madād ivābhūd abhivṛddhavepathuḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The earth, with great mountains for her breasts, trembled as if with excitement, her shaking intensified.

children.text: divaḥ patadbhiḥ kusumaiś ca kāñcanaiḥ savidyududdyotam ivābhavan nabhaḥ // AJm_9.90 //
children.translated_text: And with golden flowers falling from the sky, the heavens appeared as if flashing with lightning.'

children.text: tad alaṃ śokadainyena dattvā cittaṃ prasādaya /
children.translated_text: 'So enough of grief and despondency! Having given, make your heart serene.

children.text: nipānabhūto lokānāṃ dātaiva ca punar bhava // AJm_9.91 //
children.translated_text: And become once again a drinking-place for the world — a giver.'

body.text: atha śakro devendraḥ kṣititalacalanād ākampite sumerau parvatarāje kim idam iti samutpannavimarśo vismayotphullanayanebhyo lokapālebhyaḥ pṛthivīkampakāraṇaṃ viśvaṃtaraputradānam upalabhya praharṣavismayāghūrṇitamanāḥ prabhātāyāṃ tasyāṃ rajanyāṃ brāhmaṇarūpī viśvaṃtaram arthivad abhyagacchat / kṛtātithisatkāraś ca bodhisattvena kenārtha ity upanimantrito bhāryām enam ayācata /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, king of the gods, when <s>Sumeru</s>, king of mountains, shook from the trembling of the earth, wondering 'What is this?,' and learning from the world-guardians — their eyes wide with amazement — that the cause of the earthquake was <s>Viśvaṃtara</s>'s gift of his sons, his mind whirling with joy and wonder, at dawn of that night, in the guise of a brahmin, approached <s>Viśvaṃtara</s> as a supplicant. Having been shown guest-hospitality by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and invited with 'What is your purpose?,' he asked him for his wife:

children.text: mahāhradeṣv ambha ivopaśoṣaṃ na dānadharmaḥ samupaiti satsu /
children.translated_text: 'As water in great lakes does not diminish, so the <s>dharma</s> of giving does not diminish among the virtuous.

children.text: yāce tatas tvāṃ surasaṃnibhāryāṃ bhāryām imām arhasi naḥ pradātum // AJm_9.92 //
children.translated_text: Therefore I ask you: please give us this wife of yours, who is like a goddess.'

body.text: avimanā eva tu bodhisattvas tathety asmai pratiśuśrāva /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, without the slightest hesitation, promised him: 'So be it.'

children.text: tataḥ sa vāmena kareṇa madrīm ādāya savyena kamaṇḍaluṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Then, taking <s>Madrī</s> with his left hand and the water-vessel with his right,

children.text: nyapātayat tasya jalaṃ karāgre manobhuvaś cetasi śokavahnim // AJm_9.93 //
children.translated_text: he poured the water onto the tips of his [the brahmin's] fingers — [pouring] the fire of grief upon the heart of <s>Manobhū</s> (the God of Love).

children.text: cukopa madrī na tu no ruroda viveda sā tasya hi taṃ svabhāvam /
children.translated_text: <s>Madrī</s> did not become angry, nor indeed did she weep, for she knew his nature.

children.text: apūrvaduḥkhātibharāturā tu taṃ prekṣamāṇā likhiteva tasthau // AJm_9.94 //
children.translated_text: But overwhelmed by the unbearable weight of unprecedented sorrow, gazing at him, she stood motionless, as if painted.

body.text: tad dṛṣṭvā paramavismayākrāntahṛdayaḥ śakro devānām indras taṃ mahāsattvam abhiṣṭuvann uvāca /
body.translated_text: Seeing that, <s>Śakra</s>, king of the gods, his heart seized by supreme wonder, praising that great being, said:

children.text: aho vikṛṣṭāntaratā sadasaddharmayor yathā /
children.translated_text: 'Oh, how vast is the distance between the innermost natures of the virtuous and the wicked!

children.text: śraddhātum api karmedaṃ kā śaktir akṛtātmanām // AJm_9.95 //
children.translated_text: What power have those of unrefined souls even to believe in this deed?

children.text: avītarāgeṇa satā putradāram atipriyam /
children.translated_text: For one not yet free from passion, to give away sons and wife — [things] most dear —

children.text: niḥsaṅgam iti dātavyaṃ kā nāmeyam udāttatā // AJm_9.96 //
children.translated_text: without attachment, saying 'It must be given' — what kind of nobility is this?

children.text: asaṃśayaṃ tvadguṇaraktasaṃkathaiḥ prakīryamāṇeṣu yaśaḥsu dikṣu te /
children.translated_text: Assuredly, when your fame is spread abroad in the quarters through conversations ardent with love of your virtues,

children.text: tirobhaviṣyanty aparā yaśaḥśriyaḥ pataṃgatejaḥsu yathānyadīptayaḥ // AJm_9.97 //
children.translated_text: other glories of renown will vanish, as other lights [vanish] before the radiance of the sun.

children.text: tasya te 'bhyanumodante karmedam atimānuṣam /
children.translated_text: This superhuman deed of yours is rejoiced in

children.text: yakṣagandharvabhujagās tridaśāś ca savāsavāḥ // AJm_9.98 //
children.translated_text: by <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, and the gods together with <s>Vāsava</s> (Indra).'

body.text: ity uktvā śakraḥ svam eva vapur abhijvalad āsthāya śakro 'ham asmīti ca nivedyātmānaṃ bodhisattvam uvāca /
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, <s>Śakra</s>, assuming his own blazing form, revealed: 'I am <s>Śakra</s>!' and said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>:

children.text: tubhyam eva prayacchāmi madrīṃ bhāryām imām aham /
children.translated_text: 'I myself give back to you this your wife <s>Madrī</s>.

children.text: vyatītya na hi śītāṃśuṃ candrikā sthātum arhati // AJm_9.99 //
children.translated_text: For moonlight cannot remain apart from the moon.

children.text: dattāpi ca śṛgālasya siṃhabhāryā kim asya sā /
children.translated_text: Even if given to a jackal, what use is a lion's wife to him?

children.text: siṃhasyaiva hi sā bhāryā dhīrā yacchanti yācitāḥ // AJm_9.100 //
children.translated_text: She is the wife of a lion alone — the steadfast give when asked.

children.text: viśiṣṭamadhyahīnānāṃ samacittā jināṅkurāḥ /
children.translated_text: The offspring of the Victors (<s>Jina</s>) are equal-minded toward the distinguished, the middling, and the low.

children.text: tasmād anumatā loke [......]na tu karmaṇā // AJm_9.101 //
children.translated_text: Therefore they are approved in the world [...] not by [the results of their] actions.'

children.text: tan mā cintāṃ putrayor viprayogād rājyabhraṃśān mā ca saṃtāpam āgāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'So do not worry about the separation from [your] sons, and do not grieve about the loss of your kingdom.

children.text: sārdhaṃ tābhyām abhyupetaḥ pitā te kartā rājyaṃ tvatsanāthaṃ sanātham // AJm_9.102 //
children.translated_text: Your father will come together with those two [sons]; he will make your kingdom protected and eternal under your guardianship.'

body.text: ity uktvā śakras tatraivāntardadhe / śakrānubhāvāc ca sa brāhmaṇo bodhisattvatanayau śibiviṣayam eva saṃprāpayām āsa / atha śibayaḥ saṃjayaś ca śibirājas tad atikaruṇam atiduṣkaraṃ bodhisattvasya karma śrutvā samākleditahṛdayā brāhmaṇahastān niṣkrīya bodhisattvatanayau prasādyānīya ca viśvaṃtaraṃ rājya eva pratiṣṭhāpayām āsuḥ //
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, <s>Śakra</s> vanished right there. And through <s>Śakra</s>'s power, that brahmin delivered the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s sons to the <s>Śibi</s> realm itself. Then the <s>Śibis</s> and <s>Saṃjaya</s>, the <s>Śibi</s> king, upon hearing of that most compassionate, most difficult deed of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, their hearts melted, ransomed the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s sons from the brahmin's hands, and having conciliated and brought back <s>Viśvaṃtara</s>, re-established him in his kingdom.

body.text: tad evam atyadbhutā bodhisattvacaryeti tadunmukheṣu sattvaviśeṣeṣu nāvajñā pratīghāto vā karaṇīyaḥ / tathāgatavarṇe satkṛtya dharmaśravaṇe copaneyam //
body.translated_text: Therefore, since the conduct of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is so utterly wondrous, contempt and hostility should not be shown toward those exceptional beings inclined toward it. This [story] may also be used in [illustrating] the praises of the <s>Tathāgata</s> and in [exhorting] respectful hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: viśvaṃtarajātakaṃ navamam //
body.translated_text: The <s>Viśvaṃtara Jātaka</s>, the ninth.

children.text: 10. Yajñajātakam
children.translated_text: 10. The <s>Yajña Jātaka</s> (The Sacrifice).

body.text: na kalyāṇāśayāḥ pāpapratāraṇām anuvidhīyanta ity āśayaśuddhau yatitavyam //
body.translated_text: Those of virtuous intent do not follow the deceptions of the wicked; therefore one should strive for purity of intention.

body.text: tadyathānuśrūyate / bodhisattvaḥ kila svapuṇyaprabhāvopanatām ānatasarvasāmantāṃ praśāntasvaparacakrādyupadravatvād akaṇṭakām asapatnām ekātapatrāṃ dāyādyakramāgatāṃ pṛthivīṃ pālayām āsa /
body.translated_text: So it is heard: the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, it is said, ruled the earth — [an earth] obtained through the power of his own merit, with all neighboring kings submissive, peaceful and free from disturbance of hostile forces and the like, thornless, without rivals, under a single royal parasol, inherited by rightful succession.

children.text: nāthaḥ pṛthivyāḥ sa jitendriyārir bhuktāvagīteṣu phaleṣv asaktaḥ /
children.translated_text: That lord of the earth, conqueror of the enemies of the senses, unattached to the fruits of pleasure already enjoyed and cast aside,

children.text: prajāhiteṣv āhitasarvabhāvo dharmaikakāryo munivad babhūva // AJm_10.1 //
children.translated_text: with his entire being devoted to the welfare of his subjects, engaged solely in <s>dharma</s>, he was like a sage.

children.text: viveda lokasya hi sa svabhāvaṃ pradhānacaryānukṛtipradhānam /
children.translated_text: For he understood the nature of the world — that it is primarily governed by imitating the conduct of the foremost.

children.text: śreyaḥ samādhitsur ataḥ prajāsu viśeṣato dharmavidhau sasañje // AJm_10.2 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, wishing to establish the good among his subjects, he devoted himself especially to the practice of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: dadau dhanaṃ śīlavidhiṃ samādade kṣamāṃ siṣeve jagadartham aihata /
children.translated_text: He gave wealth, he undertook the rules of moral conduct, he cultivated forbearance, he strove for the welfare of the world.

children.text: prajāhitādhyāśayasaumyadarśanaḥ sa mūrtimān dharma iva vyarocata // AJm_10.3 //
children.translated_text: With a gentle appearance [reflecting] his intention for the welfare of his subjects, he shone like <s>Dharma</s> incarnate.

body.text: atha kadā cit tadbhujābhiguptam api taṃ viṣayaṃ sattvānāṃ karmavaiguṇyāt pramādavaśagatvāc ca varṣakarmādhikṛtānāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ durvṛṣṭiparyākulatā kva cit kva cid abhidudrāva // atha sa rājā vyaktam ayaṃ mama prajānāṃ vā dharmāpacārāt samupanato 'nartha iti niścitamatiḥ saṃrūḍhahitādhyāśayatvāt prajāsu tadduḥkham amṛṣyamāṇo dharmatattvajñasaṃmatān purohitapramukhān brāhmaṇavṛddhān matisacivāṃś ca taduddharaṇopāyaṃ papraccha / atha te vedavihitam anekaprāṇiśatavadhārambhabhīṣaṇaṃ yajñavidhiṃ suvṛṣṭihetuṃ manyamānās tam asmai saṃvarṇayām āsuḥ / viditavṛttāntas tu sa rājā yajñavihitānāṃ prāṇivaiśasānāṃ karuṇātmakatvān na teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ bhāvenābhyanandat / vinayānuvṛttyā cainān pratyākhyānarūkṣākṣaram anuktvā prastāvāntareṇaiṣāṃ tāṃ kathāṃ tiraścakāra / te punar api taṃ rājānaṃ dharmasaṃkathāprastāvalabdhāvasarā gāmbhīryagūḍhaṃ tasya bhāvam ajānānā yajñapravṛttaye samanuśaśāsuḥ /
body.translated_text: Now once, even though that territory was protected by his arm, through the karmic misfortune of beings and through the negligence of the celestial sons charged with the office of rain, drought-distress attacked here and there. Then that king, having determined: 'Clearly this misfortune has arisen from some lapse in <s>dharma</s> on my part or on that of my subjects,' and being unable to tolerate their suffering due to his deeply-rooted desire for his subjects' welfare, he asked the brahmin-elders headed by the royal chaplain, whom he deemed knowledgeable in the truth of <s>dharma</s>, together with his counselor-ministers, about the means of remedying it. Then they, believing that the Vedic sacrificial rite — terrifying in its commencement of the slaughter of hundreds of living beings — was the cause of good rain, commended it to him. But that king, knowing the facts, because of his compassionate nature did not approve of their words in his heart, [regarding] the killing of living beings prescribed in the sacrifice. And out of polite deference, without uttering the harsh words of outright refusal, he deflected their proposal on another pretext. But they, having found an opportunity in the course of a discussion on <s>dharma</s>, not understanding the depth-concealed disposition of his mind, again urged the king toward performing the sacrifice:

children.text: kāryāṇi rājñāṃ niyatāni yāni lābhe pṛthivyāḥ paripālane ca /
children.translated_text: 'The duties of kings that are fixed — in the acquisition and protection of the earth —

children.text: nātyeti kālas tava tāni nityaṃ teṣāṃ kramo dharmasukhāni yadvat // AJm_10.4 //
children.translated_text: time does not transgress these, O king, ever; the sequence of these [duties brings] the pleasures of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: trivargasevānipuṇasya tasya prajāhitārthaṃ dhṛtakārmukasya /
children.translated_text: For one skilled in the pursuit of the three aims (<s>trivarga</s>), who bears the bow for the welfare of his subjects —

children.text: yajñābhidhāne suralokasetau pramādatantreva kathaṃ matis te // AJm_10.5 //
children.translated_text: how is it that your mind seems negligent regarding the sacrifice, [which is] the bridge to the world of the gods?

children.text: bhṛtyair ivājñā bahumanyate te sākṣād iyaṃ siddhir iti kṣitīśaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Your command is honored by [your] servants as if it were direct accomplishment itself by kings.

children.text: śreyāṃsi kīrtijvalitāni cetuṃ yajñair ayaṃ te ripukāla kālaḥ // AJm_10.6 //
children.translated_text: This is the time for you, O subduer of enemies, to reap glories blazing with fame through sacrifices.

children.text: kāmaṃ sadā dīkṣita eva ca tvaṃ dānaprasaṅgān niyamādarāc ca /
children.translated_text: Indeed, you are always consecrated, as it were, through the occasions of giving and through devotion to restraints.

children.text: vedaprasiddhaiḥ kratubhis tathāpi yuktaṃ bhaven moktum ṛṇaṃ surāṇām // AJm_10.7 //
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, it would be fitting to repay the debt to the gods through sacrifices renowned in the <s>Vedas</s>.

children.text: sviṣṭyābhituṣṭāni hi daivatāni bhūtāni vṛṣṭyā pratimānayanti /
children.translated_text: For the deities, gratified by proper offerings, repay beings with rain;

children.text: iti prajānāṃ hitam ātmanaś ca yaśaskaraṃ yajñavidhiṃ juṣasva // AJm_10.8 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, embrace the sacrificial rite that brings welfare to the subjects, benefit to yourself, and renown.

body.text: tasya cintā prādurabhavat / atidurnyasto batāyaṃ parapratyayahāryapelavamatir amīmāṃsako dharmapriyaśraddadhāno jano yatra hi nāma
body.translated_text: A thought arose in him: 'Alas, how badly misled are these people, whose feeble minds are swayed by the assertions of others, who do not investigate, who believe simply out of affection for <s>dharma</s>—for indeed—'

children.text: ya eva lokeṣu śaraṇyasaṃmatās ta eva hiṃsām api dharmato gatāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Those very ones who are regarded in the world as worthy of refuge have themselves sanctioned violence as <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: vivartate kaṣṭam apāyasaṃkaṭe janas tadādeśitakāpathānugaḥ // AJm_10.9 //
children.translated_text: Alas, the people, following the wrong path prescribed by them, turn toward the perilous straits of misfortune.'

children.text: ko hi nāmābhisaṃbandho dharmasya paśuhiṃsayā /
children.translated_text: 'For what connection could there be between <s>dharma</s> and the slaughter of animals,

children.text: suralokādhivāsasya daivataprīṇanasya vā // AJm_10.10 //
children.translated_text: Or between residence in the world of the gods and the pleasing of deities?'

children.text: viśasyamānaḥ kila mantraśaktibhiḥ paśur divaṃ gacchati tena tadvadhaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The animal, being slaughtered by the power of <s>mantras</s>, supposedly goes to heaven—therefore its killing

children.text: upaiti dharmatvam itīdam apy asat paraiḥ kṛtaṃ ko hi paratra lapsyate // AJm_10.11 //
children.translated_text: Attains the status of <s>dharma</s>—this too is false; for who will reap in the next world what has been done by others?'

children.text: asatpravṛtter anivṛttamānasaḥ śubheṣu karmasv avirūḍhaniścayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'One whose mind has not turned away from evil conduct, who has no firm resolve for virtuous deeds—

children.text: paśur divaṃ yāsyati kena hetunā hato 'pi yajñe svakṛtāśrayaṃ vinā // AJm_10.12 //
children.translated_text: By what reason would an animal go to heaven, even though slain in sacrifice, without the support of its own [good] deeds?'

children.text: hataś ca yajñe tridivaṃ yadi vrajen nanu vrajeyuḥ paśutāṃ svayaṃ dvijāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And if one slain in sacrifice would go to the triple heaven, would not the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> themselves seek to become sacrificial animals?

children.text: yatas tu nāyaṃ vidhir īkṣyate kva cid vacas tad eṣāṃ ka iva grahīṣyati // AJm_10.13 //
children.translated_text: But since this practice is nowhere observed, who indeed would accept their words?'

children.text: atulyagandharddhirasaujasaṃ śubhāṃ sudhāṃ kilotsṛjya varāpsarodhṛtām /
children.translated_text: 'Having supposedly abandoned the auspicious <s>sudhā</s> (nectar), incomparable in fragrance, splendor, taste, and potency, borne by the finest <s>Apsarases</s>,

children.text: mudaṃ prayāsyanti vapādikāraṇād vadhena śocyasya paśor divaukasaḥ // AJm_10.14 //
children.translated_text: Would the celestial beings find delight on account of fat and the like from the slaughter of a pitiable animal?'

body.text: tad idam atra prāptakālam iti viniścitya sa rājā yajñārambhasamutsuka iva nāma tat teṣāṃ vacanaṃ pratigṛhyāvocad enān / sanāthaḥ khalv aham anugrahavāṃś ca yad evaṃ me hitāvahitamanaso 'trabhavantaḥ / tad icchāmi puruṣamedhasahasreṇa yaṣṭum / anuśiṣyantāṃ tadupayogyasaṃbhārasamudānayanārthaṃ yathādhikāram amātyāḥ / parīkṣyatāṃ sattrāgāraniveśayogyo bhūmipradeśas tadanuguṇaś ca tithikaraṇamuhūrtanakṣatrayoga iti // athainaṃ purohita uvāca / īpsitārthasaṃpattaye snātu tāvan mahārāja ekasya yajñasyāvabhṛthe / athottareṣām ārambhaḥ kariṣyate krameṇa / yugapat puruṣapaśavaḥ sahasraśo hi parigṛhyamāṇā vyaktam udvegadoṣāya prajānāṃ te syur iti // asty etad iti ca brāhmaṇair uktaḥ sa rājā tān uvāca / alam atrabhavatāṃ prakṛtikopāśaṅkayā / tathāhaṃ saṃvidhāsye yathodvegaṃ me prajā na prayāsyantīti // atha sa rājā paurajānapadān saṃnipātyābravīt / icchāmi puruṣamedhasahasreṇa yaṣṭum / na ca mayā śakyaḥ kaś cid akāmaḥ paśutve niyoktum aduṣṭaḥ / tad yaṃ yam aham itaḥ prabhṛti vo drakṣyāmi vyavadhūtapramādanidreṇa vimalena cāracakṣuṣā śīlamaryādātivartinam asmadājñāṃ paribhavantaṃ taṃ taṃ svakulapaṃsakaṃ deśakaṇṭakam ahaṃ paśunimittam ādāsyāmīty etad vo viditam astv iti // atha teṣāṃ mukhyatamāḥ prāñjalaya enam ūcuḥ /
body.translated_text: Having determined 'This is the appropriate occasion for this,' that king, feigning eagerness to commence a sacrifice, accepted their words and said to them: 'I am indeed blessed and favored that your lordships have minds intent on my welfare. I wish to perform a sacrifice with a thousand human offerings (<s>puruṣamedha</s>). Let the ministers be instructed, each according to his office, to gather the requisite materials. Let a site of land suitable for the erection of the sacrificial hall be examined, along with a suitable conjunction of lunar day, astronomical division, auspicious moment, and stellar configuration.' Then the chief priest said to him: 'For the attainment of the desired goal, let the great king first bathe in the concluding ablution (<s>avabhṛtha</s>) of one sacrifice; then the commencement of the subsequent ones will proceed in order. For if human victims were seized by the thousands all at once, they would clearly cause the fault of panic among the subjects.' And when the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> agreed saying 'This is so,' the king said to them: 'Enough of your lordships' apprehension of popular revolt. I shall arrange things so that my subjects will not be driven to alarm.' Then that king, having assembled the townspeople and country folk, said: 'I wish to perform a sacrifice with a thousand human offerings. But I am unable to compel anyone unwilling and innocent to serve as a victim. Therefore, whoever I shall henceforth see with the stainless eye of surveillance that has shaken off the sleep of negligence—anyone transgressing the boundaries of moral conduct, anyone defying my command—that disgrace to his family, that thorn of the realm, I shall seize as a sacrificial victim. Let this be known to you.' Then the foremost among them, with joined palms, said to him:

children.text: sarvāḥ kriyās tava hitapravaṇāḥ prajānāṃ tatrāvamānanavidher naradeva ko 'rthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'All your deeds are devoted to the welfare of the subjects; what purpose would there be, O lord of men, in a rite of degradation?

children.text: brahmāpi te caritam abhyanumantum arhaḥ sādhupramāṇaparam atrabhavān pramāṇam // AJm_10.15 //
children.translated_text: Even <s>Brahmā</s> ought to approve your conduct; Your Lordship, who holds the authority of the virtuous as supreme, is our standard.'

children.text: priyaṃ yad eva devasya tad asmākam api priyam /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever is pleasing to the king is also pleasing to us;

children.text: asmatpriyahitād anyad dṛśyate na hi te priyam // AJm_10.16 //
children.translated_text: For nothing other than what is pleasing and beneficial for us appears to be pleasing to you.'

body.text: iti pratigṛhītavacanaḥ paurajānapadaiḥ sa rājā mahatā janaprakāśenāḍambareṇa pratyayitān amātyān pāpajanopagrahaṇārthaṃ janapadaṃ nagarāṇi ca preṣayām āsa / samantataś ca pratyaham iti ghoṣaṇāṃ kārayām āsa /
body.translated_text: Thus, his words accepted by the townspeople and country folk, that king with great public display and pomp dispatched trusted ministers to the countryside and cities for the apprehension of wrongdoers, and had the following proclamation made daily in all directions:

children.text: abhayam abhayado dadāti rājā sthiraśuciśīladhanāya sajjanāya /
children.translated_text: 'The king, giver of safety, grants safety to the good people whose wealth is firm, pure moral conduct;

children.text: avinayanirataiḥ prajāhitārthaṃ narapaśubhis tu sahasraśo yiyakṣuḥ // AJm_10.17 //
children.translated_text: But with human victims devoted to misconduct, he wishes to sacrifice by the thousands for the welfare of the people.'

children.text: tad yaḥ kaś cid itaḥ prabhṛty avinayaślāghānuvṛttyuddhavāt sāmantakṣitipārcitām api nṛpasyājñām avajñāsyati /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, whoever from this day forward, out of arrogance born of habitual devotion to indiscipline, shall disregard the king's command—honored even by vassal rulers—

children.text: sa svair eva viṣahya yajñapaśutām āpāditaḥ karmabhir yūpābaddhatanur viṣādakṛpaṇaḥ śuṣyañ janair drakṣyate // AJm_10.18 //
children.translated_text: He, brought to the status of a sacrificial victim by his own deeds, his body bound to the sacrificial post, will be seen by the people drying up, wretched with despair.'

body.text: atha tadviṣayanivāsinaḥ puruṣā yajñapaśunimittaṃ duḥśīlapuruṣānveṣaṇādaram avekṣya rājñas tāṃ ca ghoṣaṇām atibhīṣaṇāṃ pratyaham upaśṛṇvantaḥ pāpajanopagrahāvahitāṃś ca rājapuruṣān samantataḥ samāpatato 'bhivīkṣya tyaktadauḥśīlyānurāgāḥ śīlasaṃvarasamādānaparā vairaprasaṅgaparāṅmukhāḥ parasparapremagauravasumukhāḥ praśāntavigrahavivādā gurujanavacanānuvartinaḥ saṃvibhāgaviśāradāḥ priyātithayo vinayanaibhṛtyaślāghinaḥ kṛtayuga iva babhūvuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the men dwelling in that realm, observing the king's eagerness in searching for men of bad conduct as sacrificial victims, hearing daily that most terrifying proclamation, and seeing the king's men vigilant in apprehending wrongdoers arriving from all directions, abandoned their attachment to misconduct, became devoted to the undertaking of moral restraint (<s>śīlasaṃvara</s>), turned away from occasions of enmity, showed mutual love and respect, became peaceful in conflicts and disputes, obedient to the words of elders, skilled in sharing, hospitable to guests, and proud of their discipline and modesty—as if the <s>Kṛtayuga</s> (Golden Age) had come.

children.text: bhayena mṛtyoḥ paralokacintayā kulābhimānena yaśo'nurakṣayā /
children.translated_text: Through fear of death, through concern for the next world, through family pride, through the preservation of honor,

children.text: suśuklabhāvāc ca virūḍhayā hriyā janaḥ svaśīlāmalabhūṣaṇo 'bhavat // AJm_10.19 //
children.translated_text: And through a sense of shame that grew from their genuinely pure disposition, the people became adorned with the purity of their own moral conduct.

children.text: yathā yathā dharmaparo 'bhavaj janas tathā tathā rakṣijano viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: The more the people became devoted to <s>dharma</s>, the more zealously the king's officers

children.text: cakāra duḥśīlajanābhimārgaṇām ataś ca dharmān na cacāla kaś ca na // AJm_10.20 //
children.translated_text: Conducted their search for men of bad conduct; and therefore no one at all strayed from <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: svadeśavṛttāntam athopaśuśruvān imaṃ nṛpaḥ prītiviśeṣabhūṣaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the king, hearing this account of his own realm, adorned with exceptional joy,

children.text: carān priyākhyānakadānavistaraiḥ sa tarpayitvā sacivān samanvaśāt // AJm_10.21 //
children.translated_text: Having gratified his spies with generous gifts of pleasing rewards, instructed his ministers:

children.text: parā manīṣā mama rakṣituṃ prajā gatāś ca tāḥ saṃprati dakṣiṇīyatām /
children.translated_text: 'My supreme intention was to protect the subjects, and they have now attained the status of being worthy of gifts;

children.text: idaṃ ca yajñāya dhanaṃ prakalpitaṃ yiyakṣur asmīti yathāpratarkitam // AJm_10.22 //
children.translated_text: And this wealth was prepared for the sacrifice, just as was conjectured by my declaration "I wish to sacrifice."'

children.text: yad īpsitaṃ yasya sukhendhanaṃ dhanaṃ prakāmam āpnotu sa tan madantikāt /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever wealth each person desires, that fuel for happiness, let him obtain it abundantly from me;

children.text: itīyam asmadviṣayopatāpinī daridratā nirviṣayī bhaved yathā // AJm_10.23 //
children.translated_text: So that this poverty, which torments the inhabitants of my realm, may be rendered without object.'

children.text: mayi prajārakṣaṇaniścayasthite sahāyasaṃpatparivṛddhasādhane /
children.translated_text: 'When I stand firm in my resolve to protect the subjects, with the means augmented by the wealth of allies,

children.text: iyaṃ janārtir madamarṣadīpanī muhur muhur me jvalatīva cetasi // AJm_10.24 //
children.translated_text: This suffering of the people, inflaming my indignation, blazes again and again, as it were, in my heart.'

body.text: atha

children.text: te
children.translated_text: those

children.text: tasya rājñaḥ sacivāḥ param iti pratigṛhya tadvacanaṃ sarveṣu grāmanagaranigameṣu mārgaviśrāmapradeśeṣu ca dānaśālāḥ kārayitvā yathāsaṃdiṣṭaṃ rājñā pratyaham arthijanam abhilaṣitair arthaiḥ saṃtarpayām āsuḥ /
children.translated_text: ministers of that king, accepting his words with 'So be it,' having had gift-halls constructed in all villages, cities, market-towns, and at road-side resting places, satisfied the supplicants daily with their desired objects as instructed by the king.

body.translated_text: Then

children.text: atha vihāya janaḥ sa daridratāṃ samam avāptavasur vasudhādhipāt /
children.translated_text: Then the people, having abandoned their poverty, having obtained wealth equally from the lord of the earth,

children.text: vividhacitraparicchadabhūṣaṇaḥ pravitatotsavaśobha ivābhavat // AJm_10.25 //
children.translated_text: Adorned with various splendid possessions and ornaments, became as if resplendent with a widespread festival.

children.text: pramuditārthijanastutivistṛtaṃ pravitatāna nṛpasya diśo yaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: The king's fame, spread wide by the praises of the joyful supplicants, extended over all the directions,

children.text: tanutaraṃgavivardhitavistaraṃ sara ivāmbujakesarajaṃ rajaḥ // AJm_10.26 //
children.translated_text: Like the pollen of lotuses from a lake, its expanse increased by gentle waves.

body.text: iti nṛpasya sunītiguṇāśrayāt sucaritābhimukhe nikhile jane samabhibhūtabalāḥ kuśalocchrayair vilayam īyur asaṅgam upadravāḥ // AJm_10.27 //
body.translated_text: Thus, through the shelter of the king's excellent policy and virtue, when all the people turned toward righteous conduct, calamities, their power completely overcome by the rise of good fortune, dissolved without resistance.

children.text: aviṣamatvasukhā ṛtavo 'bhavan navanṛpā iva dharmaparāyaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: The seasons became pleasant in their regularity, like new kings devoted to <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: vividhasasyadharā ca vasuṃdharā sakamalāmalanīlajalāśayā // AJm_10.28 //
children.translated_text: And the earth bore various crops, with lakes of clear blue water adorned with lotuses.

children.text: na janam abhyarujan prabalā rujaḥ paṭutaraṃ guṇam oṣadhayo dadhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Powerful diseases did not afflict the people; medicinal herbs yielded more potent qualities;

children.text: ṛtuvaśena vavau niyato 'nilaḥ pariyayuś ca śubhena pathā grahāḥ // AJm_10.29 //
children.translated_text: The wind blew regularly according to the seasons, and the planets moved in auspicious courses.

children.text: na paracakrakṛtaṃ samabhūd bhayaṃ na ca parasparajaṃ na ca daivikam /
children.translated_text: There was no fear caused by foreign armies, nor mutual conflict, nor divine calamity;

children.text: niyamadharmapare nibhṛte jane kṛtam ivātra yugaṃ samapadyata // AJm_10.30 //
children.translated_text: With the people devoted to the <s>dharma</s> of self-restraint and tranquil, a <s>Kṛtayuga</s> (Golden Age), as it were, came to pass.

body.text: athaivaṃ pravṛttena dharmayajñena rājñā praśamiteṣv arthijanaduḥkheṣu sārdham upadravaiḥ pramuditajanasaṃbādhāyām abhyudayaramyadarśanāyāṃ ca vasuṃdharāyāṃ nṛpater āśīrvacanādhyayanasavyāpāre loke vitanyamāne samantato rājayaśasi prasādāvarjitamatiḥ kaś cid amātyamukhyo rājānam ity uvāca / suṣṭhu khalv idam ucyate /
body.translated_text: Then, when the king through this <s>dharmayajña</s> (sacrifice of righteousness) thus carried out had pacified the sufferings of supplicants along with all calamities, when the earth was thronging with joyful people and delightful to behold in its prosperity, when the world was occupied with reciting benedictions and praises for the king, and when royal fame was being extended in all directions—a certain chief minister, his mind won over by the king's grace, spoke thus to the king: 'How truly is it said—'

children.text: uttamādhamamadhyānāṃ kāryāṇāṃ nityadarśanāt /
children.translated_text: 'From constant observation of affairs high, low, and middling,

children.text: upary upari buddhīnāṃ carantīśvarabuddhayaḥ // AJm_10.31 //
children.translated_text: The minds of rulers move ever higher and higher.'

body.text: iti devena hi paśuvaiśasavācyadoṣavirahitena dharmayajñena prajānām ubhayalokahitaṃ saṃpāditam upadravāś ca praśamitā dāridryaduḥkhāni ca / kiṃ bahunā / sabhāgyās tāḥ prajāḥ /
body.translated_text: 'For by Your Majesty, through this <s>dharmayajña</s> (sacrifice of righteousness) free from the censurable fault of animal slaughter, the welfare of the subjects in both worlds has been accomplished, calamities have been pacified, and the sufferings of poverty removed. What more need be said? Those subjects are fortunate indeed.'

children.text: lakṣmeva kṣaṇadākarasya vitataṃ gātre na kṛṣṇājinaṃ dīkṣāyantraṇayā nisargalalitāś ceṣṭā na mandodyamāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Like the beauty of the moon spread upon your body, you wear no black antelope skin; by the restraint of <s>dīkṣā</s> (consecration), your naturally graceful movements are not rendered slow in effort;

children.text: mūrdhnaś chattranibhasya keśaracanāśobhā tathaivātha ca tyāgais te śatayajvano 'py apahṛtaḥ kīrtyāśrayo vismayaḥ // AJm_10.32 //
children.translated_text: The beauty of the hair-arrangement on your head, which resembles a parasol, remains the same; and by your generosity, the wonder that rests on the fame of even those who have performed a hundred sacrifices has been surpassed.'

children.text: hiṃsāviṣaktaḥ kṛpaṇaḥ phalepsoḥ prāyeṇa lokasya nayajña yajñaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'O knower of <s>nīti</s> (policy), the sacrifice of the world, mostly tainted by violence, is pitiable for one desiring its fruits;

children.text: yajñas tu kīrtyābharaṇaḥ samas te śīlasya nirdoṣamanoharasya // AJm_10.33 //
children.translated_text: But your sacrifice, adorned with fame, is the equal of your faultlessly charming moral conduct.'

children.text: aho prajānāṃ bhāgyāni yāsāṃ gopāyitā bhavān /
children.translated_text: 'Oh, the fortunes of those subjects whose protector you are!

children.text: prajānām api hi vyaktaṃ naivaṃ syād gopitā pitā // AJm_10.34 //
children.translated_text: For clearly, not even a father protecting his children would care for them thus.'

body.text: apara uvāca /
body.translated_text: Another minister said:

children.text: dānaṃ nāma dhanodaye sati jano datte tadāśāvaśaḥ syāc chīle 'pi ca lokapaktyabhimukhaḥ svarge ca jātaspṛhaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'When wealth is abundant, a person gives gifts, impelled by its expectation; and even in moral conduct, one may be oriented toward public approval and longing for heaven;

children.text: yā tv eṣā parakāryadakṣiṇatayā tvadvat pravṛttis tayor nāvidvatsu na sattvayogavidhureṣv eṣā samālakṣyate // AJm_10.35 //
children.translated_text: But this kind of activity, marked by skill in serving others' welfare as in your case—this is not observed either among the unwise or among those devoid of spiritual strength.'

body.text: tad evaṃ na kalyāṇāśayāḥ pāpapratāraṇām anuvidhīyanta ity āśayaśuddhau yatitavyam //
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, one should understand that those of virtuous disposition do not follow the deception of evil; thus one should strive for purity of intention.'

children.text: iti prajāhitodyogaḥ śreyaḥkīrtisukhāvahaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, the exertion for the welfare of subjects, bringing spiritual good, fame, and happiness,

children.text: yan nṛpāṇām ato nālaṃ tam anādṛtya vartitum // AJm_10.36 //
children.translated_text: Is something that kings ought not to conduct themselves while disregarding.

body.text: evaṃ rājāvavāde 'pi vācyam / dharmābhyāsaḥ prajānāṃ bhūtim āvahatīti dharmānuvartinā bhūtikāmena bhavitavyam ity evam apy upaneyam // na paśuhiṃsā kadā cid abhyudayāya dānadamasaṃyamādayas tv abhyudayāyeti tadarthinā dānādipareṇa bhavitavyam ity evam api vācyam // lokārthacaryāpravaṇamatir evaṃ pūrvajanmasv api sa bhagavān iti tathāgatavarṇe 'pi vācyam //
body.translated_text: Thus, in admonishing kings too, it should be said: 'The practice of <s>dharma</s> brings prosperity to the subjects; therefore, one who desires prosperity should follow <s>dharma</s>'—this too should be impressed upon them. 'The slaughter of animals never leads to prosperity; rather, generosity, self-control, restraint, and the like lead to prosperity; therefore one who seeks prosperity should be devoted to generosity and the rest'—this too should be stated. 'The Blessed One, even in his former births, was inclined in mind toward conduct for the welfare of the world'—this should also be stated in praise of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: yajñajātakaṃ daśamam //
body.translated_text: The <s>Yajñajātaka</s> (Sacrifice Birth-Story), the tenth.

body.text: uddānam //
body.translated_text: Recapitulation (<s>uddāna</s>):

children.text: vyāghrī śibiḥ kośaleśaḥ śreṣṭhinau śaśa eva ca /
children.translated_text: The tigress, <s>Śibi</s>, the king of <s>Kośala</s>, the two merchants, and the hare,

children.text: agastyamāṃsadau viśvantarayajñavidau tathā //
children.translated_text: <s>Agastya</s>, the giver of flesh, <s>Viśvantara</s>, and the two knowers of sacrifice likewise.

body.text: prathamo vargaḥ //
body.translated_text: The first section.

children.text: 11. Śakrajātakam
children.translated_text: 11. <s>Śakrajātaka</s> (The Birth-Story of <s>Śakra</s>)

body.text: āpad api mahātmanām aiśvaryasaṃpad vā sattveṣv anukampāṃ na śithilīkaroti //
body.translated_text: Neither adversity nor the prosperity of sovereignty slackens the compassion of great beings toward living creatures.

body.text: tadyathānuśrūyate / bodhisattvaḥ kilānalpakālasvabhyastapuṇyakarmā sātmībhūtapradānadamasaṃyamakaruṇaḥ parahitaniratakriyātiśayaḥ kadā cic chakro devānām indro babhūva //
body.translated_text: As is heard in tradition: the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, whose merit and good deeds had been practiced for no small time, for whom generosity, self-control, restraint, and compassion had become second nature, and whose exceptional deeds were devoted to the welfare of others, once became <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Indra</s> of the gods.

children.text: surendralakṣmīr adhikaṃ rarāja tatsaṃśrayāt sphītataraprabhāvā /
children.translated_text: The glory of <s>Surendra</s> (Lord of the Gods) shone all the more, its splendor augmented by his presence,

children.text: harmye sudhāsekanavāṅgarāge niṣaktarūpā śaśinaḥ prabheva // AJm_11.1 //
children.translated_text: her form fixed upon the palace with its fresh whitewash-coating, like the radiance of the moon. [AJm 11.1]

children.text: yasyāḥ kṛte ditisutā rabhasāgatāni diṅnāgadantamusalāny urasābhijagmuḥ /
children.translated_text: For whose sake the sons of <s>Diti</s> (demons) bore upon their chests the tusk-pestle-blows of the elephants of the directions, rushing in fury —

children.text: sā bhāgyavistarasukhopanatāpi tasya lakṣmīr na darpamalinaṃ hṛdayaṃ cakāra // AJm_11.2 //
children.translated_text: yet that <s>Lakṣmī</s> (royal fortune), though brought to him by the vastness of his good fortune and happiness, did not make his heart tainted with pride. [AJm 11.2]

body.text: tasya divaspṛthivyoḥ samyakparipālanopārjitāṃ sarvalokāntavyāpinīṃ kīrtisaṃpadaṃ tāṃ ca lakṣmīm atyadbhutām amṛṣyamāṇā daityagaṇāḥ kalpanāṭopabhīṣaṇataradviradarathaturagapadātinā kṣubhitasāgaraghoranirghoṣeṇa jājvalyamānavimalapraharaṇāvaraṇadurnirīkṣyeṇa mahatā balakāyena yuddhāyainam abhijagmuḥ /
body.translated_text: Unable to endure his fame, extending to the ends of all worlds, won by the proper protection of heaven and earth, and that most extraordinary <s>Lakṣmī</s> — the hosts of <s>Daityas</s> (demons), with an army terrifying in its martial array of elephants, chariots, horses, and infantry, with a roar as terrible as the agitated ocean, with gleaming weapons and armor difficult to withstand —

children.text: dharmātmano 'pi tu sa tasya parāvalepaḥ krīḍāvighātavirasaṃ ca bhayaṃ janasya /
children.translated_text: but even for that righteous-souled one, the arrogance of his foes, the fear of the people that spoiled the joy of their pastimes,

children.text: tejasvitānayapathopanataḥ kramaś ca yuddhoddhavābhimukhatāṃ hṛdayasya cakruḥ // AJm_11.3 //
children.translated_text: and the course of events that presented themselves on the path of valor and policy — these turned his heart toward readiness for battle. [AJm 11.3]
