body.text: atha sa mahāsattvas turagavarasahasrayuktam abhyucchritārhadvasanacihnaruciradhvajaṃ vividhamaṇiratnadīptivyavabhāsitam abhijvaladvapuṣaṃ kalpanāvibhāgopaniyataniśitajvalitavividhāyudhavirājitobhayapārśvaṃ pāṇḍukambalinaṃ haimaṃ rathavaram abhiruhya mahatā hastyaśvarathapadāticitreṇa devānīkena parivṛtas tad asurasainyaṃ samudratīrānta eva pratyujjagāma //
body.translated_text: Then that great being, mounting a supreme golden chariot yoked with a thousand excellent horses, with a beautiful banner bearing the mark of worthy garments raised high, illuminated by the radiance of various gems and jewels, its body blazing, with both sides adorned with various sharp and gleaming weapons arranged in battle-formation, with a pale woolen covering —

children.text: atha pravavṛte tatra bhīrūṇāṃ dhṛtidāraṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: then there commenced a battle that shattered the composure of the timid,

children.text: anyonyāyudhaniṣpeṣajarjarāvaraṇo raṇaḥ // AJm_11.4 //
children.translated_text: with armor battered by the mutual clash of weapons. [AJm 11.4]

children.text: tiṣṭha naivaṃ itaḥ paśya kvedānīṃ mama mokṣyase /
children.translated_text: "Stand! Not this way! Look here! Where will you escape from me now?

children.text: praharāyaṃ na bhavasīty evaṃ te 'nyonyam ārdayan // AJm_11.5 //
children.translated_text: Strike! You are no [match for me]!" — thus they tormented one another. [AJm 11.5]

children.text: tataḥ pravṛtte tumule sphūrjatpraharaṇe raṇe /
children.translated_text: Then, in the tumultuous battle with flashing weapons,

children.text: paṭahadhvanitotkruṣṭaiḥ phalatīva nabhastale // AJm_11.6 //
children.translated_text: with the cries and shouts raised above the sound of war-drums, the sky seemed to split. [AJm 11.6]

children.text: dānagandhoddhatāmarṣeṣv āpatatsu parasparam /
children.translated_text: As the elephants charged at each other, their fury stirred by the scent of rut,

children.text: yugāntavātākalitaśailabhīmeṣu dantiṣu // AJm_11.7 //
children.translated_text: terrible as mountains tossed by the winds at the end of an age — [AJm 11.7]

children.text: vidyullolapatākeṣu prasṛteṣu samantataḥ /
children.translated_text: as the chariots advanced on all sides, their banners waving like lightning,

children.text: ratheṣu paṭunirghoṣeṣūtpātāmbudhareṣv iva // AJm_11.8 //
children.translated_text: their sharp roar like portent-bearing storm-clouds — [AJm 11.8]

children.text: pātyamānadhvajacchattraśastrāvaraṇamauliṣu /
children.translated_text: as the heroes of gods and <s>Dānavas</s>, their banners, parasols, weapons, armor, and crowns being struck down

children.text: devadānavavīreṣu śitair anyonyasāyakaiḥ // AJm_11.9 //
children.translated_text: by each other's sharp arrows — [AJm 11.9]

children.text: atha prataptā suraśatrusāyakair bhayāt pradudrāva surendravāhinī /
children.translated_text: then, scorched by the arrows of the enemies of the gods, the army of the lord of the gods fled in fear;

children.text: rathena viṣṭabhya balaṃ tu vidviṣāṃ surendra ekaḥ samare vyatiṣṭhata // AJm_11.10 //
children.translated_text: but the lord of the gods alone, restraining the enemy's forces with his chariot, stood firm in battle. [AJm 11.10]

body.text: atyudīrṇaṃ tv āsuraṃ balam atiharṣāt paṭutarotkruṣṭakṣveḍitasiṃhanādam abhipatad abhivīkṣya mātalir devendrasārathiḥ svaṃ ca balaṃ palāyanaparāyaṇam avetyāpayānam atra prāptakālam iti devādhipateḥ syandanam āvartayām āsa // atha śakro devendraḥ samutpatato rathasyeṣāgrābhimukhāny abhighātapathagatāni śālmalivṛkṣe garuḍanīḍāny apaśyat / dṛṣṭvaiva ca karuṇayā samālambyamānahṛdayo mātaliṃ saṃgrāhakam ity uvāca /
body.translated_text: But seeing the army of the <s>Asuras</s>, greatly swollen, rushing forward with even sharper battle-cries, war-whoops, and lion-roars from their excess of joy — and perceiving that his own forces were bent on flight — <s>Mātali</s>, the charioteer of the lord of the gods, thinking 'retreat is now timely,' turned the chariot of the lord of the gods around. Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, with surging —

children.text: ajātapakṣadvijapotasaṃkulā dvijālayāḥ śālmalipādapāśrayāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Teeming with fledgling chicks whose wings have not yet grown, these bird-nests sheltered in the <s>śālmali</s> (silk-cotton) trees —

children.text: amī pateyur na yathā ratheṣayā vicūrṇitā vāhaya me rathaṃ tathā // AJm_11.11 //
children.translated_text: drive my chariot so that they may not fall, crushed by the chariot-pole!" [AJm 11.11]

body.text: mātalir uvāca / amī tāvan mārṣa samabhiyānti no daityā iti // śakra uvāca/ tataḥ kim / parihara pariharaitāni samyag garuḍanīḍānīti // athainaṃ mātaliḥ punar uvāca /
body.translated_text: <s>Mātali</s> said: 'But sir, those <s>Daityas</s> are advancing upon us!' <s>Śakra</s> said: 'What of it? Avoid, carefully avoid these <s>Garuḍa</s>-nests!' Then <s>Mātali</s> spoke to him again:

children.text: nivartanād asya rathasya kevalaṃ śivaṃ bhaved amburuhākṣa pakṣiṇām /
children.translated_text: "By merely turning this chariot around, there would be safety for the birds, O lotus-eyed one;

children.text: cirasya labdhaprasarā sureṣv asāv abhidravaty eva hi no dviṣaccamūḥ // AJm_11.12 //
children.translated_text: but that enemy army, having long gained free rein against the gods, will certainly rush upon us." [AJm 11.12]

body.text: atha śakro devendraḥ svam adhyāśayātiśayaṃ sattvaviśeṣaṃ ca kāruṇyavaśāt prakāśayann uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, revealing the excellence of his resolution and the distinction of his courage, out of compassion, spoke:

children.text: tasmān nivartaya rathaṃ varam eva mṛtyur daityādhipaprahitabhīmagadābhighātaiḥ /
children.translated_text: "Therefore turn the chariot back! Better indeed is death from the terrible mace-blows dispatched by the lord of the <s>Daityas</s>,

children.text: dhigvādadagdhayaśaso na tu jīvitaṃ me sattvāny amūni bhayadīnamukhāni hatvā // AJm_11.13 //
children.translated_text: than a life with my fame burnt by reproach — [better death] than killing these creatures with their faces wretched with fear!" [AJm 11.13]

body.text: atha mātalis tatheti pratiśrutya turagasahasrayuktaṃ syandanam asya nivartayām āsa /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mātali</s>, having replied 'So be it,' turned the chariot yoked with a thousand horses back.

children.text: dṛṣṭāvadānā ripavas tu tasya yuddhe samālokya rathaṃ nivṛttam /
children.translated_text: But the enemies, whose valor was well-known, seeing his chariot turn back in battle,

children.text: bhayadrutapraskhalitāḥ praṇeśur vātābhinunnā iva kālameghāḥ // AJm_11.14 //
children.translated_text: fled stumbling in terrified haste, like dark clouds driven by the wind. [AJm 11.14]

children.text: bhagne svasainye 'pi nivartamānaḥ panthānam āvṛtya ripudhvajinyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Though his own army was broken, as he turned back, blocking the path of the enemy's forces,

children.text: saṃkocayaty eva madāvalepam eko 'pi saṃbhāvyaparākramatvāt // AJm_11.15 //
children.translated_text: he alone, by the worth of his expected valor, caused their arrogant pride to contract. [AJm 11.15]

children.text: nirīkṣya bhagnaṃ tu balaṃ tad āsuraṃ surendrasenāpy atha sā nyavartata /
children.translated_text: Then, seeing that <s>Asura</s> army broken, the army of the lord of the gods also turned back;

children.text: babhūva naiva praṇayaḥ suradviṣāṃ bhayadrutānāṃ vinivartituṃ yataḥ // AJm_11.16 //
children.translated_text: for the god-hating ones, fleeing in terror, had no inclination to turn and stand. [AJm 11.16]

children.text: saharṣalajjais tridaśaiḥ surādhipaḥ sabhāyjamāno 'tha raṇājirāc chanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the lord of the gods, honored by the gods with joy and bashfulness, slowly from the battlefield,

children.text: abhijvalaccāruvapur jayaśriyā samutsukāntaḥpuram āgamat puram // AJm_11.17 //
children.translated_text: his beautiful body blazing with the glory of victory, entered the city, with the women of his inner apartments eager [to see him]. [AJm 11.17]

body.text: evaṃ sa eva tasya saṃgrāmavijayo babhūva / tasmād ucyate /
body.translated_text: Thus that very victory in battle was his. Therefore it is said:

children.text: pāpaṃ samācarati vītaghṛṇo jaghanyaḥ prāpyāpadaṃ saghṛṇa eva vimadhyabuddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: "A base person, devoid of compassion, commits sin; one of moderate understanding, though compassionate, does so when calamity strikes;

children.text: prāṇātyaye 'pi tu na sādhujanaḥ svavṛttaṃ velāṃ samudra iva laṅghayituṃ samarthaḥ // AJm_11.18 //
children.translated_text: but a virtuous person, even when life is at stake, is unable to transgress his own conduct — like the ocean its shore." [AJm 11.18]

body.text: tad evaṃ devarājyaṃ prāṇān api ca parityajya dīrgharātraṃ paripālitāni bhagavatā sattvāni / teṣv iha prājñasyāghāto 'pi na pratirūpaḥ prāg eva vipratipattir iti prāṇiṣu dayāpannenāryeṇa bhavitavyam // tathā hi dharmo ha vai rakṣati dharmacāriṇam ity atrāpy upaneyam // tathāgatavarṇe satkṛtya dharmaśravaṇe ceti //
body.translated_text: Thus <s>Bhagavān</s> protected beings for a long time, abandoning even his life and the sovereignty of the gods. For such beings, even a blow from a wise person is unfitting, much less actual hostility — therefore a noble person should be endowed with compassion toward living creatures. For indeed, '<s>Dharma</s> protects those who practice <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: śakrajātakam ekādaśam //
body.translated_text: This concludes the eleventh story, the <s>Śakra-jātaka</s>.

children.text: 12. Brāhmaṇajātakam
children.translated_text: 12. The <s>Brāhmaṇa-jātaka</s> (The Story of the Brahmin)

body.text: ātmalajjayaiva satpuruṣā nācāravelāṃ laṅghayanti //
body.translated_text: Noble persons do not transgress the bounds of proper conduct, out of self-respect alone.

body.text: tadyathānuśrūyate / bodhisattvaḥ kila kasmiṃś cid anupākruṣṭagotracāritre svadharmānuvṛttiprakāśayaśasi vinayācāraślāghini mahati brāhmaṇakule janmaparigrahaṃ cakāra / sa yathākramaṃ garbhādhānapuṃsavanasīmantonnayanajātakarmādibhiḥ kṛtasaṃskāro vedādhyayananimittaṃ śrutābhijanācārasaṃpanne gurau prativasati sma /
body.translated_text: Thus it is heard: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> took birth in a certain great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> family, whose lineage and conduct were unblemished, whose fame was bright with adherence to its own <s>dharma</s>, and which was praised for its disciplined behavior. He, in due course, having been consecrated with the sacraments of conception, male-producing rites, parting of the hair, birth-rites, and so forth — the <s>Vedas</s> —

children.text: tasya śrutagrahaṇadhāraṇapāṭavaṃ ca bhaktyanvayaś ca vinayaḥ svakulaprasiddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: His skill in hearing, grasping, and retaining [the scriptures], his devotion and disciplined conduct famous in his own family,

children.text: pūrve vayasy api śamābharaṇā sthitiś ca premaprasādasumukhaṃ gurum asya cakruḥ // AJm_12.1 //
children.translated_text: and his demeanor, adorned with tranquility even in early youth — these made his teacher disposed to him with affectionate pleasure. [AJm 12.1]

children.text: vaśīkaraṇamantrā hi nityam avyāhatā guṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: For virtues are spells of subjugation, perpetually unfailing —

children.text: api dveṣāgnitaptānāṃ kiṃ punaḥ svasthacetasām // AJm_12.2 //
children.translated_text: even for those whose [hearts] are scorched by the fire of hatred, how much more for those of sound mind! [AJm 12.2]

body.text: atha tasyādhyāpakaḥ sarveṣām eva śiṣyāṇāṃ śīlaparīkṣānimittaṃ svādhyāyaviśrāmakāleṣv ātmano dāridryaduḥkhāny abhīkṣṇam upavarṇayām āsa /
body.translated_text: Then his teacher, for the purpose of testing the moral character of all his students, during the intervals of study, repeatedly described the sufferings of his own poverty.

children.text: svajane 'pi nirākrandam utsave 'pi hatānandam /
children.translated_text: "Without lamentation even among one's own people, without joy even at festivals —

children.text: dhik pradānakathāmandaṃ dāridryam aphalacchandam // AJm_12.3 //
children.translated_text: cursed be poverty, sluggish even at the mention of giving, with desires that bear no fruit!" [AJm 12.3]

children.text: paribhavabhavanaṃ śramāspadaṃ sukhaparivarjitam atyanūrjitam /
children.translated_text: "A dwelling-place of humiliation, a site of toil, devoid of happiness, utterly feeble,

children.text: vyasanam iva sadaiva śocanaṃ dhanavikalatvam atīva dāruṇam // AJm_12.4 //
children.translated_text: always causing sorrow, like a calamity — the lack of wealth is extremely terrible." [AJm 12.4]

body.text: atha te śiṣyāḥ pratodasaṃcoditā iva sadaśvā gurusnehāt samupajātasaṃvegāḥ saṃpannataraṃ prabhūtataraṃ ca bhaikṣam upāharanti sma / sa tān uvāca / alam anenātrabhavatāṃ pariśrameṇa / na bhaikṣopahārāḥ kasya cid dāridryakṣāmatāṃ kṣapayanti / asmatparikleśāmarṣibhis tu bhavadbhir ayam eva yatno dhanāharaṇaṃ prati yuktaḥ kartuṃ syāt / kutaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then those students, like good horses goaded by a whip, out of affection for their teacher, stirred with a sense of urgency, began to bring more abundant and excellent alms. He said to them: 'Enough of this exertion on your part. Gifts of alms do not exhaust anyone's capacity to endure poverty. Consider this:'

children.text: kṣudham annaṃ jalaṃ tarṣaṃ mantravāk sāgadā gadān /
children.translated_text: "Food destroys hunger, water destroys thirst, incantation-words, like medicine, destroy diseases —

children.text: hanti dāridryaduḥkhaṃ tu saṃtatyārādhanaṃ dhanam // AJm_12.5 //
children.translated_text: but the suffering of poverty is destroyed only by wealth constantly cultivated." [AJm 12.5]

body.text: śiṣyā ūcuḥ / kiṃ kariṣyāmo mandabhāgyā yad etāvān naḥ śaktiprayāmaḥ / api ca /
body.translated_text: The students said: 'What shall we do, ill-fated as we are, when this is the limit of our ability? Moreover:'

children.text: bhaikṣavad yadi labhyerann upādhyāya dhanāny api /
children.translated_text: "If only wealth could be obtained as easily as alms, O teacher,

children.text: nedaṃ dāridryaduḥkhaṃ te vayam evaṃ sahemahi // AJm_12.6 //
children.translated_text: we would not endure your poverty-suffering in this way!" [AJm 12.6]

children.text: pratigrahakṛśopāyaṃ viprāṇāṃ hi dhanārjanam /
children.translated_text: "For the means of acquiring wealth for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are slender, limited to receiving gifts;

children.text: apradātā janaś cāyam ity agatyā hatā vayam // AJm_12.7 //
children.translated_text: and these people are unwilling to give — so we are helplessly ruined." [AJm 12.7]

body.text: adhyāpaka uvāca / santy anye 'pi brāhmaṇānāṃ śāstraparidṛṣṭā dhanārjanopāyāḥ / jarāpītasāmarthyās tu vayam ayogyarūpās tatpratipattau // śiṣyā ūcuḥ / vayam upādhyāya jarayānupahataparākramāḥ / tad yadi nas teṣāṃ śāstravihitānām upāyānāṃ pratipattisahatāṃ manyase tad ucyatām / yāvad adhyāpanapariśramasyānṛṇyaṃ te gacchāma iti // adhyāpaka uvāca / taruṇair api vyavasāyaśithilahṛdayair durabhisaṃbhavāḥ khalv evaṃvidhā dhanārjanopāyāḥ / yadi tv ayam atrabhavatāṃ nirbandhas tac chrūyatāṃ sādhu katama eko dhanārjanakramaḥ /
body.translated_text: The teacher said: 'There are also other means of wealth-acquisition for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, prescribed in the scriptures. But we, our strength drained by old age, are unfit for their practice.' The students said: 'We, teacher, have our valor unimpaired by old age. If you would instruct us in those scripture-prescribed means —'

children.text: āpaddharmaḥ steyam iṣṭaṃ dvijānām āpac cāntyā niḥsvatā nāma loke /
children.translated_text: "Theft is sanctioned as an emergency <s>dharma</s> for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>; and destitution is called the ultimate calamity in the world;

children.text: tenādeyaṃ svaṃ pareṣām adṛṣṭaiḥ sarvaṃ caitad brāhmaṇānāṃ svam eva // AJm_12.8 //
children.translated_text: therefore what belongs to others should be taken unseen; and all this indeed belongs to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>." [AJm 12.8]

children.text: kāmaṃ prasahyāpi dhanāni hartuṃ śaktir bhaved eva bhavadvidhānām /
children.translated_text: "To be sure, people like you would have the strength to seize wealth even by force;

children.text: na tv eṣa yogaḥ svayaśo hi rakṣyaṃ śūnyeṣu tasmād vyavaseyam evam // AJm_12.9 //
children.translated_text: but that method is not fitting, for one's own fame must be protected — therefore one should act thus in empty places." [AJm 12.9]

body.text: iti muktapragrahās tena te cchāttrāḥ param iti tat tasya vacanam ayuktam api yuktam iva pratyaśrauṣur anyatra bodhisattvāt /
body.translated_text: Thus given free rein by him, those students, except for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, assented to his words, however improper, as though proper, saying 'Very well!'

children.text: sa hi prakṛtibhadratvāt tan notsehe 'numoditum /
children.translated_text: For he, out of his naturally good disposition, could not bring himself to approve of it;

children.text: kṛtyavat pratipannaṃ tair vyāhartuṃ sahasaiva tu // AJm_12.10 //
children.translated_text: but neither could he immediately speak out against what they had accepted as a duty. [AJm 12.10]

body.text: vrīḍāvanatavadanas tu bodhisattvo mṛdu viniśvasya tūṣṇīmabhūt // atha sa teṣām adhyāpako bodhisattvam avekṣya taṃ vidhim anabhinandantam apratikrośantaṃ niviṣṭaguṇasaṃbhāvanas tasmin mahāsattve kiṃ nu khalv ayam avyavasitatvān niḥsnehatayā vā mayi steyaṃ na pratipadyate / uta dharmasaṃjñayeti samutpannavimarśas tatsvabhāvavyaktīkaraṇārthaṃ bodhisattvam uvāca / bho mahābrāhmaṇa /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, his face lowered in shame, sighing softly, remained silent. Then the teacher, observing the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who neither approved nor protested against that course, firmly convinced of the virtuous character of that great being, [thought]: 'Does this one, from indecisiveness or from lack of affection toward me —'

children.text: amī dvijā madvyasanāsahiṣṇavaḥ samāśritā vīramanuṣyapaddhatim /
children.translated_text: "These <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, unable to endure my affliction, have taken the path of valiant men;

children.text: bhavān anutsāhajaḍas tu lakṣyate na nūnam asmadvyasanena tapyate // AJm_12.11 //
children.translated_text: but you appear sluggish from lack of enterprise — surely you are not distressed by my misfortune!" [AJm 12.11]

children.text: pariprakāśe 'py anigūḍhavistare mayātmaduḥkhe vacasā vidarśite /
children.translated_text: "When my own suffering, plainly manifest and not concealed in its extent, has been displayed to you in words —

children.text: kathaṃ nu niḥsaṃbhramadhīramānaso bhavān iti svasthavad eva tiṣṭhati // AJm_12.12 //
children.translated_text: how is it that you, with mind untroubled and composed, stand as if at ease?" [AJm 12.12]

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ sasaṃbhramo 'bhivādyopādhyāyam uvāca / śāntaṃ pāpam / na khalv ahaṃ niḥsnehakaṭhinahṛdayatvād aparitapyamāno guruduḥkhair evam avasthitaḥ kiṃ tv asaṃbhavād upādhyāyapradarśitasya kramasya / na hi śakyam adṛśyamānena kva cit pāpam ācaritum / kutaḥ / raho'nupapatteḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, agitated, having bowed to his teacher, said: 'May evil be averted! It is not from a heartless and hard-hearted lack of compassion that I stand unmoved by the teacher's sufferings; rather, it is because the course shown by the teacher is impossible. For one cannot commit a sin where one is not seen —'

children.text: nāsti loke raho nāma pāpaṃ karma prakurvataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'There is no such thing as secrecy in the world for one who performs sinful deeds;

children.text: adṛśyāni hi paśyanti nanu bhūtāni mānuṣān // AJm_12.13 //
children.translated_text: For invisible beings surely see humans, do they not?'

children.text: kṛtātmānaś ca munayo divyonmiṣitacakṣuṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And self-perfected sages, whose eyes are opened to the divine,

children.text: tān apaśyan rahomānī bālaḥ pāpe pravartate // AJm_12.14 //
children.translated_text: The fool, who fancies himself in secret, commits sin without seeing them.'

children.text: ahaṃ punar na paśyāmi śūnyaṃ kva ca na kiṃ ca na /
children.translated_text: 'I, however, do not see anything anywhere as empty—

children.text: yatrāpy anyaṃ na paśyāmi nanv aśūnyaṃ mayaiva tat // AJm_12.15 //
children.translated_text: Even where I see no other, that very place is not empty, for I am there.'

children.text: pareṇa yac ca dṛśyate duṣkṛtaṃ svayam eva vā /
children.translated_text: 'And between a misdeed seen by another and one seen by oneself,

children.text: sudṛṣṭataram etat syād dṛśyate svayam eva yat // AJm_12.16 //
children.translated_text: That which is seen by oneself is far more clearly seen.'

children.text: svakāryaparyākulamānasatvāt paśyen na vānyaś caritaṃ parasya /
children.translated_text: 'Another person, his mind preoccupied with his own affairs, might not see one's conduct;

children.text: rāgārpitaikāgramatiḥ svayaṃ tu pāpaṃ prakurvan niyamena vetti // AJm_12.17 //
children.translated_text: But one whose concentrated mind is fixed upon passion, committing sin oneself, unfailingly knows it.'

body.text: tad anena kāraṇenāham evam avasthita iti / atha bodhisattvaḥ samabhiprasāditamanasam upādhyāyam avetya punar uvāca /
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, for this reason, I remain in this state.' Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, perceiving that his teacher's mind was delighted, spoke again:

children.text: na cātra me niścayam eti mānasaṃ dhanārtham evaṃ pratared bhavān iti /
children.translated_text: 'My mind cannot come to the conclusion that your honor would thus transgress for the sake of wealth;

children.text: avetya ko nāma guṇāguṇāntaraṃ guṇopamardaṃ dhanamūlyatāṃ nayet // AJm_12.18 //
children.translated_text: For who, knowing the difference between virtue and vice, would lead virtue to destruction for the price of money?'

body.text: svābhiprāyaṃ ca khalu nivedayāmi /
body.translated_text: 'And I shall declare my own intention:'

children.text: kapālam ādāya vipannavāsasā varaṃ dviṣadveśmasamṛddhir īkṣitā /
children.translated_text: 'Better to take a begging bowl and wear tattered clothes, beholding the prosperity of an enemy's house,

children.text: vyatītya lajjāṃ na tu dharmavaiśase surendratārthe 'py upasaṃhṛtaṃ manaḥ // AJm_12.19 //
children.translated_text: Than to abandon shame—never should the mind be drawn into the slaughter of <s>dharma</s>, even for the sake of the lord of gods.'

body.text: atha sa tasyopādhyāyaḥ praharṣavismayākṣiptahṛdaya utthāyāsanāt saṃpariṣvajyainam uvāca / sādhu sādhu putra / sādhu mahābrāhmaṇa / pratirūpam etat te praśamālaṃkṛtasyāsya maidhāvakasya /
body.translated_text: Then his teacher, his heart seized by delight and wonder, rose from his seat, embraced him, and said: 'Well done, well done, my son! Well done, great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>! This is befitting one like you, adorned with tranquility and wisdom.'

children.text: nimittam āsādya yad eva kiṃ ca na svadharmamārgaṃ visṛjanti bāliśāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'When they encounter some pretext or other, the foolish abandon the path of their own <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: tapaḥśrutajñānadhanās tu sādhavo na yānti kṛcchre parame 'pi vikriyām // AJm_12.20 //
children.translated_text: But the virtuous, rich in austerity, learning, and wisdom, do not undergo corruption even in the greatest adversity.'

children.text: tvayā kulaṃ svam amalam abhyalaṃkṛtaṃ samudyatā nabha iva śāradendunā /
children.translated_text: 'You have adorned your own pure family, like the autumn moon rising to adorn the sky;

children.text: tavārthavat sucaritaviśrutaṃ śrutaṃ sukhodayaḥ saphalatayā śramaś ca me // AJm_12.21 //
children.translated_text: Your learning, meaningful and famed for good conduct, is fruitful, and my labor has borne fruit in your happiness.'

body.text: tad evamātmalajjayaiva satpuruṣā nācāravelāṃ laṅghayantīti hrībalasamanvitenāryeṇa bhavitavyam /
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, it is through self-respect alone that the virtuous do not transgress the boundary of propriety—hence the noble person should be endowed with the power of shame.'

body.text: evaṃ hrīparikhāsaṃpanna āryaśrāvako 'kuśalam prajahātītyevamādiṣu sūtrapadeṣūpaneyam / hrīvarṇapratisaṃyukteṣu sūtrānteṣu lokādhipateye ceti //
body.translated_text: Thus, 'endowed with the moat of shame, the noble disciple abandons the unwholesome'—this is to be applied in such <s>sūtra</s> passages. In <s>sūtras</s> connected with the description of shame, [this story should be cited] for the 'Lord of the World' section.

body.text: brāhmaṇajātakaṃ dvādaśamam //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twelfth, the <s>Brāhmaṇa-Jātaka</s>.

children.text: 13. Unmādayantījātakam
children.translated_text: 13. The <s>Unmādayantī-Jātaka</s>.

body.text: tīvraduḥkhāturāṇām api satāṃ nīcamārganiṣpraṇayatā bhavati svadhairyāvaṣṭambhāt //
body.translated_text: Even when afflicted by intense suffering, the virtuous have no inclination toward base paths, owing to the firmness of their own resolve.

body.text: tadyathānuśrūyate / satyatyāgopaśamaprajñādibhir guṇātiśayair lokahitārtham udyacchamānaḥ kila bodhisattvaḥ kadā cic chibīnāṃ rājā babhūva sākṣād dharma iva vinaya iva piteva ca prajānām upakārapravṛttaḥ /
body.translated_text: As is traditionally heard: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, striving for the welfare of the world through surpassing virtues of truth, generosity, tranquility, wisdom, and the rest, was once born as king of the <s>Śibis</s>—engaged in benefiting his subjects like <s>Dharma</s> personified, like Discipline itself, like a father.

children.text: doṣapravṛtter viniyamyamāno niveśyamānaś ca guṇābhijātye /
children.translated_text: Restrained from the course of faults and established in the nobility of virtues,

children.text: pitreva putraḥ kṣitipena tena nananda lokadvitaye 'pi lokaḥ // AJm_13.1 //
children.translated_text: The world, like a son by his father, rejoiced under that king, in both this world and the next.

children.text: samasvabhāvā svajane jane ca dharmānugā tasya hi daṇḍanītiḥ /
children.translated_text: For his penal policy was equitable toward his own people and toward outsiders, and followed <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: adharmyam āvṛtya janasya mārgaṃ sopānamāleva divo babhūva // AJm_13.2 //
children.translated_text: Blocking the unrighteous path of the people, it became, as it were, a stairway to heaven.

children.text: dharmānvayaṃ lokahitaṃ sa paśyaṃs tadekakāryo naralokapālaḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing that the welfare of the world follows from <s>dharma</s>, that protector of the human world, devoted to that alone,

children.text: sarvātmanā dharmapathe 'bhireme tasyopamardaṃ ca parair na sehe // AJm_13.3 //
children.translated_text: Delighted with all his being in the path of <s>dharma</s> and could not endure its violation by others.

body.text: tasya ca rājñaḥ pauramukhyasya duhitā śrīr iva vigrahavatī sākṣād ratir ivāpsarasām anyatameva ca paramayā rūpalāvaṇyasaṃpadopetā paramadarśanīyā strīratnasaṃmatā babhūva /
body.translated_text: And there was a daughter of a leading citizen of that king's [city]—like <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune) incarnate, like <s>Rati</s> (Pleasure) herself, or like one of the <s>Apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs)—endowed with the supreme perfection of beauty and charm, supremely beautiful to behold, acknowledged as a jewel among women.

children.text: avītarāgasya janasya yāvat sā locanaprāpyavapur babhūva /
children.translated_text: As long as she was within the range of sight for anyone whose passions were not yet quelled,

children.text: tāvat sa tadrūpaguṇāvabaddhāṃ na dṛṣṭim utkampayituṃ śaśāka // AJm_13.4 //
children.translated_text: So long was he unable to tear his gaze away, bound by the qualities of her beauty.

body.text: ataś ca tasyā unmādayantīty eva bāndhavā nāma cakruḥ // atha tasyāḥ pitā rājñaḥ saṃviditaṃ kārayām āsa / strīratnaṃ te deva viṣaye prādurbhūtaṃ yatas tatpratigrahaṃ visarjanaṃ vā prati devaḥ pramāṇam iti // atha sa rājā strīlakṣaṇavido brāhmaṇān samādideśa / paśyantv enām atrabhavanto yady asāv asmadyogyā na veti // atha tasyāḥ pitā tān brāhmaṇān svabhavanam abhinīyonmādayantīm uvāca / bhadre svayaṃ brāḥmaṇān pariveṣayeti / sā tatheti pratiśrutya yathākramaṃ brāhmaṇān pariveṣayitum upacakrame // atha te brāhmaṇāḥ
body.translated_text: And thus her kinsmen gave her the name <s>Unmādayantī</s> ('She Who Drives Mad'). Then her father sent word to the king: 'A jewel among women, O lord, has appeared in your realm—Your Majesty is the authority regarding her acceptance or dismissal.' Then the king instructed <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> skilled in reading women's marks: 'Let their honors examine whether she is worthy of us or not.' Then her father, having brought those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> to his own house, said to <s>Unmādayantī</s>: 'My dear, please serve the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> yourself.' She, having agreed, began to serve the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> in order. Then those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>—

children.text: tadānanodvīkṣaṇaniścalākṣā manobhuvā saṃhriyamāṇadhairyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Their eyes fixed and unblinking at the sight of her face, their composure being swept away by the God of Love,

children.text: anīśvarā locanamānasānām āsur madeneva viluptasaṃjñāḥ // AJm_13.5 //
children.translated_text: Powerless over their eyes and minds, they lost consciousness as if from intoxication.

body.text: yadā ca naiva śaknuvanti sma pratisaṃkhyānadhīranibhṛtam avasthātuṃ kuta eva bhoktum athaiṣāṃ cakṣuṣpathād utsārya svāṃ duhitaraṃ sa gṛhapatiḥ svayam eva brāhmaṇān pariveṣya visarjayām āsa // atha teṣāṃ buddhir abhavat </> kṛtyārūpam iva khalv idam atimanoharam asyā dārikāyā rūpacāturyaṃ yato naināṃ rājā draṣṭum apy arhati kutaḥ punaḥ patnītvaṃ gamayitum / anayā hi rūpaśobhayā niyatam asyonmāditahṛdayasya dharmārthakāryapravṛtter visrasyamānotsāhasya rājakāryakālātikramāḥ prajānāṃ hitasukhodayapatham upapīḍayantaḥ parābhavāya syuḥ /
body.translated_text: And when they were unable even to maintain a composed, mindful, steadfast posture—let alone eat—the householder had his daughter removed from their sight and himself served and dismissed the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. Then they came to this conclusion: 'This excessively enchanting beauty and charm of this girl is surely something sinister—therefore the king should not even look upon her, much less take her as his wife. For by this beauty of form, with his heart maddened, his enthusiasm for the pursuit of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and duty slipping away, delays in royal business would oppress the path to the welfare and happiness of his subjects and lead to ruin.'

children.text: iyaṃ hi saṃdarśanamātrakeṇa kuryān munīnām api siddhivighnam /
children.translated_text: 'For she, by mere sight alone, would obstruct the accomplishments even of sages—

children.text: prāg eva bhāvārpitadṛṣṭidṛṣṭer yūnaḥ kṣitīśasya sukhe sthitasya // AJm_13.6 //
children.translated_text: How much more so of a young king, dwelling in comfort, gazing with eyes fixed in passion!'

body.text: tasmād idam atra prāptakālam iti yathāprastāvam upetya rājñe nivedayām āsuḥ / dṛṣṭāsmābhir mahārāja sā kanyakā / asti cāsyā rūpacāturyamātrakam apalakṣaṇopaghātaniḥśrīkaṃ tu yato naināṃ draṣṭum apy arhati mahārājaḥ kiṃ punaḥ patnītvaṃ gamayitum /
body.translated_text: 'Therefore this is what is appropriate here.' And at a suitable opportunity they reported to the king: 'We have seen that maiden, O great king. She has merely the superficial beauty of form, but it is rendered inauspicious by ill-omens—therefore Your Majesty should not even look upon her, let alone take her as wife.'

children.text: kuladvayasyāpi hi ninditā strī yaśo vibhūtiṃ ca tiraskaroti /
children.translated_text: 'For a woman condemned [as inauspicious] obscures the fame and prosperity of both families,

children.text: nimagnacandreva niśā sameghā śobhāṃ vibhāgaṃ ca divaspṛthivyoḥ // AJm_13.7 //
children.translated_text: Like a cloudy night with a sunken moon [obscures] the beauty and distinction of heaven and earth.'

body.text: iti śrutārthaḥ sa rājāpalakṣaṇā kilāsau na ca me kulānurūpeti tasyāṃ vinivṛttābhilāṣo babhūva / anarthitāṃ tu vijñāya rājñaḥ sa gṛhapatis tāṃ dārikāṃ tasyaiva rājño 'bhipāragāyāmātyāya prāyacchat // atha kadā cit sa rājā kramāgatāṃ kaumudīṃ svasmin puravare viṣaktaśobhāṃ draṣṭum utsukamanā rathavaragataḥ siktasaṃmṛṣṭarathyāntarāpaṇam ucchritacchattradhvajapatākaṃ samantataḥ puṣpopahāraśabalabhūmitalaṃ pravṛttanṛttagītahāsyalāsyavāditraṃ puṣpadhūpacūrṇavāsamālyāsavasnānānulepanāmodaprasṛtasurabhigandhi prasāritavividharucirapaṇyaṃ tuṣṭapuṣṭojjvalataraveṣapaurajanasaṃbādharājamārgaṃ puravaram anuvicaraṃs tasyāmātyasya bhavanasamīpam upajagāma / athonmādayanty apalakṣaṇā kilāham ity anena rājñāvadhūteti samutpannāmarṣā rājadarśanakutūhaleva nāma saṃdṛśyamānarūpaśobhā vidyud iva ghanaśikharaṃ harmyatalam avabhāsayantī vyatiṣṭhata / śaktir asyedānīm astv apalakṣaṇādarśanavicalitasmṛtim ātmānaṃ dhārayitum iti //
body.translated_text: Hearing this, the king [thought]: 'She is inauspicious, they say, and not befitting my family'—and his desire for her ceased. But when the householder learned she was unwanted by the king, he gave the girl to a minister named <s>Abhipāraga</s>, who served that very king. Then once, the king, his mind eager to see the <s>Kaumudī</s> festival in its seasonal beauty in his capital city, rode forth on an excellent chariot through the city—its streets sprinkled and swept, its markets thronged, parasols, banners, and flags raised high, the ground everywhere dappled with offerings of flowers, with dance, song, jest, graceful play, and music being performed, fragrant with the sweet scent of flowers, incense, powders, perfumes, garlands, liquors, baths, and unguents, with various beautiful wares displayed, its royal highway crowded with citizens in brilliant festive attire. He came near the house of that minister. Then <s>Unmādayantī</s>, resentful thinking 'I am called inauspicious, and therefore rejected by this king,' as if from curiosity to see the king, standing there with her beauty visible, illuminating the palace terrace like lightning on a cloud-peak, [thought]: 'Let him now have the power to maintain himself, with his memory undisturbed by the sight of one who is inauspicious!'

body.text: atha tasya rājñaḥ puravaravibhūṣādarśanaprasṛtā dṛṣṭir abhimukhasthitāyāṃ sahasaiva tasyām apatat / atha sa rājā
body.translated_text: Then the gaze of that king, extended to take in the beauty of the city's decorations, fell suddenly upon her standing before him. Then that king—

children.text: prakāmam antaḥpurasundarīṇāṃ vapurvilāsaiḥ kalitekṣaṇo 'pi /
children.translated_text: Though his eyes were practiced upon the bodily charms and graces of the beautiful women of his inner chambers,

children.text: anuddhato dharmapathānurāgād udyogavān indriyanirjaye 'pi // AJm_13.8 //
children.translated_text: Though unexcited, through his devotion to the path of <s>dharma</s>, and diligent even in the conquest of the senses,

children.text: vipuladhṛtiguṇo 'py apatrapiṣṇuḥ parayuvatīkṣaṇaviklavekṣaṇo 'pi /
children.translated_text: Though possessed of vast fortitude, though bashful, though his gaze faltered at the sight of another's wife—

children.text: uditamadanavismayaḥ striyaṃ tāṃ ciram animeṣavilocano dadarśa // AJm_13.9 //
children.translated_text: With wonder-struck desire arising, he gazed upon that woman for a long time, his eyes unblinking.

children.text: kaumudī kiṃ nv iyaṃ sākṣād bhavanasyāsya devatā /
children.translated_text: 'Is this the <s>Kaumudī</s> festival personified? Or the deity of this house?

children.text: svargastrī daityayoṣid vā na hy etan mānuṣaṃ vapuḥ // AJm_13.10 //
children.translated_text: Or a heavenly woman? Or a daughter of the <s>Daityas</s>? For this body cannot be human.'

body.text: iti vicārayata eva tasya rājñas taddarśanāvitṛptanayanasya sa rathas taṃ deśam ativartamāno na manorathānukūlo babhūva / atha sa rājā śūnyahṛdaya iva tadgataikāgramanāḥ svabhavanam upetya manmathākṣiptadhṛtiḥ sunandaṃ sārathiṃ rahasi paryapṛcchat /
body.translated_text: Even as the king was deliberating thus, his eyes unsated with the sight of her, his chariot passed beyond that place—contrary to his heart's desire. Then the king, as if empty-hearted, his mind single-pointedly focused on her, having returned to his own palace, his fortitude shaken by the God of Love, secretly asked his charioteer <s>Sunanda</s>:

children.text: sitaprākārasaṃvītaṃ vetsi kasya nu tad gṛham /
children.translated_text: 'Do you know whose house that is, enclosed by white ramparts?

children.text: kā sā tatra vyarociṣṭa vidyut sita ivāmbude // AJm_13.11 //
children.translated_text: Who was she who shone there, like lightning in a white cloud?'

body.text: sārathir uvāca / asti devasyābhipārago nāmāmātyas tasya tad gṛhaṃ tasyaiva ca sā bhāryā kirīṭavatsaduhitonmādayantī nāmeti / tad upaśrutya sa rājā parabhāryeti vitānībhūtahṛdayaś cintāstimitanayano dīrgham uṣṇam abhiniśvasya tadarpitamanāḥ śanair ātmagatam uvāca /
body.translated_text: The charioteer said: 'Your Majesty has a minister named <s>Abhipāraga</s>; that is his house, and she is his wife, the daughter of the citizen <s>Kirīṭavatsa</s>, named <s>Unmādayantī</s>.' Hearing this, the king, his heart in turmoil at the thought 'she is another man's wife,' his eyes stilled with anxious thought, having heaved a long, hot sigh, his mind absorbed in her, said slowly to himself:

children.text: anvartharamyākṣarasaukumāryam aho kṛtaṃ nāma yathedam asyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Ah, how aptly made is this name of hers, with its syllables lovely in meaning and soft in sound—

children.text: unmādayantīti śucismitāyās tathā hi sonmādam ivākaron mām // AJm_13.12 //
children.translated_text: <s>Unmādayantī</s> (She Who Drives Mad), this brightly smiling one—for she has indeed made me as if mad.'

children.text: vismartum enām icchāmi paśyāmīva ca cetasā /
children.translated_text: 'I wish to forget her, yet I seem to see her with my mind;

children.text: sthitaṃ tasyāṃ nu me cetaḥ sā prabhutvena tatra vā // AJm_13.13 //
children.translated_text: Is my heart fixed upon her, or has she forcibly stationed herself there?'

children.text: parasya nāma bhāryāyāṃ mamāpy evam adhīratā /
children.translated_text: 'Such weakness of mine toward another man's wife!

children.text: tad unmatto 'smi saṃtyakto lajjayevādya nidrayā // AJm_13.14 //
children.translated_text: Clearly I am mad—abandoned by shame as if by sleep today.'

children.text: tasyā vapurvilasitasmitavīkṣiteṣu saṃrāganiścalamateḥ sahasā svanantī /
children.translated_text: 'While my mind, its resolve fixed in passion, [dwells] upon her body, her play, her smile, her glances,

children.text: kāryāntarakramanivedanadhṛṣṭaśabdā vidveṣam uttudati cetasi nālikā me // AJm_13.15 //
children.translated_text: The water-clock, suddenly sounding with its bold voice announcing the passage of other duties, stirs irritation in my heart.'

body.text: iti sa rājā madanabalavicalitadhṛtir vyavasthāpayann apy ātmānam āpāṇḍukṛśatanuḥ pradhyānaniśvasitavijṛmbhaṇaparaḥ pravyaktamadanākāro babhūva /
body.translated_text: Thus the king, his fortitude shaken by the power of desire, though trying to compose himself, became pale and thin, given to brooding, sighing, and yawning—manifestly displaying the signs of lovesickness.

children.text: dhṛtyā mahatyāpi niguhyamānaḥ sa bhūpates tasya manovikāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Though concealed even by great fortitude, that king's mental disturbance

children.text: mukhena cintāstimitekṣaṇena kārśyena ca vyaktim upājagāma // AJm_13.16 //
children.translated_text: Became manifest through his face with its eyes stilled in anxious thought, and through his emaciation.

body.text: atheṅgitākāragrahaṇanipuṇamatir abhipārago 'mātyas taṃ rājño vṛttāntaṃ sakāraṇam upalabhya snehāt tadatyayāśaṅkī jānānaś cātibalatāṃ madanasya rahasi rājānaṃ viditaḥ samupetya kṛtābhyanujño vijñāpayām āsa /
body.translated_text: Then the minister <s>Abhipāraga</s>, whose mind was skilled at reading gestures and expressions, having perceived the king's condition along with its cause, alarmed by affection lest [the king] perish, and knowing too the overpowering force of desire, approached the king in private, and having obtained permission, said:

children.text: adyārcayantaṃ naradeva devān sākṣād upetyāmburuhākṣa yakṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Today, O lord of men, as I was worshiping the gods, a <s>Yakṣa</s> appeared before me in person and said,

children.text: mām āha nāvaiṣi nṛpasya kasmād unmādayantyāṃ hṛdayaṃ niviṣṭam // AJm_13.17 //
children.translated_text: 'O lotus-eyed one, do you not know that the king's heart is fixed upon <s>Unmādayantī</s>?''

children.text: ity evam uktvā sahasā tiro'bhūd vimarśavān ity aham abhyupetaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having said this, he suddenly vanished. I, being a man of reflection, have accepted [this as true];

children.text: tac cet tathā deva kim etad evam asmāsu te niṣpraṇayatvamaunam // AJm_13.18 //
children.translated_text: If that is so, O lord, then why this silence of affectionless reserve toward us?'

body.text: tat pratigrahītum enām arhati madanugrahārthaṃ deva iti / atha sa rājā pratyādeśāl lajjāvanatavadano madanavaśago 'pi svabhyastadharmasaṃjñatvād aviklavībhūtadhairyaḥ pratyākhyānaviśadākṣaram enam uvāca / naitad asti / kutaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, may Your Majesty deign to accept her, for the sake of showing me favor.' Then that king, his face downcast with shame at the refusal, though subject to desire, yet with his fortitude unshaken due to his well-practiced awareness of <s>dharma</s>, spoke to him with words clear in their refusal:

children.text: puṇyāc cyutaḥ syām amaro na cāsmi vidyāc ca naḥ pāpam idaṃ jano 'pi /
children.translated_text: 'I would fall from merit; I am not immortal; and the people would learn of this sin of ours.

children.text: tadviprayogāc ca manojvaras tvāṃ vahniḥ purā kakṣam iva kṣiṇoti // AJm_13.19 //
children.translated_text: And from separation from her, the fever of the heart would consume you, as fire [consumes] dry grass.'

children.text: yac cobhayor ity ahitāvahaṃ syāl loke parasminn iha caiva karma /
children.translated_text: 'And what would be harmful to both — in the next world and in this — an [evil] deed:

children.text: tad yasya hetor abudhā bhajante tasyaiva hetor na budhā bhajante // AJm_13.20 //
children.translated_text: that for the sake of which the unwise indulge, for that very reason the wise do not.'

body.text: abhipāraga uvāca / alam atra devasya dharmātikramaśaṅkayā /
body.translated_text: <s>Abhipāraga</s> said: 'Let Your Majesty have no apprehension of transgressing <s>dharma</s> here.

children.text: dāne sāhāyyadānena dharma eva bhavet tava /
children.translated_text: By giving assistance in [my] giving, it would be <s>dharma</s> itself for you.

children.text: dānavighnāt tv adharmaḥ syāt tāṃ matto 'pratigṛhṇataḥ // AJm_13.21 //
children.translated_text: But from obstructing [my] gift, there would be <s>adharma</s> — if you do not accept her from me.'

body.text: kīrtyuparodhāvakāśam api cātra devasya na paśyāmi / kutaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'And I see no scope here for an obstruction to Your Majesty's fame. For:',

children.text: āvābhyām idam anyaś ca ka eva jñātum arhati /
children.translated_text: 'Who else besides us two can ever know of this?

children.text: janāpavādād āśaṅkām ato manasi mā kṛthāḥ // AJm_13.22 //
children.translated_text: Therefore do not harbor in your mind apprehension of public censure.'

body.text: anugrahaś caiṣa mama syān na pīḍā / kutaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'And this would be a favor to me, not an affliction. For:',

children.text: svāmyarthacaryārjitayā hi tuṣṭyā nirantare cetasi ko vighātaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'When the heart is uninterrupted [in its] satisfaction, earned through conduct serving one's master's purpose, what could be the disturbance?

children.text: yataḥ sakāmaṃ kuru deva kāmam alaṃ madutpīḍanaśaṅkayā te // AJm_13.23 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, O lord, fulfill your desire as you wish; enough of your apprehension of causing me suffering.'

body.text: rājovāca / śāntaṃ pāpam /
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Heaven forbid!

children.text: vyaktam asmadatisnehān na tvayaitad avekṣitam /
children.translated_text: Clearly, out of excessive affection for us, you have not considered this:

children.text: yathā dāne na sarvasmin sācivyaṃ dharmasādhanam // AJm_13.24 //
children.translated_text: that assistance in giving is not a means to <s>dharma</s> in every [type of] gift.'

children.text: yo 'smadartham atisnehāt svān prāṇān api nekṣate /
children.translated_text: 'One who, out of excessive affection for us, does not regard even his own life,

children.text: tasya bandhuviśiṣṭasya sakhyur bhāryā sakhī nanu // AJm_13.25 //
children.translated_text: such a friend, dearer than a kinsman — is not his wife a female friend [to me]?'

body.text: tad ayuktaṃ mām atra pratārayitum / yad api ceṣṭaṃ naitad anyaḥ kaś cij jñāsyatīti kim evam idam apāpaṃ syāt /
body.translated_text: 'Therefore it is wrong to try to deceive me in this. And as for what has been said — "No one else will ever know of this" — would that make it sinless?

children.text: adṛśyamāno 'pi hi pāpam ācaran viṣaṃ niṣevyeva kathaṃ śam āpnuyāt /
children.translated_text: For even when unseen, how could one who commits sin find peace — as when drinking poison?

children.text: na taṃ na paśyanti viśuddhacakṣuṣo divaukasaś caiva narāś ca yoginaḥ // AJm_13.26 //
children.translated_text: Those of purified vision, the celestial beings, and human yogis — they do not fail to see him.'

body.text: kiṃ ca bhūyaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'And furthermore:',

children.text: śraddadhīta ka etac ca yathāsau tava na priyā /
children.translated_text: 'Who would believe that she is not dear to you?

children.text: tāṃ parityajya sadyo vā vighātaṃ na samāpnuyāḥ // AJm_13.27 //
children.translated_text: And would you not, upon abandoning her, immediately come to ruin?'

body.text: abhipāraga uvāca /
body.translated_text: <s>Abhipāraga</s> said:

children.text: saputradāro dāso 'haṃ svāmī tvaṃ daivataṃ ca me /
children.translated_text: 'I, together with my wife and sons, am your slave; you are my master and my deity.

children.text: dāsyām asyāṃ yato deva kas te dharmavyatikramaḥ // AJm_13.28 //
children.translated_text: Since she is a slave-woman, O lord, what transgression of <s>dharma</s> is there for you?'

body.text: yad api ceṣṭaṃ priyā mameyam ity ataḥ kim /
body.translated_text: 'And as for what has been said — "she is dear to me" — what of it?',

children.text: mama priyā kāmada kāmam eṣā tenaiva ditsāmi ca tubhyam enām /
children.translated_text: 'She is indeed dear to me, O granter of desires — precisely for that reason I wish to give her to you.

children.text: priyaṃ hi dattvā labhate paratra prakarṣaramyāṇi janaḥ priyāṇi // AJm_13.29 //
children.translated_text: For by giving what is dear, a person obtains in the next world pleasures that are supremely delightful.'

body.text: yataḥ pratigṛhṇātv evaināṃ deva iti // rājovāca / mā maivam / akrama eṣaḥ / kutaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, may Your Majesty please accept her!' The king said: 'No, absolutely not! This is improper. For:',

children.text: ahaṃ hi śastraṃ niśitaṃ viśeyaṃ hutāśanaṃ visphuradarciṣaṃ vā /
children.translated_text: 'I would enter a sharpened blade, or a fire with blazing flames,

children.text: na tv eva dharmād adhigamya lakṣmīṃ śakṣyāmi tatraiva punaḥ prahartum // AJm_13.30 //
children.translated_text: but I could never, having obtained fortune through <s>dharma</s>, strike at that very [<s>dharma</s>] again.'

body.text: abhipāraga uvāca / yady enāṃ madbhāryeti devo na pratigrahītum icchaty ayam aham asyāḥ sarvajanaprārthanāviruddhaṃ veśyāvratam ādiśāmi / tata enāṃ devaḥ pratigṛhṇīyād iti // rājovāca / kim unmatto 'si /
body.translated_text: <s>Abhipāraga</s> said: 'If Your Majesty does not wish to accept her as my wife, then I shall assign to her the vow of a courtesan, unrestricted by any person's claim. Then Your Majesty may accept her.' The king said: 'Are you mad?'

children.text: aduṣṭāṃ saṃtyajan bhāryāṃ matto daṇḍam avāpnuyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having abandoned a blameless wife, you would incur the punishment reserved for a madman.

children.text: sa dhigvādāspadībhūtaḥ paratreha ca dhakṣyase // AJm_13.31 //
children.translated_text: Having become a target of reproach, you will burn both in the next world and in this.'

body.text: tad alam akāryanirbandhitayā / nyāyābhiniveśī bhaveti // abhipāraga uvāca /
body.translated_text: 'So enough of this insistence on what should not be done! Be devoted to what is right!' <s>Abhipāraga</s> said:

children.text: dharmātyayo me yadi kaś cid evaṃ janāpavādaḥ sukhaviplavo vā /
children.translated_text: 'If any transgression of <s>dharma</s> should befall me thus, or public censure, or the ruin of happiness —

children.text: pratyudgamiṣyāmy urasā tu tat tat tvatsaukhyalabdhena manaḥsukhena // AJm_13.32 //
children.translated_text: I shall meet all of that with my breast, with the happiness of mind gained from your pleasure.'

children.text: tvattaḥ paraṃ cāhavanīyam anyaṃ loke na paśyāmi mahīmahendra /
children.translated_text: 'And I see no other worthy recipient of an offering in the world besides you, O great lord of the earth.

children.text: unmādayantīṃ mama puṇyavṛddhyai tvaṃ dakṣiṇām ṛtvig iva pratīccha // AJm_13.33 //
children.translated_text: Accept [<s>Unmādayantī</s>] — the intoxicating one — as a priestly fee, like a ritual priest [accepts his fee], for the increase of my merit.'

body.text: rājovāca / kāmam asmadatisnehād anavekṣitātmahitāhitakramo madarthacaryāsamudyogas tavāyam / ata eva tu tvāṃ viśeṣato nopekṣitum arhāmi / naiva khalu lokāpavādaniḥśaṅkena bhavitavyam / paśya /
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Assuredly, this eagerness of yours to serve my purpose, born of excessive affection for us, overlooks the proper order of what is beneficial and harmful to yourself. For that very reason, however, I must not neglect you in particular. Surely one should not be free from concern about public censure. Consider:',

children.text: lokasya yo nādriyate 'pavādaṃ dharmānapekṣaḥ parataḥ phalaṃ vā /
children.translated_text: 'One who disregards the censure of the world, who has no regard for <s>dharma</s> or its fruit hereafter —

children.text: jano na viśvāsam upaiti tasminn atīva lakṣmyāpi vivarjyate saḥ // AJm_13.34 //
children.translated_text: people do not trust such a person, and he is utterly forsaken even by <s>Lakṣmī</s> (Fortune).'

body.text: yatas tvāṃ bravīmi /
body.translated_text: 'Therefore I say to you:',

children.text: mā te rociṣṭa dharmasya jīvitārthe 'py atikramaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Let not the transgression of <s>dharma</s> be pleasing to you, even for [the sake of saving] your life —

children.text: niḥsaṃdigdhamahādoṣaḥ sasaṃdehakṛśodayaḥ // AJm_13.35 //
children.translated_text: [a transgression] whose great fault is beyond doubt, [and] whose meager benefit is itself doubtful.'

body.text: kiṃ ca bhūyaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'And furthermore:',

children.text: nindādiduḥkheṣu parān nipātya neṣṭā satām ātmasukhaprasiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The attainment of one's own happiness by casting others into sufferings such as censure is not desired by the virtuous.

children.text: eko 'py anutpīḍya parān ato 'haṃ dharme sthitaḥ svārthadhuraṃ prapatsye // AJm_13.36 //
children.translated_text: Without afflicting even a single other person, I, established in <s>dharma</s>, shall take up the yoke of my own purpose.'

body.text: abhipāraga uvāca / svāmyarthaṃ bhaktivaśena carato mama tāvad atra ka evādharmāvakāśaḥ syād devasya vā dīyamānām enāṃ pratigṛhṇataḥ syād yataḥ sanaigamajānapadāḥ śibayaḥ kim atrādharma iti brūyuḥ / tat pratigṛhṇātv evaināṃ deva iti // rājovāca / addhā madarthacaryāpravaṇamatir bhavān / idaṃ tv atra cintayitavyam / sanaigamajānapadānāṃ śibīnāṃ tava mama vā ko 'smākaṃ dharmavittama iti // athābhipāragaḥ sasaṃbhramo rājānam uvāca /
body.translated_text: <s>Abhipāraga</s> said: 'For me, acting out of devotion for my master's purpose, what scope is there for <s>adharma</s> here? And for Your Majesty, in accepting her who is given — would the <s>Śibis</s>, together with the town-dwellers and country-folk, say "this is <s>adharma</s>"? Therefore, may Your Majesty please accept her!' The king said: 'Indeed your mind is inclined toward serving my purpose. But this must be considered here: between the <s>Śibis</s> — the town-dwellers and country-folk — and yourself, and me, who among us is the most learned in <s>dharma</s>?' Then <s>Abhipāraga</s>, with deference, said to the king:

children.text: vṛddhopasevāsu kṛtaśramatvāc chrutādhikārān matipāṭavāc ca /
children.translated_text: 'Through your exertion in attending upon elders, your authority in scriptural learning, and the sharpness of your intellect,

children.text: trivargavidyātiśayārthatattvaṃ tvayi sthitaṃ deva bṛhaspatau ca // AJm_13.37 //
children.translated_text: the ultimate truth of the three aims (<s>trivarga</s>) resides in you, O lord, and in <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.'

body.text: rājovāca / tena hi na mām atra pratārayitum arhasi / kutaḥ /
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Then you should not try to deceive me in this. For:',

children.text: narādhipānāṃ cariteṣv adhīnaṃ lokasya yasmād ahitaṃ hitaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: 'Since the ill and the good of the world depend upon the conduct of kings,

children.text: bhaktiṃ prajānām anucintya tasmāt kīrtikṣame satpatha eva raṃsye // AJm_13.38 //
children.translated_text: therefore, reflecting on the devotion of my subjects, I shall delight only in the virtuous path that bears the weight of fame.'

children.text: jihmaṃ śubhaṃ vā vṛṣabhapracāraṃ gāvo 'nugā yadvad anuprayānti /
children.translated_text: 'Just as cows following a bull proceed along whatever path he takes — whether crooked or straight —

children.text: utkṣiptaśaṅkāṅkuśanirvighaṭṭaṃ prajās tathaiva kṣitipasya vṛttam // AJm_13.39 //
children.translated_text: so too the subjects [follow] the conduct of a king, with suspicions and objections cast aside.'

body.text: api ca paśyatu tāvad bhavān /
body.translated_text: 'And moreover, let Your Honor consider this:',

children.text: ātmānam api cec chaktir na syāt pālayituṃ mama /
children.translated_text: 'If I had not the power to govern even myself,

children.text: kā nv avasthā janasya syān matto rakṣābhikāṅkṣiṇaḥ // AJm_13.40 //
children.translated_text: what would be the condition of the people who look to me for protection?'

children.text: iti prajānāṃ hitam īkṣamāṇaḥ svaṃ caiva dharmaṃ vimalaṃ yaśaś ca /
children.translated_text: 'Thus, looking to the welfare of my subjects, my own spotless <s>dharma</s>, and [my] fame,

children.text: necchāmi cittasya vaśena gantum ahaṃ hi netā vṛṣavat prajānām // AJm_13.41 //
children.translated_text: I do not wish to go at the command of my mind, for I am the guide of my subjects, like a bull.'

body.text: athābhipārago 'mātyas tena rājño 'vasthānena prasāditamanāḥ praṇamya rājānaṃ prāñjalir ity uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then the minister <s>Abhipāraga</s>, his mind gratified by the king's steadfastness, bowed to the king and said with palms joined:

children.text: aho prajānām atibhāgyasaṃpad yāsāṃ tvam evaṃ naradeva goptā /
children.translated_text: 'Oh, what a superabundance of good fortune for the subjects whose protector, O lord of men, is such as you!

children.text: dharmānurāgo hi sukhānapekṣas tapovanastheṣv api mṛgya eva // AJm_13.42 //
children.translated_text: For devotion to <s>dharma</s>, heedless of [personal] comfort, would be sought after even among those dwelling in ascetics' groves.'

children.text: mahacchabdo mahārāja tvayy evāyaṃ virājate /
children.translated_text: 'The word "great," O great king, truly shines only in connection with you.

children.text: viguṇeṣu guṇoktir hi kṣeparūkṣatarākṣarā // AJm_13.43 //
children.translated_text: For the attribution of virtues to the virtueless has the harshness of mockery.'

children.text: vismayo 'nibhṛtatvaṃ vā kiṃ mamaitāvatā tvayi /
children.translated_text: 'What wonder or agitation should I feel at this much in you?

children.text: samudra iva ratnānāṃ guṇānāṃ yas tvam ākaraḥ // AJm_13.44 //
children.translated_text: [You] who are, like the ocean for gems, a mine of virtues?'

body.text: tad evaṃ tīvraduḥkhāturāṇām api satāṃ nīcamārganiṣpraṇayatā bhavati svadhairyāvaṣṭambhāt svabhyastadharmasaṃjñatvāc ceti dhairye dharmābhyāse ca yogaḥ kārya iti //
body.translated_text: Therefore, even when afflicted by intense suffering, the virtuous are disinclined toward base paths — because of the support of their steadfastness and because of their well-practiced awareness of <s>dharma</s>. Hence one should cultivate steadfastness and practice of <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: unmādayantījātakaṃ trayodaśam //
body.translated_text: The <s>Unmādayantī Jātaka</s>, the thirteenth.

children.text: 14. Supāragajātakam
children.translated_text: 14. The <s>Supāraga Jātaka</s> (The Good Crossing).

body.text: dharmāśrayaṃ satyavacanam apy āpadaṃ nudati prāg eva tatphalam iti dharmānuvartinā bhavitavyam //
body.translated_text: A truthful word grounded in <s>dharma</s> wards off calamity — how much more so its fruit! Therefore one should follow <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: tadyathānuśrūyate / bodhisattvaḥ kila mahāsattvaḥ paramanipuṇamatir nausārathir babhūva / dharmatā hy eṣā bodhisattvānāṃ prakṛtimedhāvitvād yad uta yaṃ yaṃ śāstrātiśayaṃ jijñāsante kalāviśeṣaṃ vā tasmiṃs tasminn adhikā bhavanti medhāvino jagataḥ // atha sa mahātmā viditajyotirgatitvād digvibhāgeṣv asaṃmūḍhamatiḥ parividitaniyatāgantukautpātikanimittaḥ kālākālakramakuśalo mīnatoyavarṇabhaumaprakāraśakuniparvatādibhiś cihnaiḥ sūpalakṣitasamudrapradeśaḥ smṛtimān vijitatandrīnidraḥ śītoṣṇavarṣādiparikhedasahiṣṇur apramādī dhṛtimān āharaṇāpasaraṇādikuśalatvād īpsitaṃ deśaṃ prāpayitā vaṇijām āsīt / tasya paramasiddhayātratvāt supāraga ity eva nāma babhūva / tadadhyuṣitaṃ ca pattanaṃ supāragam ity eva khyātam āsīt / yad etarhi śūrpārakam iti jñāyate // so 'timaṅgalasaṃmatatvād vṛddhatve 'pi sāṃyātrikair yātrāsiddhikāmair vahanam abhyarthanasatkārapuraḥsaram āropyate sma // atha kadā cid bharukacchād abhiprayātāḥ suvarṇabhūmiṃ vaṇijo yātrāsiddhikāmāḥ supāragaṃ pattanam upetya taṃ mahāsattvaṃ vahanārohaṇārtham abhyarthayām āsuḥ / sa tān uvāca /
body.translated_text: So it is heard: the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the great being, of supremely subtle intellect, was a ship's navigator. For it is the nature of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, being inherently wise, that in whatever branch of learning or special art they wish to investigate, they become superior — the wise of the world. Now that great soul, being versed in the movements of the stars, unerring in his knowledge of the directions, fully aware of regular, seasonal, and portentous signs, skilled in the sequence of timely and untimely [conditions], well-acquainted with the regions of the ocean through signs such as fish, water-color, soil-type, birds, mountains, and the like, mindful, having conquered lethargy and sleep, able to endure the hardships of cold, heat, rain, and the like, vigilant, steadfast, and skilled in embarking and disembarking, he would deliver merchants to their desired destination. Because of his supremely successful voyages, he came to be known by the name <s>Supāraga</s> ('Good Crossing'). And the port where he resided also became known as <s>Supāraga</s> — which is now known as <s>Śūrpāraka</s>. Because he was deemed supremely auspicious, even in his old age, seafarers desiring a successful voyage would have him board their ship with respectful entreaty. Now once, merchants who had set out from <s>Bharukaccha</s> (Bharuch), bound for <s>Suvarṇabhūmi</s> (the Land of Gold), desiring a successful voyage, came to the port of <s>Supāraga</s> and entreated that great being to board the ship. He said to them:

children.text: jarājñayā saṃhriyamāṇadarśane śramābhipātaiḥ pratanūkṛtasmṛtau /
children.translated_text: 'With my sight being gathered in by the command of old age, my memory thinned by the assaults of fatigue,

children.text: svadehakṛtye 'py avasannavikrame sahāyatā kā pariśaṅkyate mayi // AJm_14.1 //
children.translated_text: and my vigor diminished even in attending to my own body — what assistance can be expected from me?'

body.text: vaṇija ūcuḥ / viditeyam asmākaṃ yuṣmaccharīrāvasthā / saty api ca vaḥ parākramasahatve naiva vayaṃ karmaviniyogena yuṣmān āyāsayitum icchāmaḥ / kiṃ tarhi /
body.translated_text: The merchants said: 'This condition of your body is known to us. And even though your strength is impaired, we do not wish to trouble you with the assignment of work. Rather:',

children.text: tvatpādapaṅkajasamāśrayasatkṛtena maṅgalyatām upagatā rajasā tv iyaṃ nauḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This ship, honored by the dust that has taken refuge at your lotus-feet, has become auspicious.

children.text: durge mahaty api ca toyanidhāv amuṣmin svasti vrajed iti bhavantam upāgatāḥ smaḥ // AJm_14.2 //
children.translated_text: Even in the great peril of that vast ocean, she would go safely — thus we have come to you.'

body.text: atha sa mahātmā teṣām anukampayā jarāśithilaśarīro 'pi tadvahanam āruroha / tadadhirohaṇāc ca pramuditamanasaḥ sarva eva te vaṇijo babhūvur niyatam asmākam uttamā yātrāsiddhir iti / krameṇa cāvajagāhire vividhamīnakulavicaritam anibhṛtajalakalakalārāvam anilavilāsapravicalitataraṅgaṃ bahuvidharatnair bhūmiviśeṣair arpitaraṅgaṃ phenāvalīkusumadāmavicitram asuravarabhujagavarabhavanaṃ durāpapātālam aprameyatoyaṃ mahāsamudram /
body.translated_text: Then that great soul, out of compassion for them, though his body was enfeebled by old age, boarded their ship. And from his boarding, all those merchants became joyful of mind, [thinking:] 'Surely the highest success of our voyage is assured.' And gradually they entered the great ocean — haunted by various fish and sea-creatures, clamorous with the restless sound of agitated waters, its waves playfully set in motion by the sport of the wind, its waves studded with gems of many kinds from its various regions, adorned with garlands of foam-blossoms, the dwelling of the lord of <s>Asuras</s> and the lord of <s>Nāgas</s>, with unfathomable depths, immeasurable in its waters.

children.text: athendranīlaprakarābhinīlaṃ sūryāṃśutāpād iva khaṃ vilīnam /
children.translated_text: Then, deep blue as if [stained] by heaps of sapphires, as if the sky itself had melted from the heat of the sun's rays,

children.text: samantato 'ntarhitatīralekham agādham ambhonidhimadhyam īyuḥ // AJm_14.3 //
children.translated_text: with the shoreline vanished from sight on all sides, they entered the fathomless mid-ocean.

body.text: teṣāṃ tatrānuprāptānāṃ sāyāhnasamaye mṛdūbhūtakiraṇacakraprabhāve savitari mahad autpātikaṃ paramabhīṣaṇaṃ prādurabhūt /
body.translated_text: When they had arrived there, at evening time, as the sun's orb softened its rays, a great portent, supremely terrifying, appeared:

children.text: vibhidyamānormivikīrṇaphenaś caṇḍānilāsphālanabhīmanādaḥ /
children.translated_text: With its waves splitting apart and scattering foam, with a terrible roar from the buffeting of fierce winds,

children.text: naibhṛtyanirmuktasamagratoyaḥ kṣaṇena raudraḥ samabhūt samudraḥ // AJm_14.4 //
children.translated_text: its entire waters unleashed in their violence — in an instant the ocean became fearsome.

children.text: utpātavātākalitair mahadbhis toyasthalair bhīmarayair bhramadbhiḥ /
children.translated_text: With great, whirling masses of water stirred by the hurricane-winds, [producing] terrifying sounds,

children.text: yugāntakālapracalācaleva bhūmir babhūvogravapuḥ samudraḥ // AJm_14.5 //
children.translated_text: the ocean became terrible in aspect, like the earth with quaking mountains at the end of an age.

children.text: vidyullatodbhāsuralolajihvā nīlā bhujaṃgā iva naikaśīrṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: Dark, many-headed serpents, as it were, with flickering tongues brilliant as lightning-creepers —

children.text: āvavrur ādityapathaṃ payodāḥ prasaktabhīmastanitānunādāḥ // AJm_14.6 //
children.translated_text: Rain-clouds covered the path of the sun, resounding with terrifying, continuous thunder.

children.text: ghanair ghanair āvṛtaraśmijālaḥ sūryaḥ krameṇāstam upāruroha /
children.translated_text: The sun, its web of rays veiled by dense clouds, gradually ascended toward setting;

children.text: dināntalabdhaprasaraṃ samantāt tamo ghanībhāvam ivājagāma // AJm_14.7 //
children.translated_text: The darkness, finding scope at the end of day, seemed to gather into solidity from all sides.

children.text: dhārāśarair ācchuritormicakre mahodadhāv utpatatīva roṣāt /
children.translated_text: Upon the great ocean, its waves churning as if pierced by arrow-showers of rain,

children.text: bhīteva naur abhyadhikaṃ cakampe viṣādayantī hṛdayāni teṣām // AJm_14.8 //
children.translated_text: The ship trembled exceedingly, as if in fear, filling their hearts with despair.

children.text: te trāsadīnāś ca viṣādamūkā dhīrāḥ pratīkārasasaṃbhramāś ca /
children.translated_text: Some were dejected and mute with terror and despair, others were steadfast and bustled with counter-measures,

children.text: svadevatāyācanatatparāś ca bhāvān yathāsattvaguṇaṃ vivavruḥ // AJm_14.9 //
children.translated_text: Others still were intent on praying to their own deities—they displayed states according to the quality of their courage.

body.text: atha te sāṃyātrikāḥ pavanasalilavegavaśagayā nāvā paribhrāmyamāṇā bahubhir apy ahobhir naiva kutaś cit tīraṃ dadṛśur na ca yathepsitāni samudracihnāni / apūrvair eva tu samudracihnair abhivardhamānavaimanasyā bhayaviṣādavyākulatām upajagmuḥ // athainān supārago bodhisattvo vyavasthāpayann uvāca / anāścaryaḥ khalu samudram avagāḍhānām autpātikakṣobhaparikleśaḥ / tad alam atrabhavatāṃ viṣādānuvṛttyā /
body.translated_text: Then those seafarers, carried about by the ship at the mercy of the force of wind and water, even after many days saw no shore anywhere, nor the familiar ocean-signs. But encountering unprecedented ocean-signs, their distress increasing, they fell into the confusion of fear and despair. Then <s>Supāraga</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, steadying them, said: 'Indeed, it is not surprising that those who have ventured into the ocean experience the tribulation of unexpected disturbances. So enough of your yielding to despair!'

children.text: nāpatpratīkāravidhir viṣādas tasmād alaṃ dainyaparigraheṇa /
children.translated_text: 'Despair is not the remedy for calamity; therefore enough of embracing wretchedness.

children.text: dhairyāt tu kāryapratipattidakṣāḥ kṛcchrāṇy akṛcchreṇa samuttaranti // AJm_14.10 //
children.translated_text: But through courage, those skilled in accomplishing their task surmount difficulties without difficulty.'

children.text: viṣādadainyaṃ vyavadhūya tasmāt kāryāvakāśaṃ kriyayā bhajadhvam /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, shaking off the wretchedness of despair, devote yourselves to action when the opportunity for action presents itself.

children.text: prājñasya dhairyajvalitaṃ hi tejaḥ sarvārthasiddhigrahaṇāgrahastaḥ // AJm_14.11 //
children.translated_text: For the splendor of the wise, blazing with courage, is the foremost hand that grasps the attainment of all goals.'

body.text: iti te sāṃyātrikās tena mahātmanā dhīrīkṛtamanasaḥ kūlasaṃdarśanotsukamatayaḥ samudram avalokayanto dadṛśuḥ puruṣavigrahān āmuktarūpyakavacān ivonmajjato nimajjataś ca / samyak caiṣām ākṛtinimittam avadhārya savismayāḥ supāragāya nyavedayanta / apūrvaṃ khalv idam iha samudre cihnam upalabhyate / ete khalu
body.translated_text: Thus those seafarers, their minds made courageous by that great soul, eager to sight the shore, scanning the ocean, beheld beings of human form, as if clad in silver armor, rising and sinking. Having accurately ascertained the omen from their appearance, they reported to <s>Supāraga</s> with wonder: 'An unprecedented sign is indeed observed here in the ocean. These—

children.text: āmuktarūpyakavacā iva daityayodhā ghorekṣaṇāḥ kṣuranikāśavirūpaghoṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: As if demon-warriors clad in silver armor, with fearsome eyes and ugly noses sharp as razors,

children.text: unmajjanāvataraṇasphuraṇaprasaṅgāt kṛīḍām ivārṇavajale 'nubhavanti ke 'pi // AJm_14.12 //
children.translated_text: Through the play of their rising, sinking, and flashing, seem to be sporting in the ocean waters—who are they?'

body.text: supāraga uvāca / naite mānuṣā amānuṣā vā / mīnāḥ khalv ete yato na bhetavyam ebhyaḥ / kiṃ tu /
body.translated_text: <s>Supāraga</s> said: 'These are neither human nor non-human. These are indeed fish, so there is nothing to fear from them. However:'

children.text: sudūram apakṛṣṭāḥ smaḥ pattanadvitayād api /
children.translated_text: 'We have been carried exceedingly far from either of the two ports.

children.text: kṣuramālī samudro 'yaṃ tad yatadhvaṃ nivartitum // AJm_14.13 //
children.translated_text: This ocean is called <s>Kṣuramālī</s> (Garland of Razors)—so strive to turn back.'

body.text: caṇḍavegavāhinā tu salilanivahenaikāntahareṇa ca pāścātyena vāyunā samākṣiptayā nāvā na te sāṃyātrikāḥ śekur vinivartitum // athāvagāhamānāḥ krameṇa rūpyaprabhāvabhāsitasitasalilaṃ phenanicayapāṇḍaram aparaṃ samudram ālokya savismayāḥ supāragam ūcuḥ /
body.translated_text: But driven by the current of fierce velocity and the westerly wind that carried them inexorably in one direction, the ship could not be turned back by those seafarers. Then, proceeding further and beholding another ocean whose waters were white, illuminated with a silvery radiance, pale with heaps of foam, they said to <s>Supāraga</s> with wonder:

children.text: svaphenamagnair iva ko 'yam ambubhir mahārṇavaḥ śukladukūlavān iva /
children.translated_text: 'What is this great ocean, whose waters seem submerged in their own foam, as if wearing white silk,

children.text: dravān ivendoḥ kiraṇān samudvahan samantato hāsa iva prasarpati // AJm_14.14 //
children.translated_text: As if bearing the melting rays of the moon, spreading all around as if with laughter?'

body.text: supāraga uvāca / kaṣṭam / atidūraṃ khalv avagāhyate /
body.translated_text: <s>Supāraga</s> said: 'Alas! We are being carried exceedingly far indeed.'

children.text: kṣīrārṇava iti khyāta udadhir dadhimāly asau /
children.translated_text: 'This ocean is known as the <s>Kṣīrārṇava</s> (Milk Ocean), garlanded with curds.

children.text: kṣamaṃ nātaḥ paraṃ gantuṃ śakyate cen nivartitum // AJm_14.15 //
children.translated_text: It is not safe to go beyond this—turn back if it is possible.'

body.text: vaṇija ūcuḥ / na khalu śakyate vilambayitum api vahanaṃ kuta eva nivartayitum atiśīghravāhitvād vahanasya pratikūlatvāc ca mārutasyeti // atha vyatītya tam api samudraṃ suvarṇaprabhānurañjitapracalormimālam agnijvālākapilasalilam aparaṃ samudram ālokya savismayakautūhalās te vaṇijaḥ supāragaṃ papracchuḥ /
body.translated_text: The merchants said: 'We cannot even slow the vessel down, let alone turn it back, because of the extreme swiftness of its course and the contrary wind.' Then, having passed beyond that ocean too, beholding another ocean whose waters were golden-hued, tinted with the radiance of gold, its waters tawny as the flames of fire, those merchants, filled with wonder and curiosity, asked <s>Supāraga</s>:

children.text: bālārkalakṣmyeva kṛtāṅgarāgaiḥ samunnamadbhiḥ salilair anīlaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Blazing like a great fire, as if adorned with the beauty of the young morning sun, with its not-blue waters rising high—

children.text: jvalan mahān agnir ivāvabhāti ko nāma kasmāc ca mahārṇavo 'yam // AJm_14.16 //
children.translated_text: What is the name of this great ocean, and why [is it so]?'

body.text: supāraga uvāca /
body.translated_text: <s>Supāraga</s> said:

children.text: agnimālīti vikhyātaḥ samudro 'yaṃ prakāśate /
children.translated_text: 'This ocean is known as <s>Agnimālī</s> (Garland of Fire).

children.text: atīva khalu sādhu syān nivartemahi yady ataḥ // AJm_14.17 //
children.translated_text: It would be exceedingly good if we could turn back from here.'

body.text: iti sa mahātmā nāmamātram akathayat tasya saritpater na toyavaivarṇyakāraṇaṃ dīrghadarśitvāt // atha te sāṃyātrikās tam api samudram atītya puṣparāgendranīlaprabhoddyotitasalilaṃ paripakvakuśaparṇanikāśavarṇam aparaṃ samudram ālokya kautūhalajātāḥ supāragaṃ papracchuḥ /
body.translated_text: That great soul spoke only the name of that lord of rivers, not the cause of its water's discoloration, out of far-sightedness [to avoid further panic]. Then those seafarers, having passed beyond that ocean too, beholding another ocean whose waters gleamed with the splendor of topaz and sapphire, resembling the color of ripe <s>kuśa</s>-grass leaves, asked <s>Supāraga</s> with arisen curiosity:

children.text: pariṇatakuśaparṇavarṇatoyaḥ salilanidhiḥ katamo nv ayaṃ vibhāti /
children.translated_text: 'What is this ocean that shines, with waters the color of ripe <s>kuśa</s>-grass leaves,

children.text: sakusuma iva phenabhakticitrair anilajavākalitais taraṅgabhaṅgaiḥ // AJm_14.18 //
children.translated_text: As if in bloom, with its wave-crests variegated with heaps of foam like flowers, stirred by the swift wind?'

body.text: supāraga uvāca / bhoḥ sārthavāhā nivartanaṃ prati yatnaḥ kriyatām / na khalv ataḥ paraṃ kṣamate gantum /
body.translated_text: <s>Supāraga</s> said: 'O caravan-leaders, let effort be made to turn back! It is truly not safe to go beyond this.'

children.text: kuśamālī samudro 'yam atyaṅkuśa iva dvipaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This ocean is called <s>Kuśamālī</s> (Garland of Kuśa-grass)—like an elephant beyond the [reach of] the goad,

children.text: prasahyāsahyasalilo haran harati no ratim // AJm_14.19 //
children.translated_text: With waters irresistibly overwhelming, it seizes and carries away our joy.'

body.text: atha te vāṇijakāḥ pareṇāpi yatnena vahanaṃ nivartayitum aśaknuvantas tam api samudram atītya vaṃśarāgavaiḍūryaprabhāvyatikaraharitasalilam aparaṃ samudram ālokya supāragam apṛcchan /
body.translated_text: Then those merchants, unable to turn the vessel back even with their utmost effort, having passed beyond that ocean too, beholding another ocean whose waters were green from the intermingling of the radiance of bamboo-hued emerald and <s>vaiḍūrya</s> gems, asked <s>Supāraga</s>:

children.text: marakataharitaprabhair jalair vahati navām iva śādvalaśriyam /
children.translated_text: 'Bearing the beauty of a fresh meadow, as it were, with waters of emerald-green radiance,

children.text: kumudaruciraphenabhūṣaṇaḥ salilanidhiḥ katamo 'yam īkṣyate // AJm_14.20 //
children.translated_text: Adorned with foam beautiful as white water-lilies—what is this ocean that is seen?'

body.text: atha sa mahātmā tena tasya vaṇigjanasya vyasanopanipātena paridahyamānahṛdayo dīrgham uṣṇam abhiniśvasya śanakair uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then that great soul, his heart burning at the onset of this calamity upon the merchant-folk, having heaved a long, hot sigh, said slowly:

children.text: atidūram upetāḥ smaḥ duḥkham asmān nivartitum /
children.translated_text: 'We have come exceedingly far; it is difficult to turn us back.

children.text: paryanta iva lokasya nalamāly eṣa sāgaraḥ // AJm_14.21 //
children.translated_text: This ocean is the <s>Nalamālī</s> (Garland of Reeds), as if the edge of the world.'

body.text: tac chrutvā te vāṇijakā viṣādoparudhyamānamanaso visrasyamānagātrotsāhā niśvasitamātraparāyaṇās tatraiva niṣeduḥ / vyatītya tam api samudraṃ sāyāhnasamaye vilambamānamandaraśmimaṇḍale salilanidhim iva praveṣṭukāme divasakare samudvartamānasyeva salilanidher aśanīnām iva ca saṃpatatāṃ veṇuvanānām iva cāgniparigatānāṃ visphuṭatāṃ tumulam atibhīṣaṇaṃ śrutihṛdayavidāraṇaṃ samudradhvanim aśrauṣuḥ / śrutvā ca saṃtrāsavaśagāḥ sphuranmanasaḥ sahasaivotthāya samantato 'nuvilokayanto dadṛśuḥ prapāta iva śvabhra iva ca mahāntaṃ tam udakaughaṃ nipatantam </> dṛṣṭvā ca paramabhayavihvalāḥ supāragam upetyocuḥ /
body.translated_text: Hearing this, those merchants, their minds blocked by despair, their bodily vigor draining away, given over to nothing but sighing, sat down right there. Then, having passed beyond that ocean too, in the late afternoon, when the sun's disc of rays was lingering as if wishing to enter the reservoir of waters, they heard the tumultuous, exceedingly terrifying, ear-and-heart-rending roar of the ocean—like that of the ocean itself surging, or like thunderbolts crashing down, or like bamboo groves crackling when seized by fire. And upon hearing it, overcome by terror, their minds quaking, springing up at once and looking all around, they saw that vast mass of water plunging down like a waterfall, like an abyss. And seeing it, utterly bewildered with supreme fear, they approached <s>Supāraga</s> and said:

children.text: nirbhindann iva naḥ śrutīḥ pratibhayaś cetāṃsi mathnann iva kruddhasyeva saritpater dhvanir ayaṃ dūrād api śrūyate /
children.translated_text: 'As if piercing our ears, terrifying, as if churning our minds—this roar of the angry lord of rivers is heard even from afar.

children.text: bhīme śvabhra ivāgrataś ca nipataty etat samagraṃ jalaṃ tat ko 'sāv udadhiḥ kim atra ca paraṃ kṛtyaṃ bhavān manyate // AJm_14.22 //
children.translated_text: And before us all this water falls as if into a dreadful abyss—what ocean is this, and what further remedy does your honor see here?'

body.text: atha sa mahātmā sasaṃbhramaḥ kaṣṭaṃ kaṣṭam ity uktvā samudram ālokayann uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then that great soul, with agitation, having said 'Alas, alas!,' gazing at the ocean, spoke:

children.text: yat prāpya na nivartante mṛtyor mukham ivāmukham /
children.translated_text: 'That from which, once reached, none return—like the open mouth of Death,

children.text: aśivaṃ samupetāḥ smas tad etad vaḍabāmukham // AJm_14.23 //
children.translated_text: We have reached that inauspicious place—this is the <s>Vaḍabāmukha</s> (the Submarine Fire).'

body.text: tad upaśrutya te vāṇijakā vaḍabāmukham upetā vayam iti tyaktajīvitāśā maraṇabhayaviklavībhūtamanasaḥ
body.translated_text: Hearing this, those merchants, [realizing] 'We have reached the <s>Vaḍabāmukha</s>!,' abandoning hope of life, their minds bewildered by the fear of death—

children.text: sasvaraṃ ruruduḥ ke cid vilepur atha cukruśuḥ /
children.translated_text: Some wept aloud, others wailed, and some cried out.

children.text: na kiṃ cit pratyapadyanta ke cit trāsavicetasaḥ // AJm_14.24 //
children.translated_text: Others, their minds deranged by terror, could do nothing at all.

children.text: viśeṣataḥ ke cid abhipraṇemur devendram ārtiprahitair manobhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Some in particular prostrated themselves to the lord of the gods (<s>Indra</s>), their minds dispatched by anguish;

children.text: ādityarudrāśvimarudvasūṃś ca prapedire sāgaram eva cānye // AJm_14.25 //
children.translated_text: Others resorted to the <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Rudras</s>, <s>Aśvins</s>, <s>Maruts</s>, and <s>Vasus</s>—and yet others to the ocean itself.

children.text: jepuś ca mantrān apare vicitrān anye tu devīṃ vidhivat praṇemuḥ /
children.translated_text: Some recited various <s>mantras</s>; others bowed to the Goddess in the prescribed manner;

children.text: supāragaṃ ke cid upetya tat tad viceṣṭamānāḥ karuṇaṃ vilepuḥ // AJm_14.26 //
children.translated_text: And some, approaching <s>Supāraga</s>, making various desperate gestures, piteously wailed.
