children.text: āpadgatatrāsaharasya nityaṃ parānukampāguṇasaṃbhṛtasya /
children.translated_text: 'You who always remove the terror of those beset by calamity, who are endowed with the quality of compassion for others—

children.text: ayaṃ prabhāvātiśayasya tasya tavābhyupeto viniyogakālaḥ // AJm_14.27 //
children.translated_text: This is the time that has arrived for the employment of that extraordinary power of yours.'

children.text: ārtān anāthāñ charaṇāgatān nas tvaṃ trātum āvarjaya dhīra cetaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Turn your mind, O steadfast one, to rescuing us—afflicted, helpless, come to you for refuge—

children.text: ayaṃ hi kopād vaḍabāmukhena cikīrṣati grāsam ivārṇavo 'smān // AJm_14.28 //
children.translated_text: For this ocean, in its wrath, seeks to make us a morsel, as it were, through the <s>Vaḍabāmukha</s>.'

children.text: nopekṣituṃ yuktam ayaṃ janas te vipadyamānaḥ salilaughamadhye /
children.translated_text: 'It is not right for you to disregard these people of yours, perishing in the midst of the flood of waters.

children.text: nājñāṃ tavātyeti mahāsamudras tad vāryatām apraśamo 'yam asya // AJm_14.29 //
children.translated_text: The great ocean does not transgress your command—therefore restrain this restlessness of his.'

body.text: atha sa mahātmā mahatyā karuṇayā samāpīḍyamānahṛdayas tān vāṇijakān vyavasthāpayann uvāca / asty atrāpi naḥ kaś cit pratīkāravidhiḥ pratibhāti / taṃ tāvat prayokṣye yato muhūrtaṃ dhīrās tāvad bhavantu bhavanta iti // atha te vāṇijakā asty atrāpi pratīkāra ity āśayā samupastambhitadhairyās tadavahitamanasas tūṣṇīṃbabhūvuḥ // atha supārago bodhisattva ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇena jānumaṇḍalenādhiṣṭhāya nāvaṃ samāvarjitasarvabhāvaḥ praṇamya tathāgatebhyas tān sāṃyātrikān āmantrayate sma / śṛṇvantv atrabhavantaḥ sāṃyātrikāḥ salilanidhivyomāśrayāś ca devatāviśeṣāḥ /
body.translated_text: Then that great soul, his heart pressed by great compassion, steadying those merchants, said: 'There comes to mind for us a remedy even for this. I shall employ it now—so be courageous for a moment, good sirs.' Then those merchants, their courage restored by the hope that 'there is a remedy even for this,' their minds attentive to him, fell silent. Then <s>Supāraga</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having arranged his upper garment over one shoulder, kneeling on the ship with his right knee, with all his being concentrated, having bowed to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, addressed those seafarers: 'Let the honorable seafarers listen, as well as the special deities dwelling in the ocean and the sky!'

children.text: smarāmi yata ātmānaṃ yataḥ prāpto 'smi vijñatām /
children.translated_text: 'From the time I remember myself, from the time I attained discernment,

children.text: nābhijānāmi saṃcintya prāṇinaṃ hiṃsituṃ kva cit // AJm_14.30 //
children.translated_text: I am not aware of ever having intentionally harmed a living being anywhere.'

children.text: anena satyavākyena mama puṇyabalena ca /
children.translated_text: 'By this truthful declaration, and by the power of my merit,

children.text: vaḍabāmukham aprāpya svasti naur vinivartatām // AJm_14.31 //
children.translated_text: May the ship turn back safely without reaching the <s>Vaḍabāmukha</s>!'

body.text: atha tasya mahātmanaḥ satyādhiṣṭhānaprabhāvāt puṇyatejasā ca saha salilajavena sa māruto vyāvartamānas tāṃ nāvaṃ vinivartayām āsa / nivṛttāṃ tu tāṃ nāvam abhisamīkṣya te vāṇijakāḥ paramavismayapraharṣoddhatamānasā nivṛttā nivṛttā naur iti praṇāmasabhājanapuraḥsaraṃ supāragāya nyavedayanta // atha sa mahātmā tān vāṇijakān uvāca /

children.text: sthirībhavantu bhavantaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Be steadfast, good sirs!'

children.text: śīghram āropyantāṃ śītāni / iti ca tena samādiṣṭāḥ pramodād udbhūtabalotsāhās te tadadhikṛtās tathā cakruḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Hoist the sails quickly!' And thus commanded by him, those in charge, their strength and vigor springing from delight, did so.

body.translated_text: Then, by the power of that great soul's truth-declaration (<s>satyādhiṣṭhāna</s>) and by the splendor of his merit, the wind reversed itself along with the swift current and turned that ship around. And seeing the ship turned back, those merchants, their minds elated with supreme wonder and joy, reported to <s>Supāraga</s>, preceded by bows and congratulations: 'The ship has turned back! The ship has turned back!' Then that great soul said to those merchants:

children.text: atha muditajanaprahāsanādā pravitatapāṇḍaraśītacārupakṣā /
children.translated_text: Then that ship, resounding with the laughter of delighted people, with its beautiful white sails spread wide,

children.text: salilanidhigatā rarāja sā naur gatajalade nabhasīva rājahaṃsī // AJm_14.32 //
children.translated_text: Was splendid upon the ocean, like a royal swan in the sky when the clouds have departed.

body.text: nivṛttāyāṃ tu tasyām anukūlasalilamārutāyāṃ vimānalīlayā svecchayaivābhiprayātāyāṃ nāvi nātiśyāmībhūtasaṃdhyāṅgarāgāsu pravitanyamānatamovitānāsv ālakṣyanakṣatrabhūṣaṇāsu dikṣu kiṃ cid avaśeṣaprabhe divasakaramārge pravṛtte kṣaṇadādhikāre supāragas tān vāṇijakān uvāca / bhoḥ sārthavāhā nalamāliprabhṛtibhyo yathādṛṣṭebhyaḥ samudrebhyo vālikāpāṣāṇā vahanam āropyantāṃ yāvat sahate / evam idaṃ yānapātraṃ nirghātabharākrāntaṃ na ca pārśvāni dāsyati / maṅgalasaṃmatāś caite vālikāpāṣāṇā niyataṃ lābhasiddhaye vo bhaviṣyantīti // te supāragapremabahumānāvarjitamatibhir devatābhir anupradarśitebhyaḥ sthalebhya ādāya vālikāpāṣāṇabuddhyā vaiḍūryādīni ratnāni vahanam āropayām āsuḥ // tenaiva caikarātreṇa sā naur bharukaccham upajagāma //
body.translated_text: When the ship had turned around, with favorable water and wind, proceeding at its own pleasure with the ease of a celestial mansion, and the twilight-blush not yet fully darkened still lingered on the horizon, and the canopy of darkness was spreading, and the star-ornaments of the quarters were becoming visible, and some residual light remained on the path of the daymaker, as night's authority began—<s>Supāraga</s> said to the merchants: 'Sirs, caravan-leaders! Let sand and pebbles be loaded onto the ship from the oceans—<s>Nalamāli</s> and the others—that have been seen, as much as it can bear. Thus this vessel, weighted with ballast, will not tip to the sides. And these sand and pebbles, considered auspicious, will surely bring you the attainment of profit.' The merchants, guided by the deities whose minds were won over by their love and respect for <s>Supāraga</s>, took from the shores—shown to them [by the deities]—jewels such as <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl) and the rest, thinking them sand and pebbles, and loaded them onto the ship. And by that very single night, the ship arrived at <s>Bharukaccha</s>.

children.text: atha prabhāte rajatendranīlavaiḍūryahemapratipūrṇanaukāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then at dawn, their boats filled with silver, sapphire, beryl, and gold,

children.text: svadeśatīrāntam upāgatās te prītyā tam ānarcur udīrṇaharṣāḥ // AJm_14.33 //
children.translated_text: Having arrived at the shore of their own land, they honored him with boundless joy.

body.text: tad evaṃ dharmāśrayaṃ satyavacanam apy āpadaṃ nudati prāg eva tatphalam iti dharmānuvartinā bhavitavyam //
body.translated_text: Therefore, thus even truthful speech grounded in <s>dharma</s> averts calamity—how much more so its fruit! Thus one should be a follower of <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: kalyāṇamitrāśrayavarṇe 'pi vācyam evaṃ kalyāṇamitrāśritāḥ śreyaḥ prāpnuvantīti //
body.translated_text: In the section describing reliance on spiritual friends also, it should be stated: 'Thus those who rely on spiritual friends attain the highest good.'

body.text: supāragajātakaṃ caturdaśam //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourteenth, the <s>Supāraga-Jātaka</s>.

children.text: 15. Matsyajātakam
children.translated_text: 15. The <s>Matsya-Jātaka</s> (Fish Story).

body.text: śīlavatām ihaivābhiprāyāḥ kalyāṇāḥ samṛdhyanti prāg eva paratreti śīlaviśuddhau prayatitavyam //
body.translated_text: For the virtuous, even in this life their noble intentions are fulfilled—how much more so in the next! Therefore one should strive for the purity of moral conduct.

body.text: tadyathānuśrūyate / bodhisattvaḥ kila kasmiṃś cin nātimahati kahlāratāmarasakamalakuvalayavibhūṣitarucirasalile haṃsakāraṇḍavacakravākamithunopaśobhite tīrāntaruhatarukusumāvakīrṇe sarasi matsyādhipatir babhūva / svabhyastabhāvāc ca bahuṣu janmāntareṣu parārthacaryāyās tatrastho 'pi parahitasukhopapādanasavyāpāro babhūva /
body.translated_text: As is traditionally heard: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, it is said, in a certain not-too-large lake—beautiful with its waters adorned by <s>kahlāra</s>, <s>tāmarasa</s>, <s>kamala</s>, and <s>kuvalaya</s> lotuses, graced by pairs of geese, <s>kāraṇḍava</s> ducks, and <s>cakravāka</s> birds, strewn with flowers from trees growing along its shore—was born as the lord of the fish. And through habitual practice in many former lives of laboring for others' welfare, even there he was engaged in bringing about the benefit and happiness of others.

children.text: abhyāsayogād dhi śubhāśubhāni karmāṇi sātmy eva bhavanti puṃsām /
children.translated_text: For through habitual practice, both wholesome and unwholesome deeds become natural to people;

children.text: tathāvidhāny eva yad aprayatnāj janmāntare svapna ivācaranti // AJm_15.1 //
children.translated_text: Thus, such deeds of the same kind are performed effortlessly in another birth, as if in a dream.

body.text: iṣṭānām iva ca sveṣām apatyānām upari niviṣṭahārdo sa mahāsattvas teṣāṃ mīnānāṃ dānapriyavacanārthacaryādikramaiḥ param anugrahaṃ cakāra /
body.translated_text: And that great being, his heart as deeply attached to them as to his own beloved offspring, conferred the highest benefit upon those fish through the progressive methods of generosity, kind speech, beneficial conduct, and the rest.

children.text: anyonyahiṃsāpraṇayaṃ niyacchan parasparaprema vivardhayaṃś ca /
children.translated_text: Restraining their inclination to mutual harm, and fostering mutual love among them,

children.text: yogād upāyajñatayā ca teṣāṃ vismārayām āsa sa matsyavṛttam // AJm_15.2 //
children.translated_text: Through diligence and knowledge of skillful means, he made them forget [their] fish-nature.

children.text: tat tena samyak paripālyamānaṃ vṛddhiṃ parāṃ mīnakulaṃ jagāma /
children.translated_text: That community of fish, well-protected by him, attained the highest growth,

children.text: puraṃ vinirmuktam ivopasargair nyāyapravṛttena narādhipena // AJm_15.3 //
children.translated_text: Like a city freed from calamities by a righteous king.

body.text: atha kadā cit sattvānāṃ bhāgyasaṃpadvaikalyāt pramādāc ca varṣādhikṛtānāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ na samyag devo vavarṣa / asamyag varṣiṇi ca deve tat saraḥ phullakadambakusumagaureṇa navasalilena na yathāpūrvam āpupūre / krameṇa copagate nidāghasamaye paṭutaradīptibhiḥ khedālasagatibhir iva ca dinakarakiraṇais tadabhitaptayā ca dharaṇyā jvālānugateneva ca hlādābhilāṣiṇā mārutena tarṣavaśād iva pratyaham āpīyamānaṃ tat saraḥ palvalībabhūva /
body.translated_text: Then once, due to a deficiency in the merit of beings, and through the negligence of the divine sons in charge of the rains, the rain-god did not rain properly. And when the rains failed, that lake was not filled as before with fresh water, white as blossoming <s>kadamba</s> flowers. And as summer gradually arrived, with the increasingly sharp rays of the sun—moving sluggishly as if weary from heat—and the earth heated by them, and the wind, as if following flames and desiring refreshment, seeming to drink the waters each day out of thirst, the lake became a mere puddle.

children.text: nidāghakālajvalito vivasvāñ jvālāvakarṣīva paṭuś ca vāyuḥ /
children.translated_text: The blazing sun kindled by the summer season, the sharp wind like a drawing flame,

children.text: jvarāturevāśiśirā ca bhūmis toyāni roṣād iva śoṣayanti // AJm_15.4 //
children.translated_text: And the feverish earth, not yet cool—seemed to dry up the waters as if in anger.

body.text: atha bodhisattvo vāyasagaṇair api pratarkyamāṇaṃ prāg eva salilatīrāntacāribhiḥ pakṣigaṇair viṣādadainyavaśagaṃ vispanditamātraparāyaṇaṃ mīnakulam avekṣya karuṇāyamāṇaś cintām āpede / kaṣṭā bateyam āpad āpatitā mīnānām /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, seeing the community of fish—being watched even by flocks of crows, let alone the birds roaming the water's edge—overwhelmed by despair and wretchedness, barely able to flap about, was moved to compassion and fell into reflection: 'Alas, what a terrible calamity has befallen the fish!'

children.text: pratyahaṃ kṣīyate toyaṃ spardhamānam ivāyuṣā /
children.translated_text: 'Day by day the water diminishes, as if competing with their lifespan;

children.text: adyāpi ca cireṇaiva lakṣyate jaladāgamaḥ // AJm_15.5 //
children.translated_text: And even now, the arrival of rain-clouds is seen only after a long time.'

children.text: apayānakramo nāsti netāpy anyatra ko bhavet /
children.translated_text: 'There is no way to retreat; who could be a leader [to take them] elsewhere?

children.text: asmadvyasanasaṃhṛṣṭāḥ samāyānti ca no dviṣaḥ // AJm_15.6 //
children.translated_text: And our enemies, delighted at our misfortune, are closing in.'

children.text: asya niḥsaṃśayam ime toyaśeṣasya saṃkṣayāt /
children.translated_text: 'Without doubt, from the exhaustion of this remaining water,

children.text: sphuranto bhakṣayiṣyante śatrubhir mama paśyataḥ // AJm_15.7 //
children.translated_text: These [fish], still struggling, will be devoured by enemies before my very eyes.'

body.text: tat kim atra prāptakālaṃ syād iti vimṛśan sa mahātmā satyādhiṣṭhānam ekam ārtāyanaṃ dadarśa / karuṇayā ca samāpīḍyamānahṛdayo dīrgham uṣṇam abhiniśvasya nabhaḥ samullokayann uvāca /
body.translated_text: 'What then would be appropriate here?' Reflecting thus, that great soul saw one refuge for the distressed: a truth-declaration. And with his heart pressed by compassion, heaving a long, hot sigh, looking up at the sky, he said:

children.text: smarāmi na prāṇivadhaṃ yathāhaṃ saṃcintya kṛcchre parame 'pi kartum /
children.translated_text: 'I do not recall ever having deliberately killed a living being, even in the greatest extremity;

children.text: anena satyena sarāṃsi toyair āpūrayan varṣatu devarājaḥ // AJm_15.8 //
children.translated_text: By this truth, may the King of Gods rain, filling the lakes with water!'

body.text: atha tasya mahātmanaḥ puṇyopacayaguṇāt satyādhiṣṭhānabalāt tadabhiprasāditadevanāgayakṣānubhāvāc ca samantatas toyāvalambibimbā gambhīramadhuranirghoṣā vidyullatālaṃkṛtā nīlavipulaśikharā vijṛmbhamāṇā iva pravisarpibhiḥ śikharabhujaiḥ pariṣvajyamānā iva cānyonyam akālameghāḥ kālameghāḥ prādurabhavan /
body.translated_text: Then, through the quality of that great soul's accumulated merit, through the power of his truth-declaration, and through the influence of the gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, and <s>Yakṣas</s> propitiated by him, from all directions appeared untimely clouds—yet [resembling] timely ones—bearing reflected images of water, deeply and sweetly rumbling, adorned with streaks of lightning, with vast dark peaks, expanding as if with spreading summit-arms embracing one another.

children.text: diśāṃ pramiṇvanta iva prayāmaṃ śṛṅgair vitanvanta ivāndhakāram /
children.translated_text: As if measuring the extent of the quarters, as if spreading darkness with their peaks,

children.text: nabhastalādarśagatā virejuś chāyā girīṇām iva kālameghāḥ // AJm_15.9 //
children.translated_text: The dark clouds shone upon the mirror of the sky, like the shadows of mountains.

children.text: saṃsaktakekaiḥ śikhibhiḥ prahṛṣṭaiḥ saṃstūyamānā iva nṛttacitraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Praised, as it were, by delighted peacocks whose cries were joined together and whose dances were wondrous,

children.text: prasaktamandrastanitā virejur dhīraprahāsā iva te ghanaughāḥ // AJm_15.10 //
children.translated_text: Those masses of clouds shone with steady, deep thunder, as if with the composed laughter of the steadfast.

children.text: muktā vimuktā iva tair vimuktā dhārā nipetuḥ praśaśāma reṇuḥ /
children.translated_text: Pearls of rain were released, as if freed by them; torrents fell; the dust was quieted;

children.text: gandhaś cacārānibhṛto dharaṇyāṃ vikīryamāṇo jaladānilena // AJm_15.11 //
children.translated_text: The fragrance of the earth spread abroad unceasingly, scattered by the rain-wind.

children.text: nidāghasaṃparkavivardhito 'pi tirobabhūvārkakaraprabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: The power of the sun's rays, though amplified by contact with summer, disappeared;

children.text: phenāvalīvyākulamekhalāni toyāni nimnābhimukhāni sasruḥ // AJm_15.12 //
children.translated_text: Waters flowed toward the lowlands, their girdles turbulent with lines of foam.

children.text: muhur muhuḥ kāñcanapiñjarābhir bhābhir digantān anurañjayantī /
children.translated_text: Again and again, tinting the horizons with golden-tawny radiance,

children.text: payodatūryasvanalabdhaharṣā vidyullatā nṛttam ivācacāra // AJm_15.13 //
children.translated_text: The streak of lightning, delighted by the musical sound of the cloud-drums, seemed to perform a dance.

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ samantato 'bhiprasṛtair āpāṇḍubhiḥ salilapravāhair āpūryamāṇe sarasi dhārānipātasamakālam eva vidrute vāyasādye pakṣigaṇe pratilabdhajīvitāśe pramudite mīnagaṇe prītyābhisāryamāṇahṛdayo varṣanivṛttisāśaṅkaḥ punaḥ punaḥ parjanyam ābabhāṣe /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, as the lake was being filled from all sides by rushing streams of pallid water, as the flocks of crows and other birds fled at the very instant the rain-torrents fell, as the community of fish, having regained hope of life, rejoiced—his heart driven by delight, yet apprehensive that the rain might stop—addressed the rain-cloud again and again:

children.text: udgarja parjanya gabhīradhīraṃ pramodam udvāsaya vāyasānām /
children.translated_text: 'Roar, O rain-cloud, with deep and steady [thunder]! Drive away the joy of the crows!

children.text: ratnāyamānāni payāṃsi varṣan saṃsaktavidyujjvalitadyutīni // AJm_15.14 //
children.translated_text: Rain gem-like waters, blazing with the brightness of continuous lightning!'

body.text: tad upaśrutya śakro devānām indraḥ paramavismitamanāḥ sākṣād abhigamyainam abhisaṃrādhayann uvāca /
body.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, supremely astonished in mind, came to him in person and, honoring him, said:

children.text: tavaiva khalv eṣa mahānubhāva matsyendra satyātiśayaprabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This is indeed your great power, O lord of fish—the surpassing power of your truth;

children.text: āvarjitā yat kalaśā iveme kṣaranti ramyastanitāḥ payodāḥ // AJm_15.15 //
children.translated_text: For these clouds, pouring as if from overturned pitchers, thunder sweetly.'

children.text: mahatpramādaskhalitaṃ tv idaṃ me yan nāma kṛtyeṣu bhavadvidhānām /
children.translated_text: 'This is a great lapse of negligence on my part—that I do not attain the opportunity of employment

children.text: lokārtham abhyutthitamānasānāṃ vyāpārayogaṃ na samabhyupaimi // AJm_15.16 //
children.translated_text: In the duties of those like you, whose minds are risen for the welfare of the world.'

children.text: cintāṃ kṛthā mā tad ataḥ paraṃ tvaṃ satāṃ hi kṛtyodvahane 'smi dhuryaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore grieve no more—for I am the foremost bearer of the duties of the virtuous;

children.text: deśo 'py ayaṃ tvadguṇasaṃśrayeṇa na bhūya evaṃ bhavitārtivaśyaḥ // AJm_15.17 //
children.translated_text: And this region, through the refuge of your virtues, shall never again be subject to such affliction.'

body.text: ity evaṃ priyavacanair abhisaṃrādhya tatraivāntardadhe / tac ca saraḥ parāṃ toyasamṛddhim avāpa //
body.translated_text: Having thus honored him with kind words, he vanished right there. And that lake attained the fullest abundance of water.

body.text: tad evaṃ śīlavatām ihaivābhiprāyāḥ kalyāṇāḥ samṛdhyanti prāg eva paratreti śīlaviśuddhau prayatitavyam iti //
body.translated_text: Therefore, thus for the virtuous, even in this life their noble intentions are fulfilled—how much more so in the next! Thus one should strive for the purity of moral conduct.

body.text: matsyajātakaṃ pañcadaśam //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fifteenth, the <s>Matsya-Jātaka</s>.
